--- 帖子 #4 ---
Trotty, I am trading from work through a firewall which doesn't like the chat software. I miss you guys too. The twist that I added to this method can be described by the following: 1. I have always open a M1 chart during trading which helps me fine tune my entries &amp; exits. 2. I tend to take quick profits. My daily target is 30-40 pips with 3% risk. So usually using the Dance rules I can achieve this in 3-4 trades (each from 8-15 pips). My SL is no more than 15-19 pips. If I judge from M1 that action doesn't like me I stop the trade earlier than 19 pips. 3. Other than that the name of the game is to react quickly during the normal Dance bounces (MA, RN, etc.). IF you reach daily target then you immediately quit for the day. If you reach daily loss you also quit. In time I will mention a couple of other things that I found to be helpful in getting higher winning %. Kostas

--- 帖子 #14 ---
Lee, In my experience it's best to take the first touch on the M15 scale. The second may be an attempt to cross. On the other hand, I have found that on the M1 scale most times is better to take the 2nd touch. This means that while the M15 bar touches for the first time, the M1 will touch fake you up and then come back down to take your small SL. It will then go back up in the right direction. I call this head-fake and has helped me a lot to avoid some bad trades. Kostas

--- 帖子 #68 ---
Alex, According to the Dance you can follow the trade by following your SL at the previous 15M bar. So for a long trade your SL is 2-3 pips below the low of the previously closed 15M bar. Opposite for short (+spread). What I have found to work for me is to grab quickly your profit before that (12-15 pips per trade usually). Obviously, in this way you may loose opportunities for many more pips but it has the advantage to give you higher winning% since even in a fake bounce you can almost always get 10-15 pips. Kostas Kostas

--- 帖子 #69 ---
Alex, Near the end of the original thread there is a post from Clay which has a script which opens two trades. With this you can close one off early as Kostas suggests and then set the other to either breakeven OR set the SL to where you have just closed the other one..... assuming of course that the price is no less that 5 pips (maybe more, maybe less) from the current price. What this will acheive is 50% profits at a point where you want...... at this stage, I'd recomend you take a look at Kostas success's as this will be a great indication of when to take profit and then set and advanced SL ahead of behind that. If price moves back, it hits the SL which will already be in profit, if it continues forward, you are still in the trade and you can follow the PA with your stop losses. Another thing to bear in mind, my broker allows me to close partial trades. So if I have a whole lot in (1.0) I can close an amount of that (in 1/10th's). So..... you could even close off partial trades of the trade that is continuing. It requires a little more involvement and is not 'by the rules', but it is an option. I am not sure if ALL brokers offer this. Regards Lee

--- 帖子 #87 ---
Understanding the rules is vitally important with the Dance strat. Ignore a rule at your peril, you will be seeing your hide on a platter. This trade had far too many bullish bars in the retrace for a valid entry. We are looking for a swift 2/3 bars. 4 clean bars might be acceptable but approach with caution. What isn't mentioned in the literature is to keep price action in mind if you don't get a great looking setup for a touch trade. Once that big doji candle closed across the 35/50 mavs, I would have seriously looked at getting in on a break of that bar short. What does this price action tell you? It tells you that the bulls have hit a buffer at a point of interest. The 35/50 are areas of dynamic support and resistance and if the candle pushed through but was then pushed back all the way to the ma's again, it's an indication that the drive up is running out of gas at the resistance area. A break of that bar short then becomes a decent place to consider a trade IMO.

--- 帖子 #91 ---
3xtrader, My trading plan is the following: I use a daily target of 30-40 pips with a 3% risk per day. Therefore, I adjust my lot size to correspond to this target. The target is usually achieved by 3-5 trades per day with each trade giving me 10-15 pips. Some rare days when I was brave and felt that I had an AAA trade I was able to finish the day with just one quick trade. 98% of my trades achieved target before 30 min and most of those before 15-20 min. When I first started using the Dance my account allowed 0.1 lot for the 3% risk. Now I operate at 0.3 lots. My final target is to get to an account size that allows 3-5 lots (at 3% risk) and have a daily profit of 1000 Euros/day. Most of the fight is not achieving your daily pips (which I get almost all the time) but adjusting your psychology for the bigger amount of money at stake when the lots increase (at least that's my struggle). Kostas

Regardless of the speed you use, pressing F12 will move things forward quickly. You can press it once and it will move forward a little, I dont mean it will move a bar, but it will move within your current bar. Press and hold it and it will move forward faster. The reason this is usefull is that you can actualy have the sim on pause and F12 will still work, which means that when there is no trade 'on', press and hold it until you get near some areas of interest. YOu may have to enable this function in theoption menu, as it also works on live charts when you go back in time! Lee

Hey Ninja, One thing to be aware of and this applies to anyone who is now using the two trade script. If you have lowered your lot size so that you can open two trades at once and one of them gets stopped out at BE, then you need to be carefull how you count those pips. If you normaly trade 1.0 lot size and you drop to two times 0.5, if one hits 20 pips and one gets stopped out at BE then you have only really got 10 pips as your trade was only at 50%. I am sure you guys are aware of this, but I thought I best raise it, just incase. LEe

--- 帖子 #176 ---
Hey Kosta. I obviously don't consider myself an experienced trader but I can't really see how else you could grow an account. I have gone from one to two lots now - scary eh? If all you ever did was trade the same lot size, it'd take you an eternity to get to a big enough account to make all the effort worth it. The only way is to increase the lot size when your account is big enough that the next size up is around 2/3% of the account. I would see it as reward for you effort and ability rather than something to worry about. You should embrace and relish that you have made it to the next level - it's the next rung of the ladder to your personal fortune!. By growing your account and taking good trades, you get to reward yourself by making even more money per trade! Always remember that nothing fundementally changes when you increase your position size so the only change is in your head. That bit, unlike everything else, is the one bit that traders still have a total ability to control!

I just started reading "Trading in the Zone." This PDF was included in Clay's original zip-file of The Dance. Boy, I really wish I had read this BEFORE I jumped into the "deep end of the pool." As far as I'm concerned, this book is just as important, if not more so, than the Dance manual. If you think you understand all of the rules of The Dance but are still having problems getting consistent wins, then you need to read this book. I have the following scripts if people want them (they are set for a 5 digit broker - but I can tell you how to change them - it's easy enough). Please note, the buy and sell scripts work off the global variable (F3) settings for lot size. So you will need to adjust this to ensure you get the correct lot traded. 1a Buy @ 12SL &amp; 15TP 1b Buy @ 12SL &amp; 30TP 1c Buy @ 12SL &amp; 50TP 2a Sell @ 12SL &amp; 15TP 2b Sell @ 12SL &amp; 30TP 2c Sell @ 12SL &amp; 50TP 3a Move SL (this moves all current SL's on the chart) 3b Move TP (this moves all current TP's on the chart) 3c Move SL to break even. PA needs to have moved sufficiently far from your entry 4a ECA Emergency Close All. Close all active trades on the account 4b/c/d These have not been tested as they close various trades across different pairs. 5a DCO Delete chart objects. This deletes the messy arrows, trendlines and little marks that your trades leave behind. (I have not tested this to see if it removes standard trendlines or SR.... so be careful) A_Setlot size. This was in the original set from Clay, I am not sure if it is needed or not, but you have to adjust this so that the others do not defer to it. Regards Lee

--- 帖子 #309 ---
Hiram, 1) I personally like to focus on just one currency. My favorite is GU but in general my suggestion to newbies is to focus on one currency that has low spread and good movement. You get plenty of opportunities and staying with one currency you learn how it moves and you build "anticipation". 2) I use pivot points as an addition to the Dance, since price seems to react nicely there. When pivot points coincide with MAs (i.e. confluence) it makes me even more confident in my trading. In addition, I use pivot points as potential take profit targets. Kostas. P.S. I was "trolling" through the section on Trading Systems and came across the " Tkpower8 ATM " method. Bunch of fancy indicators that Clay warns about in The Dance manual so I can't comment on the system itself. However, when you click on the link to download the Beginner ATM manual, you get taken to a different site: http://www.electrolegal.com/forum/vi...php?f=17&amp;t=209 If you look at how they have their chart set up, you'll see a nifty "info panel" on the right hand side that contains a FOREX calendar along with the expected impact on various currency pairs. At the time of typing this the PA on the 5minute was looking healthy with a nice hangman followed by a nice bull candle, however, it seems the 5minute 10ema has dragged the price down. I will not move my BE as I want to see what happens, but it's looking like it will get hit. I will post a close chart when its done. Apologies for lack of detail on the chart, I am using the small laptop again. Lee *edit* Just closed the final part of the trade out for 35 pips as price seemed to stumble around the 15minute 10ema. I think it will keep going, but maybe I'll look for another entry above all this confluence on a re-test..... maybe! So that's three parts at 15/25/35 pips giving me 25 pips total for the trade. I'll just explain that last bit about why I got 25 pips for the trade.... I don't want you to think that I think you are stupid, equally so, I don't want anyone not understand it. When you split a trade and take serperate profits, your pip counter (if you use one) and the account history show amount of pips gained on each trade closed! So even if you only open one trade, but do three partial closes, it will show you 3 sets of gains, each with their own pips. A common mistake (and I made it a few times) is to count these gains seperatley and state that you had XXX pip gain, in the case of my last trade, to some it may look like I just made 15+25+35 = 75 pips, but as I split my trade by three parts, I averaged 25 pips, which was infact the total. This is important if you are trading to a pip target, like Kostas and I am doing. If you are trading for % or £/$ profit, then it's irrelevant. I hope my hash of an explanation means something to someone .

--- 帖子 #329 ---
The FIRST thing to try is to close MT4 and then re-start it again and see if your indicator now works. If it doesn't, you usually have to compile it before it will work. In other words: 1. Copy the indicator(s) to the experts &gt; indicators directory. 2. Press F4 (or Tools &gt; Language Editor on the top menu) to access the Editor 3. In the Editor, find the indicator on the list on the right and double click. It should open and display the code. 4. Press F5 (or File &gt; Compile from the top menu). The code should compile and should see a "0 error(s), 0 warning(s)" in the Error message box at the bottom. 5. Close (exit) the Editor and you should be back in your chart screen. Now try to reapply the indicator to your chart and see if it works. Hope this helps. Hiram PS: also try changing your chart's background color using Properties. Some indicators assume that you'll be using the default black background and are set to display using white text. I like a chart with a white background so an indicator with white text won't appear to be working (ie: won't show up) unless I change the background to a darker color.

--- 帖子 #352 ---
Haven't counted them but they do happen. On the other hand, being patient helps avoid some head-fakes and increases winning%. You just have to fight the urge to get in right away. It's probably time that I talked about M1 head-fakes. Let's imagine price coming from above to touch 35/50 on M15 (which means you are going to go long). Many time the price will touch, then go up (gets you in the trade), but then quickly reverses (head-fake) and overshoots the 35/50 by 10-12 pips (and takes out small SLs and stops you out). It then quickly goes back up in the right direction. All this can be observed in the M1 TF and what I normally do is wait for the second touch-overshoot to get in. This means that I miss some opportunities when the price directly shoots up but gives me higher probability trades. Kostas.

--- 帖子 #367 ---
As Kostas says, the higher timeframes are important. Technicaly the higher the MA the more important it 'should' be, therefore a 50 on the 1hr is the equivalent of a 200 on the 15minute, therefore you would expect more resistance there. High timeframe PA is also suppposed to be stronger too. That said, Clay oringial started his strategy with 5 minute chart entries, however he stopped using it because he found he was taking signals on it, rather than using it for entries only. Though.... if you look at the strategies employed by Kostas and Clay, although they share the same overall trading strategy, Kostas' attitude to taking profit was very very differnt to Clays. He admitted himself that he was prone to swinging for the heavens on each trade and nearer the end of his thread, he did state that he thought Kostas's method of taking pips when they were there was the right way to go. He has also said the same in emails to me. If you take this information, then the 5minute chart makes sense. Signals on there 'should' give over less pips, but if you are happy to take those pips, then it really doesn't matter. Obviously, Kostas has taken this one step further and now takes entries off the 1minute chart, which infact means he is trading the 5minute chart, whereas you and I are trading the 15minute chart. Essentialy you need ALL the timeframes. Though..... to many and you will start seeing counter signals and there will be to many reason to not go in. My advice, based on my VERY limited knowledge, would be to settle on however many timeframes you want and then do NOT change them. I am unlikely to use the 4hr, for some reason the idea that everyones 4hr charts are differnt upsets me a little, therefore I do not trust it, at least not with this strategy. One thing that is starting to happen to me and Kostas touched on it today, the smaller timeframes really do tell the story of the standalone candles. You can see a candle on the 15minute and think it didn't bounce off that MA, when infact it did and it gave up 15 pips then retraced again. The 15minute (or which ever TF) won't show you this but the lower ones will. And again, this ties in well for me when you start thinking about taking lower levels of pips. After wading through "Trading in the Zone," here's what I've determined are the most important take-aways (that I plan to paste next to my monitor!): The 7 Rules of a consistent winner: I objectively identify my edges. I predefine the risk of every trade I completely accept the risk or I am willing to let go of the trade I act on my edges without reservation or hesitation I pay myself as the market makes money available to me I continually monitor my susceptibility for making errors I understand the absolute necessity of these principles of consistent success and therefore I never violate them . The 5 Fundamental Truths of the Market: Anything can happen. The Market can change directions at any moment. It can go up, down, sideways, or stay the same. It’s past history or direction is no guarantee of future direction. Anything can happen. You don’t need to know what is going to happen next in order to make money. In fact, trying to predict what’s going to happen next leads to emotional distress, fear, anticipation, elation – all emotions that cloud your judgment and prevent you from seeing what the market is presenting. There is a random distribution between wins and loses for any given set of variables that define an edge. What you need is an edge that puts the odds in your favor – and then you need to take enough trades so that the probabilities work in your favor. An edge is nothing more than an indication of a higher probability of one thing happening over another. All it does is put the odds in your favor over the long term – it does NOT predict individual winners and losers. Every moment in the market is unique. It doesn’t matter what the market has done in the past because the past is history. Just like each flip of a coin is a unique event with the same 50/50 probability, each moment in the market is unique. You can become the Casino instead of the Player if: You have an edge that genuinely puts the odds of success in your favor (your trading system) You think about trading in the appropriate manner (the 5 Fundamental Truths of the Market) You do everything you need to do over a series of trades (the 7 rules of a Consistent Winner) Then, like a casino, you will own the game and be a consistent winner.

--- 帖子 #370 ---
I found the same advice in "Trading in the Zone." The author recommends trading in sets of 3's (ie: entering 3 trades at the same time on the same pair and under the same conditions). The first trade is closed out as soon as you get a couple of pips and is basically to cover the cost of your spread. The second trade gets closed out at your normal TP point, usually an area of S/R. The 3rd trade is your "swing for the heavens" trade that you let run wild for as long as you like, or that you put a trailing stop on before going to bed. The idea of putting on multiple trades and taking "progressive profits" is supposedly (according to the author) more profitable over the long term than the "all or nothing" approach most of us take. Hiram

It's like we were saying this morning. The trade you took, DID give up some pips, but they were small. The key is to taking them. Now, if you suspected that the trade would only give a little then you are prepared for it and will close out the trade on the first sign of it coming back at you. What I am trying to say is that the safety of a setup is relevant to the level of pips you want from it. If you go for small amounts, then you can, almost, take every single bounce out there. HOwever, if you are looking for good trades that allow you to close early if you 'wish', then yes, you do need the good setups. THe statements from Clay were about keeping your 'head' right. If you can recognise that you are having the 'make it back' thoughts, then you are halfway there to stopping them, BUT only halfway. If you can sit it out or ONLY take the perfect setups, then you are doing well. If however, you take the next trade and continualy know that it was the wrong thing to do almost as soon as you are in it, then yuo are trying to get even, and that rarely works. If you find you are taking losing trade after losing trade, your mind is definately in the 'wrong' place and you should stop. Stop and think about it, walk away, dont look at charts, but just recognise what is happening. When I take losses, I reevaluate what went wrong and then I pick the next trade VERY carefully. If a loss has come from a tight stop or something similar that really couldnt be helped, then I will try to get back in the game, by waiting for a GOOD setup. Here is a trade I took this morning based on the following confluence: H1-10 with M15 10/50 with M5 10/50 (very rare confluence). In addition, the M15 35/50 were separated and price usually bounces around the two MAs in these cases (which is why we call it ping-pong). So I thought I can capture one bounce from the M15 50 to the M15 35 (11 pips). The only disadvantage with this trade was the fact that the MAs were relatively flat and hence didn't have a particular direction to favor. The trade turned out well and I let it run to the round number 1.4450 for a total of +19.8 pips. In general, the ping-pong areas are probably OK to try in H1 and M15 timeframes when price is ranging. Just be careful when the price shoots up/down from these areas (which it usually does when it decides where it wants to go). As you see in my trade it decided to go opposite from my short but I was following closely with my stop. I was actually hoping to get to the weekly pivot 10 pips lower from where I closed the trade. --- 帖子 #437 ---
The 'touch' trades are best taken when the relevant MA is at a steep angle. The lower the angle the lower the chance of a good bounce. The angle should be in the same direction as the previous trend, ie if price were moving north it would drag the MA's north with it and they would be pointing somewhere between 1 and 2 on the face of a clock (45 degrees roughly). So when price retraces south and the touches the relevant MA then you would trade it Long (north) again. The angles are very important if you are trading a single MA and especially so with the 10ema's. However, that is NOT to say that price does not bounce when they are flat, it's just that 'flat' bounce is NOT part of the rulebook. The other indication that a 'touch' might be a good trade is when it is in confluence with something else..... confluence meaning that it is sitting on top of, joined with, next to, paired with etc etc. Though we only have a few indicators in this strategy, there are easily enough to give a fair few confluence trades per day. We have the following (and if you do not have these, then I suggest you get them (and it probably means you have not read the isntructions correctly): Round Numbers 15minute: 10ema, 35 SMA , 50ema 1hr: 10ema, 35 SMA , 50ema Daily: 10ema, 35 SMA , 50ema Additional indicators, which a few of us have added, please only add the pivots if you are new to the strategy. Despite not having many indicators and can see how only a few soon add up when trading many timeframes. Pivot points 1m: 10ema, 35 SMA , 50ema 5m: 10ema, 35 SMA , 50ema 1hr: 62ema Therefore as you can see, at any one time you 'could be' (not for beginers of this strategy) trading with upto 15 ma's (3 per 5 charts) with matching pivots and RN's. Confluence is the convergance of any of the indicators either within their own timeframe or between the timeframes. A few examples: The 15minute 50ema and the 1hr 10ema. The 15minute 35, the 1hr 50 and a RN The 1hr 35, the 1hr 50, the daily pivot. The more confluence something has, the higher the ' probability' it has to react the way you beleive it will. Now something worth noting, that is in the instructions and if you missed this, then you REALLY REALLY do need to re-read the instructions (I do, once per week), when price moves in a good trend, you will find that the 35sma and the 50ema in their own timeframes start converging to follow the price. When price starts to stabalise then the two MA's drift apart. Therefore, when you take into account the rules of strong angles on touches of the MA's you can see why, as previously mentioned, confluence between the 35/50 on their own timeframe is a strong trade. I hope that has made a few things clearer..... if not, please ask again. Though, please please ensure that you are fully aware of the rulebook. It is KEY to this strategy, especialy so as we slowly start to add to it. You MUST get the basics down, this is imperative to moving forwards. If you try to do to much to start with, it will really mess with your head and one of two things will happen: 1) you will quit this strategy or 2) It might be the final straw and you quit trading. Neither of which is good! Lee

I find the best practice is to know where the MA was. So, if you are looking at price and you think it's going to move and touch an MA, be aware of where that MA is at the time you start to think the move might be on. Price will drag MA's with it, so if you see a BIG move, and it looks like there was a touch just before it, the chances are that it was a fair way off, so do NOT beat yourself over that. The best way to see this on particular moves is to go back and use the Simulator...... it's worth mentioning here that the similulator is great for going back over a day, not just 4 years ago! Kostas looks for PA around the touches and uses the 1 and 5 minute to do this. But he will need to expand on this as it's something I am trying to switch to. Trading PA on a touch is far safer than simply taking a touch, BUT you will miss some trades because of it. It's a balance that you need to decide on, Risk vs Reward.

You just have to fight the urge to get in right away. It's probably time that I talked about M1 head-fakes. Let's imagine price coming from above to touch 35/50 on M15 (which means you are going to go long). Many time the price will touch, then go up (gets you in the trade), but then quickly reverses (head-fake) and overshoots the 35/50 by 10-12 pips (and takes out small SLs and stops you out). This means that I miss some opportunities when the price directly shoots up but gives me higher probability trades. Lee

--- 帖子 #482 ---
Okay, Confluence is merely the joinging of several indicators together. It is not a trade call, nor is it 'something' to be traded. It's simply a few indicators that cause signals, but in one place. For example, it could be any of the following combination and many many more: The 15m 10ema ontop of an RN The 1hr 62ema, the Daily 10ema and a pivot point The 5minute 35 &amp; 50, the 15minute 50, the 1hr 50 all at the same point. So, as you can see, all it really is some signals you may have taken, BUT these are all in one place. My take on these thing is this. There are some people out there that will always trade the 15minute 35 touch. There are some others that will always trade the daily pivot. There are others that trade the daily chart and will always take a touch off the 10ema. Some more people will always take small bounces off round numbers. More people like the 1hr 50ema. So...... if price is approaching all of these signals and they are all on top of eachother ie CONFLUENCE: 15minute 35 Daily Pivot Daily 10ema Round number 1hr 50ema 5minute 35 &amp; 50 What do you think will happen? Is price more probable to react at this area than if it was ONLY approaching a stand alone 15minute 35sma? At that is why this is a game of probabilities. In some cases, the answer will be a NO, as price may react very well indeed to the sole 15minute 35sma, however it is FAR more PROBABLE to react at where there is confluence of signals. Hope that is a little clearer. In relation to the other question you asked. A constrainment trade and a 'clear break' trade are different things. Constrainment: Price is being held, either up or down, by an MA (or even RN/Pivot). The rules of this trade are that on the 3rd touch of the constrainment, you enter the trade. Example: If price is trying to head north, but keeps getting stopped at the 15minute 35/50 which is just above it, at the 3rd candle that touches this/these MA's, you take the trade SOUTH. Generally you will see smaller candles at this stage rather than anything with large wicks. Now, you don't see to many of these unless you trade the Asian or London markets, as by the time the US starts trading price is moving well. The constrainment trade is often seen at the start of a large move, whether that move reverses at some point is irrelevent. Therefore, the 'trade' you take is the one AWAY from the direction of where it's being held. If it's being held from going north, you trade SOUTHh. If its held from going south, you trade NORTH. A 'Clear Break' is where price approaches and 'breaks through' some previous PA, MA, RN or pivot. It is considered a clear break when price passes through AND CLOSES beyond the relevant point. In many cases, price will come back and retest this area and that is 'normaly' a good time to enter the trade. A comment from KOstas here would help, as I know this works well with the lower timeframes as you can wait for the 15miunte to break through and then possibly look for a close on one of the lower timeframes. This is higher risk, but can be a good way off getting into a trade. The constrainment trade is considered a safe trade for this rulebook. However, the clearbreak is something that I know Clay was coming too. That said, some of the examples KOstas posts are clear breaks with a 1/5minute retest. Again.... hope some of that makes things clearer, but again, I am NOT an expert. Lee

Hi Kostas Perhaps we could just analyze this, it would help me too. I took the trade (short) for a number of reasons which I thought was within the rules, but the main one was P/A at S/R &amp; R/N. I've attached a snapshot. Price had already blown through S/R and then retraced. The next bar then spiked through R/N resistance and retraced, the next bar then opened and proceeded downwards where I took the trade based on the previous bars reaction to the S/R's. I felt that as the 10ema was Below the 35&amp;50 that the main trend was still down and that price was in a simply in a retrace trying to head off back in the original direction. Subsequently price was consrtained for quite a time by the 50 &amp; 10 Ma's before eventually moving up. So in summary I thought it was by the rules. I also thought the bar I took the trade on was this :- Double Tops and Double Bottoms: The terms “double top” and “double bottom” has a very different meaning in this strategy. You can still look for the “normal” double tops and bottoms where price has moved toward and away form an area of support and resistance over a period of several bars, but for our purposes in this strategy we will further define it as two bars which have exactly the same top or bottom. If the bars are also the same length, it can define an entry point or an exit point depending on it's location on the chart. Both bars MUST have the same EXACT top or bottom, but the can be different in how they achieve that. For example, in the images below you will see some that are both wicked tops or bottoms, some that are both body tops or bottoms and some that are one of a body and one of a wick. It is the fact that they are EXACTLY the same price point that tends to indicate the reversal of price. Hope thats not too long winded, perhaps between us we can nail this one down in order to trade it correctly in future. Regards Simmo

--- 帖子 #564 ---
You have asked Kostas to comment on your trade, so I'l' leave that to him. But I am happy to answer on Double tops and double bottoms. They are taken from the highest (for tops) or lowest (for bottoms) points of the candle. That could be it's wick or it could be the body or a combination of the two. But it IS the highest or lowest points. The top of the candle you have indicated is not the body, where your arrow is, but the wick well above the body. If you look, if it was how you are indicating (assuming I am reading your chart correctly) then all candles with only one wick (top or bottom) will be double tops and bottoms, the reason for this is because you have indicated that the following candle dropped from its opening leaving no wick, which matched the close price of the previous one, but this is the case for all candle open and closes (not sure if this sentence is clear) It could be the top of the wick of a bull candle where price has retraced a little and on the following candle it goes back up and closes at exactly the same point. So in this case the first candles wick is the same height as the following candles closed body. The easiest ones to spot are either double wicks or double bodies. Examples: but not limited to these The last two are what is refered to as a DHLC - double high lower close. These are stronger signals than simple a double top without a lower close. Though they are stronger, price has moved further away from your ideal entry and would in these cases normaly require a larger SL. The examples from the manual (also posted below) provide many setups. I am not sure if Clay removed the question from the new version of the manual, but there is a douple top/bottom in the manual examples that is not highlighted. Can you/anyone spot it?

--- 帖子 #566 ---
Touch trades should be taken on the touch! The manual does state that these can be hard to get as they happen fairly quick. That said, you can still wait for confirmation on these touches, which is what Kostas has a lot of success with, but this involves using lower timeframes and you will still need to be 'there' when the trade touches the MA. You should be aware though, waiting for confirmation minimises your possible losses however, you WILL miss trades through waiting for confirmation. Some trades will touch and then shoot off, giving no confirmation, other than the fact it's move well off, before you can get to the lower timeframes and see some closing candles. It's a balancing act between more pips/risk vs less pips/risk Lee

First Touch ” trades are where price hits either a “round number” level or an MA that has held as S/R strongly before and you trade IMMEDIATELY in the opposite direction moving to BE as quickly as possible to maximize the trade. Often these trades are good for quite a bit of pips, but just as often they are only good for about 12 to 20 pips, so watch them closely for the exit.

I had some private communication with Clay and he gave me some advice that I had asked for. This was also related to the Ping-Pong areas which in my opinion are nice to trade when price is sideways. I didn't want to keep this just to myself and wanted instead to share his advice with the rest of the community here: " As for the Ping Pong areas, on m15 they aren't really much use unless the lines are AT LEAST 40 pips apart or so. The narrower the spread between the lines, the more likely trying to play it will bite you. BUT there are many, many times on H1 and D1 when it works really well. Just look at the charts and it'll start to make sense. You need a lot of screen time for that one to start to be good for you. Same with "Scooped Away." Remember we talked about not taking a trade when the 10 had "turned"? That "turning" point is where often the 10 is retested at Price heads back to the 35/50 lines and if you can notice that is what is actually happening, it makes a really low risk entry. Usualll the risk is only around 9 pips or so then price goes on it's merry way back to the 35/50 area. Keep an eye solidly on a possible "touch" trade back into the trend against your currently open position if you take this one on. Most of the time I just set my SL at the area where the Touch would happen and get out so I'm ready for that "touch" as well. I don't use the advanced rules much personally as I have discovered just how powerfully the basic rules really are if applied using the Cardinal Rule in the new version of the manual. " Clay thanks for the support from the sidelines. We all appreciate it. Kostas.

--- 帖子 #619 ---
It's part of the "Dance Tools" zip file on the link that Lee sent. It basically takes actual historical data and feeds it to you as if you were watching a live trading screen. You can make your buys and sells and then see whether or not your strategy worked out the way you thought. The advantage over trading a demo account is that you can run the simulator anytime you want, even when the market is closed. Another advantage is that you can "fast forward" the data or pause it altogether. I've never been able to get the buy/sell scripts to work but don't let that stop you. The simulator is a great way to practice The Dance. Simply watch for the right type of formation, hit pause, draw your trendlines or whatever, jot down on a piece of paper whether you think prices are going to go up or down (and by how much), and then hit "play" to continue the data stream and see if you were right. Clay mentions in the manual that the "secret to his success" was that he spent around 99% of his time on the simulator and only about 1% of his time actually trading. OK, I might have the numbers wrong but the fact remains that successful traders, like professional athletes, are created on the practice field. Have a good weekend! Hiram

--- 帖子 #643 ---
Morning all, I have not made any trades this morning..... so no charts just yet. One thing I have been working on is the scripts. I had problems with the risk script, the one that sets your risk each day (or infact, each time you use it). Basically, it wouldn't work. I have now worked out why and it may be the same case for some of you, so I wanted to post the answer up. This is a work around so, sadly, there is no easier way. For those of you that have 5 digit brokers and brokers that do not allow trade lot sizes to two decimal points then this is what you have to do: Edit the risk script and ensure that your risk is set to a 150 pip stop loss (or 15 for a 4 digit broker). Then ensure that the 'trade management' answer is 'true'. You then need to ensure that there is a setting in the 'global variables', found by pressing F3 or through the options, for 'ordersize' (as shown in the picture below). Check carefully as you do not want two of these, but if there really is not one there then 'add' a new one. The script changes this figure and as you can see in my example, the figure is set to 1.75 (and no, this is not my normal risk.... are you crazy? ), however my broker will not allow two decimal point trade, it will only allow one. Therefore I will need to manually change this figure to either 1.7 or 1.8. Of course, as I mentioned before, this is a work around. It is probably just as easy to grab the calculator and work out your risk anyways, but this will do it for you providing you are happy to edit it after. Be aware, if you have a round number account balance and you use (i think) an even risk number, the script may actualy work for you, but this is likely to only happen once. Once then figures change, the second decimal point gets used. If anyone knows how to edit the script to only enter 1 decimal point,t hen that would be nice. As always, ensure the risk reflects your trade number volume. If you are entering two or three trades (as I do) then this number needs to be half or a third of your actual overall risk, else you are entering a lot more than your chosen risk. Shout if you have any problems. You should REALLY be using scripts. If you are not, say so, and we cna try and help. Lee

Hi Lee I got mine working like this :- My broker is 5-digit. first I modified the script :- double Lots = 0; bool UseMoneyMgmt = true; extern double RiskPercent = 3; extern double StopLoss = 150; string Input = " Buy Price "; This is so I didn't have to change percent risk and SL manualy every time. Next :- Lots = NormalizeDouble( AccountBalance()*Risk/StopLoss/(MarketInfo(Symbol(),MODE_TICKVALUE)), 3 ); Highlighted in red "3" this sorted out the decimal point in the lot size calculation. Ah! just saw the post above, not sure why setting to '3' worked for me but it did ! (Micro lots !) Cheers Simmo

--- 帖子 #688 ---
Finally... got back in the game earlier with nice trade. Wasn't ground breaking, but it was 3.1% of my account balance, which has not happened in while. I have been giving a lot of thought to these scripts AND more importantly, the Take Profits. I think Kostas' recent success's prove that TP's are one of the fundamental keys to getting this system to work. In my earlier trade I had my usual three part trade, ie I use three scripts to enter the trade based on a 1/3 of my total risk per trade. My usual setup (and current until i make a decision) is three trades at 12SL and TP's at 15/30/50 pips. However, this got me to thinking of how to get to a break even point asap if things reverse on you. If you move to BE at the point of your 15pip TP getting hit AND price reverse on you, you are still at risk in the trade, therefore you need a minimum of half the trade to close at 15TP (or 12 if you do not wish any profit) to ensure that you are not only safe, but that you infact do make a small profit. So, spliting the trade into 4 parts (has to be 4 parts as the scripts use the global lot size setting) makes sense with TP's at 15/15/X/X. Now the other thing I want to try and do is to ensure that with one trade (untouched) I can get my 30 pips per day. So, I need to work out what the two X's will need to be in order to get a 30 pip trade. With two part trades taking 15 pips each, this leaves another 90 pips to be taken between the remaining two trades. I could take the option of having them both set to 45 pips, which in effect makes this a two part trade rather than a 4 part trade, which is okay if you are better at watching PA then I am, but doesnt allow you top take advantgage of a markign moving in your direction. OR I can decide on two more settings. However much I lower the 3rd TP from 45 I will need to add to the next. I have several 'round' options: 1) 30 &amp; 60 2) 35 &amp; 55 3) 40 &amp; 50 I think the 30/60 is the better option to ensure pips get booked asap without making it just to tough to get to the 30 pips. I will try and test this out, but the main point of this post was to get you think about how to use your trades and TP's to your advantage. Of course, to keep it real simple you could just have a whole trade TP at 15 pips and try and get two of those per day, but I like the option of having something that can 'run' with the market if it decides to take off. Any thoughts/comments? Regards Lee (from Russia with Love)

--- 帖子 #714 ---
You've GOT to read "Trading in the Zone" by Mark Douglas. It's included in The Dance materials. It covers the most important aspect of trading - your mindset. It's your mindset going into a trade that makes you risk more than you should; makes you hesitate to take profits until the trade moves against you; and that prevents you from taking a loss early on in the hopes that it turns around (which it never does). All of the other books on trading, including those specific to FOREX, mainly deal with the "mechanics" of trading along with significant portions that cover technical trading vs fundamental trading, chart patterns, money management, etc. There's a good reason Clay included the "Trading in the Zone" ebook as part of The Dance. Read it before you commit time with any other book. Hiram

--- 帖子 #718 ---
"Dance trades" are after "constrainment" (price moves in tight range - for short below 35 and 50 ma- 10ma below 35&amp;50ma- touching 50 ma and droping, opposite for long). There should be min 3 or 4 candles touching ma's. Touch trades - after some strong move first touch of 10 or 50 MA. Depends on strengh of breakout. It's hard to explain in few words, i had problems at start when to enter trade. At the beggining you should look for perfect setups. 14th on cable: Nice constrainment, very small wicks, price above 35&amp;50 ma, 10 ma to, 3rd or 4th touch 50 ma as entry. Strong move up and 10ma touch.

--- 帖子 #753 ---
Hello folks, just subscribing . My story in short... I am a long.. VERY LONG term trader LOL. I employ the Livemore approach. Here it is in a nutshell. 1. Establish the overall trend (day charts and up) 2. Determine overall conditions (sentiment, some fundies.. for example the current EUROZONE failure ) 3. Enter at the BEST price possible 4. Add to position as profit is generated form previous entries. 5. Exit all trades when 1 and/or 2 have clearly changed See item 3 ?? In my opinion this approach(the dance)...will allow me to enter at the best price possible. Till now I have been using daily S/R to generate entries. Since S/Rs are very subjective many times I would enter a little early and see drawdowns. The drawdown is no problem as the Market corrects that with time. But being human , I would like to minimize that drawdown... LOL. Now I am not a fan of indicators... I do not use them in my trading other than drawing a line. But in this case I can see that the indicators are not "the" driving factors. This approach in my opinion is excellent in that it concentrates on pattern recognition (around the MAs) plus very simple PA analysis (I like simple). Keep up the good work fellows and I declare that all of you are very so VERY CLOSE to become the greatest Traders... Peace JEss

--- 帖子 #784 ---
BC, Welcome to the thread. My response to your questions: 1. Best to wait for candle close. For touch trades I use M1 to fine tune entry. 2. Sometimes the price will fake breaking the MAs and then come back down in your direction. I usually take these trades. If I am in and it hits my SL while breaking the MAs, I will observe closely using M5 and if it looks right I may re-enter. 3. Good question about porcupine areas. Usually they have more than 2-3 candles but the way I found easier to identify is that the body of the candle is very small compared to the very long wicks. 4. From your second post: I don't have the D1 on my charts all the time. I have the H1 which I switch to H4 a few times per day and to D1 a couple of times to see where the price is going. It's not that D1 is not needed, just my approach to the Dance method is more short term so I have H1, M15, M5 and M1 always on. Read through this thread and you will see how I use the method. 5. SL of 40p on my last trade is NOT according to the rules. Use the 19-20p SL. It's just that when I feel strongly about a target area I will leave the price some more breathing space (it comes with experience..) This reminds me to talk about targets. Learn to identify important support/resistance areas (from higher TFs, pivots, RNs, etc.). They will help you immensely using this method (which utilizes the MAs as a moving support/resistance). Kostas

@Fugly As Blackcat indicates Clay would take at the touch and not the COB. There are certain times you would wait for COB, but those are few. The idea is that when u take the trade at the touch instead of COB you get most of the move. This also alows u to stay in the trade. Otherwise your small SL gets hit. So the confidence to take these trades is not only in the strategy but also the following items: 1. The SL is tight. So that controls your risk to a minimum. 2. If u stick to the rules, your trades attempts should be few and at high probability. Peace Jess

--- 帖子 #889 ---
This is my first post here after lurking in the shadows for some time. First of all, many thanks to Kostas for continuing Clay's method. For confirmation of direction, what I have been using for some time with good success is the ol' 123 reverse formation on the 1 minute chart. For example, if a bounce occurs to the long side on 15 minute chart, I would watch the 1 minute chart to make a low (that's the number 1 point), next bar make a higher high than the previous bar (that's the number two point), and third bar make a lower low than the second bar, but not surpass low of first bar. At this point, if price goes above high of second bar, I have a resting buy stop one pip above number two bar. You will lose a few pips doing this, but when you finally get in momentum will be on your side in your chosen direction. This is a well-known formation to most traders, so I'm probably stating the obvious to most of you, but I hope it helps. If I knew how to post my chart I could have given a visual, but still figuring that out. Regards, Wally

--- 帖子 #923 ---
I would have assumed that prices would have bounced back up to the 35/10 area and begun to ping-pong. However, you seemed to have caught a strong upward move so congrats. Isn't it funny how obvious everything is after the fact? By the way, you learn in "Trading In the Zone" that you don't have to know which way prices are going to go in order to make money - so quit trying to predict the market. This is also implied in The Dance manual. The key is to learn the candle formations (like pin bars, double tops, etc) or behaviors (like price movement around RN's) that have a high probability of affecting prices in a certain way. You then have to be patient until you can spot one of those formations or behaviors taking shape and then "place your bet" that prices will react the same way they've done in the past. In other words, you put the odds in your favor. Since this is a "high probability" trade, not a "guaranteed" trade, you "hedge your bet" by putting in a tight stop loss, just in case prices decide not to follow past performance. Looking at trading this way tends to take off a lot of the pressure of trying to "read all the tea leaves" in order to predict which way prices are going to go. Simple, right? Hiram

--- 帖子 #924 ---
Great post and I agree with you 100%. I am very analytical and statistical in the way I approach trading so this mindset suits me down to the ground anyway. I seem to remember that in trading in the zone, he talks about how a losing trade isn't always a bad trade and a winning trade isn't always a good trade. Basically if the odds are in your favour and you have followed your rules and maintained your discipline, whether each individual trade wins or not is irrelevant in the long term. I personally believe that traders (especially when starting out) can get too obsessed with winning every single day and trying to win every trade, Its certainly a mistake I made in the past.

It's worth mentioning here, that looking back through the days charts can make you doubt yourself sometimes. I am not suggesting by any means that you do not do this as it is a great exersize to do, but the entries are NOT always as obvious as they seem after the move. The post a few back demonstrates this but the only way to test it and see would mean going into the simulator, and if you are interested, it's something I would suggest you do. For the new guys out there, and Yes!!! I am still new too. When price is approaching an MA, especially the lower ones on a big move, just watch carefully and you will see how much that MA moves. The platform gives you, in my opinion, a 'If price were to close now' view on where the MA is. (EDIT) Just thought I might explain this a little better. When the bar closes the MA will move more, so its not quite a 'if it were to close now' thing, but I'm just trying to highlight a point and I took it to the extreame. This means that at the top of a move, the MA angle will be sharp upwards, as you see a two bar retrace, assuming they are long bars, by the time the price reaches the MA, it could very well now be 5 pips away from where it was at the START of the move. I will end here 8O) but I know there will be more questions about 'when do you trade it then'?. The reason I am ending is because I do not know! This is the major difference between 'touch traders' (Clay) and 'Touch PA traders' (Kostas). Hopefully this will help others too. •‘2 bar rule' met? (for 10EMA touch trade) •Are the MAs at least 45 degree angle? --- 帖子 #1016 ---
Yup, Though my concerns would be the 10 pip gap between the MA's. From my perspective, the reason this is okay is becuase it gives a clear area in which you place your SL, ie 5 or so pips behind the further MA. However, if you take the trade according to the rules, a touch trade should only have around an 11 pip stop. Therefore, if your other MA is 10 pips out and it gets hit, your spread will take you out of the trade. Now, if these are together, this is entirely different! I have been trading a very very very very short time and I have NO idea how the dynamics of the market actualy work, but I liken the MA's to pending orders. When price approaches and an MA a pending order is triggered (or millions of them are) and price reacts. Now if you have the 35 and the 50 on top of eachother, the momentum there is stronger than two seperate MA's even at a smaller distance. Thats MY view on it, which is why I am very cautious on trading the 35 or 50 when they are not on top of eachother OR at the very least, ontop of TWO other things. The trouble when they are seperated is that the further one often acts as a magnet. So, this then presents you with a few problems. 1. Do you take the first ma and risk it moving to the second. If you do this, do you have a small SL, take the hit and then take another trade or do you have a large SL beyond the second MA and risk it being hit when price moves beyond it, thereby taking a large loss. 2. Do you wait for price to move to the second MA and then perhaps miss it because it doesn't and it moves off from the first. Point no.2 can be countered by using the 5 minute chart for entry, but despite Kostas' huge success with this, it's not with the 'Cardinal Touch Rule'. The last thing I want to do is complicate things, because I think this is where I have slowed my self down. But, can you see what I mean? Lee

--- 帖子 #1055 ---
A good/big 'touch' trades on the higher timeframes are normaly going to be against the 15minute trend, simply because after a decent move, the 15minute trend and it's MA's, have moved a fair way and the higher timeframes get left behind. The exception to this may be when price has been moving through the MA's in a 'sideways' market. When this happens the MA's move into what Clay called 'MA soup'. However, when this does happen, it tends to reduce the effect of the MA's and you look for a constrainment trade rather than a touch. The key to these is knowing when to take profit. I 'try' and use the 15minute 10ema for this. But, it's new for me so I can't say if it works or not. Lee

--- 帖子 #1078 ---
Wilkohsg, Good questions here. I have answered them in the thread before but it doesn't hurt for one more time: 1. No, I mean daily 3% risk or 3% profit 2. I trade on average 30-40 pips daily. By adjusting the lot size these pips represent 3% of my equity. As the account grows, so does the lot size so that always 30-40 pips represent 3% (I started from 0.1 lots and now I am at 0.5). If I loose 3% for the day (40pips) then I stop trading (it doesn't happen often, some days I will just break even). Of course, I don't expect to keep doing this for ever, otherwise in a couple of years I will need George Soros to trade on the opposite side of my trades . So my target is to grow the account to around 30-40K and be able to trade 4-5 lots with 30-40 pips which will be around 1,000E daily profit. After that the account will be growing less and less in terms of growth%, but I will be happy with 1,000E daily income . Hope this helps, Kostas. P.S. This will be the last time I mention my MM rules and trade plan. Keep this post handy and if others ask you can mention this post.

--- 帖子 #1091 ---
The M3 level is just the midpoint, in this case between the main PP and R1. Not quite sure why its called M3 on my charts actually because surely that's M1? oh well! I imagine opinions differ somewhat on using midpoints, but in all of my trading experience, midpoints on FX are just as important as the main levels, especially if the main levels have a large gap between them. Also I do see what you mean now about constrainment on the 5min chart, however for me that was basically a pure 15min trade as the set-up was so strong. I will always take what the 15min chart is telling me a lot more seriously than the 5min chart, which is purely for helping with entries in my opinion.

--- 帖子 #1106 ---
NKE, Many times a good M5 rejection bar will give a good signal. On the other hand, you may loose some trades this way because a touch can happen right away. The Dance trades in general look counterintuitive but this is because you think you are going against the action. Of course, if you trade with the trend (i.e. price above M15 30/50) then is is not counterintuitive because all you are doing is using a correction to get with the trend at the best price. In my case, M5 helps a lot but if you are getting confused stick with the M15 only. Kostas

--- 帖子 #1202 ---
This is correct. If price does not touch the MA DURING the trade, then it is not a valid DANCE entry. This is not to say that it wouldn't be a good trade with PA , but it's not a DANCE entry. Mr Bear, and anyone else new to this strategy, do NOT get upset about missing these 'near' touches...... there are tons of them, and if you let it get to you, you will start 'trying' to take them and sods law - you will take the ones that do not work. Will is spot on here..... there will be many more opportunities, don't rue the near misses, as that is all they are .... near misses. The only other thing that you should try and take into account is where you are going to take profit. Kostas is an expert at taking pips where they present themselves, but 'taking profit' is not something that came up to much in the original thread as it was something that Clay was working on and was 'getting too'. If you are happy to grab pips where you can then this may have been a good trade, but if you want trades to run, then you have to ask yourself if this trade would have done that! 10 pips below the entry is the RN and 10 pips below that is the Pivot point (I know some of you do not see that). It's a delicate business - taking profit - because no one can really tell you how you 'should' trade. If you use AND watch PA, then you can, in my opinion, take many many trades, if you set TP areas, then this trade probably wouldn't have been so good, simply because the risk vs reward wasn't to hot. (just my view on things)

Not even considered it. Things to take into account - price had already moved some distance on most pairs before London even opened, this is not 'normaly' the case. --- 帖子 #1234 ---
The one thing I have picked up massively over the last week or so, though conversations with Lucklady is that your SL is highly relative to your entry. If your entries are weak then you need a larger stop loss, if they are good then you can get away with a smaller one. Higher timeframe entries also need larger stops. It's a balance I am afraid. The last few days I have been taking entries off lower timeframe PA...... 5 minute for 15 minute and 1hr trades and the 15minute for 4hr trades. When you do this, your stop is usualy a few pips + Spread beyond the last wick. However when you trade off 'touches' you can often need a little more because quite often you dont really have a line in the sand to draw it. The best thing to do is to post your trades and we can comment on them when you post them. The two major things to take into account - the better your entry, generaly the smaller your stop 'can' be. The higher the timeframe trade (especially touches) generaly the larger the stop needs to be. Lee

--- 帖子 #1278 ---

--- 帖子 #1279 ---
The way Myfxbook.com does it (I think) is ANY peak-to-valley P/L decline is considered drawdown even if your account is still positive. For example: you gain 20%, then lose 12%... your drawdown will show as 12%, even though the account is still positive. If you continue to have a P/L decline from this point your drawdown will continue to get larger. If you make some gains, then 12% drawdown is the maximum drawdown you've incurred until.... something bad happens. It is computed after every closed trade (I think). So basically, it'll show your worst Profit/Loss decline from any Profit peak or beginning balance if you're never profitable. Hope that helps.

--- 帖子 #1358 ---
Hello, I've been lurking in this thread for a few weeks, and trying to make Dance trades on a demo account. I'm still jumping the gun a lot, don't have the patience to wait for completed bars. Anyways, I'm still learning and on my demo account I acctually had the exact same problem with GoMarkets as Willhuang; See quote and solution below. If you look in the Buy and Sell script, there are lines like these: OrderSend(Symbol(),OP_BUY,lots,Ask,3,Ask-StopLoss*Point,Ask+TakeProfit1*Point,"",255,0,Green); It seems that GoMarkets doesn't accept setting the TP and SL at the same time as placing the order. The solution is to change these lines into: OrderSend(Symbol(),OP_BUY,lots,Ask,3, 0,0 ,"",255,0,Green); I did try with different values on TP/SL, but all returned with errors. If you want to see the error messages, you need to add the following: Inserted Code [font="Arial Black"]int ticket; ticket = OrderSend(Symbol(),OP_BUY,lots,Ask,3,Ask-StopLoss*Point,Ask+TakeProfit1*Point,"",255,0,Green); if (ticket &lt; 0) { Print("OrderSend failed with error #",GetLastError()); return(0); }[/font]

--- 帖子 #1363 ---
Mr Bear, See below for a pic of my scripts. I had problems with these before too. I have highlighted some of the numbers that I 'might' have changed. There are a couple of things that you need to check out. 1. Do you use the auto risk changer? If so, you need to establish the smallest size lot you can place. If in my case it is 0.1 then you need to ensure that the auto risk is rounding up to this number, which it does NOT do with the scripts supplied by Clay. Just make sure that your numbers are the same as my numbers. I am not sure who gave me this answer but they are in this thread somewhere. 2. If you do NOT use the auto risk, then create an 'ordersize' in the global variables. If you do not know how to do this, post back here and I will show you, but I beleive I had done this in the thread already too...... but am happy to show again. Lee

--- 帖子 #1380 ---
This is a countertrend trade, not recommended in the basic rules. On page 55 of the M15 manual Clay briefly discussed Advanced strategies. "Scooped Up" or "Scooped Away" is one of those. This trade was my interpretation of his rules for a trade like this. I entered at the retouch of the 10 EMA in the next candle. I managed to make a few pips profit, it was a BAD profitable trade. (A trade that was profitable but not within the basic rules.) Price is now more pips lower than my "small" profit was after entry. My small profit was less than my stop-loss for the trade as well. This means that my risk was not favorable for this trade. Endroute and Clay both emphasized to not take counter-trend entries and to be patient and wait for great setups. This was the first "scooped" trade I have seen and that is why I screen captured it. I am not criticizing anyone for taking counter-trend trades . (edited : Please read Lee's following post)

--- 帖子 #1381 ---
Intu, 'My' interpretation of the 10ema scoop is when price breaks the 10 AND then comes back to test it and moves off with it. What you have there, in my view, is a breakout, not a scoop. I know this last comment is easy in hindsight, but you will see now that the 10ema did not scoop the price. Clay never really got into these, as you pointed out, it was going to be for the advanced class. But if you look back through his examples when he was telling people why their 10ema bounce did not work, each time the 10ema has rejected the following test which in turn has started a new trend (however short it may be). Nothing wrong with your trade per se, but just wanted you to know my view on it. Personaly, I think it's going to be very hard indeed to catch a 10ema 'scoop' if the 5min PA is not used....... how do you know it's been scooped? unless of course your now three candles past it.... the one that broke it, the one that tested it and then the one (hopefully) that tests it again. I think he put this in the advanced class because I think you gota be pretty ballsy to take it. If it breaks, comes back and tests it and comes back AGAIN....... I wouldn't want to be taking it. Just my two pence worth!

--- 帖子 #1446 ---
BC, Post, if possible, some of your trades up and we can help you with them.... of course this will all be with hindsight. In relation to the porcupine..... As soon as you start seeing large wicks and some sideways movement, just start being cautious......... There is a clue about your mental state in your question (not to insinuate that A) I am a doctor or B) you are insane ). Just remember, you get plenty of trades with this strategy (or whatever version of it you are using), so you do not to even start thinking about working out how long a porcupine will last or when one is forming. When you see long wicks - on any timeframe, then you know its time to stay out. Have a look back over your charts and see what 'time' these wicks happen. If you find that its a fairly regular time, then set an alarm somewhere that tells you to go do something different or that tells you not to trade. Clay warned me about summer a few weeks back, telling me to be careful. Basicaly, a large number of the bigger trading institutions are on vacation now, so the volume is not like it was pre-summer. Now this doesn't mean that there will not be more volatility, it simply means that when something moves in one direction alot, there is less holding it back on each move. So, it will swing one way for 50 pips, with little resistance and then possibly swing back for 45 pips, whereas when the market is at full operation, this same move may only have been 20 pips each way. Obviously this can work in your favour, providing you get the right move. The only two things I can suggest is: 1. Be VERY careful about your trades - look for LOTS and LOTS of confluence. 2a. If you are in a move and price starts moving against you, then move to BE asap or close out the trade. 2b. If you are in a move and price starts moving with you. Either ensure you are not being greedy and your 'take profit' is still in place OR quickly throw a 5 pip trailing stop on your trade (as it is moving up - NOT down). I have had two strong (strong based on what I normaly do) GU trades over the last two days using this method. I have not posted them as the entries were nothing to do with 'The Dance'. I was in a trade and it started climbing - fast. So when it start approaching a key - about 15 pips out from it, I threw up a 5 pip trailing stop. It hit the area, bounced back for 20 or so pips and then stuck around there fore a while. Obviously, despite it bouncing back for 20 pips (roughly) I closed out at 5 pips short of the 'then' move. Price did eventualy continue on, about an hour later, for another 100 pips or so but you can't catch them all! Lee

--- 帖子 #1452 ---
Guys, I know that the 4hr doesn't form part of the original 'Dance', but I think you should start being aware of it. To me, it seems to be fairly influential at the moment. So, just be aware of when it closes and take into consideration what you think the candle will mean when it closes. Also.... be aware that different brokers 4 hr charts close at different times. This means you need to be looking at your 4hr charts every two hours. I wouldn't take trades on the back of any of the candles specificaly, as these tend to require long stops, but if the closing candle is opposed to what you thought looked like a good trade then just be careful. This doesn't mean the 4hr trumps lower timeframe candles, as we all know a turn has to start somewhere. But be careful out there! Lee

For a lot of the time the E/U and E/J follow broadly similar trajectories and sometimes it seems you can get a touch on one that does not quite make it on the other - so keeping an eye on both would seem to be a good idea. However, I get anxious when the 2 are doing different things. If for example the E/J is approaching the 1H 10EMA but the E/U is marching confidently on with nothing to hold it back should we take the the E/J touch and rely on either the E/U to 'listen' to the E/J or for the U/J to compensate? Or should we only trade when things are nicely aligned between the two or..... Or am I overcomplicating it? All thoughts welcome!!

--- 帖子 #1480 ---
Don't take it unless you see a signal! However much they may follow eachother, they are different pairs. If you get strong US news and weaker JAP news then you can expect them to do their different things. Also....your take profits will be different too. There are some pairs that are realyl similar.... is the EUR/JPY and the CHF/JPY, as the CHF is strongly linked to the EUR, but even those differ slightly. It's entirely up to you, but ask yourself..... are you that sure about the signal on the other pair that it will allow you to take a trade on a completely different pair. If you were trading long term, then it may be more viable, but with tight stops, I would avoid it. It may well turn, but it may go that extra 5 pips beyond your stop loss to do so. Lee

I received the following private message but I wanted to answer this in public. So M..... excuse my copying your message here: " Hi, Kostas! I want to ask you one question, if you don't mind. 1. When did you realize, that you're constantly successful? I've just read beginning of old dance thread and as I see you became successful from day one of using dance strategy or at least some of dance rules, am I right? 2. So I'm asking myself a question, was this because of previous forex experience and learning or it was just something in dance, that suits you perfectly? 3. For example, if you started using only dance from day 1 of you forex trading/learning, do you think you would be successful? Thanks in advance. " 1. I am NOT constantly successful! It is true that most days I end up positive, some days break-even and very few days negative. My trades are now at around 71% winning ratio. So NOT every trade is a winner. The loosers I cut quickly and my best winners are the ones that I take profit quickly at 15-20p. What I do lately is take most of my profit there and leave a small portion of my trade to go further (most times the small portion will be stopped out). It is true that almost from the first day I used the Dance, I found it to "click" with my trading philosophy which is why I got these results (so far). 2. As I said, the method suited me perfectly but my previous 2.5yrs trading experience in trading was absolutely necessary. 3. I don't think so. You need to learn and understand some basics about trading first (S/R, Pivots, Round #, price action bars, etc. need to be understood first). The Dance gives you an advantage while you maneuver between these important points that price reacts to. Glad to answer these. Don't get discouraged as you learn. My most important success so far was that I didn't give up when I was almost ready to quit. Kostas

--- 帖子 #1682 ---
You will most times find the price action before a news release shows you which way its going to go ultimately, the only problem is you sometimes get wild swings on high risk news before it settles into that direction which could take you out only to go the way you thought in the first place.

--- 帖子 #1683 ---
A few rather simple thoughts: If the news is in line with the markets expectations then I think you can argue that it is already priced in and that whatever The Dance is saying will reflect it. If it is not in line then I guess it can go either way (which simplistically you could say is 50/50). Therefore between the ones that are in line and the 50% that go your way I think you can conclude that you will be more right than wrong with The Dance set up (assuming that it is usually right). A very tight SL is probably the answer and staying away from the very volatile releases.

--- 帖子 #1684 ---
Actually, apart from very important news, I tend to ignore the news in general if I have a strong setup. Of course, sometimes my SL will get hit by the news noise but very often a strong setup gets me in profit in a few seconds. Sometimes, I use slightly larger SL if news are close (~15-18p) but most times around 10-12p. It seems to me that most news tend to move the price quickly to where it was going to go even without the news. Only the big impact news should be avoided (e.g. NFP, bid rate, etc.)

--- 帖子 #1692 ---
I still use the "head-fake" concept but only on the touch trades. It requires to have the M1 open and observe closely what happens when the price touches the MA. I do NOT use the "head-fake" for the regular 35/50 bounces (for these I wait for the right M5 rejection bar). Usually, if there is confluence (e.g. MAs with pivots or round numbers or MAs from different TFs) then the price usually checks all of them. So I wait until the price touches the last one of them and then enter the trade. I haven't measured any pips but the fake is usually easy to spot. Just keep your M1 open on the next touch and you will see what I am talking about (don't take the first M1 touch, wait a few minutes for the price to retrace and then take the second deeper touch). Again, sometimes the price will never come back and you will loose some opportunities but on the other hand this filters several bad trades.

During chop first priority is to observe the following: 1. If the chart is a "porcupine" (bars have long wicks on both sides and small bodies) then DO NOT trade 2. If bars are normal but M15 MAs are flat then I would suggest no trading but if you really want to trade you could use the 10 MA for small profit with a tight SL. NOT recommended for newbies though . In general, I would stay away from choppy periods .

--- 帖子 #1717 ---
i read the manual and saw the thread here mentioned confluence, what does "confluence"means? does it mean a confirmation of the 15m and 1h chart both touching MAs?

--- 帖子 #1718 ---
yes, but a confluence is also when RN AND M15 MA are at the same level it could also be M15 35 AND H1 10 and so on...

--- 帖子 #1719 ---
C onfluence occurs when multiple points of resistance/support occur in very close proximity . For us this means: MAs from different timeframes, Round Numbers (RNs), Daily Pivots. When two or more of those occur close to each other the price has more chances to react (this is because more traders will react to this point, some traders may react to an MA, some others to an RN, etc.). Usually, the more of these points that are in confluence, the bigger the reaction.

--- 帖子 #1827 ---
Good piece of advice. You saw the results! As I said before, you always need to be aware of major support/resistance points (H4 or Daily). Dance is providing additional S/R moving points (i.e. the MAs) where price reacts to and that's our bread and butter, but the high timeframes provide important S/R that we should always be aware of. If you look at my charts, you will notice some yellow lines of varying thickness on the M15. Every morning before I start trading, I change my M15 chart to H4 and Daily and I mark the important S/R, the more important the S/R the thicker the line. Then I switch the chart back to M15, and use the Dance MAs to trade but the yellow lines always tell me what's ahead. If there is a Dance signal but I have a yellow line right ahead, I do NOT take the trade.

--- 帖子 #1853 ---
I would challenge you at this one, Kostas1 I am very interested in MQL programming, and I am working on automatizing the Dance system right now (while trading manually on the side, of course). The main difficulty for the moment is the "MA touch". As many of you might have noticed, there's no REAL touch of the MA line by price at the momnet you enter a trade. When the price tends to the MA, the MA tends AWAY from the price, because the MA is calculated on CLOSE. So, you can only see the perfect touch AFTER the "touch bar" is closed.. but it's too late to enter the trade then! So, you must do some extrapolation of the MA to estimate the touch point. This is fairly easy for a human, but less so for a robot... Sorry for this post that's a bit off topic; I still closely following your fellow traders learning to dance better

Have taken the liberty of cutting and pasting: " Quadruple witching refers to the third Friday of every March, June, September and December. On these days, market index futures , market index options, stock options and stock futures expire, usually resulting in increased volatility. How It Works/Example: Although futures and options generally share simultaneous expirations on the third Friday of every month, quadruple witching days only occur four times a year. The last hour of these trading days, from 3:00 to 4:00 p.m. EST, is referred to as the quadruple witching hour . On quadruple witching days, and especially during quadruple witching hours, many investors attempt to unwind their futures and options positions before the contracts expire. This a ctivity frequently includes repurchasing contracts and closing out position mark et capitalizations. Why It Matters: Quadruple witching days are usually accompanied by considerable volatility in stock and derivative prices, as well as increased trading volume. As a result, investors can anticipate and plan for the potential effects of these relatively turbulent trading days. " Am currently coding an mq4 indicator as we speak that will automatically disable my mouse on these days....will share when i get it working

Hi Norg, I am surely not an experienced Dancer, but I think also this answer to be on Clay's Manual. The "music" I hear tells me that the retracement to the 10MA in two bars is valid after the swing high of the last stronger move, of at least 15 pips. So this exclude picture nr. 4 Also very important is the angle of the MA10, as higher the ° the better the trade possibility. BUT: also very important in my opinion is the P/A on the small TF at the moment of the M15 MA10 touch. M1 and/or M5 must show you that the move is going to go back to the previous direction. Otherwise you risk to enter a touch "through" the MA10 and you never know where it will arrive (just look at the other MA or S/R or RN). Moreover you also need a look at the higher TF's. Where is the stronger direction at the moment ? Should I mostly look at long or short moves at the moment ? Just try to understand where our leading Dancer (the market) will most probably go next, as we have to follow. Or we will thump its feet... and I think the Market doesn't really appreciate that

The only thing missing was a good angle of the MA's, but in my opinion it was compensated by all the other above mentioned factors in favor of the trade. One more thing I want to add is: I've found that discretionary entries, based on good analasys, are on top of mechanical, robot like, ones.
