--- 帖子 #2051 ---
I was reading through the thread and seeing the success people are having with this method, but also see that a lot of people have a hard time with the touch trades and issues with confidence as you move up to bigger lots. I would suggest to everyone that you drop your risk per trade down to 1% or less. For me I trade with .5% risk on each trade right now, I am not suggesting that is doable for everyone I know what it is like to trade a small account, but I also know that over leveraging yourself is the surest path to failure. With no intent whatsoever to hijack this great thread and all the hard work that has gone into it I wanted to share my trading approach over the past several months I have made a number of changes to my own trading to simplify things for me, as this may help some of the people that are struggling with the touch trades. I now trade the 5min charts exclusively and use the 5/10/50 emas, the 18 sma and the 30 minute 18 sma (the 35sma on the 15 min chart my favorite ma). Essentially what I do is trade single bar bounces off of the 5/10 emas in a strong trend (the mas are parallel they happen all the time on the 5min charts), if it takes more than 1 bar to get back to the either the 5 or 10 and retrace, I wait for a bounce off of the one of the other mas, and will only trade touches off of the 30 min 18sma the rest of them I wait for the candle close. Once a trade gets to +10 i set it to BE and wait, if it starts to retrace back hard I will close it for a small profit but most of the time they end up running for 15-30 pips, at which point I will move my stop up higher and see what happens. Using this approach I keep my risk very well contained with stops around 10 pips or less, the trade is either going to run or it is not. For me keeping the risk small on each trade has allowed me to add lots and trade almost on autopilot with this approach.

--- 帖子 #2059 ---
I have always been a little more careful about the touch trades and have always favored the 5/10 bounces, why take risks you don't have to right. What I always had problems with was that it seemed like a lot of the time the bounces off of the 5/10 would not go my way so one weekend I pulled out all my trade data and looked at the failed trades vs successful 5/10 bounces in a trend and found that better than 70% of the 2 or more bar retraces were going to fail but 85% of the single bar retraces resulted in successful trades (for the purposes of this exorcise this meant price continued in the direction of the prevailing trend and my initial sl of 10 pips + spread would not have been hit). I use the 5min chart exclusively and pretty much define the trend by the direction of the 30 min 18sma, I use a mtf ma indi to diplay this on a 5min chart, this is the same as the 35 sma on the 15min chart. To be honest I don't play the if it is below x line only go short ect, though I do respect the 30 min 18sma as a strong resistance point, and love bounces off of it and if price is far enough away from it and retraces to it in a candle it is a great touch trade. My main entries are all bounces off the 5/10 in a strong trend (MAs parallel), on the 5min chart. I only do touch trades off the 30 min 18 sma (35 sma on the 15) if price is a ways away from it and it occurs in a single bar, otherwise I wait for PA to show a bounce or a good pin off the MA and will take that trade with the prevailing trend. I have attached a chart I threw together, there are other entries on the chart that are good but not identified on it, thumbs up means a good trade and thumbs down is bad. I included some comments on the chart and all these trades would be take as soon as the bar that bounces closes.

--- 帖子 #2078 ---
I don't remember where exactly, but I have read a study that any MA that you draw will be respected sooner or later. It's just a mathematical regression of the price to the mean. The reason we use the specific ones in the Dance is that these are observed by the biggest amount of traders. Therefore, when the price approaches them there is a higher probability of a reaction there. This is why confluence works better since even more traders pay attention (for example, many traders trade only H1 and many traders trade only M15. When price approaches H1 10 the first group gets ready to react, when price approaches M15 35 the second group gets ready, but when H1 10 and M15 35 are confluenced both groups will react). Don't get confused, stick with the original MAs and hone you technique with them before you try anything else.

--- 帖子 #2161 ---
Interesting day to test a new approach today. I suppose the thing we don't know about how Endroute trades this is whether he will just take every touch regardless so long as it's a one candle retrace or whether he use more discretion than that, looking at pivots, S+R, RN's and price action. These two charts are from 5.00am ish GMT to 3.00pm ish GMT. They include some price action trades around the MAs and some touch trades off the 5+10. Black = winner, white = loser. The pound obviously had a rocky day and fell a long way in a big and pretty even trend. The thing about trends of this nature is that once you are past the ADR for the pair, you find yourself thinking "it must be over by now". trading this way though, I just think you've got to take every touch and accept that the losses will come, especially as the trend ends on you. Don't worry too much about ADR, maybe just keep it mind and don't try to chase after too much if it's over it. EJ was a very different animal. It ranged tightly until NY and then broke out in a volatile sorta way. Even so, keep taking the touches and they paid dividends. You obviously need these mas roughly lined up but I think when it's breaking out of a tight range, you have to accept that they won't always be totally parallel. You will notice that some of the trades with a ring around are in the middle of the candle. Obviously, some touches are at the right point but then price goes against you for a period before either taking your stop or coming back around into profit so the touch ends up in the middle of the candle. All in all, I make it 4 good price action setups at the mas but these are far more subjective. 8 sound touch trades 3 failed trades About 70% success rate if you'd taken all those trades but a lot less if you weren't happy with the price action setups. That said, if you are letting those winners run, you would still be fine at 50%. The other thing to note is although that sounds like a fair few trades, you wouldn't catch them all and some would overlap others if you are letting your winners run - unless you are brave enough to add to your position. Hope this helps, i will do some more later in the week.

--- 帖子 #2166 ---
Frnds, I have been trading the original “dance” strictly by the manual for few days now. I have studied my losses and other failed charts posted here with interest. I observe that while these failed trades were mostly by the rules; they violated the core principle of the system. As I understand it, this system is designed to catch safe pips in middle of a trend. This means for trading this system there has to be two things: First there must be a fresh new trend. This has been stressed enough in manual and that explains few errors by beginners here. Basically we don’t trade flatline or porcupine and crossing MAs. The MAs must be steep. We don’t try to catch beginning of a trend. We only jump on retracement AFTER a trend has started. Only exception is constrainment trade. But that’s anyway pretty easy to spot and hardly gives any trouble to beginners. Second point to understand is the trend must not be ending. This is the part I found difficult to master. We take a trade by the rule and then find it just goes and hits SL. This explains those situations. While I didn’t find any warnings about this in manual, I think it’s not difficult to see warnings if we are aware of this rule. For example, a reversal pin bar in uptrend IS a fair warning. Now even if we see a buy trade exactly by the rule it would be safe to pass it after that trend ending signal. Some of the reversal signals are discussed in manual and watching these signals in higher time frames (Edit here- made it bold) will save newbies a lot of pips and tons of frustration. Another warning not mentioned in manual can come from good old wave count. After a move has already seen 3 waves in its direction, there might be at least some mild correction. No wonder seniors say we should take only “first touch”. Maybe they have intuitively understood the basic premise of this strategy. I will just add a chart where I lost money. Just to clarify what I mean. While I think this observation has helped me a lot, please remember that I am absolutely new to this system and by no means an expert. Because of that reason I would request senior members to please comment especially if they find something wrong in this observation. Because else this post may mislead others instead of helping. Fairly long post but felt like sharing my genuine observations clearly. Trade well

He may not be able to answer as he is an infrequent visitor to the thread. A retrace is part of the ebb and flow of anything traded. Buyers and sellers are involved in every move. Every direction price is going, there are either buyers making money and sellers losing money or the exact reverse. So, say it's a bull market (long), there will be points where it will move bearish (short) for a small time. It's primarily because some of the people making money take their profits and close part or all of their position. This temporarily alows the bears to win out and push the market a little lower. But, if it's a bull market, the bulls will soon enough take over again to push it back up. This will carry on until there is a reversal point where finally either more sellers have come in at a certain point or enough buyers have taken their money allowing sellers to take over. These retraces are ideal points to get into the right direction of the current trend, expecting price to go back from where it came. You said it is "5 bars". This isn't true. It's as many bars as it takes, could be 2, could be 20 but at some point, there will be a retrace. Regarding how to enter, you are looking for a reaction. As price approaches the mas, look for it to start to loose momentum, stall a little bit. Sometimes it will bounce back, only for it to try again and break right through the ma. You are playing the odds here so anything can and will happen. But, you enter at the touch or around the area that it touched one of the mas, so you will be trading on a bearish coloured candle in a bullish market and visa-versa (this may feel odd at first). My advice is to stick with kosta and not Endroute. Kostas advice is ideal for those starting out and using M15 as your main TF is more reliable and easy to understand than M5. Study hard, read, read, read. It's not something that will stick overnight.

Good day all...it's been a while since I've posted here, but always reading! For some of the newer people in here this might help. I know it helped me a lot to "see" price dancing. When I'm watching the charts and price action...I constantly ask myself "what is the price doing?" It sounds silly, but if you dissect and really think out loud what the price is actually doing it really helps. Is price constraining on a certain MA, is price trying to reverse from a clear down or uptrend, is there a lot of fighting between longs and shorts and price is porcupining, etc. It's a simple question to yourself..."what is the price doing" ... let the price show you it's hand. Then check your MA's to make sure they're steep and the 35/50 are preferably on top of each other. Then wait for the price to attempt to "touch" or play the constrainment. Hopefully that makes sense or will help some people.

What people don't realise is that it's NOT about the pip count it is about the profit you make from those pips. A guy who taught me system a while ago always bragged because he made like 500 pips a day or something but moneywise it was less than 1% of his count per day which did not make a lot of sense to me. If 20 pips a day grows your account by 2% then it is a lot better than 1000 pips a day that does not grow your account at all. That's what makes this system excellent because of the small stop loss you can risk more and thus make the same profit with a quick 30 pip trade compared to a day trader that need 200+ pips to make the same amount of money

--- 帖子 #2349 ---
I am not that brave like some of you to follow the trades at the end of the previous M15 bar. I usually take my 10-15p and run with most of my trade. Sometimes, I will leave a small portion to run for more but with small SL and usually it is stopped out. Case in point. This morning's M15 10 touch confluenced with H1 10. I got +9p since I took profit at the Weekly Pivot. Rest was stopped out by the sudden thrust upwards. My suggestion to some of you is to try this partial profit method. Take profit at 10-15p for 85% of your trade and leave the rest according to the original rules. This way you get the quick profit and even if you are stopped out on the rest, all you need is 3-4 trades like that per day (easy to find 3-4 +10p opportunities with the Dance). Many times when the price reverses suddenly you have already taken your profit, so you have a winning trade where others have losses. GREED is NOT GOOD

--- 帖子 #2370 ---
Survivor, Depending on how this thread has evolved, its unlikely that you need multi timeframe templates. If you want a 100e/sma to appear only on the 1hr chart, then set it up, then edit it and look in 'Visualisation' and ensure only the 1hr box is ticked. You can do this for most indicators and objects. If you have a common MA, such as the 50 what you want to appear on the 15min, 1hr and 4hr, then just ensure those boxes are ticked. In relation to your Pivot indicator, you may need to adjust your time settings to ensure it starts the new day in accordance with your broker. Having said that, there are prefered time settings, and prefered brokers for 'feeds'. If you dont like the size of the 'lines', then you will either need to A) Hope there is a setting that you can edit or B) get hold of the MTQ file, which will allow you to edit it. Failing that, you will need to get hold of another Pivot idicator. Regards Lee

--- 帖子 #2384 ---
Good question. I've found that due to the nature of the Dance, price will usually retrace all the way back to the starting point. So, if you move to BE it will surely hit the BE on the remaining trade. But if you give your remaining 15% 4-5pips space it has more chances to survive. On the other hand, loosing 4-5p on 15% of the trade is not bad. You still have a good profit and doesn't hurt your daily target. For example, if you start with 2 lots and get +13p for 1.7 lots and -4p for 0.3 lots, it gives you 149E instead of 157E. Of course, you could consider taking all the profit (2 lots) at +13p for 184E. The problem is that if then the trade shoots up in your direction for 30 pips or more, you feel stupid for not participating in that (total: 157+60= 217E). It seems that I do it mainly for psychological reasons so that I don't feel bad for missing a strong run after taking partial profits.

--- 帖子 #2415 ---
I was talking about my understanding from posts 1 to 3350 ( . PipEasy has several positions open for months or years even, both long AND short. He always trades 2 standard lots (2x100K equivalent) per position. But he can open 7 longs (of 2 lots each) within a few hours if he sees momentum. Check his recent examples in the last 2 pages of the thread. Anyway, these hints just do no justice, as the whole thread (and especially his posts) is worth reading from start to end. Took me a week but it was worth every minute of it. Same for the original Dance thread and the Choros thread. In short, when you would reach a point in your account growth where you have to trade more than a number of standard lots to continue growing at the same rate, liquidity at your broker at least would be an issue, so you wouldn't get a correct fill (getting partial fills, lots of slippage and so on). Been there: I took a 1K Euro (live) account to 35K in a few days back in 2008 Q4 (extreme volatility period - with a 200:1 leverage) and my orders started not behaving right (think 10-12 standard lots). Know how it feels to see a position not being able to be closed fully and going partially at least 100,200 pips in the red? I went crazy, lost it all within 3 days, and vowed to find out what went wrong... I was lucky to have the courage NOT to blame my broker, as this would leave me in self-inflicted blindness forever. So getting in and out in 2 lot chunks, multiple times within an hour, is much more easy and allows you to grow the account (not a single trade, I don't think that was the meaning) to infinity. A very similar (long term) approach was also hinted in another classic (in my book at least) thread, the "No Free Lunch..." http://www.forexfactory.com/showthread.php?t=56907 where Peter Crowns described taking hourly inside bar setups one after the other and not worrying about closing positions. Just another way to enter repeatedly in the market in small chunks with a good edge. That was the first thread I came across after starting my search back then. Sticking to the Dance for the moment, I am now very far from those numbers still.. And by the way, your posts have been a great contribution here among others, so I just wanted to contribute something as well for you and for everyone on the thread. My plan is one day soon to stop just "dancing" for 15-30 pips and move to the PipEasy style. My target for that is a 30K account. Even then, all the concepts of the Dance provide excellent entry techniques with very small risks, so I consider myself very lucky to have found out about it. Cheers, Christos

--- 帖子 #2428 ---
Here is another of my crazy observations. Its NOT dance and not even tested. But i have been seeing them quite often and have found them to be very consistent. When all the MAs are bunched up, wait for price to cross either side. Then look for a candle that wicks through all MAs and then closes on same side. This typically indicates direction of next move. Basically what we are looking for is- after price has crossed MAs, one final failed attempt to bring price on other side. In the attached chart after price moves above MAs, Bears make one final assault here to bring the price down but fail. This often shows direction of future move. Have not tested it yet and am not even trading them but looks promising to me. Maybe we can buy much ahead of first touch if it works. Greenhill: Nice observation there about EU touch trade. higher mas not in same direction there so should have been passed.

--- 帖子 #2495 ---
A while back someone raised a question about the false "touches" on the 10EMA. I mean the frequent situations where there is no touch in real time, but by the close of the bar it looks like a perfect touch, because the price has dragged the MA along with it. The answer, at that time, was that the dance waits for a true 10EMA touch. And the responder suggested that the false touches that didn't work out were bad enough to make this a good rule. I've been thinking about this and I don't think it's necessarily correct. Just imagine the following situation. Price is falling and the 10 EMA is really steep. Lets also say that the MAs are nicely arranged with 50 on top, 35 just below, then 10 EMA, then price. Price comes up for one bar, and now on the second bar it is approaching the 10 EMA. Then price starts to stall out, say 3-4 pips below the 10EMA. Dance rules say no trade, and wait for the touch. But what if you took the trade? 1) Price starts to drop, and the trade is a winner. Here you get a winning trade where the dance gives you no trade at all. 2) Price comes out of its stall and goes up to touch the 10 EMA. Here, you get a worse entrance on your 10 EMA trade. This might end up costing you some pips, depending on how you exit. 3) Price stays in a stall and the bar ends. Now you would be on the third bar and violating the 2 bar rule. In this event, you might either move the stop up very tightly, or just exit the trade with either a very small loss or gain. The risk of entering in this situation seems very well defined. You are basically putting an extra 3-4 pips at risk on a 10EMA trade, and in exchange you are hoping to get more trades in your favor. Is it worth the risk? I don't have a clear answer to that. From looking at the charts, it seems like these near misses happen all the time, and thus it also seems like people are passing up on many decent opportunities. Kostas might have something to say about how to judge when price has stalled between the 5 and 10 EMAs and is moving in the other direction. I've seen that he has taken these sorts of trades from time to time. Sorry for the length (and possible presumptuousness) of this post.

--- 帖子 #2559 ---
I won't pretend to be an expert, but I will take a shot at answering this one. First, a trade going against you doesn't mean you did anything wrong. Sometimes, in any strategy, the best set up will still be a loser. That doesn't make it a bad trade. It's also worth noting that we don't have the larger time frame, so the chart doesn't show the complete picture. It's possible that there was info in the higher time frames that would shed light on this situation. Here, there were a few possible entry points. 1) Enter on the first touch of the top MA and placed your stop below the bottom MA. This is a valid dance trade. When the MA's are separated, it looks like some people wait to see price will reach the last MA. But, by the rules, I think its OK to take from a touch on the first MA. 2) Enter on the touch of the bottom MA. This would also be valid and by the rules. I don't yet know how one decides between the two. Kostas' experience suggests that, at least on the GU, the last MA acts like a price magnet in these situations. And yet he still admits entering early out of fear that he will lose the trade. 3) Enter at COB, as you did. Here I have a question. As price moved down to hit the MAs, you are expecting a bounce upward. But in this instance, price broke through both MAs, and then moved back up to the top MA by the end of the candle. So, why do you now expect a bounce up? Couldn't you just as easily treat this as price moving up to the MAs and then bouncing down? I know that that question is really easy to ask with the benefit of hindsight. I will only point out that by the time you entered your trade, price had moved through both MAs, and then back through them both again. People here have recently been questioning price behavior when both the 35 and 50 are crossed. Also, at any of the three entry points, it looks to me like you should not have had a big loss. On the next bar, the price moved up 10 pips or so. I think, in this situation, that that is probably enough to move to break even, or at least tighten the stop some. Others might very well disagree on this point. I will note, however, where I've seen similar examples where one poster got stopped out, another broke even, and Kostas took the trade off the bottom MA and ended up with a net gain. I'd be very interested to hear what other, more experienced people think about this trade.

--- 帖子 #2577 ---
The two bar rule is specifically for 10 ema touches. Whatever the rules might say, from my experience (others may not agree), when the 35/50 is quite far from the 10 and there is no news, and the space is covered in a few very large bars, then something is up. I've tried trading these as touches, but they can be difficult because they may blow through, and even when they close at the MA, the large move (as it did in the chart you posted) went on to retrace to a larger timeframe MA. For me, such powerful bars are a warning to either stay out or take pips quickly.

--- 帖子 #2611 ---
There isn't a net pip option for Account Summary. It might be possible to write an EA that did what you wanted. That's beyond my competence. You don't have to enter each entry and exit into a spreadsheet. You can simply paste the html version of the report into the spreadsheet, and then it's a question of massaging the data. That will depend on how many currencies you trade, and which ones. Basically, the yen based currencies have a different number of decimal places in the pip values than the others. You have to normalize them. All it takes is a couple of conditional formulas, and its not that hard to do. It's alot easier than the manual entry route. And, if you set it up right, it is reusable too.

No problem. One correction though. The indicator counts everything that shows on your "Account History" tab. So go there, right-click to choose custom period and choose "Today" so that only today's trades are shown in the Account History. This way the indicator will only count today's pips.

--- 帖子 #2625 ---
It's not only counting pips per day. Usually, when I am in a position I need to "feel" the action and not keep calculating total position every second. Don't forget that many of my trades last a few minutes, sometimes seconds. With this indicator showing the green or red pips continuously on my screen I can free my brain to concentrate on the trade action and "feel" if there is more green for me or if it's time to get out. Also, I don't have to look on the small MT4 trade section to see how the trade is going which also makes me worry when I see big amounts of money going up&amp;down per pip (scary with big lots). As a result, my brain can process as little information as possible, I zone in the trade and notice the green pips go up or the red pips go down. When I feel it is time to get out I press the button. I am not sure if the above blur makes sense, but use the indicator when your lots grow bigger and you may find it useful. I don't have experience from other trading software but for MT4 this is the easiest way to avoid worrying about $$$ and concentrate on daily pips. Money management and compounding do the rest....

First is a tweezer top. Entries now seem to be confined to constrainment, 10EMA touches, and 35 and 50 EMA bounces. In the original dance thread, Clay confirmed a number of entries as price action entries. These, I think are legacies from Clay's study of EOHater's method. At a point where there is likely to be support or resistance, EOHater will enter following a good candle pattern: hanging man, shooting star, engulfing, tweezer top, etc... Clay would sometimes call these decent entries, and sometimes qualify the statement by saying that they were not "by the rules" dance entries.

--- 帖子 #2643 ---
This raises an interesting question, at least for me. For me, one of the hardest things about this system is figuring out what action to take when the 35 and 50 are not neatly together. I think it offers the biggest room for judgment. I've been reading up on EOHater's approach. He treats the 35/50 EMA on M15 slightly differently than the dance. When the body of a candle crosses both the 35 and 50 and closes with a small wick, he enters in the opposite direction on the close of the candle. In many ways, the Dance approach to these trades is a refinement and probably an improvement to the EOHaters approach. It takes more trades. It catches trades where there is a bounce and the candle close would only show a wick through one or both of the EMAs. Here are a few situations: 1) The MAs are on top of each other. In this situation, the Dance approach will catch many more trades. The EOHater approach will make a few more pips on the trades it catches. Both of them will lose on a complete blow through. And Kostas' approach of fine tuning the trade by waiting for good PA on the 5 minute chart may be a great compromise between the two. 2) The MAs are far apart but parallel or converging. The Dance approach makes you decide which MA to use. This creates both opportunities, and trades where you end up kicking yourself for entering too early. The EOHater approach will give you less trades, but has the advantage of being very mechanical. This is where I really think Kostas' fine tuning may be best. At the first MA, the fine tuning approach would wait until there were some actual signs of a bounce. 3) The MAs are spaced some and diverging (as in the posted trade). Survivor says this is an area where you can't trust the bounce. On this trade, if you followed the EOHater approach and entered at the close of the candle, there would have been an OK, but not a great trade. But notice that the same chart has another situation that is very similar where any entry would have generated a loss. I don't have any firm answers for any of this. I'm just raising an area that I am struggling with, and giving a lot of thought.

--- 帖子 #2673 ---
It looks like you were trying to do a 10EMA Touch trade. There were a few ways in which the trade you took were not by the rules. The trade didn't follow the Two Bar Rule. Instead, your trade was after three full green bars. There was a by the rules entry two bars earlier than where you entered, but it would probably either ended in a BE trade, or a loss. You didn't trade on the "touch". 10EMA touch trades don't wait for the close of bar. Moreover, when you took the trade, there were three consecutive bars that had touched the 10EMA. In general, its best to try to catch the first touch of an EMA. (That may not be as crucial with a 10EMA trade, if the other conditions are clearly met. I don't know about this and would like to hear other opinions.) And from your long wait, it looks like you either didn't have a stop in place, or the stop was bigger than 22 pips or so. By the dance rules, a 10EMA touch trade should have a tight stop. I think Clay says no more than 9 pips for these. Some people might go for a bigger stop, and it can depend on other support in the area. In any event, no dance trade should have a wider stop than 19 pips. If you need a wider stop than that, then at least be aware that you are not strictly going "by the rules." It's possible that you had something in mind other than a 10EMA touch trade, in which case all my comments do not apply. Personally, I don't see any dance trade in that area, except for the one two bars before your entry. Of course, I could be wrong. It would not be the first time.

--- 帖子 #2701 ---
Warning: Fairly long somewhat theoretical post I have read somewhere criticizing the system for not providing any reasons why dance works. Dont remember where i read that though. Anyway have been thinking about it for some time now. Here is what i think: 1. Its based on self fulfilling prophecies. When there is a big move say upwards, people who didn't buy lower (Even worse who sold lower) are left frustrated. They will certainly look to re-enter (Or cut shorts) on any pullback. Now, everyone will look at different things- Mas, fibbo, pivots. That's why Confluences work so well. It just means many types of traders are looking to enter there. 2. Also notice that we look at steepness of MA. This shows how fast market has moved and how greedy traders must be after seeing this move. If its fairly steep nobody will like to miss it and they will jump at 10EMA. If its flat they will wait for 35/50 ma. 3. Finally, note the two bar rule. Why it's there? Suppose price breaks out north sharply. Now as it falls towards our entry at 10 EMA, we want buys to be concentrated at 10 EMA. If its falls slowly in many bars that means many buyers have already jumped in before price reached 10 EMA - meaning buyers were distributed at different levels during fall. However if it falls sharply that means buyers are holding their guns and their power will be concentrated at 10 EMA. Hope that makes sense to someone.

--- 帖子 #2706 ---
Hey Hop Just a point on your indicator. A 'perfect pin' is not one that has an equal open and close. For eg the one you show is not a pinbar it is a doji. A doji is a neutral bar that could indicate a pause or a reversal. The 'perfect' pin bar is hard to define but it has the following characteristics: range at least equal to the last few bars closes within 10% of extreme close lower than open ( for short, reverse for long) Preferably fakes out a SR level or a previous swing to trap traders Your existing pin identifier is probably sufficient as is...then it is up to the trader to assess. thks

--- 帖子 #2707 ---
if i may add, that white signal isnt even a doji. a doji is shaped like that (with 2-3 variations), it indicates market slowdown primarily and MAYBE reversal but it must appear after a trend, up or down, say 3 bars can indicate a trend. but where that white marked doji appear doesnt indicate anything because there isnt any trend at that moment.

--- 帖子 #2759 ---
I can't speak as a successful user -- only as a student. Clay not only says that 19 is the maximum stop, it also seems like he uses it as an emergency stop. In many places, it looks like he moves the stop to 6 or 7 plus spread. For 10EMA touch trades, he says 11 pips max for the stop. Three points on this: 1) If you look at the charts, its pretty easy to see that a good trade will usually move quickly in your favor. 2) The main reason for using a bigger stop is because there is support/resistance on the other side of your trade. In these situations, it might be better to wait to see if those areas will get tested. 3) With stops so tight, there is very good reason for trying to find a broker who doesn't trade against you. You might still fall victim to stop hunting in general, but with an ECN or STP broker, you can at least have some confidence that your stop in particular is not being targeted. Let me ask a question: Can you think of a situation where you have an A+ dance trade, but you also need a bigger stop?

--- 帖子 #2891 ---
Dont get frustrated mate. Losses are part of trading. As for your querry here is what i think. In 15M chart, its NOT a good constrainment in my view. Three reasons: 1. how you see all MA moving down? at those candles 10EMA was actually pointing up. And thats not after you took the trade. 10 EMA was rising even after close of first candle. watch carefully. In my experiance best constrainment happens when all MAs parrallel and pointing same way. Here 10EMA is actually pushing the prices up. 2. No wicks through constraining MA is a bad omen in my experience. Only when price wicks through constraining MA and fails to break it then i take the constrainment trades. 3. Notice how even 10EMA is also "constraining" the price. Price should be touching only one constraining MA. in this case difficult to say which MA is contraining the price upper or lower one. NOT a valid constrainment in my opinion. We are just forcing a trade here. In 1H chart you have already noted yourself that MAs are wide and flattenning. Constrainments are best against rising or falling MAs. Flat MAs are no no for me. There are many other reasons for failure of this trade in HTF. but i wont confuse you with them. Even in 15M there were plenty of warnings. You always getting it wrong? Do this - WAIT. Wait for 10 EMA to cross 35/50 both and price to move very far from 35/50- at least three bars. Then let price retrace to 10 EMA in two bars. Take the trade at touch of 10 EMA with 10 pip SL . Book your profit fast at 20 pips- and magic- You will have a winning trade. Then repeat it when later when price retraces next time time to touch parallel or on top of each other 35/50. Then you have another winning trade. In short- take only the very best first touches and see magic. Learn to wait for perfect setup. Most of the time we lose becayuse we try to force a trade where there is none. Looking at chart long and hard to find a trade is bad habbit. Trade only when a trade jumps out at you without effort. As an aside,to me today not looking good for dance as of now

--- 帖子 #2915 ---
Well, I am not doing a lot of constrainments but in my opinion after you decide it's constrainment and the MA starts to point up or down then get in exactly on the MA. Alternatively, wait for a rejection bar and get in after it closes (this should be done early otherwise you may loose the move). First way is better since it allows for a small SL and if you are stopped out you can try again.

--- 帖子 #2916 ---
Hey Fx prince In my opnion it was a valid entry. I avoid such trades only when 35/50 are flat and wide. this this case 35/50 converging and bending down. Even 10 EMA was bending down. So it was a valid entry But i really dont understand why you coudnt enter if you spotted the constrainment. Here is how i would have traded it. After you spot it, sell AT the 10EMA - because thats constraing MA and we dont see many wicks above it, so unlikely to get a better price to sell. SL: once you have entered,check last wick high through 10EMA. Keep your Sl slightly above that high. In this particular case i see that EVAN 35/50 is very close above 10 EMA. Now since you know even if price breaks 10EMA its likely to find resistance at 35/50. So even sa safer SL would have been above 35SMA. I can see that even with that safe an Sl you would have hardly needed 15 pip Sl. But also note that if price CLOSED above 10 EMA the setup would have become invalid. So even though your sl might not have been hit, look to close the trade at minimum loss if that happenes. You will rarely lose more that 4-5 pips with such good setups. So what keeps you from taking it? Fear? read the manual again then EDIT: you could have taken that trade anytime during the fall.and still above described method would have worked. But as price goes far from 35/50 trade becomes weaker and weaker EDIT: am sorry that i cant posts charts to explain things. That will be true for all future posts. The H1 10EMA varies from the M15 40EMA, quite a bit more than I expected. I'm sure this has something to do with the nature of the exponential weighting. I saw them vary by as many as 19 pips in a quick comparison that I just did. With sharp turns, they tend to vary by 10-15 pips with some regularity. That's not that much, but people do tend to assume that you can simply multiply time periods to get the same MAs on smaller charts. And with this system, its quite often the difference between getting stopped out or not. With simple MAs, multiplying gives closer results, but they still tend to vary by a couple of pips. That comes from the "noise" of peaks and valleys in the intermediate bars on the smaller charts. I also checked the 50EMA vs. the 40EMA. Not much surprise there: they are basically always parallel and close to each other. It would be completely pointless to have both of them on a chart at once. If we have a math genius on the forum, perhaps we could come up with a situation, or a group of situations where the 10EMA on the H1 varies from a confluence of the 35SMA and 50EMA on the M15. The problem is pretty easy to state but beyond my ability to solve: 1) Define 50 variables, one for the close of each of 50, 15 minute candles: C1 through C50. 2) EMA(C1, ... C50) = SMA (C16, ... C50) This condition describes a perfect intersection of the MAs. 3) EMA (C16, C20, C24, C28, C32, C36, C38, C42, C46, C50) - EMA(C1, ... C50) &gt; 15 This means that the difference between the EMAs is bigger than our stop loss, which I think is enough to invalidate confluence. --- 帖子 #2974 ---
Hi Duffy, I am not a math genius. However, I loaded about 7000 15M bars of GBPUSD in an Excel, and calculated the SMA35(15M), EMA50(15M) and the 10EMA(1H). Let's define the case you are looking for: The SMA35(15M) and the EMA50(15M) are within 3 pips of each other (confluence) AND the 10EMA(1H) is more than 15 pips away from EMA50(15M). It turned out that this occurs 1-3 times per month, but in all of these cases, it is always after a big move (more than 150 pips within a few hours) and just when consolidation starts (the move stops and reverses even slightly) this case described above appears. Last 3 appearances are on November 16, 17:45 GMT, October 26 11:15 GMT and October 19 13:15 GMT. You can backtrack your charts and see these. The bottom line is that : In such cases there is no chance that you will have a 50EMA touch trade on the M15, as it has to be very far from the price to create such a scenario. If I was a math genius, I could possibly provide mathematical proof, but this simple test should be enough to drive the point home. Further, just for information, the formula for EMA calculation (at least the way it works in MT4, there are alternative methods) is: (2/(MAperiod+1))*CurrentClose+((MAperiod-1)/(MAperiod+1)*PreviouscandleEMAvalue. Therefore, the EMA essentially contains ALL the bars in the chart, but only uses the latest bar for each iteration. This has some other interesting implications for the Dance trades, but I would leave it for some other time. Hope this helps. Christos

--- 帖子 #2986 ---
Hi Will, it's to do with the 15M touch trades (usually the 10EMA ones) where you see the price moving up to the EMA (let's suppose it is below it when starting), misses it by 1-2 pips and then reverses for 20 pips. After the 15M bar closes, the wick would have obviously "touched" the EMA but this did not happen in real time. I am sure you've seen this. Well, the EMA formula in essence says that if price closes (MAperiod+1)/2 pips away from the EMA, then the EMA moves in the direction of the price by 1 pip. For the 10EMA, this number is 5.5 pips. So let's take an example: A 15M candle opens 33 pips below the EMA10 in a downtrend. If this candle closes at this same opening price, then the EMA10 will move 6 pips down in the next bar. If however the candle moves up from the open 27.5 pips - towards the EMA, the EMA would only appear to move down by 1 pip. So the wick would still be 4.5 pips below the EMA at that point in time - no touch. But if then the price moves - within the same candle - back down to its opening price (33 pips below the EMA10), then the EMA10 would move 6 pips down and it would appear as a clear "touch" to anyone watching the chart. Magnificent trade by the rules, done for the day, etc., alas, you would have missed it if you waited for the real touch. Therefore, the implication is this: if you are looking for a touch trade, based on other confluence always as the manual suggests, then you can simply place a Pending limit order a few (4-5) pips below the previous EMA price and increase your stop accordingly (manual says 11 pips above EMA), avoiding the missing of an "almost touch" as in the example above. Again, this applies IF the rest of the analysis suggests that a touch trade would be a good opportunity. Otherwise, it's not a good trade anyway . BTW, I am actually applying this and it takes some of the stress away when waiting for a touch trade. Opposite applies to an uptrend (e.g. watching the EURJPY right now to add to my constrainment trade from the morning). Same things apply in any timeframe (formula for 10EMA does not change). For the EMA50, a difference of 25.5 pips would make a 1 pip move, and so on. SMA touches do not work like this, because the SMA changes a lot less with each candle (at times when there is a short term reversal of price). SMA touches can be taken exactly at the touch (when you see it happen). I hope I am not confusing things too much. Again, a math teacher would probably be able to write it up better than this, but I hope it is clear. Cheers, Christos

Hay guys. I had your query pointed out to me by a friend and (especially as several of you are using my PipTracker ) thought I would throw an indicator together to show this situation. If you want to take a look, place it first on a blank chart so that other indicators don't confuse what you are seeing It will show the following - Green line = M15 50EMA White line = M15 35EMA Orange line = H1 10EMA Vertical pink bars when Green and White are less than 3pip apart at the same time as Green and White are more than 15pips apart Note. You can put this on any timeframe but obviously if greater than M15 then it won't be as accurate as the M15 MA's will only be reading values once per chart period (ie on an M30 chart you will only see every other M15 value) Also, the Orange H1 10EMA will show historically as being 'stepped' because there is no way (I know of) to determine its position at 15,30,45 minutes past the hour so at these times it will actually be comparing the M15 MA's against the final hourly position of the H1 MA. --- 帖子 #2994 ---
The real time position of an H1 10EMA on an M15 chart is: (2/11)*currentprice+(9/11)*LastHourEMAvalue Current price is the current Bid of course. LastHourEMAvalue is the value that this EMA had when the last xx:45 candle closed (last quarter - end of the hour). This variable should not change until the close of the next xx:45 candle in the chart. Initialize the variable with just the close price of the first xx:45 candle you come across in the chart bars. This is the way MT4 calculates EMAs in general. Similar things would apply to other EMA/timeframe combination. Hope this helps, Cheers, Christos

--- 帖子 #2995 ---

--- 帖子 #2996 ---
I hate it when I have to open the MT4 manual. I've always been good at Pseudocode but never a real programmer. Although I learnt Python last year because I wanted to run my own statistical price tests. Anyway... On a 15M chart: if(TimeMinute(Time[0]))==0 { if LastHourEMAvalue==0.0 { LastHourEMAvalue=Close[0] } else { LastHourEMAvalue=(2/11)*Close[1]+(9/11)*LastHourEMAvalue } CurrentEMAvalue=(2/11)*Close[0]+(9/11)*LastHourEMAvalue } else { CurrentEMAvalue=(2/11)*Close[0]+(9/11)*LastHourEMAvalue } The if condition detects whether this is the first candle of a new hour, and then calculates what the EMA10 of 1H timeframe should be at the close of the previous hour, taking into account the close of the previous candle which is a xx:45 candle, therefore it is a close of the last hour. If this is not the xx:00 candle (the else clause), then we do not recalculate the price of the 1H EMA. Initialize with double LastHourEMAvalue=0.0 You would display the CurrentEMAvalue on the chart. The LastHourEMAValue is an internal variable. I hope that this is more helpful, and again I am not a good coder, so there might be mistakes in the above snippet. Cheers, Christos

--- 帖子 #3002 ---
Confluences make for stronger trades, especially when they come from different sources. RN and Pivot confluences tend to give dancers much more confidence in the trade. Same goes for the confluence of unrelated MAs-- for example the 35 M15, and the 62 H1. But if the confluence is something that is virtually guaranteed to occur, simply because of the way the numbers are calculated, then I personally think it should either be discounted or disregarded. And I'm not trying to find an edge that can be proven mathematically. I think it's possible to disprove an edge by testing it. And I think its also possible to gain confidence in an edge with experience. But I'm way too much of skeptic to think that an edge can actually be proven.

--- 帖子 #3007 ---
[quote=Pucter;4212063]Hello, dancers, i think, there are 2 universal emas: ema20 - used on charts starting from 30min and higher, and ema50 - used on charts starting from 5min. If you compare them between timeframes, you wil see that ema20[30] is around equal to ema10[1H] often referenced here, ema200[15] is equal to ema50[H]. [quote] I ma sorry, but the above IS NOT TRUE mathematically! Because of their recursive nature, you cannot say that the X EMA on Y timeframe is the same as 2X EMA on Y/2 timeframe. Their values can be close enough, but the exact formulas to calculate them are different!

Guys i was reading the Trading in the Zone PDF, just wana share with u what i read. 3 IMPORTANT FUNDAMENTALS "there are always constant, never-ending, unknown, hidden variables that are always operating in the market- always The best traders don't try to hide from these unknown variables by pretending they don't exist, nor do they try to intellectualize or rationalize them away through market analysis. Quite the contrary, the best traders take these variables into account, factoring them into every component of their trading regimes. He knows that every trade has an uncertain outcome 2) He predefines his risk 3) He always cuts losses short. 4) Has a systematic way to take profit. Not adhereing to these fundamental principles is the equivalent of committing financial and emotional suicide. -pg 77&amp; 78- Guys i am writing this as a reminder for myself whenever I am trading the Dance trading method, Thanks to Clay we are able to look for setups that repeat day after day , year after year that gives high probability of buy or sell- that is our edge. Having an Edge is not the only component to successful trading, we need to know that there is no certain way that price will go the way we want it imagine trading during a Frankfurt Fakeout or London fakeout and u get what i mean. we already have the 3 fundamental components build into the stop loss rule and the 2 losses in a row per day rule. it's up to us to stick to it. We can't get 100% wins all the time so the rules help us stay Net positive in the long run.

--- 帖子 #3026 ---
THE "UNCERTAINTY" PRINCIPLE If there is such a thing as a secret to the nature of trading, this is it: At the very core of one's ability 1)to trade without fear or overconfidence, 2) perceive what the market is offering from its perspective, 3)stay completely focused in the "now moment opportunity flow," and 4) spontaneously enter the "zone," it is a strong virtually unshakeable belief in an uncertain outcome with an edge in your favor. The best traders have evolved to the point where they believe, without a shred of doubt or internal conflict, that "anything can happen." They don't just suspect that anything can happen or give lip service to the idea. Their belief in uncertainty is so powerful that it actually prevents their minds from associating the "now moment" situation and circumstance with the outcomes of their most recent trades. By preventing this association,they are able to keep their minds free of unrealistic and rigid expectations about how the market will express itself. Instead of generating the kind of unrealistic expectations that more often than not resulting both emotional and financial pain, ( Oh man how many times this happens to me cos of my rigidness ) they have learned to "make themselves available" to take advantage of whatever opportunities the market may offer in any given moment. "Making yourself available" is a perspective from which you understand that the framework from which you are perceiving information is limited relative to what's being offered. A perspective from which you make yourself available takes into consideration both the known and the unknown: For example, you've built a mental framework that allows you to recognize a set of variables in the markets behavior that indicates when an opportunity to buy or sell is present. ( take our Dance method for instance here) This is your edge and something you know. However, what you don't know is exactly how the pattern your variables identify will unfold. With the perspective of making yourself available, you know that your edge places the odds of success in your favor, but, at the same time, you completely accept the fact that you don't know the outcome of any particular trade. By making yourself available, you consciously open yourself up to find out what will happen next; instead of giving way to an automatic mental process that causes you to think you already know. Adopting this perspective leaves your mind free of internal resistance that can prevent you from perceiving whatever opportunity the market is making available from its perspective (its truth). Your mind is open for an exchange of energy. Not only can you learn something about the market that you previously didn't know, but you also set up the mental condition most conducive to entering "the zone." - pg 71 &amp; 72 -

You might want to take a look at Elliot Wave Theory. It can get way too complicated, but basically the idea is that a trend consists of five legs: three surges and two retracements. On the surges you are talking about, the retracements would be pullbacks to the 10EMA. Not saying it's necessarily true, just that it's a similar observation.

First off: Don't worry! I am only a newly graduated newbie myself and I can tell you that although it seems difficult at first, it becomes so easy with time that you can't believe you weren't getting it at the start. In terms of filtering, there are a lot of good things to look for that are covered in both Dance threads. If you haven't read all the original thread and all of this thread then definitely do that as a lot of questions you'll have are covered. Basic important rules: 1. Take the first 10 touch and the first 35/50 touch only. 2. Take a 10 touch only on a two bar retrace. Not one bar, not three bars. 3. Watch out for a 35/50 touch if it is one massive bar that retraces, often times momentum will push it far through. But the main thing is keep practising. You won't believe how much easier it gets with time.

--- 帖子 #3142 ---
something to read over the weekend.. Page 129, the Disciplined Trader by Mark Douglas If our hypothetical trader wants to develop into an effective and consistently successful trader, he will need to engage in some selfimprovement. He will need to understand that the market is always right and that he can profit from that tightness if he doesn't impose a rigid mental structure on its behavior. He needs to release himself from his fear of being wrong so that he can observe the market's behavior from an objective perspective. Otherwise,his fear of being wrong will have the effect of making him wrong. He will also need to establish some definite trading rules to guide his own behavior and learn how to adhere to those rules. If he had been operating out of a definite set of trading rules he would have never let the loss accumulate sufficiently that his pain would take him out of the trade. If, however, he refuses to acknowledge and accept his current state of development by blaming the market for his losses or trying to convince himself that somehow he wasn't responsible for what he ended up with, then he would be indulging himself in illusion. He would be denying who he is and, in effect, cutting himself off from the information he needs to become who he wants to be.

--- 帖子 #3145 ---
I believe that past a certain minimal point, forex markets are fractal. By this, I mean that there does not appear to be any meaningful difference between what works on one time frame and what works in other time frames. I have never seen a book that qualified an indicator, or a tool like Fibs or trendlines, by saying that they only work in certain time frames. Even wave theory asserts that there are sub waves within the legs of its greater waves. Thus, it seems to me that the smaller view is substantially similar to larger views. If people really believe that smaller time frames contain too much "noise", there is an easy way to test this idea. Simply show a bunch of unmarked charts to these people and see if they can distinguish those that came from a noisy time frame as opposed to those which contained more signal. Let them use all the tools they want, so long as they don't know what the underlying data points are. It would be interesting to see if anyone could pass such a test There are a few main differences between time frames: first, there is the impact of the spread and commission. This factor weighs fairly heavily in favor of longer time frames. Second, there is the size of the stop. This one goes in favor of shorter time frames. Then there is the amount of screen time one needs to devote. This one goes in favor of long time frames. Then there is the psychological burden of having a trade open, vs. the psychological strain of hovering over the mouse waiting to close a scalp. This one, I think, depends on the make-up of the individual. Finally, there is the swap. There are certain long term trades that suffer from having to pay interest (Australian trades right now). Right now, I'm leaning towards shorter time frames. Why? Because I'm learning. Learning comes from experience. Experience derives from the number of good trades you make, and there is simply more opportunity to get good trades faster on a short time frame. This speeds up the learning process. That advantage, for me at least, outweighs the extra costs that might be involved in trading shorter time frames.

--- 帖子 #3193 ---
I love constrainments. Reasons- Very reliable and hardly any drawdown. Here are the constrainments I spotted early today. Notice common characteristics- Strong trend indicated by parallel or on top of each other 35/50. Converging 35/50 acceptable but never diverging . All Mas parallel and pointing towards same direction - not one going up another going down. BTW i use this for ALL dance trades. You dont want to be in market when MAs are in a mess. Many small candles that touch the MA. If candles are away from MA don’t count them. Number of candles will be minimum 3 though much larger in smaller time frames. Often price will wick through the constraining MA at least once- don’t panic. In my experience this just confirms the trade. In fact I am skeptical of trade when no candle wick through constraining MA. Look for slightly larger profit here than touch trades. Look for slow movers for constrainment- like AU,UC etc. Fast movers are better for touch trades. Entry and Exit: 1. After you have spotted the constrainment wait for next candle. In next candle when price comes to constraining MA enter. 2. SL- Below/ above wick of the last candle that wicked through constraining MA. OR 10 pips below last candle low 3. Exit- Normal dance exit at S/R area in HTF. OR trail SL with 15M candle. So you could have taken any one trade today morning and achieved target in one trade. Not- GBP chart follows in next post. Had a similar constrainment in EU but i passed it because it never wicked through 10EMA. But was a valid by the rules trade.

--- 帖子 #3197 ---
Very good subject to discuss here. Here is my approach: 1. My focus is the M15 MAs. Trend is defined my the M15 35/50 and the price in relation to that (price above 35/50 then only long). 2. Optimize entry/exit by observing M5 action. 3. If higher TF (H1, H4, Daily) MAs are in front of my trade then I take quick profit quickly. This means that if my M15 signal tells me to go long but 15-20 pips in front of me there is higher TF MA which tells me to go short then I am very careful with this trade or even not take it at all. 4. If higher TF (H1, H4) gives a signal before the M15 does, I take the higher TF signal. In this case, the SLs need to be a little bigger and you need more patience for the trade to develop. If this is an H1, H4 10EMA touch then the trade is quick and the profit big. Daily 10 touch is more tricky because sometimes price will overshoot by 20pips or more before turning around, so I rarely take these. The higher TF 35/50 bounce is even trickier but when I observe the M5 bouncing from an H1 or H4 35/50 area, I wait for the M15 to reject the same area and then I will take a trade. Overall, when learning the method, stay with the M15 signals but be aware of the higher TF MAs. When they agree with your M15 signal (either confluencing or with their direction) then your trade will be very strong. As you start becoming proficient with these, you can start testing 10EMA touch trades from H1 and H4. You don't need much more to be successful, just become an expert with these and your account WILL grow.

Hi guys, I'm back after "laying low" and taking a break from trading for a while. For the past 2 weeks or so, I've been successfully trading the 1 or 2 hours BEFORE the NY market opens (around 5-6:30am Houston time). It seems that during this time, the London market has more often than not already established a nice trend that I can jump in on and ride for an easy 20 or 30 pips. The trends tend to be nicely formed and are usually consistent with the hourly and daily charts making entry decisions pretty easy. However, once the NY market opens, things really get hectic and it's not long before it's difficult to tell which way the market is headed. I end up looking at trends on the 15 min that run counter to the the hourly and daily, trends with very short durations, and trends that are not really trends at all. This makes trading pretty much a random shot in the dark. It's like swimming in a quiet river or stream. Before the NY market opens, the "water" is pretty calm. You can tell which way the current is flowing and even see which way the fish are swimming. It's pretty easy to simply float along in the direction of the trend. But the NY market opening is like a rowdy gang of Americans "crashing" the party and disturbing the prevailing peace and quiet. They start splashing and chasing each other around, kicking and yelling and stirring things up so much that before you know it, the market "waters" are so murky you can't tell which way is up! I know that Clay teaches to only trade during the overlap of the London and NY markets but it seems that the NY market, at least lately, really adds a lot of "static" making it difficult for me to make a buck. Anyway, just an observation. The other major change I've made over the past few months is to simplify my trading. I finally deleted every single chart on my trading platform except the GBPUSD. This is the only pair I follow and is the only pair I trade. Know what? Since I've decided to focus on only one pair, I've begun to "know it" like never before. I'm starting to better see how it moves and how it behaves. It's really improved my trading. Well, this is Friday and since I've already racked up over 50 pips in the major down movements this morning before the NY opened, I'm done for today. Hope every one that follows this thread has a Merry Christmas and a profitable New Year! Hiram

Hello in the simple dance manual there is a check list with a terminology that I don't quite understand. What is a "race back" a "pull back" and "more than 2 bars" please. Thank you Minos

--- 帖子 #3242 ---
Pullback (Dance style-like): http://www.swing-trade-stocks.com/pullbacks.html

--- 帖子 #3243 ---
A pull back is brief reversal of price after it starts trending to some expected level. In real time, you can only anticipate that something will be a pull back, you can't know for sure whether its a pull back or a reversal. In the Dance, the expected areas for pull backs are the MAs and sometimes Round Numbers. A pullback can also be to any other area -- a round number, a fib level, a pivot point, an area of support or resistance. A race back is simply a pull back that happens quickly. "More than two bars" is the dance rule for when a pull back goes on for too long and invalidates an entry. A bar is the same thing as a candle -- it's simply two full time periods on your chart from open to close. If a pull back takes more than two bars to happen, then the trade is no longer a valid dance trade. (Note: this rule originally applied only to the 10EMA touches. The new manual seems to apply it to 35 and 50 touches as well.) As an example, suppose there is a breakout long. Price then starts retreating. It prints two full bearish candles but has not yet hit the 10EMA. Then, on the next candle, it continues south and finally touches the 10. That would be more than two bars, and would invalidate the entry. Hope this helps.

--- 帖子 #3269 ---
Hi Scullmeister, nice to have a MA Bounce Trader here, I would appreciate to read your comments on this thread. Surely many others could explain it better than me, but here is how I see it: we consider "Touch trades" when the price hits an EMA10 (as an example) on a retracement (2 bars on M15) of a previous move of at least 15 pips in a certain direction. Price goes downwards (at least 15 pips for being a correct signal), then it makes a retracement of 2 bars (M15), Touches the EMA10 and start again in the previuos trend direction. I hope it is clear somehow There are anyway several pictures and explanations on the Manual.

--- 帖子 #3283 ---
First, I'm very happy to get my "present" and am planning on spending time today going through it. I do have one comment at the outset. Quite a bit of what happens in the Dance depends upon the steepness of the MAs. With the new version, I see at least 40 degrees for the 14 EMA touches, and 25 degrees for the 35/50 touches. This is a very slippery idea. The steepness of the MA depends first on how you set up your chart. I've attached four different versions of exactly the same chart from MT4. The only differences are the height, the width, and the width of the bars. I have an angle trendline which doesn't change its angle as you move from chart to chart. Just look at how the Yellow MA changes its angle in relation to the fixed trendline from chart to chart. So, what angle is the Yellow MA for dance trading purposes? It's impossible to say. For an individual trader, I think this means that you have to keep your charts consistent. But there is a further problem. MT4 adjusts the vertical scale of the chart to fit recent price movements. This means that where there is less volatility, you will tend to get steeper angles with less pip movements. If someone wants me to show this in examples, I can do that as well. There are ways to normalize this. I think MT4 allows charts with fixed vertical scales. But I think it's more important simply to be aware of this phenomenon, which has more to do with chart set-up than anything else, and to adjust your idea of steepness according to the charts that you use.

--- 帖子 #3284 ---
Indeed. Which is why I don't have auto scaling on my MT4 while all my charts have a fixed price scale (50p for M1, 100p for M5, 150p for M15, 200p for H1). This way you develop a "feeling" for how steep an MA is.

--- 帖子 #3290 ---
Here is a write up that i posted in another thread about discussion on "disadvantage" that retail traders face against BIG guys. Hope it helps someone. I find a lot of people confusing market makers with BIG guys. Here is a write up that will help. In forex market there are basically two types of participants. Market makers and traders (market takers) 1. Market maker is someone who gives a two-way price to his customer. Like our brokers who continuously quote two way prices to us. Say GU is quoted as 1.5980 and 1.5982. Broker is willing to buy GU at 1,5980 and sell GU at 1.5982. How do they make money? They hope that given large number of customers, someone will buy GU (at 1.5982) and someone will sell GU (at 1.5980) at same time. They simply hope to pocket the spread. Of course this depends on having large number of customers. Otherwise they will have a position opposite to clients. Suppose someone sells at 1.5980 but no one buys at 1.5982. So they have a long position now. They have several options in this case. A. They can hold the position if they believe GU will go up. – Very unlikely. Most of market makers have strict rules against taking views/holding positions. B they can hold the position for short time and hope someone buys from them in future. Note that even if price moves against them by spread to 1.5978 and 1.5980 they can still exit at cost if buyer comes and buys at 1.5980. C. However, in most of the cases they will simply go ahead and sell to “their” broker (most likely some bank). They will normally get narrow spread of say 1.59805 and 1.59815. So they still make 0.5 pip. So spread is the fodder of market makers. Naturally. Larger customer base means more income for them. So a big guy simply means the one with most customers in market maker sense. They DONT take positions and DONT influence prices. 2. Trader is market taker. Like us he takes a position in market. HE buys/ sells from his market maker (Broker). Here only benefit one can have is a good view because we are paying the spread. So market must move in our favor by more than spread before we can hope to make any money. What does BIG guy means in this sense? Big guy is one who simply takes large position sizes. Does he have any advantage over retail traders? NO. In fact he has huge disadvantages because of large positions. Because of his large positions he will most likely have to pay higher spread than retailers. Sometimes his own selling will bring price down and he will have to sell successive lots a lower and lower price. He simply can’t sell at exact level like us. His cost of trading is huge. So he can’t play for small moves. He is forced to take fundamental or at least slightly long-term view. He can’t capture small moves. He can’t even reverse his position quickly. Often, reversals will mean huge spread loss even if market doesn’t move at all. So get this right- only market makers have certain advantage. But they are not active players who influence prices. BIG traders are those who drive markets and they are at huge disadvantage from us. Imagine paying 30-40 of pips in spread and trying to make money! No wonder very few “BIG” trading guys have survived this market for long. I don’t know any firm trading forex and making Consistent money. So don’t let anyone fool you with talk of big guys and disadvantages of retail traders. Don’t let negativity come in. Analyze your charts and trade. EDIT: These big guys are basically hedge funds, trading desks of big banks etc. Sometimes they take positions in billions and hold it for years altogether. I Dont know of any big guy bothering about retailers 5-10 pips. And i PITY them instead of being AFRAID of them- Imagine against how much disadvantage these poor chaps are trading. Feel sorry for them. If anyone is still not convinced, i just had a little chat with a BIG guy few days back. Minimum position they have ever taken- 250 Millions. View- Betting on short euro, short dollar, long commodities for next FIVE years. Are they interested in my 20-30 pip "scalping"? hell NO!

--- 帖子 #3292 ---
I'm reading The New Market Wizards now. The first interview in the book is with a guy who was the head currency trader for Solomon Bros for several years. The guy said that at most banks, the traders either break even or lose money on their speculative trading. They make their money in one of two ways: first off the spread. Second, if they get a big order, say for a couple of billion dollars, they will put in an order of a couple of hundred thousand for the bank before they start putting in the client's order. The client's order pushes the market in their favor, and then they get out of their position when the client's order has been filled. This kind of insider trading is legal in forex, and the bank can make a couple of million in a short period when it does this. (And of course, the reverse will happen if the client tries to pull a position quickly.) People often think that the big boys can make a ton simply by their ability to push the market around. By putting on a position, they actually move the market in their direction. What this fails to take into account is how they will then get out of the position. It's not clear that they can do that without pushing the market the other way.

--- 帖子 #3350 ---
Just for Fun (?). These are the Dance Emas (+ the EMA62 and the SMA200) applied on Renko bars of 5 pips each... Candles do not follow the time (M5, M15...) but only the movement of the price. They do not close at a certain time, but only when the pre-defined price move (in this case 5pips), has been done. Could take a few seconds or one hour, it doesn't matter. I will not add any comment. Think what you want I surely do not need to "circle" or "arrow" the entry points. And surely I am NOT suggesting to trade using them. Just a "Picasso" image of our daily charts to be observed.

I'm going to disagree respectfully with the idea that the "scooping up" of the 10 EMA invalidates a 35/50 bounce trade. I'm attaching a screenshot of Triple A+ trades from the manual. Take a look at how many of the 35/50 bounces have a 10 EMA that is scooped up. Also think about it: if the 10 EMA was still so steep as price hit the 50, that would mean that a 50 bounce trade would almost always come only after a failed 10 EMA touch opportunity. That's not what I've seen here.

--- 帖子 #3358 ---
Hello... I think we are talking about "scooped up" in different sense. Simple bending of 10EMA is inevitable when price hits 35/50. I think it's mathematically impossible to have 10EMA pointing down when price touches 35//50. I dont call that scooped up. I dont know if its correct as per manual, but my "scooped up" bars always show trend reversal and 35/50 bounces are likely to be broken after such bars. Unfortunately i cant post charts but here is a doc on my dance trades. - http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...29#post4164729 Look for contra trend bars there. Hope that clears things for everyone.

--- 帖子 #3369 ---
The Dance doesn't use any indicators other than MAs. Some people will also add pivot lines, and maybe Fib retracements, but they aren't a part of the original strategy, and Clay encourages people to keep it simple. As for direction, the rule is simple. Always trade with the trend of the moment. The Dance, on M15 charts, defines the trend by the relation of price to the 35 and 50. If price is above both the 35 and 50, then you look for longs. If below, you look for shorts.

--- 帖子 #3399 ---
I've been thinking quite a bit about the trailing stop idea. It seems to me, at least in a trade like this one, that there is a simpler way to skin the cat. The way this trade has been going, the next logical trade to occur is a 10EMA touch trade. We know where the 10 EMA touch will be, and we also know where we would place a stop on that touch. So why not simply move the stop to that point, instead of using a trailing stop on a bar by bar basis. Sometimes this approach will give you a tighter stop than the trailing approach, but there are other times where it will give a wider stop -- especially after the first bar of a two bar pullback to the 10. The big attraction to this approach is that it gives a logical approach to exiting the trade, and it is one that is based on dance rules. Similarly, when the 10EMA has turned so that a new trade would be "scooped up" and thus invalid, it would also be time to get out of the trade. I'd appreciate any thoughts/criticisms anyone has of this approach. I'm thinking of trying it out with split lots.

I have been struggling with touch trades primarily because I just don’t find “perfect” as per rules setups. Those which I do find tend to fail too often by my taste. Am certainly doing something wrong. Will keep working on it on simulator till I perfect it. Any help will be appreciated. But I have been doing pretty well with constrainments. However, my worry was constant waiting- waiting for a containment to appear then waiting for price to shoot in my direction- often price will remain constained for hours altogether before breakout. Therefore recently I have started milking containments themselves instead of waiting for a breakout. Maybe it will help someone. Find a nice constrainment. Watch out for them in HTF- 1H and even 4H in slow movers like AUD, CAD, JOY CHF etc. During slow hours don’t give up when you don’t find touch trades. There might be a constrainment forming somewhere. Look for nice parallel Mas, all pointing in same direction. One going up one going down doesn’t work very well. Then watch HTF for any obstruction. Say if you find 1H constrained check out 4H and 1D to see if there is any serious obstruction. Remember that only very serious obstructions will hold against a constrainment. Most often constrainment is a warning that HTF obstructions are going to be broken. Optimize your entry. For shorts - See what highs the constrained candles are making- it might be constraining MA or a RN or just 5-6 pips above the MA. Then enter double your normal lot at this identified high. You can enter double lot because of extremely small SL needed in constrainments – so the risk is same as touch trades. Generally candles would be making lower highs for short- enter right near the top with previous high plus 2 pips as SL. For longs do reverse. Now when your trades comes in +15 to 20 pips depending on previous candles size book half of your position. Let half (your normal lot) run. Price will go to constraining MA multiple times- enter another lot there. Book one lot again in +15-20. Keep repeating. Let one lot run for a big profit when breakout happens. Advantage of this strategy is even if the constrainment fails you have already milked it enough. If constrainment works then you are the king of pips! Here are live examples attached. About charts: Both are today’s charts. USDCAD 1H and USDCHF 4H. I traded CAD and was bored enough of milking it so called it a day before formation takes its natural course- SL or TP on last lot. I passed CHF because it was on 4H requiring larger SL and therefore smaller position. Also there was trouble in daily. However some fine tuning with 15M and it wasn’t tough to trade. I passed it only because I saw better opportunity in cad. If there was no other constrainment I wouldn’t have hesitated to milk CHF. Note: Todays chart was not "perfect" constrainment but it worked for me. I will post as i see perfect setups. Also in past i have posted charts of what's perfect constrainment according to me. EDIT: 15-20 pips is for 15M. In 1H 4H reward are much higher- usually 30-40 pips in slow movers and in EU or GBP it could be even more. --- 帖子 #3411 ---
This is great stuff. Thanks for posting it. There's another way to approach the positioning here that might give much more profit: 1) Start with two lots like you say. SL is say 7 pips. 2) At +15 you sell one lot just as you do. 3) Then when it comes back to restraining you buy one lot. So now you are at +1 on the two positions even if you get stopped out. 4) Round two at +15, you sell one lot. Again no difference. But at 5) Instead of buying one lot and booking the 8 pips profit, you now buy two lots and only book +1 profit. That means at this point you are carrying three lots, at no risk. If you get stopped out, you will book at least 2 pips (actually more since you can move the stop loss on the original trade with each bounce as the constraining MA moves in your favor.) 6) Now as price moves in your favor, you have two lots to run with the constrainment instead of one. Each time price comes back to the constraining MA, you get an opportunity to add another lot to run with the trade if it breaks. Lets say that on a short, you got three returns to the constraining MA, and then a break that you would cash for 50 pips. In your method, you would net 95 pips. By adding lots, you would instead net 215 pips. Of course, you might just break even, where in your method, a break even would still have netted you 16 pips or so. For me, this is all academic, since I have at least as much trouble finding constrainments as you have with touch trades. But I thought I would throw the idea out there. And of course, it doesn't have to be an all or nothing proposition. You could always book some profit, and pyramid your position with the rest of your unrealized gain.
