--- 帖子 #4172 ---
G'day Duffy, I strongly suggest that you consider fixing the scale of the charts. I know Kostas does this, and I have been doing it since just after I started trading forex. A very big part of this strategy is that the MAs have to be at a "significant angle" to show trend strength and market momentum. So, it is vital that we do not get fooled by charts which are showing deceptive information. If you allow the charts to be dynamic, small moves look more significant than they are during sideways and choppy markets, and what looks to be a good angle becomes flat once price makes a move. For example: Here is this morning's chart of Cable using dynamic scale. The red trendline is a "Trend by angle" set to 45 degrees. The blue one is just a normal trendline running paralell. Notice how the price is also showing pretty large bars... looks very volatile as with dynamic scale, the it is drawn so that the bars fill the screen. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Now look what happens when price drops by a around 60 pips, which is a pretty average move for Cable, which typically moves more than 100 pips when it moves, so this is not a "big move", but a less than average move for this pair. Now the "Trend by angle" is still at 45 degrees, but trendline is at less than 30 degrees. What looked like a very volatile whipsaw is now looking more like what it really was, a fairly narrow piece of sideways price action. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Now let's look at that same piece of chart with the vertical scale fixed to a set value of 10 pips per label on the price axis (This is my preferred scale for 15 minute dance charts). I will also show how this is done for those who do not know, but that will be in the another post, as there is a limit to the number of attachments per post. So, here is the first chart again but with the scale fixed and a 45 degree "Trend by angle" and normal trendline drawn parallel to it. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Now, after the move down.... the flat bit still looks flat, the move looks moderate a moderate size. Everything looks as it really is ,..... every time,.... all the time! Attached Image (click to enlarge) Here is a shot of my chart showing the same period as yours. My MAs are flat, the price looks sideways, and on the M15, Dance strategy would say this is virtually a "no trade day" as the 35/50 MAs are too flat! You will also see that my 35/50 MAs are thin lines. I use my modified MAs for these, and once they have reached a "decent" angle, they get thicker, making it very easy to recognize when the band has arrived and it's time to start dancing. Attached Image (click to enlarge) I stayed out and watched from the sidelines for this reason, and, in my opinion, this is one of the greatest features of the Dance..... it keeps you out of the market when it is not good to trade, and knowing when NOT to trade is far more important that knowing entries and exits!

--- 帖子 #4173 ---
If you want to fix the scale on your charts, here is how it is done, but first, here's a dramatic example of why you'd want to.... Here are two M15 charts showing the same period for the USDCAD. The ONLY difference is that the one on the left has dynamic scaling and the one on the right has the scale fixed to 10 pips per price label. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Step 1. Fix the scale. First, bring up the chart properties by either: clicking on the chart and pressing the F8 key at the top of your keyboard. OR Alternatively, you can right click on an empty spot on the chart and choose the "Properties" at the bottom of the popup menu. In the chart's Properties popup, choose the "Common" tab at the top and click the "Scale fix" box to put a tick in it. Attached Image Click OK, and it is now fixed. Step 2. Adjusting the scale to size and moving the chart. Instructions are below the picture. Attached Image (click to enlarge) Adjusting the scale. Now you have to adjust the scale to suit, by clicking on the price scale, hold down the mouse button and drag it up and down and the scale will change. Release the mouse button and it will stay there. Note that it can be a bit fiddly to get it exact, but you just have to be very slow with the mouse while "fine tuning" and you can get it to what you want. Careful! It is not possible to "lock" this so it is important that you don't accidentally click on the scale while working, as it will change it. Moving the Chart up and down. Fixed charts do not "follow price" so when the price moves higher or lower, you have to drag your chart manually by clicking on an empty space in the chart window and dragging it up or down. That's it! Now 10 pips always looks like 10 pips, flat always looks flat, and if it looks like it is moving then it is actually moving! Enjoy working with charts that don't tell lies!

--- 帖子 #4174 ---
Bigtent: I think this is great advice, and you have explained everything well (better than I did when I was making the same point awhile back). I do use fixed scales for charts H1 and below. For the daily and H4 charts, I still use a floating scale, but that's because I don't ever make "steepness" decisions off of them. Per Kostas' example, I use 50 pips for M1, 100 for M5, 150 for M15 and 200 for H1. (I've recently thought that 100 for the M5 may be too much. It tends to make moves look smaller than they appear on my M15 chart.) My comment about measuring steepness probably led you to believe otherwise. Steepness depends on a bunch of things that don't have to do with price. Even fixing the scale to 100 doesn't mean that the steepness on my chart will be the same as it is with someone else using 100 pips fixed. It also depends on the vertical size of the window, and the width of the bars you are using. The important thing, I think, is remaining consistent on your own charts and getting to know them. And for this, I think using a fixed scale is a pretty basic requirement. One final thing: sometimes it may look like my posted charts are a bit inconsistent in scale. That's because I sometimes blow up smaller pictures, or contract down images that look very large to me from the start. On my screen, a ten pip move on the M15 always looks the same.

--- 帖子 #4179 ---
When I get the same opportunity on both and if it is an AAA trade I will take the GU for faster (and bigger) profit. But it is very rare to get the same quality trade on both. What happens usually is that a AAA trade (e.g. a strong move and a 2 bar retrace to the 10, a 35/50 that are on top of each other, strong confluence etc.) appears only on one of them. The same trade may appear later on the other but not always with the same elements (i.e. a confluence will scream on one of them but it will not be as strong on the other). You are correct about EU changing a bit. Actually, the change is in a good way. We now have a more volatile pair but which is more predictable (i.e. it covers more pip distance in the day but still respects the usual CHOROS points). In addition, it seems to respect price action formations in our TFs more than GU. On GU you get a lot more fake formations (for example, I trust an EU M5 bounce formation at the M15 35/50 area more than GU).

The problem is you are attached to the money you are trading and you want more of it, you have to get to the place where you literally you don't care about wins or losses. This is not say go out and become reckless or take dumb trades. With that said I still take a dumb trade at least once a week, but it does not bother me and I don't beat myself up over it. Until you get to this point you are going to struggle, setting arbitrary rules like quiting after x losses may help in the short term but the time you quit and then see a 100 pip run up on an a+ setup you will more than likely be back to your old ways.

--- 帖子 #4213 ---
I don't believe that you can get away from emotion, as it is fundamental to your being, you can only control it more than it controls you, but even then, those emotions are still there. If you discipline yourself, that comes from the emotional need to succeed, as well as the emotion of fear of letting other emotions adversely affect your decisions. It's not about being emotionless, because that is impossible for healthy human beings. Rather, it is about understanding which emotions are going to help you and which emotions will hinder you, and using the "good" emotions to suppress and control the "bad" emotions (which are still there), and that is achievable.

--- 帖子 #4214 ---
You can't be emotionless, that's for sure. But I think that's the ideal as far as trading is concerned. To utilize your pattern-recognizing abilities without permitting other factors to interfere. We can never switch off our emotions while trading, but we can try to minimize them as much as possible. What I'm talking about is not something that can't be done. Of course some emotion, some feeling, some desire is the driving force behind all this. But the top professionals in every field do not allow their feelings to take control when they perform their tasks, much more when those tasks are primarily mental. I can't imagine a surgeon operating successfully under strong emotional influence, at least not when the operation is a difficult one. I can't imagine a chess master doing well while being outraged. And so on. I don't think "discipline" and "will power" are especially effective when it comes to this. Probably one's self-image is more important. Instead of trying to discipline yourself, you should focus on trying to change the way you view yourself. Then the correct actions come natural.

--- 帖子 #4215 ---
Discipline is precisely what you are describing. Discipline is control, to be disciplined is to follow what you have learned or planned, and not allow things to distract you from that, and that includes emotions. Will power is just another term to describe the strength of consciousness that is required to achieve discipline. The ultimate in discipline is to appear to act autonomously, without the need to ponder on the decision. One other thing, things such as trader's discretion, "gut feelings", discretion, and "more art than science", all things that are all about feeling more than rational thought, which means they are actually emotional, but the difference is that they are the applications of the "good" emotions. PS: I still think "Trader Spock" would be great at this game!

OK. For those that keep asking me in PMs what are those yellow and magenta lines: READ THE THREAD before asking something that has been discussed.... Anyway, in the beginning of my day, I mark the H4 highs/lows with yellow lines as the price tends to react there. Lately, I mark the Daily high/lows with magenta to differentiate from the H4. I do this only on my main chart, i.e. M15. When there is confluence of these lines with pivots, RN, MAs then I consider them as very strong CHOROS points of interest.

--- 帖子 #4246 ---
Guys, Before everybody starts finding new TFs and new MAs that work, keep this in mind: 1. There are probably many MAs that price reacts to. If you start expecting the price to bounce from everywhere it will get very confusing. 2. If you thing you have discovered an MA that price respects more than the ones we use, then put it in your charts, observe it for a few weeks, trade it for a few weeks and if it still looks good post it here for further discussion. 3. Sometimes specially for beginners it may be best to concentrate on just one MA and one TF 4. Most important TFs and MAs are the most common ones which means that they are the ones that most people use, which is why price reacts there, most of the time. 5. KISS (no, no, not that KISS but K eep I t S imple S tupid )

--- 帖子 #4259 ---
Four good trades, and one so-so, today, and I missed them all. 1) Constrainment. This constrainment, with a couple of small hiccups, lasted for 20 bars on the M15. It’s less well formed on the H1 but goes for 5 or 6 bars. I saw this one when it was about four bars in. I had already been burned on one off hour trade in the afternoon. So I thought “I wonder if Survivor would take this now.” But instead of watching, I was away from the computer and then went to bed. By the 15th bar, this trade is simply crying out that it needs to be traded. Good for 30-40 pips, plus whatever Survivor milked from the lead up bars. The question I have here is which bar would you first enter on? And also, if you milked it, how many pips would you be looking to take per round? 2) 10 Touch. Winner, BE or Loser. This is almost a perfect 10 Touch trade.. Steep MA, two bar retrace, little resistance ahead, and a confluence with an RN. If you took this at the touch with a 9 pip stop, as Clay recommends, it’s a loser by less than a pip. With a bigger stop, and a 15 TP, its an easy winner. But if you shot for more than 15 pips, it should come back and break even on the re-test of the RN. That’s how I see it by the rules. And this is where I am puzzled. Kostas played basically the same trade and held it past the RN retest, for big gains. Will upped his bet when it came down to the RN, and did really well on it. Bigtent took the RN as a separate trade, got stopped on the touch trade, but made out on the RN trade. The differences in approach here puzzle me. I don’t know what I would have done if I had been up. My guess is that I would have played it according to Clay’s rules, got taken out by half a pip, and then stare at the forum in amazement at other people’s success. By the way, I do have an opinion about the news. I think its a very bad idea to enter into trades right when news breaks, and during the immediate shifts that follow the breaking news. But, if you are already in a dance trade, and the news is coming up, I don’t see any reason to get out of the trade. Kostas has observed that the news seems to respect the Dance. I don’t know if that’s true or not. But the news does seem to amplify whatever is happening. So, if you are in a Dance trade already and the news breaks, you might get a really big swing. If it goes in your favor, they you will probably hit a much bigger profit than usual (and this will cause you to remember how well the Dance fits with the news). But if the trade turns against you, you will simply hit your stop, with maybe a slight bit of slippage. Compared to the potential upside, I think the slippage risk is pretty small. So, all in all, I think sticking with a Dance position when news is about to break is a good bet. 3) 10 Touch. The MAs are steep, and its a one bar retrace. I think its definitely a by the rules trade. But I passed on it anyway. The upspike 3.5 hours earlier basically respected this same level, and the Daily R2 and a Round number are just above this touch. On top of that, the two bars before the pullback are a doji/pin followed by a hanging man. These things combined made this a no trade for me. (Here, my question is when, if ever, I should start seeing these signs as a signal on its own?) 4) 35 Bounce. This is a bad trade that was good for 30 pips. I saw this trade coming, and knew I would be tempted to take it against my better judgment. So instead, I went back to sleep and called it a day. The MAs are diverging, and there was almost a touch of these MAs a few hours back. In this instance, I would first want to pass on the trade. Then, I would be tempted to wait for a touch of the 50, instead of taking the trade off the 35. Here, I would want that because of the potential confluence with the Daily R1. In hindsight, I should have stayed up and waited for confirmation for this trade on the M5. There was a nice engulfing candle there that provided a decent entry signal. 5) 50 Bounce. No trade. The MAs are way too far apart now, and the 50 is actually pointing the wrong direction. Often, after a first bounce off the 35, you will get another Bounce from the 50 on the next go round. But this one is no set-up at all. The rest of these are after London close, so are not by the rules. 6) 50 Bounce / 10 Touch. This is an almost ideal break of the MAs followed by a retrace to the 50 in confluence with the 10. The break is only 16-17 pips, which is a bit small. The bounce itself is at the conjunction of the 50 and the 10, and the Daily R1 is also now supplying some resistance. Good for 25-35 pips. 7) Higher Time Frame Confluence. This is not strictly a dance trade, but it definitely follows dance principles. There’s a confluence here of a strong S/R line, the M15 200, the H1 35, and the H4 10 and 35. (The Daily 5 is also right in the neighborhood, but not as close as the others.) If not taken as a touch, it would be easy to get in after the hammer on the H1 or even on the H4. 8) 10 Touch. This trade breaks the two bar rule, but I don’t think thats the reason not to take it. Rather, all the confluence that is in favor of taking trade 7 also says to pass on this one. 9) 35 Bounce. I have mixed opinions on this trade. It’s off hours, and the higher time frames are now all bullish, so that counsels against taking the trade. The 35 is still pretty steep, but the 50 is almost dead flat. On the plus side, the Daily R1 is supporting the trade. As a touch trade, its probably a loser, unless you moved to break even or took profit very fast. Here, if you waited for confirmation on the M5, you might get into the trade after a near pin, followed by a bearish engulfing candle. And that would lead to a pure loser. Charts in order are M15, H1, H4 and M5.

I mentioned in my summary about being burned on an off hours trade yesterday, so I thought I should probably post it. Here's what I wrote in my journal: I entered this trade because it looked like a perfect confluence of the H1 62, 50, 50SMA, and 35. It was off hours, and that was a bit of a danger sign. But all the MAs are pretty steep and they are right on top of each other. I entered with a limit order as a touch trade. I initially lefth the stop right where you can see it, just above the Daily Pivot. I planned on taking out half profit at 15 pips, and letting the other half maybe run back to the Daily S1. The trade never went anywhere in my favor. It got to +3 briefly twice. Then it spent 15 mins hovering between +3 and -1.5. and then it took off in the wrong direction. If I had held to my stop, it would have missed my stop by less than a pip. But the stop was big, and I had no confidence at that point (which may have been my failing on this trade). Also, I had a yoga class to go to, and couldn’t stay to manage the trade for much longer -- which is even a lamer reason for getting out when I did. Anyway, I closed manually at about -15.7 pips ( I tried to get out at 15, but there was movement between my impulse and the actual click). Immediately afterward, price fell back in my favor, and even got to +11 pips. In the end, it should either have been a 9 pip loss, or a break even trade. I managed to get the worst of both possibilities. Actually, what I should have done is wait for a Kostas style confirmation on the M5. If I had done that, I might actually have had a winning trade on this one. So in the future, when going for a higher time frame trade, it will be best not to take the trade off the touch on the higher time frame. Instead, wait for confirming price action on a lower time frame. The moves tend to be big enough that the lost pips won’t be that big a deal. Here’s what ideally should have happened. First chart is H1 of the entry. Second chart is M5 showing what I think I should have done. Third chart is M15 showing the actual exit.

Sorry for missing that one. About off hour: I take well formed constrainments in off hours. I believe that by nature constrainments are likely to be formed better during slow hours.Active fast markets will rarely give well formed constarinments. That's the reason i watch for them BEFORE major market open. Taking the trade: " By the 15th bar, this trade is simply crying out that it needs to be traded. " That's when you should go for the kill. After enough screen times some setups BEG and cry to be traded- Please trade me please! Milking- I am very careful with milking fast movers. They rarely get constrained long enough and with large enough candles. Here also i see very small candles. Of course initially it was possible to milk it for few pips but at those candles i wasn't sure if it's a good constrainment. By the time i was sure candles were too small. In any case i am not very keen on milking fast movers. Here is how i actually traded it. Not how i would have traded. Of course, many improvements are possible in hindsight. Also i have just made up the chart with whatever i remember. Numbers may not be precise. But thats roughly how i actually traded it. Hope that helps

1) 10 Touch, 50 Bounce. This is one of those 35/50 cross and retest trades. For two bars, price made a clear break of the 50, with the 10 at a fairly steep angle on the 10. It comes back for a retrace to a confluence of the 10, 50 and the Daily Pivot. Good for 25, 50, 70 or 80 pips depending on where you put your take profit. 2) 10 Touch. Loser, but no trade. First touch and steep MA, but there is the Weekly Pivot, a Round Number, and an S/R area just below acting as support. On top of that it takes 5 bars from the low to hit the 10. So, I see it as no trade. If you took this at the projected touch, it would hit a stop loss of up to 14 pips, so it’s probably a loser. With a bigger stop, you might be able to squeeze 15 pips or get a break even on it. 3) 50 Touch. First touch. MAs are steep and parallel, but pretty widely separated. It also has confluence with H1 35. As a touch trade, this one works quite well. Fine tuning the entry on the 5 only seems to confuse things here. The best entry I see there gives up 15 pips, and calls for a pretty wide stop. Still, I think this is a good trade. Getting out of the trade, however, is tricky. It easily gets 15 pips. But it could also then lead to a break even if you held on to all or some of the trade. If you could avoid break even, this trade could go for 40-50 pips. 4) 10 Touch (and non-Dance Trade). I drew two arrows here. The top one highlights the 10 Touch, which I think is a no trade. It suffers the same problems as trade 1, but at this point the Round Number and S/R line have already acted as support. To top it off, price tested the S/R line with a pin bar (almost a hammer). The bottom arrow shows the trade I took today. I decided as price was pulling back from the S/R line that I would pass on any 10 Touch Trade. And then also decided I would enter long if the bar closed as a pin with some bullish momentum. I got in at the weekly pivot. Then I waited for a half hour before price finally took off and hit the 10. The 10 trade turned out to be even worse than it looked in advance. I took off half the trade at +18. The next big Dance decision came in deciding whether to reverse position at trade 5: 5) 35/50 Bounce. The MAs are steep, but have already started to diverge. There is also confluence with the 200. On its own terms, I might have tried this trade as a scalp. And a scalp would have been good for up to 14 pips, or would have given a Break Even. Since I was already in a risk free trade, the question was whether to chance the reverse or hold onto the trade. I decided that the diverging MAs were bad enough not to take the trade on a reversal, and that I would wait through any short bounce and try for my take profit at the Round Number above. It twice bounced back 14 pips before finally breaking through the 50. If I had not taken off half my position, I would definitely have exited somewhere in here, probably at the worst possible point. It broke through to the Round Number, and I met my daily target with the one trade. 5a) On H1 Chart. Right after the Round Number, it hit a triple top on the H1, again right near the 35. It is also testing the M15 100 on that bar. If I were still trading, I would have been sorely tempted to take this trade. And it turned out to be a great trade, worth 100 or more pips. 6) 10 Touch “almost”. This is the only decent 10 Touch trade of the day, and it doesn’t quite make the touch. The Daily S2 is in the way, but is far enough away to get at least a break even. Good for up to 27 pips, if you could find an entry. (This might be the type of situation where it’s best to enter on the close of bar. But I’m just no good at all at figuring out these near touches.) 7) 10 Touch. This is the first true touch after a long drop. In this case, I’m beginning to think that one should count an obvious near touch as a first touch, even when the touch doesn’t actually happen. Or at least take it into consideration. Here, the touch comes 8 bars after the low. Price has made progressively higher lows. I think this is a bad trade and should be passed.

We talked about it in the past. If the confluence of our normal signs MAs, RN, Pivots contains trendlines it makes it even stronger. But trendlines are so subjective that can confuse the decision making process. I had very nice trades where there was such a confluence, the price broke the trendline (fake move) and then continued in the right CHOROS direction. So careful with the trendlines.

--- 帖子 #4310 ---
1) 10 Touch. Winner or BE. This trade comes before London/Frankfurt open, so is not strictly by the rules. The MA is nice and steep. The touch comes and retraces to form a dragonfly doji, moving 9 pips in the trade's favor, before giving it back to a second touch. I think lots of dancers would either take a break even on the move back to the 10, or get out with a small profit. I've seen any number of posts where people say that the bounce happens, and then if the trade starts moving against you, it doesn't often come back. And I think that may be true. Here's a case, however, where it comes back strongly. Holding on would give you 30 pips at the Weekly Pivot or 44 at the Round Number. 2) 10 Touch. Loser. I had just finished watching the Oscars (Tivo recording) and was at the computer when this set-up happened. It looked much better in real time than it down on this chart. It's a second touch, and the top was at a Round Number, together with an S/R line. But the price action at the top wasn't terribly bearish, and the retrace to the 10 was a perfect two bars, and the 10 was at a near perfect confluence with the 200. I put on a limit order, and missed getting into the trade by 3/10ths of a pip. There was an immediate bounce of over 7 pips, and I left the computer to go to bed. It turns out I should be happy that the limit didn't get hit. Seven pips was about as far as it got, before it blew through everything. (I think the lesson here is just not to take these trades when they need to break through significant support/resistance, or at least be sure that that S/R is far enough away.) 3) 35 Bounce. This is a very interesting situation. The 35 and 50 are maybe slightly diverging, but they are also getting pretty steep. The Round Number is between them, and the Daily Pivot just underneath, in confluence with the 100. The H4 150 (an EOHater MA) is just six pips underneath the bottom that forms here. How to trade this? Taking the bounce off the 35 would be a by the rules Dance trade, and it would work out well. But I don't think many people would take this as a straight dance trade. If you waited for a good rejection candle on the M5 chart, you would find one. It would eat up 15 pips before you got into the trade. You would then get 12 pips in your favor before the trade dipped back again to BE. And then after kicking you out, the rocket ship would take off. EOHater treated this as a cross and reverse. Survivor has talked about that on the H1 chart. This one works on the H1 chart as well. When after a decent trend in one direction, a candle retraces and crosses both the 35 and 50, and then closes near the MAs with a short or no wick, EOHaters says to fade the retracement. Here, the bar in question does exactly that. It also coincides with a one hour candle that crossed the 35 50 and 62. And on top of that, the close of the bar is within two pips of a Fib retracement from Friday's low. That's alot of non-Dance stuff. But EO's cross and reverse is very, very close to the Dance bounce trades. With all of the above, there should be some area where a person could get in near the bottom of this move. (Assuming you weren't lazy and asleep, like me.) The harder question is how to stay in the trade. It would be really tempting to close out with the consolidation around the Daily R1. Did anyone actually catch this move? 4) 10 Touch. This is the first touch after the long move. The Weekly R1 got tested 5 times leading up to this touch, and that's not a good sign. On the other hand, during the same time there were generally higher lows. All in all, I think this is a good trade. In keeping with the suggestion of taking price action into account, I've marked a tweezer bottom 5-6 bars before the touch. That area would be my stop for this trade, and if price closed below it, I would strongly considering reversing the trade. Instead, after several bars, this trade would finally yield 15-30 pips. 5) 10 Touch Constrainment. Instead of bouncing off the Weekly R1, price has not started to bounce off the Round Number. This doesn't look like that good a trade to me, but its worth noting that 5 bars out of 6 have their lows defined by the 10. I would be interested in hearing whether Survivor thinks there is a constrainment trade in here.

--- 帖子 #4311 ---
This is a very good point. Kostas uses price action to "fine tune" entries on lower time frames. That's not part of Clay's Dance, but definitely has become a core aspect of Choros. We haven't had too much discussion on exactly what constitutes a good rejection on the lower time frame, and, as with most things, I would love to hear anything Kostas has to say on the matter. Clay talked about two other kinds of price action with the dance. First, in the thread, he constantly reminded people to "look to the left". Here, the idea was mostly to look for trades that came in areas where there was confirming support or resistance. Second, he would also sometimes take trades that were not strictly by the rules because of the price action. The one that comes immediately to mind is double tops or double bottoms where the tops or bottoms were EXACTLY the same.

If you held a 15 pips stop, you might make some money, but with Clay's nine pip stop, its a loser. 2) 50 Bounce. Break Even. I think the MAs are steep enough going into this bar. This is the bar where they begin to get really flat. And they were also converging going into this bar. The retrace to the MAs from the top is very long, but this bar is a big retrace, so its not the series of small bars Clay warned against. It's also definitely not a nice two bar retrace. There is a 13 pip drawdown, followed by an 11 pip upswing. You might get a few pips out of this trade by exiting quickly, but its probably break even. 3) 10 Touch/50 Bounce. This is a retest of the 50 and the 10 after price has crossed the MAs. I tried to get into this trade on the previous bar, where the touch did not happen. My limit order got missed by half a pip. When that bar formed a dragonfly doji, only two bars after the very bullish pin doji, I decided that I would not take the touch on the next bar (the bar marked for this trade). My reasoning was that this would now be the fourth bar in the retrace, there was a good support level below the trade that had held up three times already, and the near touch on the last bar would make the real touch here be sort of like a second touch. I think my reasoning was pretty good, despite the fact that it turned out to be wrong. I'd be happy to hear if someone disagrees. Good for 15 pips. 4) 10 Touch. Loser. This is one of those trades that is good "by the rules" but would be a no trade if you look at price action. First, look to the left: the high here is 1/10th of a pip off the last swing high, almost a perfect double top. The first two bars forming this high are within a half pip of each other. The first has a long top wick. The second is a dragonfly doji, and the third is a long legged doji. Combined these show a possible reversal, combined with extreme weakness and indecision. Now, combine these things with the top bar coming exactly at London close (price tends to revers at London close), and I think there's more than enough reason not to take this trade. If anything, I think there might be good enough reason above to enter the trade short. 5) Price action only. This part is strictly not dance. Look at my purple S/R line. This is a weekly S/R line that I put on the chart probably 4-5 weeks ago. Today, it catches the bottom on five distinct moves. On the third of these, I contemplated taking the trade, but I was also still thinking about taking the touch trade that I saw coming after the move up. It's not my thread, so I don't know whether it is "too far from the path" or not, but Kostas incorporates other things than the Dance into Choros, and really, neither are "systems" but strategies. It provides a framework around which you can learn to read and judge price action, and make your decisions accordingly. Remember, even Clay said to "Make the Dance your own".... So, personally, I love things like this. I've added a couple of trades that were "not quite Dance" but more a few "steps" I picked up elsewhere and incorporated it in. How many times do you see "systems" where some profit consistently, and others lose just as consistently? Common as... It isn't the "systems", it's the match or mismatch between the style and the trader. "Systems" and their rigidity are science-like, whereas "strategy" and "style" are more art, and I think that is where we should be striving to go. Where you can "see it" and almost "feel it"... not just waiting for when A=B and X&gt;Y then...... That's robotic and like most EAs, the systems by themselves simply do not work. You have to add discretion and experience - the "art". I think the ultimate aim of any trader should be to develop their own trading style, and the best way to do that is by adopting things from others and modifying them to fit in with what suits you. After all, you are going to be doing the trading. Now that's what I want to achieve..... I'll let you know when I get there!

--- 帖子 #4332 ---
The Confluence is really what makes these "scooped" up trades so powerful. In last nights move, price bounced right off of the Feb 9th high of 1.3743. Thus the probabilities were that the move off of prior support - since it was coming off of a higher time frame (H4) - would be strong. However according to dance rules, we cannot simply buy at that bounce of support until we have addtional confirming factors. Thus once price was "scooped" up by the M15 10 &amp; 35 ALONG with the H1 10 we knew our direction; we then received our confirmation and bought at the 2 bar retrace to the M15 10 @ approx .3760. We simply manage the trade from there and sell incrementally at each area of overhead resistance. In this instance you could have used M5 price to "fine-tune" your final exit and sell the remaining positions once the M5 candle opened below the M5 10.

--- 帖子 #4348 ---
Guys, here is a concept that helped me tremendously when I first started trading. It's nothing new and most of you already apply it, however just the "idea" alone is a helpful reminder of how we should view the market. Perception is everything in trading and thus you should always divide the market into 2 zones. Your "buy zone" and your "sell zone"; and those "zones" are divided by a "Zone Line". Once you mark your zone line, you can then confidently enter the market in the direction of the zone you are in using your strategy. This zone line should be the same "area" on all of your charts. Everyone might have a different idea of where that zone line is, however, regardless of where it is for "you", as long as you adhere to your rules, you will statistically beat the market. Consistency is the key to success in this business. We cannot expect the market to consistently provide us with an income, if we cannot consistently apply the same methodology. The reason why the failure rate is soo high in this business is because most people consistently do the "same" things over and over again and if those "same" things are in line with the "herd mentality", they will lose. Just a few ideas that might help in developing a strategy whether it be the Choros or any other approach. Happy Trading.

--- 帖子 #4364 ---
Nothing is 100%, and if you look at it, most levels are never truly "rubbed out" forever. The best example of this is when you see support broken then it becomes resistance and after it has been broken again, once again it becomes support. Just because it has been previously broken doesn't mean it will not come into play again. If you watch price at most of these levels as it encounters them, you'll usually see it pause and splutter about before it goes past or reverses. When you have a confluence, the effect is added and made stronger, and it is often enough to cause the level to hold and cause a reversal.

--- 帖子 #4405 ---
Thanks to you for asking. Concerning the scooped up on the daily chart, my approach to the strategy is actually very simple (perhaps too simple ? Don't know, Time will say it ) : In the Moving Averages I "just" see dinamic S/R levels, and I see moving Trend Lines. Just defined at the moment, by the Market of that specific TF. In the same way I would trade TL and S/R I just consider that all a matter of edge. As the price comes very near to a S/R or TL I have (usually) a bigger % that it will bounce from that point, than from the middle of the "channel". Moreover as we are learning, the first or second time of any touch has more % than the further ones. If we have a Confluence of more of them, we also have an higher % of traders probably acting in the same way. That is our edge. As soon as one of those levels (S/R, TL, MA) is "broken" I look at where it could be the next possible significant level for the price to bounce (of course it is not always so, otherwise I would be rich already since a long time ). Now, as the Higher TFs lead the main trend, I see that on EUR Daily we are still long (or better said above 35/50), so I MUST still think that the price will still move upwards. All the other MA's in lower TFs have been broken. Even the Daily 10. So the next possible "wall" to keep the trend upwards is the 35. If that will be broken then the 50, then the 62, then the 100, than the 200. This is the way I look at levels, starting from the M15 upwards. Below Daily they are all moving down, so as I trade mainly the M15 I would look for shorts now, but I will take particular care as soon as the price approaches the 35 on Daily, as I know that I would be basically still be still trading counter the main trend, and because from that point the bigger Daddy (Daily) could let hear his stronger voice and all smaller children could wake up. If not, then I will trade short even more confidently and will perhaps look at the weekly for identifing a next possible bounce level. That's all.

--- 帖子 #4406 ---
This discussion relates to my bad bounce trade the other day. There, some people had the opinion that the trade was unadvisable because the 10 had turned. It was not quite a scooped up situation, because the turning came quickly. But the examples from the original Dance thread show situations where Clay said not to take the bounce trade because price had already flipped under the 10 on the way down, and was hugging it. I think this shows a few possibilities 1) Price pulls back to the 35 quickly without hugging the 10 on the way, and the 35 and 50 are steep. This is the best type of bounce trade. 2) Price pulls back quickly to the 35 without hugging the 10, and the 35 and 50 are flat. This is a clear no trade. 3) Price comes back slower to the 35 and hugs the opposite side of the 10 beforehand, while the 35 and 50 are flat or diverging. This, I think, is what Survivor is calling the best scooped up setup. It's kind of like a reverse constrainment, and the 35 and 50 are showing that they will get out of the way. And 4) Price comes back slower to the 35 and hugs the 10, but the MAs are steep and parallel. This is a mixed signal, and thus a no trade. You might as well flip a coin here. I doubt I'm saying anything new here, but just trying to write it out so that I can make sure that I make sense of it.

Yesterday saw a bounce off the Daily 35, and we went into this day with the Daily in an uptrend still, while the H4 is in downtrend, and the H1 is flat and volatile. Moreover, Asian markets had a fairly strong down move going into the day. Overall, the picture is confused at best. 1) Constrainment. Survivor says these have come back into vogue, and even I could have spotted this one. Five of seven bars almost perfectly touch the 10, which is steeply down, with the 35 and 50 both steep and parallel. Any of these could also be taken as a 10 touch. But 6 10 Touch trades in 7 bars is more than just a 10 touch. Easy, easy trade if I had been around. 2) 10 Touch. The 10 is still steep and it meets the two bar rule, but with all of the 10 Touches in the constrainment, this one is probably pushing it. 3) 10 Touch, 35 Bounce. This is close to the kind of retracement that precedes a big move up. Price has crossed the 35 and 50 by more than 15 pips, and then come back in one bar to touch both the 35 and the 10. But I didn't take this trade, and I think it was for pretty good reasons. First, there has already been a stall for 5 bars, this shows some pretty clear indecision. Second, there was a retrace touch of the 35 just a few bars back. That would make this the second touch, which is not what I've seen before when it makes a strong move up. So, I made the right call here, and decided that it was more likely that price would drop back down. What I did not foresee was the exhaustion spike that would precede the fall. Somehow, I think a trader like EO would have gotten 25 pips on this upswing, and then immediately have reversed and taken oodles of pips on the way down. I sat and watched. 4) 10 Touch. This touch came after the London close. It's after a very long move and is the first touch. Given the time of day, I don't know whether I would take this trade. During London or New York hours, I think the shape of the bars leading to the trade look very bad. There's already a clear higher low in place from the last swing. I think this trade is by the rules but not great. Depending on when you move to break even, this is either a breakeven trade or good for about 15 pips. I'm not posting the charts, but here are a couple of observations on the higher time frames if you care to look. On the Daily, price basically moved from the 35 down to the 50, tested the 50 by about 20 pips, and has now come back to sit almost exactly on it. On the H1, there was a retrace early in the day back to the 35, 50 and 62. If you recall, yesterday, price hit the first, bounced off, came back to hit the second, bounced again, and then hit the third and bounced again before moving on its way. Today, price first pierced the 35 and 50 and bounced back. Then it went and tested them again, and reached the 62 before bouncing back again and then plunging down on its big move. Maybe there really is something to the power of the H1 62? (I thought I posted this yesterday, then found it again today buried in a sea of windows.)

--- 帖子 #4425 ---
Many people put either the multi time frame indicator on, or use the approximate equivilents. On the 15 minute chart, these show about where the 10, 35 and 50 would appear on the H1, H4, etc... The multitime frame indicator shows a line that looks like steps. The approximate equals are 40EMA = H1 10EMA, 140 SMA = H1 35SMA. These are not completely accurate, but they come within a few pips. I include some MAs from other sources. I have basically all the MAs that EOHaters put on his charts. That includes the 200 on basically all charts, the 62EMA and the 50SMA on the H1. And I also put the 100EMA on all charts, because I've used it elsewhere. I won't take a touch or bounce trade off the other EMAs, not unless there is a huge amount of confluence in favor of the trade. I think Clay would call the extra MAs distractions. He's a much, much better trader than I am. I'm trying to learn what I can from the EOHaters thread at the same time that I'm learning the dance. This may be biting off too much at once, so it's not something I would recommend to anyone else. In fact, there are times when I think I should stop the scattershot approach, and just focus on one kind of dance trade, not even the full three basic trades -- just one.

--- 帖子 #4429 ---
Daily started having closed almost dead on the 50, on a bearish candle. All other time frames are bearish. The jury is still out on whether the 50 will hold, or whether a downtrend will start on the daily. 1) H1 Constrainment, M15 Ping Pong. On the M15, coming into the day, price has been bouncing between the 50 on the top and the 35 on the bottom. On the H1, this same area looks like a constrainment around the H1 10. In this situation, Survivor says to ignore the uncertainty of the lower time frame, and go with the edge shown on the H1. What the M15 shows, however, is a perfect place to put a small stop -- just above the 50. Also notice, once the 35 breaks, even though the H1 is still in a constrainment, there is a pretty good touch on the 10 on the first green bar after the 35 break. 2) 10 Touch. This is a nice 10 touch trade, with a clean two bar retracement. There are no support areas in the way of making 15 pips. Theres a near confluence with the Monthly S1. 3) 10 Touch. Now this is at least the second, and maybe the third touch. There has been consolidation for seven bars before the touch, and the consolidation is all around an S/R line. The 10 is still steep. And even on the best count, its a three bar retrace from the low. The only thing this has going in its favor is the confluence with the round number. No trade. 4) 10 Touch, 35 Bounce. This is an ugly version of the kind of trade that Bigtent discussed earlier. The 50 is flat and diverging. Price has reversed to come up through the 35 and the 50. And on this bar there is a pullback to the 10 that is also a bounce off the 50. (On a side note, at the close of this bar, this would also qualify as an EO cross and reverse trade - since the bar crossed both the 35 and 50 and then closed with a fairly small bottom wick.) Unlike Bigtent's example, there is no "scooping up" on display here, and the 10 and 35 are not quite on top of each other. On top of that, the last three bars have all shown real weakness at the top, showing pretty strong resistance at the 100 (my black line). I think this would be a tough trade to take, but its another example of how, after price crosses through both the 35 and 50, it will come back down to retest one or both, and generally around the level of the 10 at the same time.

What we mean is that all MAs should be going in same direction. In this trade, 10 EMA was constraining price down but 35/50 were rising and wanted to push price up. SO i would not take this trade. You never know which MA will win- 10 or 35/50. But same chart gave a good example of constrainment trade. Switch to 1H for same pair and see how it looks? Thats what i will trade. Not a perfect example. I like even smaller candles but i took this trade anyway. Also note that HTF MAs should not be against your trade. In this case we are going long so there should be no HTF MA above the price . Otherwise such MA can act as resistance and hold price down. Check the 4h and d1 charts of EURUSD.. All our mas are below tha price that's why i took this 1h Trade. Hope that helps clarify things.

--- 帖子 #4449 ---
The Daily is now officially in no-man's land. we may be ping ponging between the daily 35 and 50, so there is really no direction at all. H4 is in a downtrend, but seemingly on a retrace, so again, no help here. H1 is likewise stuck between the major MAs. Going into the Frankfort and London sessions we are moving down, but I don't think it means much. 1) 35/50 Bounce. No trade. The MAs aren't really flat, but its hard to say that they have picked up much of a direction either. Technically, they are down. And since the last cross of the MAs, this is the first touch. So, I suppose it is a "by the rules" trade. So why is it no trade? First, look at how badly the 35 and 50 have been respected in the recent bouncing around. We have had three full crosses in a few hours, with hardly a decent bounce to be seen. I take that as a signal that other technical factors are weighing more heavily now. Second, this area has acted as support three times in those moves, but never has it shown any resistance. Sometimes support becomes resistance, but when it's already proved that its not likely to do that, there's no reason to insist otherwise. Third, and perhaps most strongly, we are coming off a triple bottom almost exactly on a support resistance line. Even with the nice two bar retrace, there is no way that you should take this as a touch trade, and if you looked for a decent entry on the M5, you would find no trade. 2) 10 Touch. This is the first touch on the 10 EMA. I passed it because it violated the two bar rule. And then I regretted passing it, knowing that many people will take the first touch, even if it violates the two bar rule, so long as the MA is steep enough. NY open came around here, and it led to a fairly long consolidation period. With no help from the upper time frames, I had no confidence in either a continuation or a reversal. 3) Constrainment. First there is a two bar retrace to the 10. As the second or more touch (given the consolidation), I don't think this is a great trade. Then we have four hours in a row with the bodies constrained by the 5EMA, and three of the wicks constrained by the 10. To me, this looks like a good constrainment opportunity. 4) H4 35/50 Bounce. This is the trade I was waiting for after passing on trade 2. The H4 35 and 50 are headed down, and they are almost on top of each other. And there is confluence with a round number and a support/resistance line. Combined, I think this makes for an easy trade, and it would have been worth 20-25 pips. Unfortunately, my broker's MT4 server went down for 6 hours, and I missed this and Trade 3 as a result. 5) 10 Touch. This is probably no trade. It's either 4 bars to the touch, or 9, depending on how you cound. It's also way too late in the day. On the plus side, the touch would also form a tweezer bottom. The problem with that, however, is that by the time you see the tweezer formation, its too late to get into the trade. By this time, its pretty clear that this trade would be looking to get in on a ping pong game between the round number and the first double bottom. There may be a good reason to do that, but it's not a dance trade. H1 Chart: 6) Notice how the early downtrend was playing ping pong between the H1 35 and 50, which were very wide apart. Taking any of these would be very advanced dance trading. I'm not looking for this sort of trade in real time. If I were, I would want to take one in the direction supported by the higher time frames, but today, there was no direction from them. Still, the respect shown the H1 MAs helps explain why the 35 and 50 got so ignored on the M15. 7) 62 Bounce. The 62 is not a Dance MA. It comes from EOHaters thread. He loved it, and would take touch trades off of it all the time. This is an H1 version of the cross and retest. Good for lots of pips. 8) H1 10 EMA Touch. First touch of the H1 10. The angle is very steep, and this looks like a good trade. My only concern here would be that the H1 is starting to look like a porcupine.

--- 帖子 #4488 ---
My guess is that you are using the same type of MA on both the 35 and the 50. Make sure that you are using a Simple Moving Average for the 35, and an Exponential Moving Average for the 50. They should both be calculated on the Close. If you haven't ever done it, you should consider opening a chart and putting up the different variations of moving average for the same period (in MT4 there are simple, exponential, smoothed and linear weighted). The differences are remarkable. Also take a look at different data methods (close, typical price, etc...) It's worthwhile just to see how changing the variables on indicators will change their behavior.

These actually stay pretty close to the values of the higher time frames, but they aren't perfect. (For help in translating the charts, I use Red for 50, Yellow for 35, and Green for 10. As the MA gets smaller, you go further up the colors of the rainbow. So 5 is Violet.) The short dotted line is for H1, and the longer slashes are H4. We were in a downtrend coming into the 17th, but the more important message from the higher time frames is that the GU is playing pingpong on the H1 chart. Thus, even though we are in a downtrend, we also started the day near the bottom of the range we have been in. 1) 10 Touch almost. This is the first touch of the 10 after the cross of the 35 and 50. MA is steep, and there is a nice two bar retrace. It also happens to coincide with Monday's Low (but I don't think that should be given much weight). If you could get in this trade, you might get out with 10 pips. It never makes it to 15, and is probably break even. The more important thing about this touch, I think, is that it is almost a first touch, and that means it's a good idea to be careful on the next touch of the 10, 2 bars later, which turns out to be a loser. 2) 50 Bounce. This is a good pullback to both the 50 and the H1 10. The 50 and 35 could be steeper, but they are converging. Moreover, recently, I've noticed that price seems to be respecting the H1 10 more than either of the M15 MAs. Basically, it appears that the best trades are when there is a confluence with the H1 10. This one is good for lots of pips. 3) 10 Touch. 2 Bar pullback, and there are oodles of confluence. It's taken 5 bars to get here from the swing high. And it looks like we are on are way to the second lower low. The top had a pinbar, followed by a hanging man, followed by a bearish engulfing bar. I passed on this trade. 6) 35 Bounce or H1 10 Touch. There's a confluence here with a round number. Here, price almost gets to the 35, but not quite. --- 帖子 #4511 ---
I'm about halfway through the initial selection process for the outline. Early on in my involvement, I posted a 5 or 6 page .pdf which was my summary of the dance rules as I understood them. Clay seemed to like the summary. It's not 10 or less simple rules. But keep in mind, there are three distinct major entries for the dance on the M15, so 10 rules may be a bit optimistic to cover all three. If you want to see my .pdf, search the thread for dancesummary.pdf Here is the quickest summary I could give: 10 Touch - 1) Trade only with the trend of the moment. (Trend of the moment is defined by price and the 10 in relation to the 35/50) 2) 10 EMA is very steep (as if pointing at 1 or 5 oclock) 3) Price pulls back 12-15 or more pips in one or two bars to touch the 10. 4) Enter in direction of trend with stop loss of 9 plus spread. 5) Move to break even as quickly as possible. 6) Exit to taste. But, 7) Avoid trading into heavy resistance. 35/50 Bounce 1) Trade only with the trend of the moment. 2) 35 and 50 are fairly steep and parallel. (Now thinking 2 and 4 oclock). 3) 35 and 50 are not diverging. 4) Price pulls back to the MAs on a fairly sharp pullback. Two bars is best, but there is leeway here. 5) Either trade on the touch, if everything is perfect or 6) Fine tune the entry on the M5 by looking for a good price action entry (hammer, hanging man, engulfing bar), or confluence in the M5 (a parallel dance pattern in both time frames). 7) Stop Loss of about 15, but never more than 19 pips. 8) Move to break even quickly. 9) Exit to taste. Constrainment 1) Trade only with the trend of the moment, and there must be some trend. 2) At least three wicks in a row, or the body of three candles in a row, touch one of the MAs and then are rejected by the MA. 3) It's best if the candles are small and in a well defined high/low range. 4) There is no larger MA in the way of the trade. 5) The last candle before entry must close on the trend side of the MA. 6) Enter on the next touch of the MA. 7) Stop loss very tight, maybe 6-8 pips plus spread. 8) Move quickly to Break even. 9) Exit to taste. Keep in mind that these brief summaries are my interpretation, and others might have a different perspective. Also, this loses quite a bit of the subtlety and learning that has gone on over the last 10 months. So, you might want to start with this, but you really will get a much better feel by going through things in more detail and by studying the thread. Preparing the outline is taking me through my third reading of the thread, and I can't even begin to say how much more I am seeing this time around. So, maybe I shouldn't have posted this. In my opinion, there really is no substitute for doing the work and putting in the time it takes (however much time that might be).

I'm not sure how I would play this in the future, but it seems to me that the right play is to take both trades (or even three in a row). Second trade was good for 50-100+ pips. 2) H1 62 Bounce. Here's an example of how the difference in chart scale can make a world of difference in the appearance of the price moves. I have my H1 charts set to a fixed scale of 200 pips top to bottom. On my chart, that doesn't look very close to a touch of the H1 10. It's 5 pips off as the bar closed, and was still 3-4 pips off if you extrapolated the MA down. Also, I can see how it looks like a constrainment on your charts, but it doesn't look like that at all on mine. (By the way, I'm not saying that my chart is better. Here, it clearly would have kept me out of what turned out to be a good trade. Instead, my point is simply how different the same data can look.) Another thing troubles me about the H1 charts. Three bars after your entry there appears to be a clear touch of the 10. In real time, it didn't look that way at all, and there was no touch at all on the equivalent that I use on the M15. I set three limit orders in this area last night, and price trailed away each time before I got filled. Clearly you are jumping in at a better time, while I'm standing on the dock waving.

--- 帖子 #4592 ---
There were two personal goblins that I had to fight before getting succesfull: 1. The goblin named Mr. Greed , saying to you: "You stupid fuck, you closed your trade at +15p, look at it going to 100 now...". When you listen to Mr. Greed, you apply his advice to the next trade waiting for 100p and all you get is -30p or more if the next goblin takes over. Even worse, you may re-enter the same trade when it is already too late and just when you enter, it quickly goes against you. 2. The goblin named Mr. Right , saying to you: "Man, this trade is closing in to your SL but since you are always right you can't loose this trade. Move your SL another 30p." Then the trade moves more against you and he says: "This is too close for comfort, you should move the SL further away since you are always right..." And so on and so forth and before you know it you are attached to a stupid position that keeps going against you. When I managed to stop listening to Mr. Greed and Mr. Right, I became successful. They are still there, I just stopped listening...

--- 帖子 #4593 ---
We share number 1, however, I never do the second. My stop is 15 pips max, and it never goes more, because 15 x 2 positions is 2%, and that is my maximum risk per trade. One of mine, particularly after a loss, chasing a trade where I have missed the entry because I have come in to late, or I have hesitated through doubt (fear). That often means that my stop is closer than it should, and it chokes the trade, because I cannot move my stop and there is no room to manouvre or choking the trade to minimize losses (the Fear Goblin says, "1% loss is better than 2%!"), and actually creating a small loss and missing a winning trade.

--- 帖子 #4609 ---
Basically, if price is above the 35/50 MAs, you should be long, if below, short. However, this is so for all time frames, and if they disagree, you will often see the price change directions as it hits the various MAs from each. Generally, HTFs win over the lower ones, but all in all the result is usually price pingponging between them, creating chop until it works its way free of the area where they conflict. THe EU is a case in point at the moment. Within a 20 pip range you have MAs from M15, H1, H4 and D1 all mixed up (Clay called this MA soup). If you look at the lower TFs (the MTF MAs are all there to see) you can see how the price is just bouncing around them and going nowhere, really. Attached Image (click to enlarge) If all TFs are in agreement, it is usually easier to trade.

(It's a big image, so you'll probably need to click and expand it) Attached Image (click to enlarge) On the H4, it appears to be pushing hard on this level, with price highs lowering, forming a bearish pennant pattern and the H4 10 is constraining the price in that direction. Attached Image (click to enlarge) So, not predicting anything, but it may just end up with a move downward and it is worth keeping you eye on it. Comments welcome!

--- 帖子 #4625 ---
It's possible you are right, but there is no way to know unless you test it. There are also a great many people who firmly believe that its impossible to get the results that Kostas has gotten, day in and day out, for the last 10 months. They KNOW that 2.5% per day is unachievable, and the mere fact that someone is doing is will not shake their knowledge. Sometimes people needlessly bind themselves by their own convictions about what is and is not possible. if you want to show that a 12 or 15 pip stop loss can't work with the Dance on higher time frames, then do some tests and show the results. Also, I've never been convinced by the signal/noise distinction people make between charts on higher and lower time frames. If there were an obvious distinction between those kinds of charts, then someone familiar with the behavior should be able to tell what time frame he was looking at simply by looking at the bars on the chart. As an experiment, I'm attaching three charts. They have the 10 EMA (green), the 35 SMA (yellow), and the 50 EMA (red), with the 100 in Black and 200 in White. The first question is whether any of these look more noisy that the others? Second question is: Rank the charts in order of how well you think they Dance. (Extra credit to anyone who gets the time frames right for the charts, and counting gaps is cheating.)

I would like to share with everybody and especially the newbies like me my current psycology. I started dealing with FOREX 6 months ago. I didn't have any strategy, risk management or proper psycology. I only had 300 USD to lose and so I did After 2-3 months I discovered the Dance manual. I started reading and reading until I undertood the basics of it. I am currently trading live using the dance rules and with what is left from my account which lets me use very small lot sizes. The results are 60% wins-40% loses. Before the dance they were 10% wins - 90% loses . Few days ago I finished reading the "Trading in the zone" book. I can say that it changed completely the way I am thinking about FOREX. If there is anyone who hasn't read that book yet, DO read it immediately. At the moment, I am still a bit confused about the Dance rules because I have noticed that the Dance manual has been revised for M15 and M1 charts. Also, I see a lot of people here using more MAs than what Clay says in his manual. But whatever it takes and even if it take me 1 year of reading, I WILL manage to become consistent and succesfull. And I think all newbies should think this way. Don't stop trying if you really like trading. Regards Iero

--- 帖子 #4647 ---
Everyone here is following latest 15M manual and i dont think anyone is playing with 1M yet. I would suggest even you start with 15M because that's what clay advised IMHO. Many use other MAs. I use 100H and 62H MA other than manual. Everyone has his own tastes and i dont think this should distract you. Also note that i use many mas because they give me HTF equivalents. For example i use 40 EMA in 15 m because it gives me approximate location of 10 EMA in 1H even when i am looking at 15 M chart.I would suggest sticking to original mas initially and add as you become comfortable.

--- 帖子 #4648 ---
I'm glad you are learning this method as it works very well. As far as using the M1 I think some use it to fine tune their entries which you may or may not do as you get better with the Dance. The additional MAs are also something people use as they progress. I have added the 21ema to mine as I have found for me that it adds an extra spot to look for opportunities. Also a lot of people have the higher time frame MAs (such as the 140sma = H1 35 or the 200ema = H1 50) on there M15 charts so they can see an approximation of these on just one chart. Keep up the good work and remember this is a method (NOT a set in stone system) that you can adapt and adjust as you improve.

At first sorry for my english: I trade with the dance charts, but with my own rules.My enties work for me 75% win 25% loose. It depend on your own skills, it can be better too. I trade on 1M chart since years. I show you how it works. I watch the M1 M5 M15 chart (GBP/EUR) And of course the trend on the higher timeframes. Very important: on the M1 timeframe 1 have two more MA's: 135 ema 525 sma These are the 10 ema and 35 sma on the 15 chart.

--- 帖子 #4655 ---
I trade not the touch of the ma's, but my setups are in this areas. The price touch the 10/35 ma and when goes below/abow the 35 sma (1M) I Waiting for a pin bar or hammer or a constaitment. And then take the trade. Stop 5pips+spread, after 4-5 pips i close half of them, and i trail my stop, at the peeks and valleys. My target is often RN and pivots. I take the trades only when the price is enought far from RN's, for good profits.

--- 帖子 #4656 ---
I tested this setups month, and i trade on live account. It works, but you need to backtest it and learn the setups. And it is very important to understand peeks and valleys!!!

--- 帖子 #4657 ---

--- 帖子 #4658 ---
Peaks and valleys are the high and low points of swings. Here is an article by Pring about peaks and troughs (valleys). Attached File(s) Peaks_and_Troughs_Pring.pdf 181 KB | 515 downloads

--- 帖子 #4659 ---
How i trade: In the morning (GMT+1) at 8-10 I wait for a break out. The price need to come back to the 15M Ma's. And then I watch, the peeks and valleys. I open trade only when the price is below/abow the 35 sma, it is very important!!! Do not open trade when the price break through the 35 sma, you need a good setup int this area!!! Patience! Wait, wait, and wait! There are days without setups! Wait, wait, and wait!!! When you risk 1%, you close the half of your trade in 4 pip+ , and the second half in 10 pips, your risk was 1% and you win 1%. 75% winer 25% looser, and you are ok. In half of your trades you can catch the first 4 pip, and the another half is breakeven. But with your another half you can get sometimes 25-30 pips. So, the average will be 1/1 R/R. I hope it helps. And sorry for my bad English.

--- 帖子 #4670 ---
I have Kostas Post concerning the way he mainly trades on the wall beside the monitor, as I find that is a great post for everybody. This chart (even if the first two bars Ema10 touches were during Tokyo's session not easily tradable for European time) is perhaps one of the clearest explanations of those words I've ever seen. The Master says : 1. First touch of 10: take it 2. Second touch of 10: maybe if action looks strong 3. After that no more 10 touches 4. First touch of 35/50: take it 5. After that no more 10 or 35/50 trades. 6. Wait for higher TF 10 (assuming steps 1 - 5 were on M15, then this is for H1 or H4 7. First touch of higher TF 10: take it etc. etc. etc. Look at the chart, adding at the 3 first entries (steps 1 to 4) you would have done a great job for the day, with zero DD (and the way down did not finish yet) Simple, Clear, just great !

--- 帖子 #4699 ---
EurJpy was one of the pairs Clay traded on the original thread. By his rules, one should trade it mostly during the overlap period, from Frankfurt open to Tokyo close. And you could also overlap some before and after if there is decent movement during that time. I don't see Usd/Jpy mentioned very often. The typical advice for beginners (which would include myself) is to pick a pair and stick to it. It's good advice (and advice I should follow more than I do). The big exception to this idea of sticking with one pair, I think, comes from looking for constrainments, especially on the H1 timeframe. With them, there may be the luxury of having the time to analyze what is happening and picking the best set-up available. With Touch trades, you have to be able to act in a flash, and that means that the accumulated experience you have about how a pair behaves is crucial. I firmly believe that with that kind of trading, the best traders act on instincts that have been honed from hour after hour of watching the same pairs and getting to know them inside out.

--- 帖子 #4716 ---
I read the following in a bookstore, I think from one of Ed Ponsi's books, and it makes some sense to me. In any market, you want to be trading with the smart money and against the dumb money. How do you identify the dumb money? In stocks its fairly easy. There are daily reports of odd lot transactions. Small time newer traders tend to be dumb, and it's best to trade against them. So, for a particular stock, you look at whether the odd lots have on balance gone long or short, and then you take the opposite position. In general, this proves to be a profitable strategy. Forex doesn't work quite the same way. I forget the names, but the regulators break Forex into three categories. First there are the big boys: the banks and the hedge funds. Then there are the commercial and institutional players, including insurance companies, other big corporations and so on. Finally, there are the retail customers, like you and me. But in Forex, the dumb money is the commercial money. Retail traders actually tend on balance to do pretty well, and it is the mid-size trader that is getting fleeced from both sides. I don't know if there is a day to day way to make use of that knowledge. I think Ponsi said there were some reports that would give some clues as to where the commercial money was going. But I forget what those clues are.

--- 帖子 #4739 ---
hi alienfrog, when I first downloaded the tools from the Dance thread, I encountered the same problem, too. The thing is you might have changed the lot size of buy/sell scripts to something other than 3 lots. because you cannot modify close scripts you are unable to close positions at your discretion. anyway, I had an application to decode mq4 files and decoded them. replace these files and you should be able to change the lot size to comply with buy/sell scripts. open and close scripts should have the same lotsize value.

--- 帖子 #4740 ---
actually i just remember having this problem also at some point, it was my mistake though. the problem was that i was opening a trade with say 0.1 lots (the same as i was using in my live account) but when i was using the close script it wasnt working because it had the default lot size that was 1 lots. so i had to manually alter the closing lot size to be the equal (or less) to the opening lot. maybe this is what causes you the problem.

--- 帖子 #4749 ---
The simple way of identifying it, is to look at the different TFs. You have the M15 going short and the HTFs sitting just below it. That means dancing a waltz and rock'n'roll on the same floor... collisions are inevitable. I have the MTF MAs on my chart for this reason.... looks ugly, but works. Attached Image (click to enlarge) During these times, from what I have observed, it appears that bounces off various levels are the only way to trade it as the standard Dance has problems (MA soup of sorts). The problem is picking which MA/Pivot/RN or confluence will produce a reversal, even in the short term, and which will only cause a brief interruption, with PA that fakes the reversal then reverts and continues, breaking the MA/Pivot/RN/SR whatever to take the trade out. Those who are experienced, like Kostas, seem to be able to do this. Others try and get it wrong. In saying that, I just missed by about 30 seconds, a great touch on the GU! (Wasn't pretty with the messy bars before it, but I would have given it a shot if I'd been at the computer).

Funny how it goes with this, though. Often, "good reasons" for taking or not taking a trade are not really "good reasons" but judgment calls. It's often the case that I can talk myself out of good trades and into bad trades, and I always seem to have "good reasons", until after the fact, when I realize those reasons were not really that "good" after I have pressed the button or missed the opportunity, whichever is the case. It's all part of the psychology.... where subconsciously you interpret what you see differently at different times.

--- 帖子 #4829 ---
The only problem with this process is when you let the result dictate whether your reasons were good or bad. And yeah, I do the same thing all the time. Often I know that a trade sucked the second that I took it. I actually have a category in my journal for FUBAR trades. Those are the ones that I took by convincing myself that I had a reason when I really didn't. Likewise, there are FUBAR passes. The thing is, I have several FUBAR trades that ended up making decent pips (and its not even my worst category at this point). That didn't make the trades any better. But yes, I agree that this is a funny area, and it's probably where we are most likely to start fooling ourselves. It's one of the reasons that discretionary trading can be so hard for us beginners. Sometimes your "discretion" is no more than lying to yourself.

--- 帖子 #4832 ---
First, not every good trade makes money. On my charts, it drops a little less than 12 pips from the 35 before going the other way. Even with the spread, this would not have gotten stopped out with my broker, if taken from the 35. If you took it from the 50, that's a different story, and it would get taken out on a 15 pip stop. There are three things I would consider on this trade. First, price has already moved through a number of MAs that are nearby, including the H4 50, the H1 50, the H4 10, and the H1 10. Then it runs into the M15 50 and 35. I wouldn't necessarily expect a bounce off the lower time frame MAs when price didn't stop for the higher time frames. Second, there is still another relevant MA, the H1 35, which acts as support just below. Kostas used to say that the GU likes to test all the MAs in the area. I'm not sure that this has been as true recently as it used to be, but its something I always have in the back of my mind. Third, look to the left. There's an area of support/resistance that has caused a reaction or consolidation between 6360 and 6370 several times just in the last two days. What to do? Kostas would almost certainly wait for a good bar on the M5 to fine tune this entry. I would like to do the same sort of thing, but haven't gotten the knack. Or you could wait until the last MA, in this case the H1 35, before making the entry. Or you could make the entry as you did, but adjust the stop to be wider based on the above considerations. Of the three, I think the last alternative is probably the worst. And again, I don't think it was a bad trade. Not every trade that loses is a bad trade. In this case, however, I think a basically good trade could have been improved by either paying more attention to the higher time frames, or by using Kostas' fine tuning method. I'm attaching the M5 chart. It shows that using tuning, you would clearly stay out where the touches actually occured. They are strong bars down. But after the two big down bars, there is a hanging man, and then two bars later, a hammer. Either of those might have been good entry points. (Again, take this with some reservation: I suck at fine tuning in real time.)

I posted the screenshot of the trade at the bottom of the last page, the GU trade is the second one. When I say "by the rules" I'm referring to the original Dance rules. Hi, everyone. Wondering how to deal with the 10EMA repainting itself. It really bugs me when it causes me to miss a trade. Here is an example. Chart #1: At the start of the candle there is a big gap between price and the 10. We don’t know where it’s going yet and we don’t have an entry signal. Chart #2: Big move upward which, BTW, is exactly what we are looking for! The 10 repaints as price moves upward. By the time the candle closes the bottom pin is touching the 10 for a perfect entry signal! But it’s moved so far that we missed the trade. Chart #3: I’ve tried extending the previous trendline if I see the possibility of a move. If the bar hits my “extension” I’ll take the entry. I figure it’s close enough to a good entry point that if I’m right about PA then it will make pips. I haven’t seen this mentioned anywhere in the thread. Just wondering if any others have seen this and how they handled it? BTW I did not take this trade because 35/50 was diverging! But I wanted to show the example.

Isengoz, I was hoping a more experience dancer would weigh in on this, but since they haven't I'll take a shot at analyzing your trade in dance context. At best I'm right and someone may confirm me, or at worst I'm wrong and someone will correct and teach me. Now I'm not good with the advanced dance concepts yet, so I will only speak according to the basic rules from the manual. I don't see any dance "rules" followed here. You entered between the 35 and 50, which is a no-no in the manual. It's really a price action trade, with the confluence of the 10, 35 and RN as resistance. You broke two of the major dance rules: 1) Never trade when the 35/50 is diverging, and 2) Always trade above (long) or below (short) the 35/50, never in between (except maybe advanced which, again, I am not). And you almost paid for it - price tested the 50 but bounced against you, broke the RN, and even touched your 1.6503 resistance point before going your way! That happens, of course, but even with the signs of the downtrend in your favor, if it were me I would have felt that I just got lucky when it wasn't stopped out. I like your entry reasons - the dead end and complete retrace of the third top, then the downtrend reinforced by the next bar with the long wick. Also, H1 looks good: 3 nice bearish candles, 35/50 close, and all MAs turning down - good bearish TOM. But at decision time, is all this enough to override the 35/50 diverging? Maybe the strong H1 chart is enough, but not for me because I always get burned when I break that rule. So I see this as a well-analyzed price action trade with help from the overhead resistance. But not so much a dance trade. BUT... as you say, your reasons for entry were excellent reasons. Plus you taught me a little more from your post. And at the end of the day you are up +15 pips, right? Congrats on a good trade and thanks for sharing it!
