--- 帖子 #4900 ---
You can add as many monitors as you like by adding video cards to your computer. Here is how to do it for a desktop PC: To add one additional monitor, buy a regular video adapter (or "card") and install it. You can get one at your local computer store, or Best Buy (in the USA), or even Walmart, probably for $20US. Tell them why you want it and what kind of computer you have and they will help you select the right card. If you want to add two monitors (3 total) get a "dual monitor video card." The card will install in a PCI or PCI-Express slot in your computer, and will provide (one or two) additional ports where you connect the two additional monitors. There are several different types of monitor connections, so it is important that you know the make/model of your computer so you get the same kind of connection as your current monitor. If you aren't sure, and you have a Dell, HP, Compaq, or other brand name, just call the manufacturer and they will sell you the exact right card for your computer. It probably won't even cost more, maybe a little but not much. Of course, you will also need to buy the extra monitor(s). Again, make sure you get the right kind that connects to your new video card. Here's a link to a shopping search site that shows a bunch of dual monitor video cards. This is just to give you an idea of prices and descriptions - don't buy one from here unless you know it will match your system! http://www.nextag.com/serv/main/buye...dapter&amp;psort=1 Once installed, open the Display properties in Windows and you will see options for how you want to set them up, i.e., which one is left or right side, which one shows Start button, etc. Most laptops already have dual monitor capability built in. All you need is a second monitor and off you go! Here is a YouTube video that describes very nicely how to do it: Inserted Video (Wow, it puts the video right in the post just by cut and paste the link. Hope that's allowed.) Many new computers (e.g., Dell Optiplex models) come with dual monitor capability as a standard feature. This has been so for a couple of years, so if you have a newer computer check your original documentation. You probably only need to connec the "Y" cable that came with it (that you didn't know what it was for!) to a new monitor. You will LOVE having more than one monitor! You'll never go back to single monitor again. Any questions let me know. I don't want to digress the thread too much from the Dance so feel free to PM me. Good trading to all!

--- 帖子 #4907 ---
There are not really any "Sunday Candles", as what is shown as "Sunday" is actually the trading that is done in Sydney on Monday morning, so it is "Monday Trading". This is to do with your broker's server and time settings. If they use GMT or London time, you will see "Sunday Candles". Many brokers use central European time, which does not show those candles as the opening of the market in Sydney corresponds with midnight. in Europe as opposed to "10 PM" in London. So, you are stuck with it unless your client can adjust the time of your charts independently from your broker's feed (this would actually be easily done with an "Offset"). The only other alternative is to get another broker/feed.

--- 帖子 #4943 ---
In case you are new to this thread, may I offer some advice. I have learned that CONFLUENCE CONFLUENCE CONFLUENCE is the key!!!! Let me give an example here. If I see that we have moved away from the 35/50/62 EMA and we are moving back up towards it, I will then look for a recent pivot (high or low) in that area. If I see that, I will move to a smaller time frame, such as the 15 minute and look for a reversal signal such as a pin bar or my personal favorite, STOCHASTIC DIVERGENCE. I love to play stochastic divergences on the smaller time frames, even as low as the 3 minute. The confluences on a trade like this was: hit of a EMA on the 1 hour, pivot, and divergence on the 15 minute stochastics. The more confluence you have, the greater your potential reward will be. I also keep my risk very low. There's no need for a 50 pip stop on a 1 hour chart! Just some words of advice. I have enclosed a pic of my broker statement for this week. 14% growth in 2 days assuming no more than 1.5% risk per trade. Good luck! As a side note, for more info and ideas on divergence trades I HIGHLY recommend the bella divergence thread on ff.

Yes, if you adhered to the first touch rule, then only the first trade would follow that rule. Also, note that the second and third touches here also violate the two bar rule. If I recall correctly, Iero takes these trades using a different standard. As long as the 35 and 50 are both steep and parallel, and I think he has said less than four pips apart, he will take any touch on the 10. By his criteria, I think that means he would take the first three trades you have marked, but not the fourth since the 35 and 50 are already diverging and about 9 pips apart. I haven't used Iero's approach, but it would certainly have worked yesterday. Sometimes it seems like following a rule sucks. Even so, I still think its better to maintain discipline. I have nothing against someone adopting Iero's rule and following it. The danger comes when people start shifting the rules they are willing to follow simply because they want to get into trades. I tend to fall into that trap fairly easily.

--- 帖子 #5004 ---
In general, I agree with this statement with the following important differences: 1. The higher TFs have less noise 2. But they require more patience and different money management. As far as my trading goes, I am rather good at the M15 or lower but I am not that good at H4 or higher. What I mean here is that I do not use the H4 signal to get high number of pips. But I do use H4 signals to scalp 15-30 pips per trade. In this way I get a very high winning% from higher TFs since even if the move is head-fake, usually the price will bounce for 15-30 pips before fooling you (example: From a strong uptrend you see a 2-bar retrace to the H4 10. You would expect to get long when the H4 bounces on the 10 and then wait at least 4 hrs for the next bar to close and get your pips. What I would do instead is quickly take 15-30 pips. Obviously, I would loose the big amount of pips that such a bounce could produce but on the other hand if the move is fake I still get my profit.) Keep in mind that I use big lots to trade this way. The correct way to trade the H4 would be to have 1/4 of my normal lot size so that I can have my daily 2% with more pips (e.g. 120pips instead of 30 per day)

--- 帖子 #5042 ---
On the account size question, I have used this less than $30 on a mini account. That allowed me to take two positions at 0.01 lots per position, which is a "penny a pip" on USD pairs. My scheme is as follows... Goal is 45 pips per day (~3%) Two positions per trade, at 1% or less each. One I take profit at around 15 pips (~1%) and the other I trail dance style, or maybe close at 30 pips, since that is my daily target met. Initial stop is 15 pips on each position (~2% total), but I reduce that as soon as possible. Using the above scenario, you can start as low as $15, and the two positions at 0.01 lots, 15 pip stops are 1% each. When the account reaches $30, the lot size can increase to 0.02 per position. At $45, it increases to 0.03 lots, $60 to 0.04 lots..... That way your risk never exceeds 2% per trade, and you get compounding action which is slow at first on a small account, but will accelerate as your account grows. I use trading scripts to place the trades, which also calculate the lot size from the account balance, so I never have to look at that, I just concentrate on each trade and count the pips. (This reduces the stress of looking at $$$$). I believe that this is better than demo, as you are "real world" trading, but the amount is so small, that you can afford the risk, and you will grow with your account. When you are ready to "trade big" your account will have grown and you will already be "trading big"! Using this method, with a few months it is possible to grow a tiny account into something substantial. If you were able to realize the 45 pips per day goal for 18 months (396 trading days), your account would be $1M! (see spreadsheet) Attached File(s) My compounding.XLS 69 KB | 717 downloads

--- 帖子 #5043 ---
I would suggest reading Clay's latest manual on the M15 time frame and carefully studying it, especially the examples contained in it. Then I would consider moving through the posts linked in the Table of Contents one topic at a time, focusing at first on the types of entries that make the most sense to you. And then, I would go back through both the Choros thread and Clay's original thread. Don't hesitate to ask questions. This place is very friendly, and you will be amazed at how willing people are to help you. The only stupid question is the one that you don't ask, especially if the answer could prevent you from blowing your money. As for the higher time frames, Clay believed that signals on higher time frames are stronger than those on lower time frames. He based the Dance on the M15, I believe, because he likes frequent action, and because stops tend to be smaller. Keep in mind that trading on a higher time frame is only going to save you screen time if you are content to put in pending orders. You might also have to look into some sort of automated trade manager to tend trades while you are away from the screen. This style of trading may or may not suit you. But if you are going to be looking at small time frames to fine tune your entry, you will need some other mechanism to save you screen time. It's possible that you could work out something with alarms to grab your attention when price gets to an area that may be of interest. That sort of thing might fit well with the flexibility of a student schedule.

Quite so! I haven't been able to get it happening yet either, but that really is one of the main points. The fact that you can start with peanuts and the account will grow as your ability does should also not be overlooked. How many times have you heard the story of someone practicing on demo and perfecting their skills, only to then jump into a real account and blowing a fair sized account? That requires a psychological leap, and ensuing failure can ruin a person's trading career. I've seen a few quit because of this. This strategy avoids that because there is no "leap" from demo to real. If you trash the account in the early stages, it's no big deal to throw another $10 or so in to get it going again. If the account has become sizable, it means that you have traded well and consistently for some time, you know how to trade and therefore the odds of you trashing it are very long!

--- 帖子 #5046 ---
If your goal was 45 pips per week, instead of per day, it would take eight years to grow $30 to $1M. Lower that to 36 pips per week, and you are talking about 12 or 13 years. With consistency, astonishing success is just a matter of a little bit of patience. What Bigtent is showing you is that you can learn the consistency, in a very real environment, without having to risk very much at all. The method he's pointing out is priceless. There are two tricks to making it work, in my opinion. At the outset, you have to take the trading very seriously even though there is almost nothing at stake. This requires the seriousness of the compulsive gamer. Then (and Kostas is probably the one who can speak best on this topic now), when there is quite a bit at stake, you have to be able to treat the trading as if it were a game despite how much money is on the line. Ultimately, the money should become irrelevant, and the only issue is how well you are trading, not how much you are making.

Remember, I am using this setup on a 5 digit broker, and there is no problem. That's fine. The indicator shows the spread in points, and on 5 digit brokers, 1 pip is 10 points. You shouldn't have any problem with nuances like that, since they are your charts, your broker, and you should be familiar with what it means.

I'd be happy to hear more about advanced entries. But I think I should also explain something about the structure of the Table of Contents. If you look closely, some headings are indented more than others. I meant an indented heading to be a subheading for one that is less indented. Thus, under the heading advanced, there are the following types of advanced trades for discussion: M15 Touch Almost/M5 10 Touch, Scooped Up, Ping Pong, Clay's M1 Simple Dance, etc... Maybe I should have made the structure of the ToC more self explanatory? At one point, I had lots of levels and sublevels going down 3 or 4 tiers deep. Then I decided that that was really stupid and arcane, so I dumped the explicit outline format and flattened the structure quite a bit. And I might have lost some of the clarity in the process of simplifying.

--- 帖子 #5132 ---
Not really. It's a cool indicator called "gspot" (COUGH, COUGH, ). I use it only on my M5. Based on my observations about gaps which I have described in this thread before, price tends to fill the gaps in bars, sooner or later. So, I use it with the settings (0.7, 35, 500) and when I see a gap, I keep an eye on it as an added element for direction confirmation. I do NOT use it on it's own, but when I have the CHOROS elements ready (e.g. for a long bounce) and I see a gap upstairs then I use it as an additional confirmation and/or price target. P.S. From discussions with other traders, it seems that not everybody gets these gaps with their broker. My broker FXPro seems to be consistent in these along with some ECNs (e.g. I have confirmed with others on MB Trading and FinFx). So don't go start looking for other brokers and gaps, this is just something helpful to my trading but has nothing to do with CHOROS.

--- 帖子 #5192 ---
We discussed this a few times before, the fact that even at news time we can trade the CHOROS rules. The issue is the increased volatility at these times requires bigger SL , and one thing I hate is loosing capital. So I made the following guidelines for me: 1. At normal news time if I haven't completed my daily target, I reduce my regular lot size in half and I shoot for double the pips with double the SL 2. At NFP and Official Bank rates announcements, I reduce my lot size from 1/8 to 1/10 and I use a SL that is difficult to hit (but if it is taken out, I don't loose a lot of money). Yesterday was case 2, and the 54p were the equivalent of 6p. After that I performed two regular lot size +12p scalps and my total was 6+12+12=30p at which point I finished for the day.

--- 帖子 #5246 ---
And they make the spread on each of his trades, whether he wins or loses. That's their "commission", so as to speak. As I understand it, it's only with small sub-lot sized positions that they really have to cover the position. The full lots portion (16 of the 16.8) could be added/substracted from the dealer's market position as the trades are placed, and Kostas margin serves as the security for this. So, Kostas' winnings or losses could be passed straight through from the market to his account if he wins or vice-versa should he lose the trade, so the broker loses nothing. They still get the spread!

I played with EA's using a trailing stop and scaling in with trades. It worked like this.... As your trailing stop moved into profit that bit protected by the trailing stop is the "secured profit". Trades were then taken at a lot size that risked only a portion of the secured profit, so you would never turn a win into a loss. As the trades progressed, more trades were added and the compounding was mental! I made a demo trade at 2% risk that returned over 250% on a 5 minute chart..... but over the month the return was less than 200% because that was the only good trade! Problem was, like all trend follower EAs, it was nice when it got a nice run, but the whipsaws when it ranged soon ate away at the profits! Now to find a method that avoids the whipsaws, catches the trend early and follows it closely without blowing out the trailing stop. I heard you can find one of these EAs easily, just look between the eggs laid by a hen with teeth and the manure pile left by a rocking horse. Let me know when you see them!

--- 帖子 #5270 ---
The other day I was watching a documentary ("Human Ape") which examined the differences in intelligence between humans and apes. In one experiment, the scientists presented a box to a kid and then showed to her a sequence of moves to be repeated in order to get a candy from inside the box. The kid repeated the moves exactly as shown, and got the candy. The interesting part is that most of the moves shown to the kid were obviously unnecessary. The kid could have gotten the candy just by performing one simple movement. Yet, the kid repeated all the moves shown to her, even the unnecessary ones. Even more interesting is that when the same experiment was done with a chimpanzee, the chimp omitted all unnecessary moves and only performed the necessary one in order to get the candy! My initial reaction to this was WTF! The chimp can see that most moves are unnecessary and can use a shortcut, but the human kid can't ??? However, as explained in the documentary, this is EXACTLY what enables humans to create such an advanced civilization: Human kids are programmed to follow complex patterns that they learn from adults without questioning their usefuleness or practicality. This way they can quickly adopt complex patterns of learning and behavior because they don't have to re-invent the wheel. Let's transfer this to forex: It took me a long time to realize that the best way of learning how to trade is to EXACTLY copy a successful trader without questioning his methods. At least not until you become as proficient as that trader. By the way, this is valid in most other aspects of life: One should strive to copy the behavior of someone who is good at social relationships or the training of someone who is good at a certain sport etc. Only after one has already been successful it is advisable to try to improve on their methods. The reason is really simple: If you try to invent your own system or try to combine several different systems, you are actually not using the huge experience of successful traders and are trying to re-invent the wheel. So, a newbie should find a successful trader and imitate him closely. His initial focus should not be on trying to improve the system, but on trying to understand the thought processes of that trader. Of course if everyone was doing this successfully, then the markets would evolve and make certain systems obsolete. But then new successful systems would evolve and the same cycle would be repeated

--- 帖子 #5272 ---
Here is how I have been trading “touches”. This is not core dance and I am sharing my method with permission from kostas. My intention is never to divert you from main choros. Only intention is to help if possible. I have not been very successful with touch trades and only way for me to trade touches is to NOT trade them! However, I have tried to understand basic philosophy behind touch trades. That is to “enter on retracement”. Having understood this, I increase my strike rate by not entering at touch but only after I see a definite pattern. Then also i enter only after price breaks below previous candle and buy only after price breaks above previous high. High Momentum(impulsive) and low momentum (correcdtive): No fancy indicators here. Momentum is speed with which price is moving. This is shown by length of candles. A large candle shows high momentum and small candles show lack of momentum. I like to enter with high momentum against low momentum. Setup: These are same setups given in manual. Early in the trend two types of setups can be taken. A. Continuation pattern: Rejection bars are often good continuation setups. B. Failed reversals: Early in the trend, market will often try to reverse the move. This traps contra trend traders and any failure of such reversal is a good continuation signal. After prices have moved reasonably far in direction of trend, deeper corrections are expected. In such cases, above two entries are more likely to give false entries. We should rather expect a “complex correrction” after a deeper move. A complex correction is nothing but an a-b-c move. Essentially, it is a contra trend move in two legs with a small with trend leg in between. C: Reversals: When we see a reversal pattern in low momentum move we expect continuation of high momentum move. This gives good entry after an extended correction. Expect few failed reversal before major reversal. Entry points, SL : Stop loss entries are safest. It’s generally safe to place and SL entry order few ticks above/below setup patterns. Once entry is done, first stop loss can be placed in the other direction of setup. For examples, in a bearish rejection bar, place SL sell just below the low. Here is a rough GU 1H chart. Will post more charts if someone is intrested.

--- 帖子 #5277 ---
Interesting stuff. There is quite a lot there. We humans do a lot of stuff that is unnecessary, and mostly it's inherited cultural baggage. True story.... At a power station close to where I live, they had to add a sight glass to the side of a large, odd shaped water vessel. The engineer went away to do all the calcs, and when he came back a couple of days later proud of his results, he found the glass tube already mounted on the side of the vessel, and markings every so often showing how many litres were at that level, etc. He asked the tradesman how he did it, and the tradesman told him that he mounted the glass, measured and poured in so many litres, marked it off, and repeated! Sometimes education can cloud the issue until you can't see the forest for the trees! In regards to the copying a seasoned trader, sportsman, etc. There is some merit in this, but there is also another side of the coin. I'll use the sportsman example. Often, great sportsmen do not make great coaches, yet mediocre, less talented sportsmen that had to "work at it" often do. The reason is that the "edge" that make the great sportsmen great, is not actually transferable, as it "comes natural" to him. He cannot describe it nor can he understand why others cannot see it the way he does, etc. On the other hand, the sportsman who has less talent and had to work harder, does understand his charges' position and can therefore help them go forward. The same thing goes in learning in most spheres. The "expert" in the field is very often the worst teacher. Same thing applies to trading. There are traders who can trade successfully just looking at the naked chart. They do it intuitively. Most people will have no chance to learn that, as they can never have the other person's intuition. Put simply, you cannot transfer talent, intuition and the resulting discretion. This is why most people require a system, and some sort of indicators to use, but the problem is that there is always some discretion required. I think the real journey is to find a system or strategy that can expose and make the best of your personal talents and discretionary abilities. That's all systems and strategies really do. To borrow from Clay, you need to get the market to "play a tune that you can dance to" .... and that is a very personal thing, once you boil it down! Gees... we've become all deep and meaningful on this thread, and we're supposed to be dancing!

--- 帖子 #5331 ---
Be careful guys! We expect extreme volatility in the market today at 5:00 PM ET US no matter which way the Greece Confident vote goes. Please see http://video.cnbc.com/gallery/?video=3000028617 and http://www.guardian.co.uk/business/2...-moment-crisis for more information. Risks Associated with Trading Off-Exchange Retail Foreign Currency During Economic News Announcements As with all major economic releases, there could be significant price volatility with this announcement. Currency spreads will typically widen just before the release and will remain wide for a few minutes after. If the announcement is a shock to the consensus estimate, the price of the currency pair could gap significantly. For example, the price on the EURUSD trading at 1.2820 - 1.2822 just before release could gap up 60 pips to 1.2880 - 1.2882, without any available prices available between the price of 1.2820 and 1.2882. A Buy Stop placed before the announcement at 1.2830 would turn into a Market Order and would be filled at the prevailing price 1.2882. The same would be true with a Sell Stop. Approximately four years ago we saw a gap of approximately 200 pips on the GBPUSD on a Non-Farm Payroll announcement. While this is an extreme example, it nevertheless is a possibility with trading during economic announcements. Consequently, plan on the spreads widening and, if you are trading with a Buy or a Sell Stop entry order, do not anticipate being filled at your entry price. You will be filled at the prevailing market price after the release, which could be significantly different from your desired price of your entry order. Please be advised that due to the volatility of price fluctuations during the news, it is possible to see a delay in execution due to the additional verification necessary for each trade. We would like to thank you for your continued support and wish you success in your trading. Best Regards, IBFX

OK, many questions here. First, let me state that my MM has changed from the time the thread has started, till now. 1. My daily target is now 1%. 2. SL is usually larger than TP. With the winning ratio of the CHOROS trades I can afford that. But I am following the trade closely. With the first sign of price hesitation I will close it even at 6-7 pips. Otherwise, I will let it run for more. 3. Rarely, I am able to capture my daily target with one trade. 4. I do not let the trade hit the SL if I think I screwed up. For example, if as I enter the trade I see the price run against me 6-10 pips I will probably manually exit, unless I thing it's a head-fake. So, 2 losses for me doesn't mean -36p. 6. Sometimes, when I see a good confluence target and I need to leave the office, I will put a relatively big SL at a safe distance. 7. I am not stopping at 2 losses in a row. If I do get 3 losses in a row (very very rare) I am definitely stopping.

--- 帖子 #5362 ---
Many people have adopted a fixed scale for their charts to deal with this issue. Following Kostas, I use 50 pips for M1, 100 for M5, 150 for M15 and 200 for H1. The angles given in the manual, in my opinion, are an imprecise guideline. There are many factors that can change the appearance of the angles without altering the underlying data. If you even use auto scaling, the chart will tend to overemphasize moves in flat markets, and to overemphasize moves on charts that display fewer bars. Thus, I think the best way to approach this is to use consistent chart scales and chart sizes.

--- 帖子 #5419 ---
In this trade, when taken, the MAs are actually fairly steep, but they have just turned. So I'm not sure that this is the fault of the trade. Or, maybe it might be worth noting that steepness is not just something measured at the moment of the trade. You also have to look at how wavy the lines have been recently. A simpler way to arrive at the same caution is simply to look at the higher time frame. A cardinal rule is to avoid trades when the MAs are strongly diverging. And higher time frames generally carry more weight than lower time frames. Here, on the H1, the 35 and 50 are very strongly diverging. For me, this is a warning signal against taking this touch on the lower time frame. Survivor, I wonder if you took the H1 35/50 EO cross and reverse here. It's a really good example. (The cross and reverse trade I'm talking about is a trade where you fade a candle that crosses both the 35 and 50, with almost no wick.)

Have you run the A_SetLotSize script beforehand? A_SetLotSize: This script sets the size of Lots you will be trading for each session. IT MUST BE SET FIRST for each session or the next two scripts (A_Buy &amp; A_Sell) which execute a buy and a sell WILL NOT work. It is pre-set to a 15 Pip SL but when clicked launches a pop up you can use to change the risk and the SL setting if you want to. That is not recommended.

--- 帖子 #5460 ---
Hi Kostas, Thank you for your kind words. I think the discussion about the scripts doesn’t need to be continued; however this issue is of course related to Choros since these scripts are the core scripts of Choros. I’ve found the solution and share it with others who might face the same problem in the future. The reasons of my problem that the buy and sell scripts didn’t work, were the following two points: · Some brokerages execute your market order in MetaTrader as “Market execution” . This is good regarding you will not get requotes – your market order will be executed at the actual market price for sure, without the need to modify your order price if the price moves in a fast pace. However, in this execution mode of MetaTrader the MetaTrader terminal doesn’t allow you to set Stop Loss and/or Take Profit orders while opening your trade (you have to attach SL and TP later by modifying your trade). At such brokerages (e.g. Oanda, IBFX) the original buy and sell scripts won’t work until you modify the code as I described above. · I set the leverage too low. For the suggested risk percent (1.5% per trade equals 3% per position consisting of 2 trades) and Stop Loss (15 pips) to work, you need approx. 1:30 leverage. If you want to trade two currencies at the same time or apply a higher risk per position or a lower SL of e.g. 10 pips, you need at least 1:50 leverage, preferably more. So you could face problems at US brokerages where the leverage is limited by law to 1:50 at most. You could get along with 1:50, but you will definitely need at least 1:50 leverage. Solution: Firstly make sure of you have 1:30 leverage at the least. Secondly use a broker which apply “Instant execution” for market orders in MetaTrader, or modify the scripts or use other scripts. Bigtent, thank you for your help. It’s very kind of you. I will try your scripts.

--- 帖子 #5490 ---
Salute, I have to continue with my findings regarding the scripts in order others could draw a lesson from it. A_SetLotSize – it’s not enough to execute this once per session. If you trade different pairs, and not every pairs are xxxUSD, the A_Buy and A_Sell scripts will trade an incorrect risk percent. You can execute the A_SetLotSize script as much as you want; it doesn’t do any harm. If you want to see the lot size per trade prior to execute the Buy/Sell scripts, you could insert the following line into the A_SetLotSize script, before the “if(Lots &gt; 0)…” line: Comment (DoubleToStr(Lots,2)); You should execute the A_SetLotSize script every time you would trade a pair where the quote currency (BASE/ QUOTE ) is not the same as in your previous trade. I recommend you to use the scripts created and used by Bigtent. You can find them here: http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...98#post4672798

--- 帖子 #5509 ---
"Learning by Imitation in Humans Humans are genetically predisposed to learn from each other through imitation. This is especially true and even inevitable with babies and small children. In fact, the human brain as well as the brain of primates and birds contains mirror neurons that fire when an animal observes the actions of another animal, especially another animal of the same species. Neuroscientists speculate that these mirror neurons are important for understanding the actions of other people, and for learning new skills by imitation. Learning by imitation helps the individual human quickly learn basic skills such as tying their shoe to survival skills such as learning how and what to eat. Furthermore, learning by imitation allows humans to bequeath traditions of culture, music, art, and sport from one generation to another. Many behavioral scientists have come to see learning by imitation as an important expression of intelligence."

--- 帖子 #5522 ---
Here’s another way to solve the weekend spread problem. This drove me crazy, too, until I found this solution. 1) Find the folder in your MT4 installation files which contains your account name. It will be under the History folder. My broker is Oanda , so in my case it is “C rogram FilesOANDA - MetaTraderhistoryOANDA-MT4 Practice” 2) In this folder you will find a file called symbols.sel. This file contains the current spread info. 3) At a time during the day when spreads are normal, save a copy of this file. You will need to close MT4 to save it or you will get an error that the file is in use. 4) Now on the weekend, open MT4, go to File/Login, and uncheck the “Save account information” checkbox. Click the Login button. 5) Close MT4 6) Now copy the symbols.sel file (that you saved previously) to the “C rogram FilesOANDA - MetaTraderhistoryYourAccountName” folder. You will want to overwrite the existing file with the saved file. 7) Open MT4 and DO NOT LOG IN TO YOUR ACCOUNT ONLINE! You will see the normal spreads and now you can run the demo. 8) When the market opens just go to File/Login and log in to your live account. it will update the symbols.sel file with current spreads and you are back to normal. Hope this helps!

--- 帖子 #5576 ---
This issue has been discussed in here before. My take on it is that rarely you get the same quality signal on many currencies. Several times I have seen that both EU and GU give the same signal (e.g. M15 35/50 bounce) but in all cases one signal was better quality due to other factors (e.g. confluence with RN, other TF MAs, etc.). So in cases where you get the same signal in more than one currency, choose the best confluence signal and trade only that currency, full lot size.

--- 帖子 #5617 ---
We had more discussions about this in the thread. Read MORE carefully. For one last time: - Touch is when the price barely touches the MA and quickly withdraws in the original trend direction. This is why I mostly use M1 to get into these. Sometimes the touch appears after the bar closes due to the MA movement. So to catch all of them you should be willing to take some risk and "guess" where the MA could go when the bar closes. - Bounce is when the price stays on the MA for a few bars before giving a rejection formation and goes back, sort of "bounces" from the rubber band (MA). Here I use M5 to see the rejection early.

--- 帖子 #5618 ---
Many times, doing a late evaluation of a chart will not reveal what was happening with the touches at real time. We have already discussed a lot about touches that appear after the price has continued its trend, while in real time there was no touch. And sometimes there will never appear a touch even though the trade was valid in real time, like in the following USDCHF trade I had earlier. That's why it's very difficult to make an accurate analysis of a chart after the bars have printed. ETA: I could make an indicator that would mark the points where price touched the 10EMA projection for already printed bars, although that would only serve backtesting purposes.

--- 帖子 #5643 ---
The way I see it price is always being constrained by something: S/R levels, MAs, Bollinger bands, trendlines, pitchforks etc... they are all visual indicators trying to draw a constrainment line. When price is ranging in a tight area then the constrainment lines are flat, and they get steeper and steeper as the trend increases. The idea behind most systems is to trade close to the constrainment indicator and towards the direction of the trend - however small that trend may be. So basically the whole trading should be a simple idea: For starters, you can set a take profit that is equal to the stop loss (say 15 pips), and just enter at a point where your take profit is more probable to be hit than your stop loss. You only have to overcome the spread to be profitable. That's the theory, anyway

--- 帖子 #5745 ---
It's not really that hard to devise a logic behind this. What the program does is simply checking a few bars behind and adding checkmarks to various properties for each bar. Is it small enough (as a percentage of the ATR) ? Does it close above or below the MA ? Does it have a wick crossing the MA ? Is the slope of the MA in the correct direction ? Is the slope increasing from one bar to the next ? Do the bars form higher highs/lower lows ? Etc. Then it's just a matter of setting a limit for the percentage of bars that should be having each property, and determining what values are good. Eg, if you want to find what defines a "small slope" for each MA, you can either do some tests and measure what you think is a good slope and then hardcode it in the program, or perhaps find a formula for calculating the slope values for any MA. Basically the slope is nothing more than a percentage movement. For example, I have noticed that as a general rule when the timeframe increases by 4, the average bar increases by 2. Ie, you may expect that going from 15M to 60M you will having bars twice as large on average.

--- 帖子 #5781 ---
Yes, that's exactly what it means, it sets the standard for an ideal "by the rules" trade, meaning that whenever this condition is not met the probabilities of your trade will decrease in some level... that doesn't mean you won't find times when rule wasn't met and the trade would've worked. But you must remember trading is a probability bussiness and we must do everything in our hand to increase our probabilities. So here's a graphic example of a perfect by the rules 10 EMA touch trade, notice too how the more times 10 EMA has been touched, the probabilities of our trade being succesful decreases, that's why it's recommended to take first or second touch of the 10, not further touches... Hope this helps!

--- 帖子 #5786 ---
That's a difficult question and the answer is never going to be clear. An easy answer would be to reset the counter when the 5EMA crosses the 10EMA, but there are cases like the one below where you must reset the counter even if the 5EMA doesn't cross the 10EMA. In such cases you just watch the trade fading and you reset the counter when the distance between the 5EMA and the 10EMA becomes approximately what it was when the trend started. In most cases "we just see it", but trying to code it made me look for more clearly expressed criteria.

--- 帖子 #5812 ---
Too early for this. Only the other day I coded the functions that will record each signal in a file, together with details about it and whether it would have been a win or a loss. But now I have to finalize the scoring system in order to start getting any meaningful statistics. The price action system is also in place now and it is possible for the program to wait for price confirmation before giving a signal. It detects double top/bottoms, pinbars, OEBs, hammers, or simple price reversals at swing top or bottoms, in all timeframes. The most important change I am about to make is alter the way that the trend affects the quality of the signal. I tend to believe that trying to jump on a very fast moving train is almost as dangerous as standing on its way. So, instead of increasing the signal quality as the 10EMA slope increases, I will probably consider as the best signal the one where the 50, the 35 and the 10 are almost parallel. Actually this is what the 2-bar touch rule accomplishes: It makes sure that the 10EMA is not too steep at the moment of the trade, avoiding the uncertainty of explosive retracements.

--- 帖子 #5838 ---
During the weekend I finalized the conversion of the program to an EA so that I can now do some backtesting. There are no trades yet, just signals recorded in an Excel file together with their details and whether they would be wins or losses. While I was doing the first tests, I noticed something very peculiar. A pattern of very frequent losses in a situation that I was expecting would be a win. As we know, such a pattern is equally useful to a winning one because if it is consistent one can simply reverse the direction of the trade. At first I thought that I had something wrong with the spread, but it was ok. Then I thought it should be a programming mistake but found nothing. I made the same test with different pairs, but only one pair showed this behaviour. I backtested it with tick data for 3 years, and it showed a consistent losing pattern of about 85% which is amazing. Even then I wasn't convinced so I looked myself at as many trades as I could, even using charts from different brokers. I couldn't find a single mistake. So now I am really preoccupied with this because if it is true it will be simply fantastic. There was an average of 4 trades per day for this pattern, each for an average sl/tp of 20 pips. If I reverse the direction of the trades, and if 3 are wins and one is a loser, this will mean a totally mechanical way of getting an average of 40 pips per day. But I'm not saying anything more because I still am not convinced it is true, an 85% rate over the course of 3 years is too much for a computer program. However I don't know what else to do in order to find the mistake, I think I have done everything possible. We'll see...

--- 帖子 #5864 ---
I'm not an expert on scoop ups, but I think it's different from a cross and retest, this is what I understand of each: A scoop up trade is when PA starts to come up and can't close below 10 ma, so it eventually crosses 35/50 and closes above them. So a scoop up trade would be taken before the cross of the 35/50 in the expectance that PA will cross them and go higher. A cross and retest, as its name says is taken after the price has broken through 35/50, then you'll wait for a retest of this levels (remember we use this MA's as dynamic S/R) and at this point of the retest you enter the trade in the direction of the cross... I hope I made myself clear and this helps you... have a great week mate!

--- 帖子 #5919 ---
I do not want to show off, please consider this as sharing information for our benefit, but this week was good for me. This week on Monday, my first trade was a looser but after that one until yesterday I had 5 winners and 2 BE (One lucky trade included). All days ended with profits. Today I had 2 wins and 3 losses, the good thing was that the losses where controlled and the winners where bigger meaning that today ended with a little profit too but I stopped for the day after those three losses. This week my account has grown 14.5% so I´m very satisfied with the outcome. Here are some things I find useful to remember: Do not rely only on MAs, always look for confluence with levels like Pivots, PPA or RN (In that order). Always look at Higher and Lower Time Frames before entries to have an idea on where the price is going. Always look to the left to see where price have bounced before (PPA - Previous Price Action). If price bounced there once, it will probably bounce there again. Use those PPA levels to fine tune your entries and exits. I find that H4 swings are very strong PPA levels for entries. And even M15 swings are useful when setting your targets. Even my lucky trade this week reacted well to a H4 PPA resulting in profit. In order of preference I use the following levels for confirmation, considering the first as the strongest: 1. Pivots (Calculated at NY close) 2. H4 PPA 3. RN Look for CHOROS Signals (Touches, Constarinments, etc.) in confluence with those levels for higher probability trades. Last but not the least, consider Demand and Supply Areas (I’m not talking about Support and Resistance levels). I’m talking about areas where you can expect a lot of buyers (Demand) or a lot of Sellers (Supply). You can have an idea of where those areas are looking to the left, for example if you see a huge break out UP at some level, it means that there where more buyers than sellers there. So, after some days or weeks, when price is going down into that area again, you can expect some reaction that can go from dozens of pips to a complete trend reversal. Have those areas in mind so when price gets there pause, wait, and consider changing form looking for SHORT CHOROS Signals to start looking for LONG CHOROS Signals or vice versa. Happy trading

--- 帖子 #5924 ---
Well, at the end of the day important is to find out where and why most traders act and in what direction: that's the reason of any trend move. The most "levels" come together (Confluence) the most % probability we have to get into a move together with other trades. So welcome S/R welcome Pivot, Fibo or whatever helps us to make money BUT I just wanted to give a further input to your consideration, based on my personal point of view (therefore of course very subjective, so take it with the due care): try to start to look at the MAs as they would be actually moving S/R levels. They are that, and move accordingly together with the trend. Price can bounce of S/R levels (Touch trades) or can test and retest them before proceeding further (Constrainments). I saw that price reacts to Dance/Choros MAs more times than not (if you keep in mind all the other rules of course). That's why I feel confortable with this great Strategy. (thanks again Jedi Masters Clay and Kostas)

--- 帖子 #5938 ---
I usually wait to see rejection bars at a reaction point. I mostly use M5 but at touches I use M1. For example, let's say I see price approaching a RN confluenced with H1 10 from below and I expect shorting it. As soon as the M5 gives a rejection I enter at the close (e.g. if I see a pinbar I will enter at the close of that bar). For touches, I enter when I see rejection from M1.

--- 帖子 #6060 ---
The futures trade lower than spot because there is no carry cost in futures. To get equivalent spot prices, you factor in the interest rates as seen at: http://www.cmegroup.com/equivalents and you'll get the spot price.

--- 帖子 #6089 ---
When I graduated a smart classmate of mine that did civil engineering conjoint with a finance degree, got a trading job at Macquarie Investment bank of Australia. About 2 years ago I got a chance to ask him about it. He said something along the line that the banks allow their traders to be flexible in their trading and each trader will be responsible for a few markets. However the banks are very very strict with certain rules concerning risk and are not afraid to fire on the spot for any mistakes. The sticking point he told me was, it is not unusual for successful bank traders to quit their job thinking they can duplicate their success at home. When they become a home trader they usually don't adhere to the strict trading rules set by the banks like money management etc. They lose enough money at home to give up and apply for their job back again. When they are at their job the second time they suddenly start making money because they are bound by the strict rules. Irony at its finest. It was certainly a defining point for me in my own trading. Edit: Oh yeah he did say that he can make much much higher percentage of returns if he was trading at a smaller size and not with the kind of volume imposed by the bank. So I really think the small boys like us have some advantages. Edit: I just remember another thing he told me, the bank impose a rule on him, he cannot have more than X% of his funds being risked at any one time from his total open trades. After Y% amount of lost in a day which he said at that time haven't happen to him yet, he have to stop trading for some time.

--- 帖子 #6226 ---
Hi 2121, my suggestion is also always watch at the Higher TF. M15 alone may be good, but the % of a successful trade increase strongly if there are signals also on the higher TF as well. This is the " Confluence ". Here we have a 35 1st touch on M15 good for something around 30 pips. M5 was actually over the 35/50, but on H1 it was the 1st touch of the Ema10 and if you look at H4 you will see that price had just crossed 35/50 and came back to retest them. (and it is still playing in that area) IMHO an Higher TF dictates the law ! Actually the best would be to take on M15 only trades according with the direction of H1, H4, Daily. The point is: the most TF are approaching to a signal, the most % your trade will be a winner ! I am not sure if I could explain well Surely other better Traders will give advice. Anyway: read, follow the charts, follow the signals, always look at the Higher TF's and you will master it too. ah, nearly forgotten: Be Patient! and wait always for the best signals. 1 or 2 per day and you could be "there" soon.

If you search "angle" in this thread, you'd find out that the dancers have abandoned the angle measurement but switched to "fixed scale" measurement, i.e., always have 150 pips range for M15 etc. Also some dancer mentioned that you'll need to study successful/failed trades to find some angle which makes you feel comfortable. --- 帖子 #6297 ---
I've been doing this quite consistently, I enter the choros trade(touch constrainment whatever) at a buy/sell stop order after a price action unfolds, bull bear engulfing, Double top Lower close, inside bar and pin bars. I exit my first half at the next previous price concentration where there are a lot of wicks. I move the 2nd to BE. My second half I try to let it ride. But usually get stopped out at BE. But when it wins I have been getting it out at an RR of at least 5. Once it went to 12. And historically I have seen one going over 20. On my last 26 trades on the 1H 30M and 15M I have made no losses and 4 home runs. However it is very common for me to exit the first trade for just 5-10 pips. Sometimes I feel like a scalper. If I see constrainments in the higher TF 2H or 4H I always wait for a bar action to unfold in the lower timeframe and then the same trick I told you with the exit..... Trading between SR is very reliable. EDIT: One other thing, I won't take any trade that has a lot of previous price concentration in front of it. I like my trades to have space right in front of it where there is no SR because price is almost guaranteed to get there usually in 1 bar. (that is where I exit my 1st trade) And if your trade can't cover your spread for a profit you're screwed. Yeah in that way the market for a short while becomes very predictable. I can't believe it sometimes. (the future can be predicted, why would anyone play the lottery lol) I didn't mention another thing, I need 3-4 price confirmations to get in. I am relatively picky.

--- 帖子 #6300 ---
Last thing I will say. You can take the idea from my previous post and apply it to the weekly and daily charts with no problem. Use previous price action and bar action to predict the swing and enter with a sell order. Exit the way I mention(1st order at the next PPA, SR, pivot etc). SL is always the high/low of the bar action. In fact the larger TF are easier to identify and trade than the smaller ones. You can buy Low and sell High for most swings if you confirm with PPA and Bar action. Trade any market with this method. You will notice that sideway markets On higher TF are more predictable after a bar action in some ways than trending. The problem with sideway markets with 15m or smaller TF is the spread..... Otherwise it is just as predictable. I will stop here lest I get out of topic too much in this thread. All I am pointing is, this method I am telling is not some secret method, it is universal and works anywhere with most TF and if you got a robust strategy like choros it can add to your edge.

--- 帖子 #6312 ---
I’m using a version of visual editor that I have modified to fit my needs and I have to admit that I experimented the same behavior that tonny47 mentions. The thing is that I realized that is not a problem on visual editor (at least on the version I have), the problem is moving the SL level when the current price is too close to that level. I have debugged that behavior and find out that, when the price is too close to the SL level (like 3 pips) and you move the line on visual editor, then visual editor sends the order to the broker correctly, but the broker rejects the order because the price was too close, then visual editor moves back the SL line to the original place because there is where the SL level is after the order was rejected by the broker. I assume that when price is to close to the SL level, the same thing can happen no matter what tool we are using or even trying to modify the SL level manually. EDIT: As a side note, regarding modifying SL and TP levels, Easy Order (The tool that Kostas is using) is a lot better that visual editor. The thing is that with visual editor you can send several orders to the broker while you are dragging the SL or TP line, but with EasyOrder you will send only on order the moment you release the mouse button after dragging the line.

Compliance. Yeah Bar action is what Haydel described sorry for the confusion. Always wait for a bar action and Always enter with a stop order at the low or high, no exception except for 1H constrainments. Always take your first TP at the next price concentration , pivot, RN etc. Make sure the distance can cover your spread btw. If a bar action (pin bar etc) is properly positioned, rejecting at least a few key S or R , fibs, divergence whatever price usually always react quickly and race to the next S or R maybe 95% of the time, I haven't done my stats(I am planing too) but it sure feels like it. That's it, simple. No black magic involved. Be picky and don't be afraid to walk off a half good setup because they happen almost every day on the 15m, 1H and 30M with a few pairs when I look back for a few months. They happen once a month for daily charts perpair and they happen at least once a year or two per pair on a monthly chart.( Do a visual backtest and count for yourself ) There is so many opportunities, don't be afraid to walk away from a bad deal and don't be afraid to take your TP at a guaranteed spot. On the daily and weekly a good pin bar by itself is quite reliable if you place a stop order at the lo/hi even if you don't consider PPA. I didn't want to talk too much about this because this is not by the rules anymore, so Kostas please bear with me for 1 post. I also don't feel qualified to start a thread because all my info is from this forum, I didn't made it up or discover anything. I just found that if it is applied to any good strategy the edge will be magnified. (Try it on a bolinger band, it blew me away) Edit: Ah I did not mention, to further increase your odds look for the same thing on the higher timeframe, and you can always spot areas where price are ready to sometimes jump a few hundred pips in a day or 2. Go to the lower timeframe and do the same thing the R:R can be fantastic. I can't believe traders get paid for this form of manual labor.... It's got to be the highest form of paid manual labor in the world for some trader with some account size.... I hope it helps, if it doesn't than I am probably missing something.

Hey KK, I think you might have what we call "Ceguera de Taller", in english it might be "workshop blindness" tho' I don't know the exact term... anyway it's an Industrial Engineering term that describes when workers inside a given industry will obtain the same bad results, same flaw in quality or whatever and they can't find the reason or origin of this problem, and it is usually solved by putting someone completley new to analise the process and find the flaw and also by taking the workers out of their working places and their common activities for some time, so when they come back they may have fresh perspectives... So, you can do one or both of those, look for someone you know and trust to check on your trading and tell you what you're doing wrong and take some time off, for two or three weeks, and then come back like you've forgotten all you've been doing 'till now and start with only basic Choros rules and applying some of the concepts brought here by Kostas, asos, Survivor or Bin's latest posts... Maybe this will help, my best KK, have a great weekend!

--- 帖子 #6346 ---
sticking by YOUR rules is the hardest part, but practiced enough should eventually become natural. when i say YOUR rules i mean the Entry moment and the Exits/or trail of a stop. i dont mention the Dance/Choros rules because there are only 3 types of trades and even if followed blindly without discression will give you more than 50% of wins. but my biggest problem were the entries and exits. It was bugging me what Kostas says about "i watch M1 action, i take the M5 signal", by watching these smaller TFs you can see if by approaching an area of interest you get some reverse action going (buying/selling). this is a kind of confirmation that there is going to be a reaction at the area you are targeting to enter. usualy people are anxious that they will miss the trade and jump in early, thats why you get all that jumpiness in price as you approach such areas. so this creates 2 problems, will you jump in early too by fear you will lose the trade, or too early risking a larger drawdown? this is where your discression and rules about entries jump in and its really a personal thing. lately i have managed to "constrain" myself and take later entries when i almost see the reversal in M1. this allow for smaller drawdown and tighter SL. now Exits. i believe you need to have rules there too so as the price jumps up and down you are emotionless and stick with what your rules tell you. afterall, by entering you have done your work to the best of your judgement, now that you are in the trade nothing else is in your hand other than managing it. so this is why i have set these 3 rules for my exit strategy and they work fine. overall in a week i get say 15 wins 2 Losers (of about 10 pips each) and 2-3 BE. but believe it or not even so they are clear and simple i still fail sometimes to follow them 100% sometimes and these are the times i get them to hit my SL usualy. these are the trades i let slip under my rules, under my BE and head for my SL. just remember, these are for trading with 0.1 lot. when i will be able to trade larger i will use partial closes and trailling the partial left as Binyamin describes in his post. sorry if i bore you by the long post. have a great weekend everyone.

For touch trades (with no PA confirmation), when you have time, read the Clay's touch examples in his Dance thread, he like touch trade a lot more than Kostas1, you can see how he managed those trades in real-time with full explanations. One key idea I can share is that, when you learn a type of trading method, you have to learn it fully, including how to determine the amount of SL, how to TP, when to avoid, etc., not just the entry visual patterns. If you learn it partially, your edge is not clear. It is like learning to cook a dish, you need to following the full recipe, not some. You can change and develop something yourself, but again it has to be a full story, not partial. Another thing is don't expect to have no loss to be successful, otherwise it is hard to go forward. kostas1 is doing just more than 70%.

For example, you take all the M15 bars over a time period. Then you just look for trends of consecutive bars and you count the number of bars in the trend. Dear KK007, this will be a long post for an appreciated fellow trader, and probably many will just jump on the next post because this is too long (I would probably do the same) given that : 1) I am faaaar away from judging anybody, for the still small experience I think to have 2) I always (firstly) speak to myself too when giving any advice or opinion 3) from your posts it is clear that you HAVE a good technical knowledge of what your handling with, and it makes me somehow "angry" to see that a knowledge like yours is living a moment of "disappoint", because what you deserve is TONS more winning trades that those.... 4) I deeply like and appreciate your way to open your thoughts to us all, because I think they often are thoughts each one of us has or had more than once. That's for me a step to success too... I would like to add a possible point to think a while about.... Many experienced traders say that you should go down to trade a lower timeframe only when you MASTER already its higher one.... Even more some say that you should start by the higher ones before going down. We may be one day ready to study complex unstable molecules formations, but I guess we first need to have an high degree of knowledge of the basic physics and chemistry...am I wrong here ? Look at Clay, or Endroute: Jedi Masters of knowing the MAs, Price Action, PSYCHOLOGY, Money Management and all the well know Tools or our same Passion..for them is probably now the same thing to trade an H4 or an M5. But are their M5 or even M1 Strategies not caming to us from an EXPERIENCED point of (clear) View of Price's Behavior after having been working for centuries on Higher TFs and on their Connections between each other ? It seems that you are working much in M5, but why actually ? Hurry to get a set up ? Fair to miss one ? Or even some ? (it is ABSOLUTELY not a critic, it is only a real and open question to you) Also (again only question and not critic): why do you never show the "bigger picture" of your charts on more than one TF ? Show us what you think when you enter, based on more than one TF (it would be only good for yourself, not for us all). I think that Choros, Dance and several other Strategies of serious and really possible Success base their "Entry Rules" ALSO on the point that : The more CONFLUENCE you have on your entry Set Up, the HIGHER is your winning % probability. The Edge is in what the most people will "probably" do at that moment in time and Price. If we do not have AT LEAST a confluence of Choros "signals" on more tha n one TF (not even yet touching the matter of Fibo, PA, TL, Divergence Confluences too) how can we say : That will be a winner ? It is for me a matter of a kind of common sense, of guessing what will be the behavior of the higher possible nr of Traders (using the different strategies). That's for me the "secret" of Confluence. (and actually for this reason I do not yet clearly understand why some succesful traders do not want to explain their strategies...because to me that's like thinking that if not only me, but 10 other people too will buy a Kg of Bread in my same shop, then the price of Bread in my whole Continent COULD perhaps get higher...) ...if we compare Trades to Girls and you want to pick up the really BEST one...I think you need a certain Time and Criterions to evaluate your possible partner... (just picking up always the first you see on the street may be seriously dangerous for your health too...) Trading a M15 is already like if you would choose a girl only because you saw she has beatiful green eyes and blond hair (I Love green eyes ad blond hair...my Wife has ) But trading a M5 is like you'll do it because you've only heard someone saying she could have green eyes... Not reliable enough in my humble opinion. I noticed that you had the best "calls" in your here previuos posts looking at M15 instead of M5. We are ALL impatient, that's the biggest problem and reason of losses. We see a Pin Bar with a body long like the spike (your M5 10 Touch), but that's not a good Pin bar... We WANT to see any reason to enter a trade, but we (I) should perhaps look more for reasons NOT to enter a trade...I ask me what would change thinking that way... 40 trades on M1 or M5 of which 30 are loosers and the resting 10 are good for a scalp of 3 pips each....is not worth of your concentration.... You can have more time to evaluate, to decide your SL and your TP with a ONLY one good H1 set up for the same 30 pips. My thought here is that you perhaps in this moment (like many of us often) are walking inside a labyrinth and cannot watch it from upside down. Like still trading after 2 or 3 losses in a row. We just lose the biggest picture and get victims of Mr. Fear and Mr. Greedy. Who doesn't know them ? I guess that's why Clay says: Walk away for a while. Because after we can see the labyrinth from 100 meters high and clearly see where the exit was. Practice Patience. I think this is what iForex was meaning with his 2 Trades per day. Force you to look only at 2 Girls a day... After a while you'll only look for the best 2 of the day. It is only an example for getting more picky at your trades. Better if you chose them from an Higher TF and only if in accordance with at least other 2 or 3 kind of Signal. Or even just sit one day in front of the moving chart without taking any trade at all... I guess it could provide some thoughts of experience inside us. If you won't see any serious really BEAUTIFUL Girl that day...what's up ? Next. Thanks for your sharing KK007, I feel you'll "make it yours".

--- 帖子 #6504 ---
++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++ I rarely post on this thread but a few issues need to be addressed, imho. Unless you are trading daily or 4hr, avoid the news. Times to trade? My rules for 15, 5 &amp; 1m are "Only trade the 1st three hours of the FF/London Session &amp; the same for the NY Session". Price action is usually curtailed 2 1/2 to 3 hours after these sessions beginnings. Also this gives you plenty of time away from the charts. I may begin setting up 30-60 minutes prior to session beginnings to note trend and draw helper; i.e., fibs, trend lines (very important) and note s/r levels. Do not overlook s/r levels from the 1m charts. Quite often they will tell you exactly where current buyers/sellers are lurking. One of the reasons I strongly urge certain thread policies, such as price targets, is because many times you are looking to make only a handful of pips. Think about this; How many: • 10 pip runs, • 20 pip runs, • 30 pip runs, • 40 pip runs, etc., Happen daily? Your chances of seeing +10 in you win column is INFINITELY more likely than seeing +30. Most of my trades have a set profit target. If I make that target, I'm out. If price continues in my direction, SO WHAT? Worrying about STUPID stuff like that is what muddles your thoughts. Trading, like life in general, gives you what you expect. Expect a turd on you dinner plate, and guess what? So much psychology is present in trading that we must do all we can to keep it upbeat. When I begin a session feeling funky, I get funk. If I take a good trade and it fails, I know I did what I should be doing and move on to the next opportunity. ~end rant Darryl "Today, I would like to become the man my dog thinks I am." ~ Jack Thomson - Entrepreneur

--- 帖子 #6533 ---
I observe that too. The probability of price moving to the next PPA after 1 of those pins or engulfing disregarding the trend(and if the trade is taken with a limit order) is more or less the same for 15m, 30m, H1 and H4 TF for every month this year except last august. I find the consistency a bit strange. In fact you can just blindly trade these PA in those TF I mention and come out quite well. The stats and the conclusions I mention was the result of the backtest I did and can vary with different individual so please don't trade every pin or engulfing unless you have tested it yourself. In the backtest I performed I use a pin bar and a engulfing indicator(all trades are entered when the indicator decides) just to make sure the consistency and reduce human biasness. However the exit was based upon my own interpretation of the PPA, RN, pivot etc. The consistency of these patterns got me extremely obsessed for a while. It went against everything I believe about the market.

Hi Sitting Duck, nice to see that there are more of us who just cannot resist to come back to the charts even after a longer time , welcome back to the Fight! I agree with Asos thoughts, about the 35/50 being flat and too much separated from each other, but even more about trading M15 on the simulator. It is a good training for sure, but it cannot be Highly reliable, because you somehow miss "the bigger picture". As you say a Trader surely need some skills on top of the "rules" of the preferred strategy. I am always more and more coming to the Idea that those skills are actually to may "read" the most possible "confluence" of possible Traders action at a certain given point in time in the charts (when you are thinking to enter a trade). That is given IMHO firstly surely by looking at Higher Time Frames as Asos1 says and also at other possible confluences. One is surely Price Action, another can be a broken T/L and for sure previous S/R Levels. I had a look at the moment of your trade and I have also some thoughts which I hope can help you to look with more details in the next ones. I have below 2 pics. 1) M15 alone: look at the yellow line (or at the white stars of the FDM Indicator).If you would have taken the just previous 2 bars retracement to the EMA you would have got a winner even being that level already a "danger zone" Too strong and long retracement bars mean a power behind, not a momentary breath of the price. Loot at the Price Action after that retracement (which already closes as a neutral bar) : a Pin Bar, we are in a full indecision area.Somebody would take that pin bar in connection to the Touch on H1 as a great Short Signal. I didn't show it on the M15 chart, but the bar you entered long was just breaking the Long TL on that TF. 2) Higher TF. No words here. The price is still running down. Dangerous here to look for longs anwyay. So, just as recap: 1) Always trade with the Bigger Trend. M15 is a great way to act fast and cash your daily pips, but is not the biggest picture of the actual trend and it requires ability and experience to manage. So I suggest to respect the Higher TF always, until they Sunshine Clearly show that the trend changed at their levels too. 2) after a cross of price and 10 EMA over the 35/50 tend to take only the first retracement to the 10 and to the 35/50. Kostas1 made a G R E A T post about this. Alone with those words, TIME available, patience and MM I think a Trader could live from Trading. I would copy past that post's Link but I don't know where it exactly is.... Look for that. Too long post again...I am not very good in "Zip Compressing " my thoughts...but I hope it may help you in the future. Try to look the same thing from several different point of view. It comes with the Time and Experience. One day you'll just be able to set in your mind the EMAs in front or behind the price at your will. To have the complete Panorama of the Higher TF too. To see TL breaks, and Pin Bars or other Price Action notes, playing the Melody we are all Dancing But OF COURSE there will always be losers too. Let's Keep Fighting ! Somewhere I read once that a Black Belt is nothing else than a White Belt which never gave up !

--- 帖子 #6597 ---
I can definite answer this. This is not a constrainment trade. For a constrainment trade, you need 3 recent bar in a row touching (or almost touching) the MA (and with bar close on the "right" side of the MA). It is not the case here. Even if it is a constraiment (i.e. 3 recent bar in a row touching the MA), you have to evaluate whether it is a good constrainment. About this, I cannot give you a definite answer.

--- 帖子 #6601 ---
Bin, This is the same as learning a foregin language. You are taught a number of explicit rules, but for the full grasping of the language you have to have a lot experience in the use of the language. After you repeatedly exposed to usages in different contexts, you know how to apply the language properly according to different contexts. In other words, you can't fully grasp or teach a language just by explicit rules, and experience is completely necessary. Can you call this intuition? yes and no.

...one of the possible ways to see "things" also from other points of view, trying to indentify those "rules", could be to look for previous support / resistance areas. Price will frequently bounce and break through those levels. When it breaks through it will frequently retrace to the broken level... (I think that especially E/U has the tendency to do that, more or less by each Break Out of previous Highs or Lows in whatever TF) So the most powerful confluence can be when a Choros / Dance Set Up appears at THAT Level. Price breaks through a previous S/R level into a previous big sideway area. Then it comes back *** the First Time *** with a 2 bar retracement on H1 to the EMA10. I suggest to look more and more at the "bigger picture" and to trade M15 as it would be a "fine tuned entry" of any bigger TF, or even just of its own previous history, but not limited only at the previous 10 bars. ...TP just achieved while writing the post. --- 帖子 #6784 ---
I've looked at lots of pivot point indicators. I have not yet found one that does everything I want. The most important feature to me is correct calculations (duh!). And the most important calculation feature is the ability to use NY close (5pmEST) hour as the beginning of the day. This is because, from what I have read, the rest of the world uses this hour to calculate their Daily pivot points. Pivot points work because everyone else uses them, so if your calcs are different than everyone else's, they're going to be pretty useless! I've also compared Kostas's charts to mine, and his daily pivots seem to calculate using NY close. I use PivotPoints only because it's the only indi that you can set the start hour. But I like the display of AutoPivotIndicatorc_ver5 best, and it's also the only one that will igmore Sunday data. So I always switch pivot indis on Sundays and Mondays, which is kind of a pain. AutoPivotIndicator_ver5 would be perfect if you could add 1) set start hour for Daily calcs, and 2) display price on PP levels (I know it shows in the vertical price bar to the right but I would prefer a label on the line itself). Maybe some programmer seeing this could make those things work? I just tried fxbc_S&amp;R_pivots when Binyamin posted it today. It seems to do everything PivotPoints does, and also displays price labels. Here is a comparison of three of the three indicators. Hope this helps you guys! Mega pips to all! --- 帖子 #6788 ---
I live in the US in EST time zone. Sundays are short days for the market since trading starts mid afternoon. Also, the London market does not open at all on Sunday in the US. Therefore Sunday data is not as important as the rest of the week, so some traders discount Sunday data for pivot calculations. I believe this is the thinking behind this. This would probably not be an issue for eastern time zones, and possibly European as well.

--- 帖子 #6796 ---
the stairstep MAs are the HTF equivalents of 15/35/50, made with the MovingAveragesMTF indy. using values UpperTF1=(the higher TF than the current in minutes, ie for M15 the HTF is H1 so the value is 60) a bit lower you set the ma_method_1=1 (so this is EMA) ma_method_2=0 (and this SMA) ma_method_3=1 and lower you set the MAs applied_price=0 period2=35 period3=10 i post my M15 as an example, the stairstep MAs are set like that for M5 (with UpperTF1=15) M15 (with UpperTF1=60) H1 (with UpperTF1=240) on H4 i dont use them but you can set them up for daily thats it for the startstep looking MAs, as for the rest i am not too sure, i guess it could be the 200

--- 帖子 #6797 ---

--- 帖子 #6877 ---
This post is in response yesterday by one of the Choroser asking me to explain one of my trades which I took with another member. Of all the touch trades I rarely see any touch that is the better than this type IMHO. (With its confluence and good market state) First thing to note is, market is already in a bearish trend, visible from the H1 and H4. The 35/50 for H1 is close together and steep, ripe for prices to bounce off. However in the 1st image which is a H1 image, price approaches the 35/50 H1 however just above the MA is the daily pivot(DP). From my experience, when price reach a place of confluence, price will bounce off any MA or important area but if there are higher level of areas like DP price will return to test there before turning around and go back to the direction of the trend. Therefore you can see the price react of the H1 35EMA(yellow line) 1st before testing the DP. (My entry was between DP and 50SMA the blue line) The next image is the H4 Chart, now look to the left of the chart you can see a price swing leaving a wick(also known in the chat as PPA), do your own research and you will find that price will for at least a few days react to these levels(the end of long wicks) So this became the second confluence. So the number of confluence were. H4 10EMA, H1 35MA, DP and then H4 price swing. In order of importance, kindly shared by Haydel(The market touch master lol) in August: 1) PPA 2) Pivot 3) Round Number 4) The MAs The above is not a rule, it is a guild-line which is effective after taking into account the markets states (Trending? Non Trending? Counter trending? Porcupine?) To do so look at the higher timeframe and then work your way down drawing your own conclusions. On this trade I took my 1st TP at 10pips, market retraced and took out my BE stop lost. However I have been here and done this before and I know to expect more pips! I re enter and took my TP at 25 pips at the RN. Which gave me a 0.6% increase in my account.(target reached) hope it helps.

--- 帖子 #6883 ---
Hi, yes, the general answer should be: yes, we have to look at the same principles. I would actually suggest you to use M15 as a kind of "fine tuning" of higher Time Frames Music Waves.... So, first look at the Higher TF direction and trend (and perhaps fix with an horizontal line Areas of previous S/R), then if any set up is approaching there (1st Touch, Constrainment, and so on) look for a confluence of another set up happening on an lower one (for example M15). Also always keep in your mind the Round Numbers and Price Action Bars of the Higher TF's before analysing a lower TF entry (or exit). Reading the thread you will find out the experienced Traders here (Kostas as surely first Example) use to fine tune their entries on M5 (or even M1) for set up of M15. It takes patience, of course. But better a not taken trade, that an unsure one. In my humble opinion one of the biggest "secrets" of this Game is: Confluence. 1st (perhaps 2nd) Touch, the closest possible MA's, Round Numbers, Previous Areas of Support / Resistance, Two Bars Retracement Rule, the most you see, the higher the edge of a winning trade. I hope it may give you a first Idea of the Matter.
