--- 帖子 #6900 ---
Hi, Funbux. I'm not a pro trader (yet!) but I like constrainment trades. This is not a bad setup, but not AAA IMHO. You have nice small bars touching/rejecting the 35/50 and closing above it. Best entry point would be that #4 green bar at the 35 touch with very small SL. It's almost more of a touch trade than constrainment. I would not set my SL so high - maybe 10 pips at most. In constrainment you expect price to go up (in this case). If it goes down it's an immediate failure signal. Your MAs are a little flat, in fact your long term MAs are pointing down, and you have the 5 and 10 above the entry point. It's best to have "clear sky" - that's Survivor's term. It means there is no MAs, TL, RN, SR, etc. to hinder price moving your direction. Now if you look ahead around 13:00, as those green bars are climbing - that's pretty good constrainment. the 10MA is "constraining" price, moving upward, you have clear sky (except for 6500 RN but IMHO that's the least effective type of barrier), and you're with the trend. You could enter on any touch of the 10. If you scroll back through history you'll see this happen all the time. You even have a nice retrace and 10 touch around 14:30. Survivor is Dr. Constrainment. Read all his posts - I have. You can learn everything about constrainment from him. And it's one of the easier setups to spot once you get the hang of it. Hope this helps! Mega pips to you!

--- 帖子 #6915 ---
I was chatting with our fellow traders today, explaining what I’m currently doing to trade H1 10ema and H4 10ema consistently and profitably. So I got inspired by that chat session and I have outlined some rules I use for those trades transcribing and ordering what I said on the chat room. Here you can find an addition to the basics for trading H1 10ema and H4 10ema CHOROS rules including a typical “before, during and after” example. Rules: First: Wait until the confluence of at least 4 levels (let’s say M15 35, M15 50, H1 10 and Daily Pivot) has a maximum height of 15 pips between all of them, the order doesn't matter, but all of them have to be inside that 15 pips area, if it’s less, that’s even better. Second: Make your entry on the first touched level. This rule helps to avoid the cases where I’m left waiting at the station. Third: Set your SL adding around 5 pips to the other side of the levels in confluence. I use more or less 5 pips. You have to decide according to what you see on the chart. That Maximum Height between all the levels in confluence can be stretched a little but no too much. I usually want it to be as closest to 15 pips it can be for the H1 10ema trades, if it is more than 20, then that is a NO trade. And I want it to be as closest to 20 pips it can be for the H4 10ema trades, if it is more than 25, then that is a NO trade. I’m still refining this criteria and it may vary depending on the pair. Do not take these rules as written on Stone. You have to use your good criteria so you can adjust your entries and exists, for example if the confluence includes PPA or Pivot Points and that level is very close to the MA that is going to be touched first, then you can set you entry point right on that level, even if one of the MAs is going to be touched first. That can help you to use smaller SL levels. If you have more confluence levels on a small area (15 pips or less), then you have a high probability trade, so you can extend your TP a little. Several traders trade on those levels individually so if you wait until several of those levels are together, it is sure that you will have some reaction that you can use to profit. Those levels in confluence form something like a wall of several levels. The smaller it is (around 15-20 pips) the stronger it gets. That’s what I wait for. I usually make my entry when the price touches the first level expecting that the price will start to reverse there. If it doesn’t, then the next level will hold, or even the next one, if you have 4 or 5 levels of confluence within 15 to 20 pips then there is a high probability that that small area will hold at lease for a quick scalp even against a HTF trend. Please take a look at the attached images. As you will see that is not a utopic example that you will see only once a year, that kind of setups happens several times a week on diferent pairs, so patiently wait and profit from them. Happy trading

There are a lot of peeps posting winners so let me post an interesting loser from yesterday. EURCAD, H1 35/50, H4 10EMA and DP. The confluence with the market condition makes this an AAA trade, a very hi probability trade which I once had 10 winning streaks that made me more than 5% in less than 2 weeks just trading mostly this setup. However this time the price blew through and took out my SL at -20 pips for -0.5% of my account. So what happen??? Upon inspection the mistake was earlier that day the DP has been touched numerous times and the H4 10EMA has been touch about 1 bar ago. Too much touching weakens the integrity of the structure, so when the price approach the same structure latter, the structure just yield and gave way. It was a catastrophic failure. A blow out. So what I will do next time is make sure I trade important levels that have not been touched for an ample amount of time. HOWEVER I have spent a great deal of time testing and analyzing the ability of M5 timeframes to reduce the losses of even AAA trades on higher timeframe and this is typically what I see. In the second image I posted the same chart but with 5M. Notice how if I traded the 5M it would have allowed me to enter at a better place after the blow through? It scoop down then it followed through with a rejection of the 12 EMA! For lack of better names, I call it the Kostas 5M setup.(The teacher &amp; trader of this method) And it would have been profitable. So to reduce your risk by leap and bounds and improve your entry with smaller SL, 5M can offer some assistance in achieving those goals.

--- 帖子 #6984 ---
It looks like you are talking about the Serpent's Tongue! Your pic is a perfect setup - a few minutes later, if price goes down, the MA will then move down to touch the wick of that candle. But it does not touch when price is at that level, so by now you've missed the trade! I had the same question once, and there are good answers in the Choros thread. Here they are to save you some search time. Originally, the answer was that you can just estimate an extension of the MA and where the touch will take place. I used to draw a short trendline to extend the MA at the current angle, and watched for price to touch the line. Then someone developed a great little indicator that extends the MA at its current angle. I've attached it here with a pic showing an example. It's called HCISYIYKM.mq4 (How Can I Shoot You If You Keep Moving). You just set the TF and period of the MA and you're done. I've found it very useful. Enjoy!

--- 帖子 #6999 ---
The 35/50 was NOT flat, they had been turning down for the last 3 bars. Even though they were not steep, those 3 bars made a definite downtrend, clearly reversing the previous uptrend. The 35 and 50 MAs were also close together - only 4.5 pips apart. I have edited the pic in the previous post to show these things. On the first setup it would have taken some guts to pull the trigger, because when the bar got close to the DP it would have looked like a big fat red-body down bar. But as Dancers, we must realize that this is what touch trades ALWAYS look like. The DP is a powerful S/R line, as we've discussed many times in the thread and the chat room. And if you look at M5 and M1 you will see that it was a quick move, the kind that often reverses at a S/R line. I saw this setup only minutes after the reversal, but it had already retraced about 15 pips - too late to enter. If I had seen it 5 minutes earlier, approaching the DP, and the H1 35/50, I would have been terrified to see that big red bar but I would have definitely jumped in! The second setup is PERFECT CHOROS. The rules say one or 2 bars retrace max. I like 2 bars retrace better than 1, but this time the pinbar was part of the retrace, so it was kind of more than a 1 bar retrace. AND... Here's what makes it so perfect: At 6:21am EST the M15 candle was 6 minutes old. On M15 it touched the 35 and reversed, M5 touched the 12 (kind of a magic MA, watching Kostas use it) and reversed, and, just like Kostas has told us to wait for so many times: M1 gave a rejection bar right off the 35. I tell you I would have closed my first long position and immediately opened a short. Yes I would have been nervous while it was happening in real time, but I would have trusted the setup and done it. Not only this, but the first trade target TP would logically be the first S/R level, which in this case was the M15 35. That was 40 pips. The second trade's target would have been the DP for another 40 pips. Price hesitated at the close of the next M15 bar, so I probably would have chickened out with 30 pips. IMHO, it doesn't get much better than this. Also, check the TOC doc, and I think you will find info on trading when the 35/50 is turning.

--- 帖子 #7058 ---
I attach here a series of indis to suite the Dance Strategy. The idea of the indicators is to show all HTF Equivalent MA on a current chart. The indicator is based on Swingman's code "Dance Moving Averages_V2" I only modified it to be fixed equivalence to any given chart TF: The series contains 5 indicators, so you may choose which ones you wish to have on your chart: D1, H4, H1, M15, M5. thay all contains the 3 MA of the Dance Method: 50/35/10 Only Exeption is for Period M5: 50/35/23/12 What it actually does? It Shows HTF equivelent Dance MAs on current Chart. It will hide lower TF MAs on your specific chart. For instance: if you need H1 MA shown on your M15 TF chart, will show the equivalent Dance MAs of H1 on M15. You may change the chart TF as you wish and still have the H1 equivalent MA values. If you will change the chart TF to H4 or Higher, H1 MA will not show. How I Use it: I drop all 5 indis into one template, and have each TF a default color. Reds = Daily Purples = 4H Greens = 1H Blues = 15M Oranges = 5M So no matter which TF I use, I only have one Template that suits all. Sample Template is also attached... Enjoy.

--- 帖子 #7074 ---
SO TRUE!! I go through the exact same thoughts. I would guess most traders do. Two things have helped me recently: 1. I think about how I will feel after the trade closes if A) I am wrong and I get out at BE, B) if I am right and I get out at BE, or C) if I am wrong and I get out at SL. I ALWAYS feel better after A or B than C, and I know there will always be another trade. 2. If the setup is good, and the entry is good, and I followed my rules, then I EXPECT price to go my way. So if I move to BE early, and price retraces and stops me out, then goes my way, at least I followed my rules, I did not lose money, and there will always be another trade. Good judgment and discretion is still essential, but these thoughts help me stay focused.

Kelisa I have few comments about your trades. But before all I would like you to be aware your Round Number indicator might deceiving you, as it shows line every 5 pips. It should be set to 250 so, you'll have line every 50 pips. Your first trade was open exactly on the 35. But you shouldnt open any trade blindly as it touches any ma. I was looking at M5 and see no confirmation for price rejecting the level. Also looking at the M15 chart I see strong momentum for long. in that case I would wait for confirmation bar by M15 + M5. I also noticed you were not closing this trade with loss of 20pips already. I see no stop loss line neither TP. You should have close the trade with loss at least beyond RN 2700 The second trade was looking good by the reaction, but I didnt understand why you were taking it at that price. I see no SR RN nor MA to stop the bullish break out you were trading against. Only some PPA, but it is not Dance trade. I only hope you closed it when it gives you plus 7-10 pips. I also have not seen your SL and TP lines. My last comment to you would be: look for events of confluence. dont just take levels as fore-granted. Find more excuses to shot your guns, Probability is the name of the game here.

--- 帖子 #7106 ---
KM, It is possible indeed, but I find no use for it, mainly because the main signal chart by definition is M15. There is also a technical reason, you wouldn't want your H4 and D1 charts be loaded with many slow MA from LTF, which are very similar period values. Here some samples to help you understand why you wouldn't want it: 50 of 15M is D1 equivalent = 50/24/4 = 0.25. 50 of H1 is D1 equivalent = 50/24 = 2.08 and so on... as you can see there is no use for having such slow MAs on your chart.

--- 帖子 #7124 ---
Conservation of capital, minimizing risk, is, in my not so humble opinion, the key to successful trading. Out of any given 10 or 20 trades you do, just by the law of averages at least one should be a "home run" that nets you a large profit. So the key is simply to make sure you haven't lost your ass in the other trades. Here's a snapshot of some pretty lousy trading - winning only 1 out of 4 - that still nets out profitable: 10 losers avg. 10 pips each: -100 5 breakevens: 0 4 winners avg. 10 pips each: +40 1 big winner: +75 Net profit: 15 pips, losing half the trades, Breakeven on 25% of them, and only 25% winning trades, and even with 4 out of 5 of those winners being very modest gains What makes it work is the minimized losses. And that's not an unrealistic scenario. When I was trading futures, I averaged only winning 1 out 3 trades - but my winners were, on average, 3 times larger than my losers. When I started out trading Forex, I did even worse with winning percentage - winning only 1 out of 4 trades on average, but my winners were 5 to 8 times bigger than my average losing trade, so again I still usually turned a profit. I had plenty of days with 3 or 4 losing trades of 6 to 10 pips each, balanced out by just 1 lone winner, but that lone winner was for 50 to 100 pips, so the day was still profitable. And that's a large part of what I like about the Dance strategy - the fact that you can run such tight stops if you hit your entries well...and then all you have to do is wait for those trades like shorting Eur/usd right before it falls off a cliff like it did this morning.

--- 帖子 #7125 ---
hi JB thanks for sharing. From my experience with dance i beg to differ a lil from your view. If you master good setups your win rate can be as high as 90%. In dance we are usually trading reaction to certain areas which can be quick and are usually short impulsive moves. I usually exit when price reach the next S/R or MA. (My average RR is around 0.9-1 these days for high timeframe and 0.5-0.7 for M5 trades but my win rate on average if I take from last year is higher than 80%) IMHO if your strategy have a win rate of less than 50% you need to rely on home runs. But if it is way above 50% like choros and it is frequent, sitting on a trade waiting for a home run will not be better off in the long run as compared to taking profit faster based on how price is reacting to certain S/R.(That is the result of my backtesting) A lot of trading books talk about waiting for home runs which is cool, they are probably referring to trend following system(Which usually have a win rate of 20%-45%). Choros is the exception, it took me a while to accept it(after piling up losses on demo). Keep on posting.

--- 帖子 #7149 ---
Each pairs behaves to some degree differently from each other. For example the BOJ and SNB are constantly intervening with their safe haven currencies which IMO makes certain setups less reliable in the JPY pairs than it would have been in other pairs where their central bank let them free float. For Gold and Silver I don't think they react the same way to the MA's like currency pairs and trading gold and silver the way I trade EU would be a disaster. Therefore IMHO, for choros it is good to focus on a few 1st and get to know them b4 we look at more and more pairs. The last thing is, markets are the same in the past, present and will be the same in the future because they change all the time, and that makes this game interesting. I feel that one size fit all are reserved for system that are less sensitive to how market react to their S/R.(Like most good trend following system)

--- 帖子 #7151 ---
I think there are two different broad approaches as for spotting trade opportunities with the Dance: The Choros way: would be stick to one or two pairs; live it, feel it by the tick and take LTF trades. The Clays way: would be to scan many pairs, filter to the ones that are showing perfect conditions and are obviously respect the lines, then go for only AAA entries. I like the Choros way for the many opportunities it provides per session. It is a good way for getting scalping oppts. It is very good approach for any trader targeting a daily quota. Clays way is good for less frequency trading. I think it would be also lower tension trading way. It deals with only the higher probability trades. Its is good for the ones with great patience (I wish I had more of this quality). This is how I understand it, there are two approaches for the same trading method. Use what suites you best, or develop your own prefences. The good thing here, Dance/Choros signals are working with high probability either way. Anyway, I do combine both ways: I scan many pairs, then filter up to 2 or 3 pairs to trade by LTF.

--- 帖子 #7188 ---
Mick - It will probably help you a lot to look at the many examples, illustrated with charts, posted in these forums. The original Dance material is not all written in the clearest possible manner - it can be a bit confusing even if you're fluent in English. As to your question about "Price and the 50/35 must agree", that's referring to Price ACTION - the short version is that you should look at both the moving averages AND price movement and candle formations (as described in the basic Dance material) that support the idea of buying or selling. You question about "before touching the 50EMA, the price will tuch the 10 and the 35, does that mean that you take every signals ?" - Not necessarily, no. You need to look at the price action and make a choice about whether you're going to act on a touch of the 10 EMA, or if you're going to wait for a touch of the 35 SMA or 50 EMA (which may or may not ever happen). It's a judgment call. Frog's advice is excellent - read and study the material, especially illustrated examples, and read and study the comments and material posted in the forums here. Best wishes in your trading. Jack

I like using the History Tester for training myself to make good decisions. But a lot of Dance setups involved confluence with higher TFs. Since the tester can show only one TF at a time I've never been able to see those confluences. A simple solution dawned on me last week and I thought I would share it. I used the DanceMovingAveragesMTF indi (created and shared by someone in this thread) to create the higher TF MAs on one M15 chart. I edited multiple copies of the indi and renamed them so each would show the TFs and colors by default. You might think it would be too confusing to see all those MAs on one chart. I thought the same thing, but surprisingly I got used to it in just a few minutes. You can see in the screenshot that I put up text descriptions in the same colors of the MAs to help me remember which one is which. In the lower right corner is a list of the indis in the template. You will also see that I drew 1 hour boxes. This is optional. I did this manually to get a visual display of one hour bars. The only MAs you cannot see in the screenshot are the D1 35 and 50. They are there, but above the screenshot. I've posted the template and indis in a zip file in case someone finds this useful. The only indi not included in the zip file is Moving Average, because this is the MT4 built-in indi. Mega pips to all!

--- 帖子 #7217 ---
It helps my trading significantly to trade multiple lots. Although I often trade multiple lots when I initiate a trade, I also favor picking up additional lots after initial entry. One rarely enters a market at THE best possible point, and adding positions after initial entry is one way to improve one's overall position. For example, this morning I sold Gbp/usd at 1.55800. Sure enough, that wasn't the best possible spot I could have gotten in, and shortly thereafter the market traded up to around 1.55900. Since the scenario for my initial trade hadn't been violated, I added a second position at 1.55880, which gave me an average entry price of 1.55840. Plus, since I ran the same stop on the second position as I was running on the first, I had even less at risk on the second position (I think my initial stop on that was barely 6 pips away from my entry, whereas I'd been risking about 15 pips on my initial position). Having multiple positions from different entry points also gives me greater flexibility on exiting positions. If, for example, the market moves slightly in my favor, but then appears to stall and looks like it might be rolling back against me, I might go ahead and take profits on one position, and hold the other one. If I take a nice profit on the position I closed, then sometimes even if the market moves back against me and stops out my original trade at a loss, I still have an overall profit. Example: Sold Gbp/usd at 1.55800, and then a bit later at 1.55880. Market moved down to around 1.55650, but then appeared to stall out and turn back to the upside. I took profits on my second position (1.55880) at 1.55710, for a 17-pip profit. I was subsequently stopped out on my initial position (1.55800) at 1.55920 (I'd moved the stop down a bit when the market moved down - it was originally at 1.55970), for a 12-pip loss. But overall, I still made a 5-pip profit. Whereas if I'd just stayed with my original entry position, I would have suffered a 12-pip loss - or at best, I might have moved my stop down to breakeven, or just chosen to exit at breakeven or breakeven+1. The second position, entered at a more favorable price, offered me flexibility that I was able to use to insure a profit even though the market never went more than 15 pips in my favor from the point of my original entry. Just a thought. Jack

--- 帖子 #7235 ---
Question for all: What, in your mind, is the perfect dance trade setup? I ask because it's obvious that this strategy, like all others, is most reliable when there are multiple indicators in favor of the trade. Here's mine: 1) The trend, across all time frames, is in the direction you're preparing to trade (or at least up through the daily - nice if the weekly and monthly are on board, too, but I don't consider them absolutely essential). That is, if you're looking at buying, then the trend - as defined by Dance indicators - is an uptrend across all time frames. 2) Hitting MAs across different time frames - e.g., hitting the 35 or 50 MA on the 15min and the 10 or 35 MA on the hourly, 4-hour, or daily. 3) At or near a pivot point. 4) At or near a round number. 5) At or near previous price action support/resistance area. 6) Confirmation by price action in at least one time frame (preferably the 15min)

--- 帖子 #7236 ---
JB, great question! It makes me think about defining my own strategy for myself. M15 - gives the signal. H1 - NEVER trade against H1. Daily trend - great if it matches, but not essential as long as there are a couple of candles turning the right direction and they don't look like a D1 correction about to end. H4 - I do look at H4, but it really doesn't factor into the decision to enter or not. M5 and M1 - Lower TFs are for choosing entry point. If entries match on lower and higher TFs, confidence is higher. So - when I see a M15 trend about 4-6 candles, that started by crossing the 35/50 on the second or third candle or so, and it's a relatively steady trend (no giant candles or huge spikes, of course), I start to look for the two bar retrace to touch the 10MA. Really, exactly like the manual. I may even drop to M5 and look for a 12 or 23 touch. When I see these setups I make pips. I look at some other setups, too. But the best setups for me have been the first and second M15 10 touches, taking the entry off M5 12 or 23MA. Always look for confluence near the entry target with the R/R areas JB listed, and confidence goes much higher.

G'day peeps, After a few requests, attached is my Dance_trail EA. It trails the stop to the last candle high/low. Just copy the file to your /experts folder and start MT4. Settings: Trail_before_profit Default is false. If true it will immediately, even if you are not in profit Trail_after_Pips_profit How many pips in profit you need to be before it starts trailing. (default is 6) Auto_SBE_plus_one Default is true. If you want to automatically move the stop to 1 pip profit when the trade has reached a certain value in profit. SBE_plus_one How many pips in profit you need before the stop is moved to SBE+1 Pip_buffer Default 1. How many pips below/above the previous candle to trail the stop. (Default is 1) Add_spread_on-shorts. This adds the spread to the clearance above the previous candle on shorts. (it is only needed on shorts as short trades are closed on the ask, but candles are drawn on the bid, whereas longs are closed on the bid price, which is the same as the candles.) Default is true. Attached File(s) Dance_trail.1.mq4 6 KB | 497 downloads Next are my trading scripts. They open two positions, both with 15 pips SL and one with a 15 pip TP. Lot size is calculated automatically based on the account balance and % risk in the opening box (default is 2%). This is the TOTAL risk for both trades so they should be ~ 1% each. (If 2% is an uneven number of lotsteps, the first position will be slightly larger). You must copy Money_mgmnt.mqh under expertsinclude or these scripts will not work. This file has the function to calculate the lot size. Copy Open_Dance_Short1.mq4 and Open_Dance_Long1.mq4 into your expertsscripts folder. Attached File(s) Trade scripts.zip 3 KB | 595 downloads Enjoy!

I enjoy trying to think up "crazy" trading strategies. Here's my latest: Let's say Eur/Usd is making a new (recent) low at 1.31300. You put in two orders for 100 contracts each. One is a sell-stop at, say 1.31275 and the other is a buy limit at 1.31270. Odds are massively strong that both orders will get filled - and you just locked in a half-pip profit, times 100 = 50 pips. Yes, the small problem is the one time that your sell order gets filled and your buy order doesn't, and your sell order becomes a massive loss. Hey, I SAID it was a crazy strategy! But still, those kinds of "guaranteed" winners are fun to think about.

--- 帖子 #7300 ---
Bin, My approach for H4 TF is to wait for M15 double top before entering. This results in safer trades because most times price rechecks the high TF reaction points before reacting. The disadvantage is that when there is no double-tap you will loose the opportunity to enter the trade. Alternatively, you enter right after the first M5 rejection for a scalp. P.S. When in M15 TF, I use double M5 tops (or bottoms if looking for longs).

Personally, I shoot for 10-15 pips a day - when I make more than that, I thank God profusely, and figure I've got some cushion against a losing day here and there. But any day I "escape" with a profit, I'm happy and grateful. It helps to keep in mind that you're trying "steal" a few pips when the market isn't looking.

--- 帖子 #7364 ---
I'm going to re-post an old piece of advice from Kostas - "IMO be quick to grab your pips with this method. Otherwise, use partial lots so that you grab quick profit with one part and let the rest ride". Using multiple lots has helped me substantially, as it gives me the flexibility to take profits on some lots while letting the rest ride. For example, let's say you have 5 lots (whether regular, mini, or micro), and the market moves 10 pips in your favor....if you take profits on 3 of the 5 and let the other two ride, even if the other two are stopped out at breakeven, you still have an average profit of 6 pips per lot, which is much better than having your whole position stopped out at breakeven, or even BE+1. So, if my chosen position size is 5 lots, I will enter 5 separate orders for 1 lot each, rather than just 1 order for 5 lots. It does require being quick at entering orders, but on the other hand I've found that often it enables me to pick up about half of my position at a slightly better price - let's face it, we rarely enter at THE best possible point.

--- 帖子 #7365 ---
Reading through Makron's very kind post of Kostas' comments, I already notice two recurring themes: 1 - The importance of confluence. Probability of success is enhanced significantly if there are indicators across several time frames. You know, not everyone is trading the 15min chart. You're better off if the people trading the 5min, hourly, and 4hour charts are trading with you. 2 - The number of times he says, "probably could have made more, but I took my 19" (or 18 or 10 or 15). The important phrase there is not "could have made more", but "I took my (whatever)". It's not what you miss, it's what you take that counts - and over and over again, I see him taking a profit.

--- 帖子 #7390 ---
Well logically the smaller the spread the better is it for any kind of trading Your trading style will be different than mine so I will tell you how to answer your question with you style. To answer your question of how it affects you. Your overall results is a function of your average RR and your win %. Profit = AverageRR * (win%) – (1-win%). However your win % is a function of your spread(bigger your spread the lower your win % and vice versa) So given an average RR(say 1 for your eg.) you need to find out the relationship between your spread and your win %. Find that out through statistics gathered from back/forward testing.(can be ploted on a 2d graph, spread vs win% for say an RR of 1. You can do a 3D graph too for every RR, use R or matlab) Pick a point on the spread vs win% graph and then with your RR you can figure out if you will come out profitable in the long run or not. profit = AverageRR * (win%) – (1-win%) Where win% = is a function of spread Statistics requires at least 30 data points to make a conclusion but in the market you can never test enough data. Fortunately trading is not completely a science so you don't need to use such precisions because the market is not. Just figure out how far into your analysis you need to go before you "feel" that the analysis is enough. Your conclusions have to be a function of your discretion and your analysis. A quant will tell you to lean more towards analysis, a technical trader will tell you to lean more towards discretion. Pick your weapon according to your personality.

--- 帖子 #7393 ---
B4 the math guys come in here and spank me let me define things more clearly. Total Profit % = (Total RR)*(% Risked pertrade) This is where correction is intended. In the 1st equation I assumed all the losses will be -1 RR. This will account for partial losses. AverageRR pertrade = (AverageRRWin * win%) - (AverageRRLose * Lose%) = (Total RR)/(number of trades) This stats may not be enough for you so you want to plot RR vs time to measure the drawdown or to see if you like the equity curve.

Hi Bin My understanding is that hidden divergence confirms underlying weakness in a downtrend and strength in an uptrend, and occurs after a correction. This provides a good entry point. I think it is caused by high-volume buying/selling against the correction (i.e. selling as price moves up in a downtrend and vice versa), and that it is a useful tool to be used in corroboration with Dance signals. Hope this helps.

--- 帖子 #7421 ---
Attached is a classic example of how the larger time frames provide a much clearer picture. If you zoom out to your Daily TF for the EUR/USD you can see how prior resistance, once broken to the upside, becomes future support. When you add in that same area is also in Confluence with the Daily 10EMA touch, it creates a "hot zone" which is acceptable to enter. If you also scale down to a H4 chart, you will also see that the CLOSING price is always ABOVE the H4 10EMA. By looking at these larger time frames, it will help you avoid going against the trend on the smaller M15 charts during times like these...notice how even though we had red alert announcements today by Fed and Bernanke, price still respected the higher time frames...the old adage holds true, "The higher the time - the Stronger the line....just my two cents which might help some of those who solely focus on the short-term perspective....(Not sure if I uploaded the charts correctly, as I've never attached charts on FF b4)....Happy Trading all...

--- 帖子 #7423 ---
I appreciate your comments alexLV, however there were additional factors which provided better than average probabilities on this trade which I did not include, such as 50% retracement from the prior move along with a bounce along the rising trendline, H4 bounce on 10ema... Successful trades are the ones in which the probability of that trade working out are greater than 50% and this instance, since there were soo many strong factors converging together into one area of confluence - the trade was well worth the risk (for me), as my stop was just below the 61.8% retracement (.3152). Usually the best trades are the ones that look the worst - in terms of the prior candle - just before entering. Very rarely does the prior candle look good in a trade that works out (unless its a breakout/breakdown trade). As long as all the rules of your entry are met prior to entering, you usually get paid to not "wait" to see what is behind the curtain and that is perhaps the hardest thing to do as humans, since we many times want to "see it to believe it". Clay and Kostas referred to this as "standing in front of a train" - such as in a two-bar retrace. The key is to make sure you are on the correct side of the trend on the higher time frames. Hope this clarifies my prior post....Happy Trading.

The reason why EU SHORTS didn't work is because that was the first reaction form a very clear D1 Demand Area. Supply and Demand Areas like this one on D1 (I'm not talking about Support and Resistance Levels) are very strong and usually these are turning points for trends, or big moves against the trend. So, since EU reached that D1 Demand Area we can expect a ranging market and then an Up-trend to get at least to 1.2920 Ofcourse, I could be wrong.

--- 帖子 #7510 ---
Hi everyone. I was sent a private message by someone asking me if I had been consistently profitable with the Dance trading method. Rather than just reply privately, I thought I'd post my thoughts here for the thread. Here is the question: Yes, I have been consistently profitable with the Dance method. I think it is fantastic - extremely simple and extremely effective. I have made a few posts in this thread with my exact methods, but essentially I follow the rules exactly as described in the original Dance PDF. I watch four currencies - GBPUSD/EURUSD/AUDUSD/EURAUD. All trades I open with a 50 pip TP and a 50 pip SL. I move the SL to BE at +15, and then let the trade run as it will. I put my success down mainly to two things: I follow the rules and only enter ideal setups. This took me a very long time and a lot of money to learn. I follow the rules and only enter the most ideal setups. Having a main trading screen with four currencies on it allows me to wait for the currency offering the best setup. I generally only pick the best setup and enter that, I don't do two at once. On my individual currency screens I pretty much no longer use the M1 and M5 charts, and just keep my eye on the H1 and D1 charts to make sure that they confirm the setup on M15. If not, I probably won't trade it. I don't use the daily/weekly pivots and I don't care about them. I don't use any support/resistance lines and I don't care about them. For me, the interaction between the 35/50 MAs is all I care about. I no longer wait for touches or ideal retraces, I just look at the M15 MAs and the H1 MAs and if they look good I enter. This comes from experience. You need to get your experience up first. Practice on the simulator, practice in demo. It takes time. I've been doing this system for a while and so now for me it is second nature. I'm on holiday at the moment (have been for a while), so probably won't be on very much to reply. I hope this post helps some of you. Keep at it. p.s. Shoutout to Kostas and Clay, you are both beautiful, wonderful people.

--- 帖子 #7587 ---
To every one at the Choros thread: People that believe that Choros doesn't work are eagerly looking for a method that mechanically tells them when to buy and when to sell. They are saying with honesty: "I don't want to think too much, please tell me where should I Buy and where should I Sell.". The problem with that is that not only Choros will not work consistently for them, but probably no other system will. Choros helps to understand how the markets moves and shows many details to be aware of to be profitable, Choros leads to see many details that every one should learn to really understand the market. Constant practice helps to be consistent. To take a profitable Choros trade you have to see the complete picture. For example, when you see a Choros setup forming you should think something like: Why is a Choros setup showing up on EURUSD in the M15 TF? Why the price is bouncing to get to the 10 ema or to the 35/50ma's? That bounce could be too strong so the setup could not obey Choros rules, so: What Higer Time Frames (H1, H4, D1) are telling me? What Lower Time Frames (M5, M1) are telling me? What has happened before (Minutes ago, Hours ago, Days ago,...) on that same level? What GBPUSD is doing at the same time? What other USD pairs are doing? What other EUR pairs are doing? Etc., etc., etc. You should think of many other details. Then make similar questions to set Stop Loss and Take Profit Levels. Setting fixed, unrealistic, not well thought SL and TP levels will lead to loses. Don't stop learning. There are many other details to take into consideration to be really profitable and some may think it's overwhelming, but it's not. Don't stop practicing. Let's illustrate it with learning to drive a car. There are really count less abilities, rules and details that you need to learn to be able to do it right. Let's think: Be able to start the engine without breaking the starter. Release the brakes to start moving (You may laugh at this now but when you are totally new you really need to concentrate and think about simple things like this, even the order that you are doing these things) How to use the gearbox smoothly when your car is not automatic. How to drive in reverse. Watch for other cars when you are on the road. Watch for people on the road. Watch for people on the side walks and be prepared to what they do. Watch for cars on intersections and be ready to react to them. Be aware of details to be ready to press the brakes under certain situations. Is the other driver looking at you or is he looking somewhere else? Watch the rearview mirror when turning or when you are stopping. Learn what all the signals mean and obey them. Learn what all the lines painted on the road mean. Etc. etc. etc, I'm sure you can think of many other details. When you are new to car driving, you really have to concentrate and carefully consider all that details one by one every moment that you are learning to drive, if you don't you could get hurt or you can hurt some one else. After years of driving, when you drive home from work, do you really concentrate on all those details? Yes. You are obeying all of them, you know dozens of rules, tips and abilities and you are applying them to safely arrive home. The difference now is that those abilities, rules, tips, etc. are natural, you just know how to safely drive home. And that was possible only after years of practicing. Well, something similar happens with Choros, and trading in general. Many details, not an easy task at all, but absolutely possible to be consistently profitable. And with time and practice, it becomes natural. So, as Kostas said. Stay focused and don't give up, you will learn how to dance with the market.

--- 帖子 #7758 ---
kk, As I has explained before, there are 2 kinds of scooped-ups: a) The price is in downtrend for a while and it is time for reversal. The price crosses above the 10 EMA, then retests the EMA but can't penetrate below it. This is the 10EMA scoop-up. You can see this possibility 18 bars before my trade in the H1 chart. b) In this kind, the scoop happens from the 35 or 50 MAs. In this case there was a strong confluence from H1 35/50/62 which provided the scoop-up. In your case, you had difficulties understanding the normal bounces so I don't expect you to get the scoop trade. Just look at the trade as a normal bounce from the strong confluence of H1 35/50/62, Daily Pivot and H4 10..... P.S. There is also the opposite (scooped-down) trade.

I have searched the thread but I could only find some contradictory answers. So could anyone please summarize this issue briefly? Do you reset the bar count in a retrace from the most recent high/low (for ex. a retrace in the direction of a 10EMA) after a candle in a different direction (than the ones we are counting) or not? I hope I am being clear enough ;-) ) 2) If there are more than two candles in a retrace (no matter how we reset the bar count ), however after a few more bars the price gets to the 10EMA, should it be counted as a touch for the purpose of the touch count or should it be completely ignored? 3) Finally: if I am correct (?), after evolving, it is left to some discretion whether traders allow themselves to enter few pips away from a MA (effectively taking a trade ALMOST at a touch, which, as far as I understand, wasn't allowed by the original rules (" DO NOT ENTER UNLESS THE CANDLE IS TOUCHING A LINE" )). Many pips, JK

My personal opinion on the above: choose one type of answer from your statements and stick to it. It really doesn't matter how much bars or if it's touch/bounce/rainbow, what matters is what you see and if it works for YOU. So just choose one type of answer and test/check it yourself... no other way, it doesn't matter if something is working for anyone here, because it doesn't mean, that you personally would be able to see the same and have the same results. If it won't work for say few month, you may try something else, but don't switch instantly if one or two trades won't work.

--- 帖子 #7787 ---
Hi since no one is answering your questions I will. This is just the way I do it. Of course there is a bit more to what I will explain. 1) I count when there are bars with small wicks heading to the MA. I ignore the little bars, my logic is, market can be random so unless it is obviously moving to the MA I won't count it. 2) Usually I ignore setups with more than 2 bars, but if it is the 1st touch of the MA with good M5 rejection I will usually take it despite having more than 2 bars. 3) I can't answer that unless you read Kostas1 posts in the choros thread. If I answer that you might not understand, but as a general rule I think it is a good idea to wait for a touch before you enter.

Hi all, I thought it would be appropriate to share the tools I programmed to trade the dance: 1. TouchMAAlerter (Alerts when MAs are touched). I use this in live trading (Popup alerts) and on my VPS to send me SMS when MAs on major timeframes (weekly, monthly, daily) are touched. It can alert in three ways: Popup, E-Mail and executable (which i use to send SMS). 2. TouchMA EA. Since there are no limit orders on MAs, I wrote a simple Expert that would open a position on the touch of a selected MA. This EA needs the A_SetLotSize script be run beforehand to initialize the global variable "ordersize". Hope it is useful, suggestions and feedback are welcome! Best regards, Hans P.S.: I also greatly modified the supplied dance scripts (Add new scripts for limit orders, automatically take screenshots on entries and exits, exit half position size on all trades). Hi, here is the latest version of my Dance trading tools hosted: https://github.com/bscholes/DanceTools Here is the zip-file: https://github.com/bscholes/DanceTools/zipball/master Explanation: indicators (exept std Dance): Contains THVs TzPivots. I use daily weeky and monthly Pivots + Midpoints. Price reacts very nicely around them and I rarlely need to insert manual S/R lines. BarAlert.mq4: pops up an alert on COB (for those who try to trade while working) scripts: Contains modified versions of the original Dance scripts. Modifications: Bugfix: Doesn't pop up the order window on ECN brokers who need SL/TP as separate orders. Addition: make screenshots on Entries and exits (in experts/files) ADeletePendings.mq4, A_BuyLimit.mq4, A_SellLimit.mq4 do what their names imply ACloseHalf1Currency: Closes half of all positions of the charts currency P4LOrderHistory.mq4 - Got it from FF, use it to visualize my trades experts: ChartServe.mq4: Generate Screenshots periodically. I use it on my VPS in conjunction with a web server to have my chart template on my mobile phone since MT4/mobile charting is very restricted. EventsExpert: Mails/Alerts/Executes a program if SL/TP is hit or pendings are triggered. I use it with an external program to send SMS to my phone. TouchMA and TouchMAAlerter are the same from the previous post PLEASE TEST ON DEMO FIRST, if those scripts blow your account or close your loved long-term positions or kill the house cat, I'll take no responsibility, use them at your own danger only! (so do I). Suggestions and comments are appreciated, Kind regards, Hans

--- 帖子 #7799 ---
Well, I could try to share some thoughts. To take those M5 trades as 'touch' I think would be risky because price might go further. So, basically principles are almost the same as for M15, we need a fairly steep 12 or 23EMA (23EMA is almost the same as M15 10EMA) and if we are targeting a 12EMA bounce, then we are looking for a M1 rejection or a M5 rejection and enter on the close for more safety, if we are targeting a 23EMA bounce it's the same principle. I'm not an expert at those kind of trades, just started to SEE them happening very often. To add more, I take them only when they agree with M15 trend. Grab M5 chart and mark 12, 23 EMA touches, then mark the same bounces on the M1 and you will get to see some nice P/A there.

So, let's say we have a H1 chart and at the top of the run we see a strong looking Pin bar, often price will go directly to the H1 10 EMA and ignore the M15 10 EMA. The same perspective is for H4 chart, say we have a Doji at the top of the run and price will go direcly to check the H4 10 EMA and ignore the other MA's on lower TF. To conclude, it doesn't matter what the TF is, if there is strong P/A indicating a reversal, price will check the 10 EMA and if you are trading against that flow on lower TF you might get burned.

--- 帖子 #7815 ---
Sounds reasonable. However if you see convincing PA, for example in m5 indicating rejection of the m15 10 MA then that's usually a good bet.

--- 帖子 #7816 ---
My experience is that it depends on at what time of day the HTF PA happens, if it is between London/NY, then it is very dangerous, because in this case the reversal/indecision PA normally indicates that market will try to find directional clue in the next session, and that will lead to large price movements. If it is between Asian/London or NY/Asian, then even if HTF PA happened, M15+LTF PA can still be a good bet. But this also means that we can just take direction(with the PA) shown in the NY session as the trend of the moment, and take our M15 trade in that direction. I attached two images as an example(EUM15/H1, may not be very good example, but enough to demonstrate my point), it was the London/NY transition on Friday, we see a pin in H1, rejecting the RN, the price rise sharply, if you short at M15.10 or M15.35/50 you will get burned, but if you wait long enough until the long at M15.10 happens then you may get a few pips more safely. In this case price did get rejected from H1.50, but M15.10 touch still worked, as the trend at the moment is up and quite strong. This could be personal as I got burned quite a few times during London/NY overlap for taking trades against HTF PA in the past

Hi, I will let you know why I think it didn't work(none were setups I would have traded anyway). Do keep in mind that this is how I would trade it and since your setups is in my area of expertise I will comment. As a side, I don't necessarily agree with the phrase "trade by the rule". In my humble view you should trade by your rule that you have backtested and found to be good in the long run not necessarily as someone say. So backtest everything you wanna trade. And yes do backtest, its better than practicing by trading. (And I don't mean using the sim) Anyway, For GBPUSD, I only trade with M5 confirmation if it confluence with the 15M 10 or 35/50. The more confluence the more traders from other TF will be taking it. Keep in mind confluence with HTF MAs tends to take longer to develop so set your SL accordingly from your backtest results. EURUSD, this strategy is for markets with a trend. I would like to see the market trend and leave 15M 10 for a while before I trade the 15M 10 1st touch. Remember also to trade only during active hours and get a good understanding about supply, demand and compression zones(there are concise explanations in Kennyz's thread) so you won't trade in the wrong direction. In my view price move from supply to demand in the HTF but as it does so it seems to react to the MAs we use in the LTF like 15M. So we make our money as it is moving among S/D in HTF. That is why I say it is not a good idea using sim to Backtest, you can't study the market that consist of multiple TF properly. Thanks for reading my humble views. =)

EU: 10:35, SL hit @8pips 1.2555-1.2565 is a supply zone, price got pushed down multiple times from there in the past 24 hours. --- 帖子 #7936 ---
See attached image for the GU M15 IB and Bearish engulfing, I might be talking about completely wrong trade. There were some debates about 2 bar/2 touch rule here. You are absolutely right that it isn't necessary criteria, but in your GU trades, you were attempting to take "touch" of M15.10, therefore, these rules are still useful. 2 bar/2 touch are not absolute, it is build on some insights into the nature of the movement to help filter low probability trades. My understanding of the 2 bar/2 touch are: 2 bar helps you to take retracement in a impulsive movement, 2 bar is 30 minutes in M15, if the prices takes too long to retracement, then the momentum may have already faded. 2 touch helps you to identify waves in a impulsive movement, if you remember Elliot 5 wave thingy, then 2 touch means you've completed the first 4. The move down to 3rd touch could be the end of the entire 5 waves.(There maybe wave extension, but after first 2 touch, things getting too dangerous)

--- 帖子 #7937 ---
Darkforce, the candles pointed out by you fall in the definition of IB/Engulfing only if you look at their bodies. I guess it's just about the definition that one will follow. I follow the one that says the IB (body+shadow) has to be within the range of a previous bar and engulfing, of course the other way round - lower low and higher high than the previous (original The Dance Manual &amp; PDF on price action: http://www.forexfactory.com/attachme...5&amp;d=1308305438 - from the bottom of the first post http://www.forexfactory.com/showthread.php?t=288142 ). Additionaly, none of the trades I have taken were at the "Touch" All of them were P/A - M5 pin bars. Thanks a lot though for attaching the imgs for a clearer picture and for the rest of your efforts to shed some light on the other matters. Regards, JK

--- 帖子 #7996 ---
most ppl here who are new to Choros will soon realize its not the entries but the exits you should concentrate on. That's whats separated Kostas from the herd. The entry rules are all very clear but the exits require some discretion. Kostas watches lower time frames and I've seen him say in the past he bails out early if he doesn't like the price action. How do you define "not liking the price action" clearly? Is it congestions or candle patterns or s/r breaks? Its all of these and sometimes more. Well the answer is you cant clearly define it. It comes from e-x-p-e-r-i-e-n-c-e. So you should be concentrating on the exit more than the entry as its more subjective, thats the tricky part and trade management too. Statistics indicate 80% of traders are right on the direction when they enter a trade but yet 80% of traders overall lose. Why is that? Well its because its because they don't know when to get out. You cant know when to get out until you have a lot of experience aka c-h-a-r-t t-i-m-e so that's why its important to take quick profits while you can. I remember in the early days Kostas had mentioned he would exit 80% of his position very quickly at 8-10 pips sometimes less. This ensures you get some profit however small and steadily grow your account. Most times the trade will reverse on you at some point, so its imp you take most of your profit before that, and wait for the next opportunity, don't wait for targets to be hit, because many times they wont be. If you have a target let the remaining 20% of your position stay in the trade. Go back and analyse your trades. If you followed the entry rules how many trades went immediately against you? check? I'd imagine very few ... most at least went 6-8-10 pips in your favor before turning around and going the other way hitting your stop loss or when you bailed on the full position a little before it hit your stop loss. Now ask yourself what if you had taken the majority of your profit before it reversed? Would this have helped cut your losses and result in a smoother equity curve like kostas posted in post #1.... yes it would ! If you are experienced enough with exits like kostas then its fine but if you're not and many aren't its better to concentrate on exits and trade management. Go back and read Kostas's old posts about his exits and trade management. Concentrate on the exit and take partial profits as much as you're all concentrating on entries and see if it helps. It should

--- 帖子 #7997 ---
I agree. I'd say that recently majority of my trades ended up going my way for about 8-10pips, reversing and hitting SL@BE+1. I am about to change my trade management and close half of the position while moving to BE+1. The only thing I dislike about it is that, putting your success rate aside, it worsens your RR on the trades. And, as far as I am concerned, most traders lose because they don't limit their losses (too wide stops or stops being widened when the price gets toward SL) and/or they don't let their profits run. Mathematically, that means they go toward and beyond Risk to Reward of (&gt;1):1. That is what held me back from taking partial profits early. But, it seems that with higher hit rate you can improve your expectancy. I may as well be wrong but that is my understanding of this matter so far. Have a good weekend, JK

--- 帖子 #8118 ---
Objective MA slope Hi, here's a simple indicator I have built to allow me to judge objectively the slope of various MAs. It calculates the slope of the MAs based on the percentage of price that the MA has moved between the pre-previous candle and the previous candle. So the value you see doesn't take into account the current, not yet closed candle, and it's 100% objective. Since obviously the difference between two successive MAs will be larger in higher timeframes, you can't compare the slopes of an MA on different timeframes. This means that the value of 50 may indicate a big slope for the 10 M5 EMA, but it will be a small slope for the 10 W1 EMA. This indicator is useful if you first get familiar with it, so that you will know what values are big or small for a specific MA.

weird day to trade today. a bit about my modifications of the system: after 5 good trades according to manual you should get out from trade for the day. what I did, I stopped treating be+1 and similar trades as successful. if a trade gave me less than 0,3% profit I don't count is as successfull. I change the risk depending on how many indicators push me to entry. usually it is 1% risk with 7 pips (of course sometimes I move sl behind nearest round number). but when I see few confirmations for entrance I double or triple position size with same pips on s/l(for example touch of bar on 35 sma on round number and price constraiment pushes me to use 2-3% risk by doubling or tripling position size) Therefore I don't look at profit in pips, but in %, as I can lose 30 pips at 1% risk (normal position size) and gain 20 pips at 3% risk (triple position size) as I cannot trade 5 days a week, and trade only 1-4 days a week sometimes I treat London session and NY session as separate days, so I double the amount of successful trades I can get per day Do you guys think I did the right thing by adjusting the system to myself? or shall I stick to manual no matter what?

If I was about to trail I'd switch to 5m, otherwise the large bars on 15M will wipe out your potential profits. I have also recently been researching how setting a hard TP of 1,5-2x SL would work out and it seems worth testing. Especially that it's stress reducing set-and-forget solution. --- 帖子 #8766 ---
This would be a dangerous short. Theres a concave up curve, plus long wicks to the upside mean its repeatedly testing resistance and it could be about to break. For a short i would wait for another retrace with a lower high or equal high in my opinion. I've noticed on the 15 minute you have to take the surrounding context into account before taking a trade based on price action. This is because a shooting star could simply mean its about to break in a certain direction instead of going down. So you combine price action with other analysis , like concave up support curves, to try to determine what the shooting star means. Right after the 3 downward bars with long wicks you have a hammer and then a spinning top. Ive noticed that when you have long upward wicks, it will eventually transform, if it wants to go up, to a hammer + spinning top, or a hammer and then a shooting star. Attached Image (click to enlarge)

--- 帖子 #8784 ---
Here’s a thought,, One of the key indicators for this system is the angle ofthe MA, (even if I do sometimes forget that a bit) Unfortunately different screen shapes and chart setups causethe angle of the displayed MA to LOOK different. By default MT4 seems to always fit things so that the visiblepart of the chart fits the screen neatly from top to bottom. A laptop with a ‘letterbox’ type widescreen, with the Windowsstart button and toolbar along the bottom (producing a very long thin chart)looks quite different to a large square or near-square screen. Typically this will mean that 45 degrees measured on a thinlaptop screen will equate to a much steeper looking line on a more squarescreen. The two attached screenshots show the difference. Both have the ‘Trendline by Angle’ set to the same 2 pointson the same chart and TF etc. they show quite different angles. Using the M1 (and sometimes the M5) chart and fixing thechart to 1:1 zoom (in &gt;properties&gt;common - settings) gives an entirelyconsistent angle to the MA’s making it easy to assess the angle. It doesn’t generally work on longer TF’s. - because the amountof price action going on means you just can’t see enough of the chart. I believe there are MA Angle Indicators but I’ve never gotone that worked as I wanted it to, Another solution that seems to work is to always make the ‘main’chart window (shortest time frame) as square as possible providing a consistentaspect ratio of 1:1. --- Possibly an ideal solution with this system. I’ve been trading for almost 2 years now and using MT4 thewhole time, and this issue first started bugging me quite a while ago, up ‘tilnow though I haven’t been involved with a system that looks quite so closely atthe MA angle so I haven’t done anything much about it, Does anyone have any thoughts about this? I’m kind of half expectingsomeone to tell me I’ve missed some totally fundamental setting in MT4 orsomething – ‘wouldn’t be the first time either,,,

It can happen against the 10 EMA as well but these trades are a little “weaker” and you need to keep an eye on them until you get some pips locked in from one. " From the simple Dance part 1: The Constrainment Trade can happen against any of the three Moving Averages in this Strategy. THE STRONGEST of them are always taken against the 200 EMA, or the 35 SMA when it and the 50 EMA are literally “on top” of each other and the 10 is on the side they are 'bending' toward. Usually Price will sort of “bounce along” the 35 for several bars, at least three before you take the trade. It can happen against the 14 EMA as well but these trades are a little “weaker” and you need to keep an eye on them until you get some pips locked in from one. From the Choros Trades manual: Containment: Nice parallel Mas Small candles Wicks though constraining MA are good confirmation From the Dance Summary: PRIMARY ENTRANCES 1) CONSTRAINMENT A constrainment occurs when price hugs a Moving Average, or other Support/ Resistance level for three or more consecutive bars. (There is some difference of opinion about which part of the candle needs to be constrained, the body or the wick.) A constrainment signal is better when the hugging bars are either small or getting smaller. Constrainment trades can be taken against the 50EMA, the 35SMA, the 10EMA, or even against round numbers. A constrainment signal will be better to the extent it follows the general principles: 1) Steepness of the constraining MA 2) MAs moving in sync. 3) Confluence of constraining MA with other areas of support or resistance. 4) Larger time frame shows trend in direction of constrainment trade.

One more reply from Clay sent to my email. KK has picked some really bad examples to dispute things with. Comments on the charts, and with this I'll let it drop. If anyone else wants to try to pick it apart, go ahead. Don't bother to learn price action setups, just stick to a "holy grail" and get killed. Price action is always king, the higher the time frame, the more likely it will work. On shorter time frames, stick with momentum "with the trade" entries. If you really want to learn, setup an M15 chart and put on the tester and drop the averages totally and learn to trade exclusively price action for a while. You learn quick that way. The MA's were always "eye candy" as I said in the manual, they are a guide, not a commandment carved in granite with God's finger. Endroute trades ONE ma on his charts, I have a friend who lookes for ONE SINGLE TYPE OF BAR on m15 to enter on "with the trend" and does ok. It's always been about training yourself to see what works for YOU. No one sees the charts the same as Endroute, or Kostas, or me, or anyone else. Everyone has life experiences that shape the way they "see" things. USE IT, master it, make it yours. Hi guys, I made us a simple Choros retrace EA. Only started using it today, so give it a go and see what you think. Attached Image Attached Image (edited to attached the successful trade, automatically entered and closed 4 hours after I made this post) Just drag it onto a chart and it will wait for a retrace to the 10 and enter for you. You set a SL and TP value, and it will automatically scale those to match the current timeframe and market amplitude. If you put it on a GBPUSD or EURUSD chart at the present time, it should be about 1:1, so a 10 pip take profit will equal 10 pips. For an H1 trade that would change to 22 pips, and for an M5 trade it would be 7 pips. After you put it on a chart, you can change the timeframe and it will automatically adjust to the new timeframe. So if you put it on the M15 and then decide that an M5 retrace is going to work better, just change to M5 and the EA will change the SL and TP values for you. It automatically calculates the lots as well (if you want it to), and enters at the appropriate size for your level of risk. You just choose what percentage of your account you want to risk if the stoploss gets hit, and it will do the rest. Otherwise, set it to fixed lot size and choose whatever you want. It also creates a label object that states "Delete this to enter immediately", which if you delete it, will enter immediately with the appropriate TP and SL. After it takes the trade it automatically removes itself from your chart, and it needs access to WinUser32.dll to do that, so enable external DLL calls. Any feedback or improvements, let me have them

--- 帖子 #9268 ---
@ Eur Usd: Don't get me wrong mate, but I think your chart's got too much zoom, to properly decide the steepness (slope) of the MAs. During my training (in which I still am ) I noticed that different zoom levels, combined with window size of the charts inside MetaTrader, give a variety of MA slopes. To me, this was a riddle to solve...Setting up the correct Workspace, efficient enough for me. And I came up with this (for resolution 1920x1080): Generally I work with Profiles (per pairs and TFs), which are these: Attached Image My Market overview workspace is this profile (eg. the "____DANCE_OVERVIEW_M15") : Attached Image (click to enlarge) ...and if I spot a setup being formed, I switch to this profile (eg. the "DANCE_EURJPY"): Attached Image (click to enlarge) Especially in the pair workspace (the last screenshot), resizing the chart windows per TF differently, helps me to visually balance the candlestick sizes. In all TFs I use the following MAs: - 5 EMA (Blue) - 12 EMA (LightBlue) - 23 EMA (Yellow) - 35 SMA (black) - 50 EMA (Brown) - 200 SMA (Magenta) For all TFs the Round Numbers Indicator is set up the same way: 250 (for 3-digit pairs AND 5-digit pairs) In the 15M TF at the Pair-view profile I also use THV for spotting S/R lines of the previous Day. Generally speaking, I don't know if this method of trying to dance the CHOROS is the best (or even the proper), but it seems that it's working for me. Any suggestions are welcome. - Cheers! PS.: I'm "dancing" for some months now, and things go well (in demo). Some of my results here (abstract from myfxbook.com): Attached Image

--- 帖子 #9284 ---
The only thing I know is that these MAs are used by most traders around the world. It is like fibo levels etc. We know that the candle will reverse when it touches the MA because we enter when we see a confluence. For example if we have H4 35/50 touch in confluence with H1 200 touch it is most likely for the price to reverse. If we have confirmation from price action in other time frame it will be even better etc... I hope this helps!

--- 帖子 #9340 ---
CHOROS (and other trend based systems) do not work well outside London/early US times. The best hours to trade this is between London open and first 2-3 hrs of US, otherwise you will be whipsawed...... So pick this time window, have some patience for a good opportunity and do not trade everything in sight.

An explanation on your chart. What I consider important is CONFLUENCE. The most "rules" or Price Behaviour patterns are applying at the moment of our 1st Touch, the higher will be our expectation of success for that entry. So Look at the Trend on the Higher TF (should I take all trades, or only long, only short ?) Is price retesting a previous S/R ? Are we close to a RN ? Things like those. I hope it can help you to bettere identify.

Well, it was bad but now I understand that it was also necessary. CHOROS was just the method that clicked with my experience and helped me cross to profitability. But I still believe that the previous trading exprerience helped me understand what I was doing. So if you are still in the learning curve, just stay in the game with a small account and accumulate experience. Don't try to project future profits, learn to be disciplined with your trading plan. For me, minimizing greed was a major factor in succcess.Sometimes I had hard time accepting the fact that I was out at 10 pips and the trade moved another 100 pips in my direction . But most times that I tried to wait longer the trade would turn and take my SL, so I learned to ignore what happens after I am out. Get in, grab a few, get out is the name of the game for me. That doens't mean that this is the right way to trade for you. Learn if you are comfortable with my targets (15pips per day), or if you are a more long term trader which means you need to focus in longer TFs and bigger pip targets (and bigger SL of course).

kostas, how do you calculate which higher tf ma is what on smaller tf ?

--- 帖子 #9611 ---
h4/10: 4hours = 4*(1hour)=4*(4*15min)=4*4*(3*5min)=4*4*3*(5min)=48*(5min) h4/10=5m/480

Yes, it is closer to 80%. Just a word of caution, it's very easy to get cocky when most of your trades work. So you need to keep a humble attitude towards the market and not become careless about your trades. Market is always right, you are just hitching a ride for a while. Also, be nimble with your targets. If you look at my earlier alert today, I could see the trade 2hrs before it happened. I grabbed +14p and got out at the first hesitation. If I had stayed, the trade would give me double the profit, but it could just as easily shoot up and take my SL. So I feel very good about my humble profit and don't feel that I missed an opportunity for more pips (greed devil ). This took a lot of personal discipline to achieve.....

--- 帖子 #9637 ---
Thank you for the advice! I know greed very well, but in a different way. For me, it's a mix of greed and fear. As soon as a trade is in profit, I don't want to give back even a single pipette. A red 1 min candle in a 1 hour buy setup? Almost enough to shake me out. This is my demon to fight... my entries are usually decent, it's about exits for me. Recent example: The H4 50 EMA setup in AUDUSD yesterday at 16:25 CEST. Beautiful rejection bar, I closed too quickly. I had to leave for an appointment etc. etc., but the truth is, I would have closed too early anyway. Some people say that taking profit 1 pip a trade does not kill your account. IMHO, that is not necessarily true, it depends on your winning rate. If you cut all your winners short but let your losers hit stop loss all the time, your R will be negative over the long term unless you have an unreal winning rate. That does not apply for your trades of course since your 15 pip target is proportional to your stop loss.

--- 帖子 #9838 ---
Hi this is checklist published some time ago here on the thread, look at your 35/50MA's, what trend they shows? 35/50 Bounce 1) Trade only with the trend of the moment. 2) 35 and 50 are fairly steep and parallel. (Now thinking 2 and 4 oclock). 3) 35 and 50 are not diverging. 4) Price pulls back to the MAs on a fairly sharp pullback. Two bars is best, but there is leeway here. 5) Either trade on the touch, if everything is perfect, 9 pipe SL (per “The Main Trades” doc) or 6) Fine tune the entry on the M5 by looking for a good price action entry (hammer, hanging man, engulfing bar), or confluence in the M5 (a parallel dance pattern in both time frames). 7) Stop Loss of about 15, but never more than 19 pips. 8) Move to break even quickly. 9) Exit to taste.

1. in the beginning, practice either touch trades or constraintment trades - c o n s i s t e n t l y. after it becomes second nature, practice other trade entries. 2. you took a stoploss after 60 minutes - on a m15 chart, generally a good entry will hit your TP in few minutes &amp; if it has taken over 60 minutes &amp; you witness trade is going against you, you can exit early &amp; not let it hit your stoploss. there will always be a better signal. moreover, that rectangle was not a good example of price being continuously constrained. notice that 10 ema was flat for sometime when you took the trade &amp; price was in a RANGE rather than CONSTRAINED by the ma's.

--- 帖子 #9985 ---
I'll try to explain constrainments: price after a trend move (or sometimes without) does obey 10 ema or some price level, like round number, and it keeps bouncing off and coming back to 10 ema for example or round price with quite small bars. don't confuse it with testing price as then bars are higher and not each of them touches the point - not sure if it helps

misterC look at the below two examples to understand the difference between a constrainment &amp; a range :- pic 1 shows you a constrainment of price near the 10 ema. notice small bars (more than 3-4) forming near ma's. pic 2 shows a range being developed inside the blue circle &amp; by the time an entry was made highlighted with a small green circle inside the blue circle, it was very evident that price is stuck in a range &amp; there were more sellers sitting above. price was NOT making higher highs &amp; higher lows &amp; it had to eventually drop because of a strong supply level.

Actually less than 15 CONSTRAINMENT trades, but 1000's of bounces. Please check again the definition of constrainment. It is when an MA constrains the price for more than 3-4 bars. --- 帖子 #10068 ---
Eur - Well, I basically intraday trade using the Dance/Choros strategy on the 15-minute charts - go with whatever side of the 50 the 5 and 10 are running on...unless I feel very strongly about a trade, I'll usually kick out if price goes more than 5 or 6 pips past the 10 against me, and then possibly re-enter on a first touch of the 50. Over time, I've gotten to where I'll often go with simply price crossing the 50, even if the 5 and 10 haven't quite made it there yet, as long as both are pointing strongly in that direction. On higher time frames, I watch the Hull Style ADX on both the one-hour and 4-hour charts, taking into consideration daily pivot points, support/resistance lines,, etc. Also, while volume is a tricky thing with forex, I do watch for significant spikes or drops in volume, using just a basic volume indicator, nothing fancy. Basically I'm always looking for trades where I can risk next to nothing - like buying aud/usd at .9400 with a stop around .9394 - but have a good potential reward, at least two or three times what I'm risking - I watch the daily range, and if, say, eur/usd is at the top of what's already a 120 pip range, I don't bet on it going up another 50 pips, or certainly not doing that and holding onto it. I'm not averse to taking the same position multiple times after having been stopped out for small profits or losses if the market still looks reasonably like it might go my way. I also watch the ranges and general direction of each session - Asian, London, New York - to me, it's usually a key reversal sign if London moves strongly in one direction in the morning, but then reverses back through its open after New York opens. I do NOT try to out-guess the monthly NFP Report. And every now and then, my intuition will just scream at me, "Hit that sell button on Gbp/Usd". I'm hampered by my ingrained prejudices in favor of aud and gbp and against eur. I try to catch a nice trend day when possible - there's usually at least one every week or two - and the rest of the time, I'm more focused on minimizing losses - I've found over time that if you can just avoid taking big hits, big wins will roll around often enough to keep your account growing.

--- 帖子 #10069 ---
Unfortunately, there are no magic, infallible indicators - but there are things, like the 50, 100, and 200MA, that one should keep an eye on. But I think one of the most valuable lessons is simply don't fight the market - if it isn't acting "right", just get out and re-evaluate - Try to never (I still do sometimes) get caught saying, "It's GOT to turn around and go up" (nooo, it doesn't). As I alluded to in an earlier post, Kostas alerted me to the wisdom of watching for pin bars well off the moving averages on the 5-min chart - sometimes those are just absolute gifts, especially when they line up well with potential support/resistance levels on higher time frames. If you can catch the 5-min turn on what will eventually prove to be a 4-hour, or even daily, turn, you can make a lot of money very easily.

--- 帖子 #10147 ---
Read the rules! 4. “Touch Trade Entries” must be taken off of a steep MA and are only acceptable IF Price has have moved at least 15 pips in the direction of the trade, and opposite pull back that creates the “touch” which is a short, very fast “run back” to the lines “touched”. (explained in the price action sections.) 1. Taken off a steep 10 EMA must also be above the 50 EMA/ 35 SMA Lines for longs and below for shorts. 1. ONLY trade the “touch” of the 10 EMA IF it is the FIRST or SECOND bar in the retrace, it has a VERY STEEP angle (see example later in manual), price has moved a strong “distance” of more than 15 pips and you trade it EXACTLY at the “touch” with no more then 9-11 pips SL. I can recommend: Use the simulator to learn . You will very quickly know when to enter!

--- 帖子 #10204 ---
Good morning ! So the best idea you had is learning the dance / choros ! .. and here are some answers, they should help you for the first steps. 1. The round numbers are every 50`s level ...for example in EU . 1,3600, 1,3650, 1,3700....... 2. You find the direction of the trend in m15 ! that tells you long or short for your next trade. if a higher TF confirm , is it excellent .. Open only trades , when there´s not another MA ( like a higher TF .. Ma 10 H4 or so ) in your trade direction . They can move very strong and kill your trade quickly . 3. If you open a touch trade and higher timeframes have also a touch on one of their MA´s , we call it a confluence... 4. Some traders take the M5 for entering .. some for exits ..and they are fu..ing successful with it .. But not me ! I donot take them anymore. I keep my charts as simple as possible and produce more green pips than red . Choros is not a drop and play system .. you have to train your " eyes " for it. You need some thousands screen hours... but if you really wanna trade , it´s your next wallet .. .. good luck

--- 帖子 #10231 ---
Hi Direwolf, I am not one of the seniors, but I'll try to answer your question. The way I see it, there are two constrianments in your chart. Price is constrained by the 10 and the 50 at the same time. The 10 constrains the price upwards, meaning we would look to sell, whereas the 50 constrains the price downwards, meaning we would try to buy. Usually with two MAs giving signals in different directions, we would follow the MA with the higher number, in this case the 50. In this chart however, the 50 is losing momentum, flattening out and the candles making lower lows. This does not indicate strength, so all in all, I would stand aside in this situation and take no trade. In case the 10 would be below the 50 there would be a valid trade. You would want to take the trade as close as possible to the constraining MA to keep the risk as small as possible. There is no good constrainment after price broke below the 50, so again no constrainment trade here. Hope this helps On a sidenote, there is a nice bouncing between the 10 and the 50 that could be played if they were further apart, but this is very advanced and I have never tried it live so far.
