--- 帖子 #10264 ---
This is not exact science, so sometimes prices touches to the pip, other times barely touches and yet other times overshoots. So just wait for some reaction on the lower timeframe and be prepared to enter with either scenario. If you look at the M5 at the area that I entered, you will see how price started rejecting that area, showing that it wanted to go up. My SL was a few pips below the H1 10 in case there was an overshoot.

Yeah I know what you mean. I think trading attracts (and more importantly keeps, because of their nature) people who are fighters in that they deal with failure by being more determined to succeed, thus getting into that vicious cycle of trading until something breaks - the bank account, their sanity or they succeed in it. The irony is though, that the fighter mentality actually hinders the result because it can drive that mentality to revenge trade or to fight back at the market and make the situation worse. One of the biggest skills I've learned (*cough* learning) as a determined 'fighter' in trading is when the market kicks me in the balls after deceiving me into something that was clearly going the other way that utterly infuriates me - I am to simply take it and walk away! It goes against every fiber in my body but it's the right thing to do. The perceived 'mass injustice' that needs to be rectified, the 'imbalance' that needs to be re-balanced... nup. Leave it as it is and go do something else. Hardest lesson to learn for me. I find this to be an industry that requires the determination to lick the wounds and get back in the ring fighting and yet requires the recognition to simply let it go and take it when it hurts the most. Very difficult to cultivate both attitudes simultaneously.

--- 帖子 #10312 ---
In the manual the scoop trade is stated to be against trend. Scooped Away: This is pretty simple, when the 10 EMA “turns” on one of the charts, the bar after it turns often retests the line. Sometimes the second one does like a “touch” trade in a normal setup. Either way, that retest often presents a fairly solid counter trend entry worth at least 20 pips. If you are using the Scripts properly, you can take the first TP out really quick, move to Be and wait for the trade to run your way, or bounce at the higher lines and reverse back into the trend of the moment. Just watch the charts, you'll see what I mean.

This is a trade I took this morning nicely demonstrating 2 things: 1 ) Be nimble in your targets if you play smaller TF 2) Never forget the higher TFs, specially if you are countertrend So my trade was based on M5 12 bounce short with a target around DS1, I was also ready to close at WP. I closed around the RN (1.6700) for about 13p. Another trader of CHOROS looking at higher TFs should have entered long around the area I exited since it was a nice confluence of WP, RN, H4 10, H1 35/50. The news pushed this one quickly to the next RN (1.6750). So when choosing a TF your targets and SL should be according to that TF. Of course, if your smaller TF trade agrees with the higher TF direction(with-trend) then targets can be modified if you catch the right trend in line with the main trend. Hope the above is clear

--- 帖子 #10387 ---
NOT a ping-pong. This is an early scoop-up. Usually, when price crosses above the 10, it will try to retest and then shoot up, that would be the traditional scoop-up. You took it earlier. Ping-Pong is usually when the 35-50 diverge and then the price pings-pongs between the 35 and the 50.:nerd:

No , that one is not good .. , the green candle 3 candles before would be the correct one , BUT :: there was no real trend!! So we trade retraces in a trend. If the possible trade ran without us , better donot enter .. wait for the next chance. Important is to wait until the angle is steep enough .. ( depends on the pair , in EJ I´ll never open a trade with a move less than 20 pips ) To learn quickly this kind of trading , you should use the simulator . My advice : Put it to the fastest level in M15 GBP/USD .. and watch the forming breakouts , touches .. dances .. Of course the fastest level is much too quick for a trade , but it gives you a quick view what we are looking for .

--- 帖子 #10537 ---
I know you asked Sesam this but allow me to break it down for you 1. The more screen hours you spend the more experience you gain and the more setups you can catch; trading can not be thoroughly standardized; some days you spend 1 hour and make 50 pips, some days you spend 5 hours and make nothing....there are days and days; and this leads into point two, as you can't completely standardize trading you can't really tell how many setups you find, but if you look at the market through the rules you might find enough setups to have a pretty good profit at the end of the month (in my experience, everyday gives you a good trade if you watch 6 pairs, I watch 9)...and 3rd...In the manual it's clearly stated that you can average 40 pips a day (I'm guessing that's pro level), but if you follow the rules and trade correctly I don't see a reason why you can't get an average of 15/day P.S. This system works, make your own statistics P.P.S. In the beginning don't risk more than 1% per trade/2% per day (in my opinion, but again this is relative to your risk aversion)

I'm sure that Master Kostas will have a much better reply, but I wouldn't take that one as Scooped Up, or at least not at the undecision candle where you took it (just after a strong bearish candle). I tried to imagine what was your analisis for entering there: perhaps you saw a strong bullish candle breaking through the EMA and were waiting for a confirmation of the upper move, after the possible short retracement ? If this was the reason, the doji doesn't properly look as a confirmation candle usually. It could have been a good "Double Top" Trade, but not a good Scooped Up. It ended good, but the DD was a little strong there. Perhaps was your SL was below the previous swing low ? This could make sense, but the R:R in this trade would not look very good. --- 帖子 #10604 ---
Welcome! Keep in mind that there is a discretionary component to this strategy. Yes, on NZDUSD the 35.50 MA had a relatively decent angle at one point, but if you switch to a higher timeframe you notice that there is a strong resistance level that contains the price. Also that level was hit after a pretty strong move upward, so odds are that price doesn't have enough power to shoot through, and also as Sesam mentioned today is a holiday. When trading keep in mind price action and SR levels, and of course, the Dance rules . In my opinion/experience, a way to filter 35.50 trades is to count the candles from the high / low; just like the 2 candle bar rule, you can count 5,6 for the 35.50 MAs. Only keep in mind that this filtering method is not in the original Dance rules! Use it only if you decide that it can improve your trading.

--- 帖子 #10610 ---
I should have explained better; but before I clarify, I want to emphasize again that this is not a rule from the Dance, it's just something I picked up after lots of screen time . First of all 35.50 MAs must have a decent angle. Let's say that the price makes a high and starts retracing towards 35.50 MAs; if it takes more than 5 (maximum 6) candles to get there I will not take the trade; same goes when price makes a low and starts retracing upward towards 35.50. There are few exceptions here: I might take the trade if the 35.50 are converging with a good SR level or if price makes clear candle pattern. That's pretty much it . Remember to also keep in mind what's going on on larger timeframes.

--- 帖子 #10611 ---

--- 帖子 #10624 ---
Yes, screen time will help you to better recognize touches. Keep in mind that there is repainting on the last candle; for example you can watch the chart now and have 5 pips between price and 10EMA, but after 15 minutes the touch could look perfect (case in point the GBPUSD touch I mentioned earlier). With screen time you will train yourself to spot these kind of situations and profit from them. Also, regarding 10EMA touches keep in mind: -a 10EMA touch is valid when 35.50 have a decent angle; -the price must make a move in the direction pointed by the 35.50 of at least 15 pips; -it must not take price more that two candles to return to 10 EMA; -1st touches are money makers, 2nd touches are riskier; I would take a 2nd touch only if there is a SR level converging with the 10EMA;

--- 帖子 #10695 ---
In 1987, Andy Krieger, a 32-year-old currency trader at Bankers Trust, was carefully watching the currencies that were rallying against the dollar following the Black Monday crash. As investors and companies rushed out of the American dollar and into other currencies that had suffered less damage in the market crash, there were bound to be some currencies that would become fundamentally overvalued , creating a good opportunity for arbitrage . The currency Krieger targeted was the New Zealand dollar, also known as the kiwi . Using the relatively new techniques afforded by options, Krieger took up a short position against the kiwi worth hundreds of millions of dollars. In fact, his sell orders were said to exceed the money supply of New Zealand. The selling pressure combined with the lack of currency in circulation caused the kiwi to drop sharply. It yo-yoed between a 3 and 5% loss while Krieger made millions for his employers. One part of the legend recounts a worried New Zealand government official calling up Krieger's bosses and threatening Bankers Trust to try to get Krieger out of the kiwi. Krieger later left Bankers Trust to go work for George Soros .

--- 帖子 #10715 ---
[quote=Chopy;7460274] It's basically about touches (first or not) and timeframes : Answer : We trade with the trend of the moment ( M15 ) to find the trade direction . If higher TF´s confirm .. GREAT ! Keep in mind , MA´s in higher TF´s can brake your M15 entry .. The higher TF MA´s can give a strong run , but they don´t happen " every hour " !! Also should not be in direction of your trade a round number or a Pivot . They work like a resistance level if they are in your way to target . -What are the conditions for a valid "second" first touch ? Does the price have to move for a certain amount of pips ? Does it need to open on the other side of the MA, and then come back ? Answer: There are no! First is first , second is second. A touch is a touch ! .. but after the first touch it´s more riky to enter in a second touch .. I cannot recommend it ! -Also, does the rule that says that a valid touch happen when the touch only requiered 2 candle to "get there" apply in all these different circumstences ? (once again, every timeframe and every MA) Answer : The best way to take them with the " two bar rule " is to take it with two bars to get there ..( if no 2 bars = no two bar rule ) There happen many touches .. not all with only 2 bars to get there .. but still valid if the angles are steep enough . ( the steepness of the angle shows you it´s " power " in this set up ) Wish all dancers a nice weekend .. Guido

--- 帖子 #10731 ---
Welcome to the thread! First of all please post full screen shots of the trade so everyone can see the pair you traded and get a good idea of how the price looks like. I can only guess that is EURUSD you traded, or EURJPY and your trades were executed when news were released (bad trades!!!)...anyway...post complete screenshots of your active chart. If you are here for anger and greed management you are off-topic, yes the Dance manual does have a chapter where psychology of traders is discussed but in this thread we mainly post trades that we take following the Dance strategy and try to help each other get better at taking trades using the Dance. Looking at what you posted I don't see any resemblance to a Dance trade (because if there were no news dancers would buy where you sold), so my advice is: read the manual (really read it), use the simulator (I know Sesam would/will tell you this ) and post complete screen shots. About your anger/greed thing...we've all been there...but we found a way to manage it. The thing is that this part of trading is very very discretionary because it is related to ones personality and we are all different. The only thing I can say is what everyone else would say: Don't let feelings mess up your trading...but how you do that, how you reach that point, it's up to you. You can and should read materials on this matter, because there are a lot of people who studied this subject...my recommendation is Alexander Elder - Trading for a Living (1st chapter), Mark Douglas - The Disciplined Trader. Keep in mind that how you deal with your anger / greed it up to you...the best way (again in my opinion) is to rationalize it, stay focused on the trades and don't let it affect your trading. Make decisions driven by reason and logic NOT by feelings! Hope this helps!

--- 帖子 #10732 ---

Hi jhezzz, your psychological question may not address me as I am still bloody green behind my ears. Personally, I hate giving up. So it is not an option for me. I still practice on the simulator. And to be honest: I am not profitable on the simulator all the time. But it does train my eyes to see the signals. The issue with the simulator is, it is way to fast to catch the good signals on time and ride it, even for a couple of pips. This is the challenge. The simulator is way more difficult. But once you see the signals on the simulator, you'll see the signals on live charts. Stick to Demo as I am doing it. Once you see the signals on live charts, you need to practice to filter weak signals. Coming back to your initial question of how not to give up. Just as Clay stated in the original thread. You only fail if you give up! Try to concentrate only on one signal of your preference on the simulator and try to catch that one on time . For me it is the 35/50 touch trades. You might need to lower the speed when it is aproaching your entry spot. Cheers,

--- 帖子 #11143 ---
Hey man, Remember how many times I commented on appropriate zoom? Best suggestion I have is to fix the pip axis and keep the same width on the bars. This way your eyes are trained and after a while you can easily recognize a trend (which by the way is best to judge by the 35/50 steepness, the 10 is ok only for short trades). In regards to R:R my only comment is that I never payed any attention to it. It feels to me like dictating the market what to do, and as you know the market doesn't like to be dictated.... So if I risk 15 pips and I see a profit of 10 pips trying to reverse, I will take the pips and run, so my R:R is crappy but the account is not...

--- 帖子 #11144 ---
let me please say few words more... I never look for trades 1:3, or 1;2, 1:1.... you never can be sure how much market gives you, so why you try predict your R:R? This is a probability game. tell me please if you have 100 USD lying on the table and there is 95% sure you can get it if you risk 200? What will you do? Or you prefer risk 33 USD to get this 100 USD, but you have only 30% probability you win? What I would like to say is take what market offers, your target is not R:R, your target is not 1% or 4% daily, your target IS TO TAKE GOOD TRADE and this should be your ONLY concern.

Just started with this method so I can't contribute much but here's how I set scale. (1H example). 1. Left click chart 2. Press F8 which brings up this screen.... Attached Image 3. Set scale to whatever it needs to be (as Kostas described, 1H is set to 200 pips) 4. Then use the slider (shown below) to center the candles in the chart. Be careful though because the slider is rather thin and you can easily left click and end up rescaling the chart which then means you go back to 2. Alternatively you can left click on any blank area of the chart (typically used for side scrolling) and centre the chart that way. Attached Image Hope it helps.

So you can see quick how large the opportunities are when you trade this style. And now to your question . 1 I´d always have a look about the steepnes of the angles as first. 2 Can I imagine the price will continue in the direction of the trend ( like in the morning .. no speacial important news expected or so the next 45 min or longer) For me it´s more important if the chart gives me picture that I understand! If the 35sma and the 50 ema are very close to eachother , but the 10 ema has a wide spread , that´s the time for AAA entries. That means if the price ran with the trend an I´m sure it will continue , I´m waiting for a retrace . Specially with one or two big candles( two bar rule ) like in a post I did , a couple of days ago: http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...65#post7691765 These cases happens not every day , but in the end of the week you ´ll have more green pips than red ! --- 帖子 #11444 ---
In my opinion, you are both right.... The touch of the EMA 10 is usually best taken as soon as it touches the line and take profit with the first reaction (so even if it is a fake reaction you get your profit before it takes your SL). For the M15/H1 35/50 is best to wait for a reaction first and then enter. For example when I trade the M15 35/50 I wait to see reaction on M5 and then enter for my 10-15 p.

For simply this, you might not be interested, trading manually, but DATFRA also provides an excellent simulator for MT4 to test out our "manual" strategies , such as the Dance of course. It has a nice little window with BUY/SELL, TP/SL, LOTS, and CLOSE. Then of course you get all the stats of your paper-trading. The simulator, as you for sure now, is the BESTBESTBEST and "only" way to test out our strategies and get trained well with real data market. Ah, last but not least, DATFRA has an integrated function to download accurate tick-by-tick FX history from forextester.com , one of the best for this. --- 帖子 #11538 ---
I am just goning to go out on a limb here and guess that he is talking about when the 10EMA is just starting to change direction. In these cases there might be a pullback to the 10EMA during the change of direction, but we dont take these trades because there is no trend direction. In other words, what some people would call a "choppy market" or a "ranging market". A good example of this would be the EURUSD on M15 chart an hour or so after London open today. We get a change in direction, after london open and price "turns" the 10 EMA and then follows up with a 2 bar pullback. This would not be a legitimate trade . I think this is what he is referring to. We dont take trades while the MA is just turning, we need a clear trend. Sesam once pointed out to me that a good measure of this is that all of the MA's are heading in one direction not just the 10EMA. If the 35/50 are flat we are still in to mouch of a risk for a reversal to take the trade. Cant post a pic right now. So this link will have to do. https://www.tradingview.com/x/dUBt1ZT4/ This would have ended up being a winning trade, but not a good trade in regards to risk.

So look on your chart , are 35 Sma + 50 Ema in a nice uptrend ?? are they close to eachother ?? Is it a clear retrace in a trend ? Higher Tf´s confirmed ? You better start with the simulator and get an eye for good entries. and one more reason to don´t enter : the market has a range about 15 pips the last 2 hours, what is very slow. --- 帖子 #11720 ---
Good question, I have also asked myself this many times. The process was not as straightforward for me as this summary is going to make it look. Writing about it will help me to analyze it better, probably helping to improve my trading performance in the future, so here it goes. This is going to be quite a long post as I had to change quite a lot of things in order to get really profitable. I am sure many here have taken the same path / are still struggling with some of the things I am writing about here, and I hope my experiences can be of some help to others. Before going into detail, I would like to give a short summary why I am trading Choros. As many guys here, I have tried a lot of (very different) trading systems over time. Some relied on S/R, others on price action, others on the heavy use of indicators. Some seemed to work in hindsight, like a renko system that I have tried. In hindsight I would think “Wow, I would have traded this big move for sure!” only to see that many of these moves were news spikes that only lasted seconds and were impossible to get into cleanly. That of course does not mean all renko systems don’t work, just that I could not get this special one to work for me. Somehow, I have found the Choros charts appealing visually, and the system had many characteristics that were important for me. A big thing for me is that a system should give several trading opportunities per day for me. I am not good at letting trades run and see parts of my profit being eaten by countermoves. I want to get in and out fairly quickly, and in case a trade goes wrong, I want to have a chance to make the money back soon. Many are probably thinking “uh-oh, revenge trading” right now, and that is a good point. More on this later. After spending some time with Choros, I tried other systems, but somehow ended up coming back to the Choros charts because somehow I felt a sense of attraction to them and the logic of this system. Also, Choros has some rules but can still be customized, and adapted to the current market behavior, in contrast to many semi-automatic systems that use a lot of indicators. Another thing that is important for me, the trading ideas behind Choros can be summarized quite easily and clearly (like “Choros is mostly trading pullbacks in a trend”), something that is not possible for many systems that just combine several indicators. This way, I know exactly what I am trying to do and can analyze better why it has (not) worked in my trades. What I also like is the multi - time frame approach. Often, higher time frames explain why trades on lower time frames don’t work. So, after learning the basics of Choros, I found myself to be slightly profitable. My account balance would usually look like a slowly rising whipsaw pattern: many small gains, some big losses. Sometimes a losing streak would wipe out a couple of week’s profits within a few hours. This time of trading was emotionally very difficult for me. Whenever I gave away my profits to a losing streak I had very strong negative emotions. I knew at some point that I had to stop trading for the day or I would lose too much, but after I stopped I felt miserable and stupid for losing so much money (a rather small amount actually, but I am always thinking percents with my trading). Still, quitting was never an option for me. I knew I somehow was on the right track, but I had to change some things and started analyzing my trading and most importantly myself and my behavior patterns. More on this later when I have more time to write (long post ahead).

When I did my weekly performance analysis today I found something interesting that I wanted to share, since I think many experience the same thing. The picture below shows the balance of one of my trading accounts for a certain period of time. This is the standard Metatrader report, the x-axis shows the trades, not days. There are many things one can learn from this chart, here I would like to focus on one: The interesting thing is that my performance shows three clear phases, which I have labelled A - C. Phase A: I did not really know how to trade in this period. The account balance shows a clear downtrend, the vertical lines are mostly not successful trades but me adding more money to the account. Whenever I traded, I lost money on average. Phase B: I started trading Choros and slowly got a feeling for this kind of trading. From this time on, the account balance is rising in principle for many trades in a row, but I messed up repeatedly and got my account into deep drawdowns quickly, after which I added more money to the account (vertical lines). This phase can be summarized as "I knew how to trade in principle, but I had mental shortcomings like problems with discipline or my system still had a flaw". I realized what was happening and worked hard to eliminate it, which brought me to Phase C: Rising balance, making money from trading, being profitable. Once I had eliminated the problem from phase B, my trading improved greatly, and so did my account balance. There were still three times when I reverted to my old habits, but I was able to trade my way out of the drawdown without having to add money to the account. You can see from the slope of the lines after drawdown that this was done with a high-risk style of trading - still not the best way possible. Whether you are profitable or not, I think analyzing your account history is the most important thing you can do in order to increase your trading performance! This is true for all trading systems of course, I am just sharing this here because I became profitable using Choros and adapting / customizing it. What I wrote above - indentifying your shortcomings and eliminating them - sounds very simple when written in just a few lines. In reality, it was a rather long, sometimes painful and demotivating process for me. In the end it was worth it, but I also know in hindsight that I could have gotten to where I am now - profitable trading - much easier. I hope this post can help some of you to get there quicker than I did. Thank you Kostas for all your work and efforts to help others with this thread, I know it has helped me greatly!

--- 帖子 #11861 ---
Hi maxtill, a rule of thumb that works well for me: If you have a fast correction after a strong move, look for touch trades. Strong move = steep MAs; fast correction: the manual says two candles in the respective timeframe to reach the 10EMA, slightly longer for 35 / 50. You'll develop a feel for it, read Sesamstrae's posts about the simulator. 35 / 50 especially powerful if you have a candle closing dead on the MA This one is a great example how to place such a trade: http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...86#post7473686 Slow correction (taking many candles, like the ones in your pic: Look for constrainment trades Like here, 35 / 50 constrainment, blue and purple lines: http://www.forexfactory.com/showthre...85#post7465785 In general: The more confluence (MAs, round numbers, pivot points, major Fibs etc.) the better and the more likely your trade is going to work out. Over time you'll also develop a feeling for the different currencies, like how much space is required for the touches to work. Read the manual several times, you'll discover something new every time, depending on the knowledge / experience you gained in the meantime. Also, I would try to focus on one trade type in the beginning, honing and perfect it. You can get impressive results from touch or constrainment trades alone. When you have mastered one type of trade, add more tools to your belt. The most important thing: Learn when not to trade. This is the key to profitability, and one of the hardest things to master. The examples you showed were not high probability trades. Wait till the chances are clearly in your favor, even if you miss some profitable trades. Hope this help! TG

Hi maxtill, here is a quick analysis of your first chart the way I see it: The first touch happened a few bars before you marked it, but it was not a good trade imho One could argue that what you marked is the first pullback after an overshoot. Same points as for the first touch apply. Those big overshoots usually flatten out the MAs, so no good trade. There is no "space", meaning the pullback is too small to trade it for my taste. Price didn't move far enough in one direction. There are two nice-looking pinbar-like bars touching the EMA10 as well as being repeatedly rejected by the daily pivot point, forming a mini-constrainment. I often trade a setup like this, but not this one, because You would be trading against a higher-timeframe uptrend. This could be a higher-timeframe pullback and you would be trading against it. The steppy lines (is that a word?) show H1 35 / 50 MA In this case the trade would have worked out for a good amount of pips reaching its natural target daily S1, but it was no high-probabilty setup. "Classic" dance / Choros is a trading style with multi-timeframe analysis. Being aware of what happens in higher timeframes can save you from suboptimal trades. I would recommend you do a list with pro / con points when analysing past trades. How about you start with the second setup, GU? Post what you see and we can discuss it. Have a nice weekend, TG

--- 帖子 #11871 ---
maxtill, My biggest struggle with this system has been knowing when NOT to trade as others have mentioned. I like trading, so sometimes I try hard to look for trades -- and I often find a lot of bad ones when I operate this way. Obviously, study the manual over and over and work with the simulator... this will strengthen your sense for good entries But, I have found that one very simple trick has worked well for me to keep pips and stay profitable in the longer term. That trick is: always look for reasons not to trade. If there are any reasons you should not take a trade, then don't. I have even found that it works best for me if I walk away and do something else. Come back later and check the markets again to see if things are back in your favor. Always look for reasons not to trade. If you shouldn't trade, then don't. That way you weed out the bad trades and only take A+ entries. And there are PLENTY of these. PS that includes non-technical factors like do you have enough time to manage the trade (this depends on timeframe)? Are you tired/stressed/hungry/angry? Did you lose recently and are feeling emotional? etc... Regards

Interestingly, the small devil on my shoulder urging me to take the wrong trades even when my mind knew they were not good ones is almost always silent now. But lets say GJ or GCAD in a h1 chart puuuh , im not sure if 30 pips is enough ! In fact ; we use the MA as a dynamic support/ resistance level , where the price dances with . All other is a kind of view and persolality / dircretionary trading . Basics are " steep angle , enough space to reach the targets , round numbers stuff and a little bit logical thinking, priceaction and timing!! ( During the Non Farm Payrolls , Im sure 13 pips will not be enough as a stop loss in GU ) and so on . Its all training. Good luck Guido

--- 帖子 #11988 ---
Hello n8bizz and welcome to this thread . You started well , because you didnt enter without a clean and clear entry .. the best you can do ! And your m15 chart , the 35+50 are flat .= no entry But for the beginning Id only use the 10 Ema , 35Sma , 50 Ema in every chart . The reason is simple : One of the things what shows us a Moving average is the steepness of the angle in the timeframe where we want enter . steep means strong trend . It shows us if the trend is still there or is it too sloppy for entries . Next thing is: Mas from higher timeframes can be very strong , we don t trade against them . Make sure , the trend is strong , priceaction looks nice, timing ( beware of the news or closed markets ) ,enough space to the next round number ...... higher timeframe confirms .. then enter . some like the pivot level , some not .. Last but now least : Your H1 chart shows a " MA -soup " what is when 10 Ema is between 35Sma and 50 Ema .. we don t enter then . Good luck and green pips EDIT : by the way .. EU can be very strange IMO , look at GU , this pair reacts wonderful and is better to trade . Best example is today the M15 chart .. Guido

--- 帖子 #12003 ---
Nope , no german translation , but simple. all 50 and 100 levels 1.1150 1.1200 1.1250 and so on are levels the price respects very often. and now to your eurex chart : in fact the indices are not that easy to trade , reason is the " open and close" while night and that case the lines need some hours to build a clear picture . Yes, it is possible to trade it , but take a look on the pic M5 eurex : The 35/ 50 are not tight to eachother , they re seperated what isnt a clean and clear sign for me in being stable .. or better said .. how many candles more it is still stable . The M15 is constraining all the way up onn the 10 ema , but not steep , its very sloppy . , but in opposite direction is a large gap , Id be careful with trading when theres a large gap . careful until it is closed , or dont trade against it, specially weekend gaps . If you dont have a clean view , better skip look for AAA entries and learn to handle them .. From that moment you know how a great and valid entry signal looks like , from that moment you know how to train your skills. steepness of the angles is about 12-2 and 4 to 6 EDIT , for the beginning look for GU and EJ entries , these pairs react nice with the lines and have a good mix of volatility and not too noisy . as long as they are trending , as long as you ll find nice entries . Guido

H1 we had a first touch 35 sma before and we had enough space to my target , it was much below 50 ema h1 .. right ?? H4 10 ema a second touch as well , right ?? Noo , no respect !! only the 10 Ema / very steep was nicely respected ! and that was my view how to trade the market in this kind ! Second thing what is important to know is timing!! In the european morning , we have often breakouts in trend direction .. in the european afternoon , we have often retraces, or fake breakouts when US comes with new " money" in the market. and one thing is always the same : The big fishes try to shake us out .. shaking and shaking until our accounts melting.. --- 帖子 #12203 ---
Hi digf, I'll try and explain. Start with a clean chart screen, then load on 3 "Dance" charts with the same currency say EUR/USD and minimize them. 1. Take the first "dance" chart and size it to 2/3 of your screen, timeframe 15M 2. Take the 2nd "dance" chart and size it to 1/3 of your screen, timeframe Daily and place it in the top left corner. 3. Take the 3rd "dance" chart and size it to 1/3 of your screen, timeframe 1H and place it below the 2nd one. I hope I'm clear enough, if not ask again...

--- 帖子 #12204 ---
And by the way, when you have done that, go to the top left on your screen, click on file, scroll down to where it says "profiles" click on that, go to the right and hit "save as" give the profile a name i.e. Dance and you will see it saved at the bottom of your screen for next time.

--- 帖子 #12298 ---
Hi Desiree, do you trade with the MetaTrader 4 platform? If yes, then you should open your platform, go to the File -&gt; Open Data Folder, a new window will open with all the files and folders from your platform. Copy "The Dance" folder from the Profiles folder from the Dance tools to the "profiles" folder in the MetaTrader data folder you've just opened from your platform. Restart your platform and you should be able to open a new profile named The Dance. Same goes for the templates, indicators and scripts - you have to copy all the files from each one of those folders to the respective folders in your Metatrader folder. There's only one difference with the indicators and scripts - their folders might be placed in the MQL4 folder in your MetaTrader data folder. You can find more information in the Manual under the section "Setting up the charts" and further (it might have slightly changed though, due to some Metatrader updates). If you have any questions, feel free to ask

Two trades from today: EJ and UJ M15 10ema bounces. Unfortunatelly, this is NOT the solution to your problem. This is not an error message, this is the way scripts work. You drag them on the chart, they get executed and then removed FROM THE CHART. Only EA stay on the chart and probably don't leave this kind of message. Sorry, but you need to look somewhere else. Try to uninstall the MT4, remove all the files (incl. scripts) from C:\Users\[USERNAME]\AppData\Roaming\MetaQuotes\Terminal\ Install the newest version of MT4, make sure you place the scripts in the right directory and see if it helps.

--- 帖子 #12373 ---
You never know how it's gonna turn out ;-) There are mainly two methods that I use for entries: You either enter exactly at the touch (only LEGIT TOUCH trades per manual) OR you enter based upon price action (primarily pin bars, dojis &amp; double tops/bottoms, sometimes internal bars, personally I avoid engulfing as explained in manual and don't rely on price action itself - still trade of an MA and preferably MA in confluence with pivots or/and RN), WAIT for the price action bar to close and enter immediately ON THE OPENING OF THE NEXT CANDLE . Sometimes you may mix up: you see the touch, but you are still unsure (higher timeframes not by your taste or 35/50 steep but a bit too far away) so you wait for a confirmation from price action (at the same or lower timeframe - that's tweaking your entry). Check the attachment - both methods are very clear on it: you could have entered either at the touch, which would be the best case here, but you also could have entered on the next bar after the pin. Pay attention to the 35/50 MAs ( steep and close together - repeat it constantly everytime you want to enter a touch trade), and luckily 3 resistance levels above. The more a setup you are looking at is resembling the one from attachment, the higher probability it will go your way (short in this example, but of course long for an up side down setup).

--- 帖子 #12379 ---
The MA does not affect the previous bars, just the one that hasn't been closed. It takes some practice but if you analyse historical charts you will know, that if a medium or long candle that closed below or above the MA looks as if it JUST touched it with NO wick trough it - it means it didn't. For a touch to count it had to go at least 2-3 pips (sometimes more for longer candles) through it while looking at it historically. Other method is less conservative but I have seen people using it - define a 2 pips channel around an MA (option in MT4, MA properties, Level tab) and allow yourself for entries even if the price isn't touching it, but just reaches that channel. Then, if the price takes off it will create that "artificial" MA touch anyway. But it adds more risk to your position, there will be times price will hit your SL, which normally would leave you 2 pips reserve. Same with TP - may reverse 2 pips away from it, where with a proper touch it would hit it - I hope you know what I mean.

--- 帖子 #12391 ---
1) You will trade more often but at the same time your success rate will decrease - near touches will hit your SL more often as it will be lower for shorts and higher for longs and you risk the price will reverse on you from time to time where as with the solid touches it would manage to hit TP. OR 2) Due to making your R:R worse you will lose more and gain less - SL will have to be larger by those 2-3 pips and TP will be smaller. I am staying out of those trades as there are sufficient proper touches. But this is just my opinion and Guido has more experience in those setups. Something in the middle though would be looking for some PA confirmation on M5 after a near touch - that's something I would trade from time to time. All the best to you all.

Hey Jkdt - I may not have taken your first and last trades... I like to obey the 2 bar rule. I've been bitten by not paying attention to it too many times. i personally like to consider it too many bars if price hesitates. Your last GU example is the better one for this case. While it only took 2 red bars to "get there"and touch the EMA10, there were 4 candles before that with small bodies and LONG wicks. That tells me that price has found its level for the day and may not want to try breaking it again. This doesn't always hold true, but I just personally try to stay out of those... but who cares, you watched it closely and made a profit! That is a great profit for the week. The key is just seting goals and being consistent. I try to shoot for 25-50 pips per day and I'm done. Usually I just stop at 25 and walk away. If I have already made 4 or 5 trades, and I only have a couple pips, I'll also walk away for the day because my brain gets too tired haha. Also, if I lose 2 trades in a row I have to stop for a bit and rethink what I am doing - and what the market is doing. I like your GY trade more than your GU trade. 35/50 was very flat on the GU trade, I would have waited for them to show a trend to developing. But you made a profit! The past couple of weeks have been nice and consistent for me! keep up the good trading everyone! and happy weekend! Sam

--- 帖子 #12502 ---
It was difficult for me to grasp the difference between the two as well and I'm still not sure, if I am absolutely correct, since these definitions have been used differently by different traders, but I'll try to explain how I see it. If I'm wrong, please correct me I would distinguish two explanations. 1. The first one is like you said - the time and the number of candles it takes for a setup (or a pattern) to form on current time frame. The bounce usually "builds up" and consists of several candles, which bounce into the same level and also might be constrained there. Touches are usually quicker and often form when price just touches the level and goes (might touch it a couple or several times though, but usually within 1 or 2 candles on the TF the setup is forming on, i.e. current TF). So a bounce trade in such case would provide more confirmation (both on lower TF's and on current) and the entry would be after COB at least after a couple of candles. Whereas a touch trade could be opened right after the price approached the MAs with some fine-tuning on lower TFs. Sometimes touches can turn into bounces (UC and UJ examples attached) - when a trade is taken early, but the price doesn't go quickly in direction of a trade, but forms a bounce setup with multiple bouncing candles instead. 2. The second explanation would be much simpler - the moment of entry. In this case the touch trade is taken at the very touch of the price and MA, i.e. approximately the moment the price slides through the MA without or almost without any fine tuning. And the bounce would be taken after the price has bounced into the MA a couple of times or more (which usually can be seen on the lower TFs during fine-tuning). I hope that didn't sound too confusing and sorry if it did Please see the images attached, I've tried to find several examples. If you have any questions, feel free to ask. Once again, experienced dancers, please correct me if I'm wrong. Attached Image Attached Image Attached Image Attached Image (click to enlarge)

--- 帖子 #12530 ---
Awaken, I am also practicing the method, but as far as I know a touch is a touch and PA is PA - you don't count touches to go ahead with another PA trade. You will find many examples in the manual that confirm this. However, you have to use some common sense as well - if you see the price moved a very long distance in one direction - well, you don't want to be getting in at the last station. So I would say: although PA trades are allowed regardless of touch count, the higher the count the more cautious you should be, for example look for extra confirmation, confluences, extra 35/50 steepness, etc. Also: PA has a built in 2 safety features: price itself confirms a possible continuation after a retrace (they signal the fuel that run the retrace might be already gone) and often they define a tighter than usual SL just above the formation. With touches you don't have that extra safety, essentially you might be entering at the top of a very strong candle which might be your trend reversing against you - therefore, as a safety feature for touches - they should be counted to reduce the risk of entering at the end.

Very nice observation and a nice example, Jkdt I don't trade scoops as I usually spot them afterwards and can't catch them in advance, at least not on the lower TF's. There were two nice scoop examples on EU and UJ H4 in the last couple of days though, but these require much more attention, time and proficiency IMO, so I only watched them If you see more scoops forming on M15 and have enough time, could you please post a notification in the Choros Interactive? I would really appreciate a couple of live examples. I think that it all depends on your risk management and circumstances. I usually set myself a limit of risk per trade and per day and try not to exceed it. If I take two non-related trades at one time, the same rule applies - not to exceed the daily limit and the limit per trade. Just as if it were two separate trades taken at different time. However, I am very cautious about taking simultaneous positions in highly correlated pairs (quite often they offer same signals at the same time), since that might be considered as simply doubling the risk. So if I am very firm about the setups and my daily limit allows that, I might take them both with a full position size each and be ready for the double risk (however I would already consider this as overtrading risk-wise for myself). If I'm not that confident and/or the daily limit might be exceeded, I might take each of them with half. It's possible to take only one of them with a better setup with full size, but I got tricked several times being caught in a slower trade or in a wrong one, so prefer to take both with a half position. And it also depends on the SL - if it's very small and I'm not risking more on two trades than I would normally risk on one, why not take them both with full size? But that's just my personal experience, maybe it's too discretionary. So I'm not sure if I violate the rules or not and any comments are very welcome

--- 帖子 #12543 ---
There has been some earlier chat about strategy tester and the inability to check HTFs. Well, there is an easy way out. You just need to have the HTFs prepared in regular charts in a position that doesn't reveal what's ahead (just hit HOME button and carefully scroll forward using arrows or page dn to where you wanna be). Then if you want to check what's going on there with your next setup, for example in M15, you just hit F12. Enough times to get you where you want and carefully enough so you don't spoil it. It's not a big deal, but some mt4 users still don't know the F12 (shift+F12 for reverse) works that way and this is an easy way that allows to make the simulator experience more realistic. Green pips 2 you all.

--- 帖子 #12572 ---
If rectangle is after strong move up/down and does not appear below/above round number (against trend), or below or above daily pivot (against trend) or some support/resistance point (against trend) then it means the trend will continue In other words, lets assume trend goes up. rectangle appears just below round number - bit tricky and may go up, but may be rejected. Rectangle appears above round number - I'd go for it and go long Rectangle appears just somewhere after run up, no s/r points - I'd go long but another condition. If rectangle is too long and already went over or below 10 ema - I'd think again, I'd check higher timeframes

--- 帖子 #12605 ---
Ideally, I would always want to have SL no more than 7.5 pips on a trade. Because I set my overall risk per trade 3% per 15 pips. In that case for every 15 pips I would get, it will be 1:2 R/R ratio. For 30 pips 1:4 R/R. But not always i set 7.5 pips from the start. Sometimes its 10,11,12. If it should be above that, I would probably skip the trade or wait for better entrance. That is how I do it currently. I dont know if its ideal, but I think it might be, at least for me.

--- 帖子 #12606 ---
Hello, Just my $0,02 about SL: it is all down to your personal preference. I always take touch trades with 16 SL (see historically how that works on M15...), if the setup is very good or extending by another 2 pips allows to take advantage of some extra S/R - I'll do it. But I never enter a trade of M15 with SL greater that 18 (and I have to see a solid reason to go for 18). With PA - it's way easier, top/bottom of the PA setup plus spread+1 pip max. Sometimes if I get greedy I go with 16 SL on PA trades regardless. But never do more than 18 pips SL on M15. It is personal thing though, less SL = smaller single loss but more failed trades. More SL = bigger losses but higher success rate. BUT: most important is the psychological adjustment of YOUR SL. Choose the SL so that you won't beat yourself up with too many losing trades AND at the same time you won't go into revenge trading because you couldn't handle such a big loss on one trade - and sometimes they may come in 2, 3 or more in a row even when trading with SL of high success rate - will you be able to handle that? How your SL fits in your daily SL? You need to find what best fits YOU :nerd:

--- 帖子 #12691 ---
Hello,sorry my bad english..... Stop Loss it's no more than a market order , but in volatile or thin markets your order could be filled very far from your SL price selected. This happen at futures markets frequently bids or asks are missed and nobody found counterparty and there are very bad stories. Too much people think that Margin Call at MT4 environment it's no problem because broker systems take care and your SL is respected. Sometimes your price filled is far away. Don't believe that broker will be eat some difference if your SL goes beyond your Margin Call until filled YOU MUST PAY IT , all losses generated are responsability of trader. Avoid high volatility and thin markets helps also Good Trading

--- 帖子 #12740 ---
Hi Theorize and Iero. I'm no expert, but the way I see it, the price had already gone more than 50 pips from the first M15 35/50 setup (the first red circle on Theorize's chart) before it formed a setup on H4 35/50, which is more than enough for a good trade by the dance rules. The second red circle on that chart is already the second reaction at M15 35/50 and there's a reason why everyone is saying it's best to take the first touches only. If it's not the first touch and if it's against any higher time frame setup (either 35/50, or 10ema touches), it's better to stay away, as quite often a lower time frame setup won't hold against a higher time frame setup, especially if it's not the first touch on the lower time frame. As for your question about M15 being in counter trend, I think, you won't find any H1 or H4 35/50 long trade where price would also be above 35/50 on M15; the same goes for H1 and H4 35/50 shorts - the price will always (or at least most of the times) be counter trend on M15, i.e. above M15 35/50. Hope it helps and sorry if that's not what you asked Good luck!

--- 帖子 #12799 ---
I can see two factors that led to the loss. First, you placed too tight a stop loss. Don't forget that G/J is more volatile than most pairs, so it needs a wider SL. I would have placed it 3-4 pips below that pin bar and waited for a meaningful move towards the direction of the trade before moving it to BE. Second, by the looks of it, there was no confluence of support and it does not follow the rules of a 10 MA touch trade. The MA was already flattening out and the angle is definitely not steep enough. Personally, I wouldn't have traded it for one more reason: there was a big move triggered by economic data. It is very difficult to identify the direction of the market once the initial impulse fades away. I choose to stay away from the market for a while, unless there's a very clear signal.

Today was a losing day for me - but it comes with a lesson, as usual: I mostly use a trade platform provided by my broker, and I like it because I can open it on any computer (either work or home) to place and monitor trades. I have a profile saved with my usual Choros layout, but somehow it was deleted on their server... so I opened a different profile that I thought was a Choros profile (looked identical) and used that layout of indicators for today's trading. I traded two M15 EMA 10 touches this morning - one on EJ and one on NU - both looked like really nice setups, but both quickly went to my SL. It turns out that what I THOUGHT was my EMA10 line was actually an EMA14 line... not the same. SO, if I had been trading the way I SHOULD have with the PROPER indicators I would have seen price blow through the EMA10 and would not have taken those trades. Lesson learned... If you are using a new profile whether in MT4, your broker's platform, ninja trader, etc... MAKE SURE IT IS SET UP THE WAY YOU THINK IT IS. I'm not too concerned, because I stuck to my max loss rule, and didn't keep trading so its not a big deal. Additionally, it always pays to analyze your trades afterward - especially losing trades. I know this stuff seems pretty obvious, but I just wanted to share. HAH as usual I only have myself to blame. Hope you all grabbed some pips today and have a great weekend!

Hi everybody, I see some people here having hard time to become succesfull and remind me myself few years ago when I found this holy strategy along with Master Kostas ! I would like to try and help you a little. First of all always remember that most times you trade against yourself than market trades against you. So becoming financialy free with forex,requires to be 100% disciplined. Even more than a shaolin monk is. So, these are the most important points to become succesfull using Choros: 1) Just look for steep MAs and confluences before open a trade. 2) Keep it simple. Forget scoop up, cross and retest, countertrades etc. Just take touches and constrainments. At least for the beginning... 3) Create a simple and realistic MM plan. Do not try to catch 30,40 or 50 pips per day! Just go for 10 pips + spread per day. How easy is it to get 10 pips??? It can be achieved with 2 M5 touch trades or even one trade. I take 10-20 pips just in one hour screen time most days. Now think about it. 50 pips per week! 200 pips per month. Do your math! Now lets say that I start with 500 usd and 0.2 lot and add 0.1 lot every succesfull week (depends on how much risk you want to take but try to avoid more than 10%). So, how long would it take to become financialy free??? Just try to take only these fucking 10-15 pips every day! No more than that. It wouldn't be hard at any TF... Please excuse me for all the above "I am clever" thing. Believe me, I have destroyed several accounts and I dont feel clever for that. All the above work fine for me and if you are able to get 10 pips per day, then should work for you too. I hope I helped some one!

Hi, Mercennary. I was watching all of your mentioned setups, but haven't taken any of them, so I will try and give you my opinion/analysis. 1. It's best to only take the first reactions on M15 10ema, they are the strongest. Also, remember the two bar rule 2. 35/50 were too flat for my taste; also, the way I see it, it was already the second test of 35/50 (I would consider the pin-bar at London open as the first one), so I stayed out of it. But this setup might have been traded, the only suggestion would be to enter right at the MAs, as I think that a dead-end on overlapping 35/50 was a good confirmation by itself. So if entered right at the next bar open, the trade could give almost 10p right away and even more, if held for longer (with such an entry - right at 35/50, one would be able to place a SL above DP and stay in a trade for much longer). 3. I saw it as a third reaction on H4 35/50, the 35&amp;50 started to diverge and 50ema was getting too flat, so I didn't feel too confident with it as well. However, the trade probably might have been taken after the H4 COB at WP and 50ema with a very small SL, but I would consider it as a riskier one. Also, I suppose, one of the main rules I've learnt through the many years of watching the market, learning to "dance" and listening to other dancers - one must be very picky with his/her trades. I was in your place too, I still find myself there sometimes - too eager to trade and willing to catch every setup I see. But many experienced traders said many times - before entering any trade, first of all ask yourself, why you shouldn't open it and what might be wrong with it, instead of why it is good and should be taken. Such approach helps me to fight my eagerness to trade every touch and bounce I see Of course being picky comes at a price too, e.g. I regret hesitating and missing a good entry today on GBPUSD M15 right after London open: first reaction, two nice pin-bars constrained by 10ema, the second one had a wick at 35/50, also with a M5 35/50 confirmation. But at the time the setup formed, I saw it as too flat and didn't have enough courage But what I know for sure - there will be a new day with new setups, that will be better and stronger. And last but not least, while you are learning this method and are gaining confidence with it, I would suggest to look for trades that require a smaller SL. If a trade has already gone too far from the MA's, it helps me to think of it this way - I could already be 5-10pips in profit if entered correctly, so with a 10-15p per trade target approach, it makes more than a half of my target, why would I want to risk more to gain less? Hope it helps, good luck and green pips

--- 帖子 #12960 ---
The main difference between a touch (or bounce) and a scoop is the direction of a trade. Touches and bounces are taken with the main trend (e.g. if it's a downtrend, like in your example, then the 10ema touch or bounce trade would be a short, so it could've been taken much earlier, when price went up to 10ema and bounced down, around 18-20 bars before your entry). The next touch (or bounce) short could have been taken at 35&amp;50, 4-5 bars before your entry. Scoops are counter-trend trades, so they are taken "into" the 35/50 or against them, usually with a TP either at one of the lines (35sma or 50ema) or higher, if you expect the trend to change. So in your example, it was a long taken at the 10ema (with a solid confirmation on M5 35/50). I think, there are more scoop examples in the threads than in the manual. Also, there's a very useful DanceTOC document in the first post of this thread, you can find some links to the scoop examples there. Good luck! Edit: please see the picture attached, the mentioned trades are marked there

--- 帖子 #12962 ---
One more thing, if you don't mind I've seen many experienced dancers emphasizing that in the very beginning of your learning process it is best to focus only on one or max two main setups (e.g. only 10ema and/or 35&amp;50 signals, or constrainments, etc.) on the main time-frame (M15) and master them first, ignoring all the other stuff. After you get a good understanding of the basics, it will be much easier for you to proceed to further details, fine-tuning your entries and exits, and more complicated setups. Also, working with a simulator helps a lot in order to train the eye (it can be set up on MetaTrader, I'm not sure about the cTrader though; you can find the files in the attachments of the thread). If you have any questions, feel free to ask.

--- 帖子 #13006 ---
Hi Sandman, I had the same or very similar problem (or still have? I believe, that there are no former 'addicts' so I prefer to be ready to fight these demons of mine any time), so I came across several ways that might help to overcome disciplinary issues. I've tried all of them over time. Some worked for me, some didn't, so it's up to you which ones to try, if you ever decide to. My answer will probably be long, I'm sorry for that in advance, but I hope that it will at least be somewhat helpful for you or other traders having similar issues. 1. Journaling: - a journal with all the trading details (not only regular info as pair/time/session/direction/result/type of signal, entry/exit/SL/TP levels, etc. but also - how far did the price go against and/or with the trade; what were the circumstances of an entry - 1st touch or not, agreement with higher TFs, confirmation on lower TFs, the slope of MAs, etc.; any additional comments; screenshots). - and a diary about my mental/psychological state, where I assess and record my psychological state before and during any trading day, and evaluate emotions I usually experience (greed, fear, revenge, excitement, inclination to overtrade, etc.), in order to pay special attention to the excessive ones while trading. I do have a myfxbook account as an additional journaling tool as well, but it's not the same and not as helpful for me, as being forced to write down every little detail about my trading on my own. Trust me, the additional work, time and effort I have to put into it makes me think twice before entering or even looking at a 'not-that-worth' trade. So it helped a lot in reducing the number of trades to a minimum and being extremely picky. 2. Also, some time ago I asked one of the dancers how he had coped with some of his 'demons', and this is what he recommended (hope, he doesn't mind me sharing it): " Use two separate accounts. One for the trades that are perfect / near perfect setups with the strategy you have chosen. Another one for impulse trades or trades where you think you know where the market is going to go based on gut feeling or whatever. Do this for some time and watch how the account balances evolve. " 3. Use the trade checklist (either from the original M15 manual, or this one: https://www.forexfactory.com/showthr...54#post6606954 , or create your own set of rules with a checklist), and make sure to follow it. Every time you feel the urge to enter the trade not by the rules (i.e. against your checklist), move to the other account (demo or small real). Later you will have a chance to compare the good one and the bad one and see that being disciplined pays off. 4. Backtest the strategy on your own, not only visually by watching the charts, but writing it down as well, as if you had taken these trades. I know, it's been already done so many times by other dancers and we already know all the rules and details, so why put in unnecessary efforts when everything is already here... But it did help me big time, when I was struggling with discipline to stick to the rules. For example, I knew before, that the 2-bar rule is so very important, but it wasn't easy for me to follow this rule strictly, until I had my own statistical proof that it works. Also, any taken trades will differ from trader to trader (the system is half-discretionary, so at the end of the day it's up to every one of us whether to take a trade or not), so this is very important, as you would be analyzing your own experience, personal limits and potential. Such backtest can be done in two ways. Firstly, by analyzing the two previously mentioned accounts (the 'good' and the 'bad' ones) - after some time of journaling there will be enough real-trading data to perform a solid statistical analysis. The second one, which helped me more, is to work with a simulator, but not by simply looking at it or taking the trades in the Metatrader (the results were erratic and I didn't have any statistic information left to analyze after the simulator was closed), so I decided to watch historical price movements day after day in my free time and put it all down - pause it before every potential entry, write down every entry/exit and other details, un-pause, watch slowly how it evolved, write that down as well (e.g. how far the price went against me, i.e. what SL would have let me stay in a profitable trade; potential maximum profit; potential profit if trailed by the rules; etc.). The difference between the two methods is that when you do that in real time, on either real or demo account, you are more affected by emotions; and when you do that in simulator, the emotions fade away, as it's not about your performance anymore, but about information gathering only. 5. Find a mentor (could also be a close friend or a spouse), who could be supportive and help you in overcoming your 'addiction'. Tell them about the system and its rules, about your problems and struggles, also about your goals and objectives. And report to them regularly. No lying, concealing or sugarcoating - admitting a problem is half the solution. The same effect might be achieved by setting up a public journal. It's up to an individual - what would make them feel more miserable and hold them from repeating these mistakes; and what would make them feel good, proud and happy when they are disciplined and stick to the plan. 6. Think of a physical punishment for every mistake you make. One of the FF members suggested to make 10 burpees every time he breaks the rules. Double benefit of this point is that it could help to improve both mental and physical state of a trader There also was one dancer who suggested a more extreme self-punishment - every time he broke a rule, he had to drink a shot of undiluted vinegar, said it helped him overcome many disciplinary issues. I do not recommend such extreme measures for your own health safety though 7. Before entering any trade, take a screenshot and write a comment on it, what are the PROS and CONS of the setup. Why you would or would not like to take it, and how you will react, if/when price gets to the level. If you say to yourself you won't trade it, don't trade it or trade it on a 'bad' account that was mentioned before. When the setup forms, take one more screenshot with a comment update. And the third one - after the fact. It helped me to see a picture before, during and after the signal setup, so even if a setup that I didn't take works out fine eventually, I can still see why I did not take it by looking at the first picture with all the comments, because usually they all look fine after the fact. Also, this additional work and efforts will keep you from looking at the trades that are not worth your time and attention. And it is a good tool to keep oneself from impulsive entries, as the entry and circumstances are already predefined in advance. Well, after such a long answer, it seems I have lots of disciplinary issues Some disciplined, mentally and psychologically stable and strong traders might probably think it's too much. Maybe they would say that it can be done easier and simpler. But I tried the 'simple and easy' approach and it didn't work out for me, so I wish someone would have told me these things 5 years ago, I would really be happy to use a shortcut We are all different and maybe it won't help you personally, but if this information helps anyone to get a little closer to their goal, it will serve its purpose. Good luck to everyone and sorry once again for the long message

Hi Mercennary . Not easy to say .. IMO , the timing is most important .. and often forgotten in the " chart analyses " . Very often , the price doesn t respect the MA´s around EU and US session opening for 30-60 minutes .. Look on your chart .. the 10 Ema with a " two bar rule " ( here it´s 3 bars .. but even not 5..10 or 20 bars) was playing out nicely . --- 帖子 #13066 ---
Thanks Kostas for the reply! I am really excited! LOL. And I decided to focus my attention to the 5 min setups. I am testing two new variations of the 10 or 12 EMA. Why? As many already mentioned, sometimes the price drags the EMA and make it touch the candle. So, there is no mechanical way to enter those trades. The only way would be to use a discretionary approach, thinking "oh, I feel the price will touch the EMA". And a few pips before the price touches, we would enter. I am trying to overcome this problem by testing the EMA with the option of "apply to open" instead of "apply to close". And isntead of using 10 EMA (applied to close) I am testing the 8 EMA (applied to open), so the EMA does not move when the current candle is still open. Attached Image (click to enlarge)

--- 帖子 #13080 ---
Hi guys, I've started this system again (long time reader, not big on posting!). Where I am finally having success with it is keeping my R:R at 1:1 for the first trade then aim 2:1 for the second. In the past I was closing positions too quickly getting two or three right, then having one position go against taking out all profits which became frustrating. The other thing is, taking a max of two trades per day and being prepared for a losing streak of up to 5 trades in a row (even if it is unlikely) and 10 in a disaster scenario (all based on 3% per trade). By being prepared for this and with a good R:R I seem to be doing better. With this set up (a potential of 10 trades per week) , I still only make my weekly target the equivalent of one correct trade at 2:1. Also limiting the pairs traded to just one or two is giving better results for me (GU and UJ seem to be my preference). In the current market conditions I'm preferring quick trades because here in Australia if I have winning position I'm likely to see it knocked out overnight because Trump decides tweet something or other - so better to get in and out quickly. Cheers.

--- 帖子 #13083 ---
Im not so sure about the value of backtesting, this is not a purely mechanical system but has a strong discretionary element hence success does require skill by the trader. For example, you may get a signal on smaller timeframe, but a higher timeframe may indicate an opposite direction, news might be coming up so you skip the trade, major news might have happened so the pair needs time to sort it self out, during a trade you might get a price action bar that indicates a reason to get out at BE or a small loss. Better to forward test on demo or a live account risking a small amount.

Hello, I've recently decided to adopt this system after trading Trading Made Simple for the past couple months. The problem with TMS is that while it's simple, it is an incomplete system. After extensively testing it, I've found that over the long run, it's about a 50% win with a 3:1 or 4:1 risk reward ratio. While on paper it sounds good, if any of you have studied the martingale system, then you'll understand why a 50% probability is not only nerve wracking psychology, but also potentially account exploding as well. The risk of ruin is just too high. I found this system by accident when I was experimenting with the smoothed Heiken Ashi and I noticed that price would sometimes bounce off of the HA. After reading The Dance thread and the manual this strategy appealed to me because while the risk reward is ~1:1 or 2:1, the trade probabilities look very good. Since I just finished reading the manual, I do have a couple of questions. How many trade setups are there? Per the PDFs, there appear to be 6 trade setups: Constrainment of the 50-EMA, 35-SMA (Master trade) and 10-EMA as well as the touch trade of the 50-EMA, 35-SMA, and the 10-EMA. The 10-EMA setups should never be traded counter-trend, but the 50-EMA and the 35-SMA can be for experienced traders. What does the Wick Through indicate? The manual was a little confusing and I want to know if this is considered a change of trend and you trade on the side of the wick through or do you count it as a touch trade and trade as though this is a Wick Off? My last question is, for touch trades, these days, do you guys mostly trade Close of Bar, or as soon as a moving average is touched? Thanks for your help and I look forward to trading with you guys.

EURUSD = +15.4 pips The markets have been lacking a clear direction today and I wasn't sure when or where to enter. I want to scalp, so I can trade anytime during the day but I haven't developed the skills for it yet. Following the rules, I waited for the 35/50 MAs to tell me which direction to trade. I proceeded to enter a semi-touch trade off the 50-EMA. While this isn't a strictly a Dance trade, I entered the trade because I saw a confluence of resistance that would help push price down. Within that area was the 1 hour 50-EMA, the 15 minute 35/50 MAs, the 1.15200 round number and a pivot point. The higher time frame charts also indicated a downward trend, so I decided to take the risk. The price I paid was a 7 pip drawdown. My stop loss was at 11.5 pips or just above the 1 hour 35-SMA. My exit was at the next pivot, which I find is a good place to take profits. * In regards to my chart setup, I've changed the round numbers and pivot lines to a gray color because I was getting distracted by them. They serve as confluence and not trade signals. I've also removed my 5 pip keltner channel because while it is useful for knowing when the markets are ranging or in consolidation, it was producing false signals. In my mind type 2 errors (failure to detect signals) are better than type 1 errors (false signals) because I need to trust that the trading strategy will do right by me. --- 帖子 #13259 ---
Choros is basically a scalping system. When you see a perfect Choros setup and you enter targeting for 10 pips, you will be profitable almost all of the time. When I trade the M15 10EMA touch I usually target for 10 pips, when trading the H1 10EMA I target for around 15 pips, when trading the H4 10EMA or the D1 10EMA I target for 20 to 30 pips. So in that trade I was targeting for around 15 pips, and as you can see, form the entry point to the pivot line there is around 15 pips, so I was ready to manually close the trade to get my 15 pips, but suddenly the next bar opened with that huge gap and I was +30p in profit, so in this case I let the trade run and set my target at the next RN. That is not usually the case. I admit that a couple of times I got 100 pips from Choros setups, but I realized that trying to repeat that I ended up with many loses or Break Evens. So I always remember my self that Choros is a very effective Scalping System, so when you see a "bounce off the pivot line with a rejection wick" or a bounce form any real Supply/Demand or Support/Resistance, you can be almost sure that if you see perfect Choros setups during that big bounce, you will get 10 pips at the first touch of the M15 10EMA, you will get another 10 to 15 pips at the touch of the H1 10EMA, and so on. I think that making many +10p trades is easier and more profitable than looking for a +100p huge trade.

--- 帖子 #13309 ---
My advice (doesn't mean is the only way): When trading in small TFs M15, M5 and specially when you are a beginner, it makes sense to quickly take profits so that you build confidence and equity. Early on, I would take profits for 7-10p and with two trades per day I would call it a day (20p was 3% for my lots). When trading in higher TFs it may be easier to trail stop but still the market is so unexpected and erratic that I am not sure how well it works. All of the above is very subjective to the trader's personality, risk aversion, etc., but also VERY critical to his success.

My advice (doesn't mean is the only way ): Never, ever paid attention to risk/reward and honestly I don't get why we impose RR to our trades. It will go where it will go, why does it have to follow the imposed RR? How about turning a positive trade to a losing trade because it never achieved the required RR by 2 pips???? Many of my trades (specially in noisy dates and noisy pairs like GJ) had way bigger SL than TP. As soon as you get your profit you close WITH profit. If it looks it may go the other way, close it there is always another trade....

--- 帖子 #13313 ---
i dont use trailing stops. very rare a BE-stop, when i dont want to risk a good day, but i dont like even them here my view to this RR diskussion from another thread: i prefer a higher winrate, like 80%-90% making +8,10,12 or seldom +15 pips. i dont really care about RR. when i have 20-30 pips/day (from 2-3 trades) then i change to very conservative trading mode for the rest of the day or turn off my computer. to get 20-30 pips from a single trade is nice, but there are days when the market only gives you 10 pips. in other words: psychology is for me more important than mathematics. its just my way of thinking i feel comfortable.

1. Focus on trading vehicles, strategies, and time horizons that suit your personality. 2. Identify non-random price behavior, while recognizing that markets are random most of the time. 3. Absolutely convince yourself that what you’ve found is statistically valid. 4. Use this to set up trading (entry and exit) rules. 5. Follow these rules.

--- 帖子 #13466 ---
1. "clear break is when a candle crosses clearly any of the 3 MAs to confirm an entry at the close of the candle" - No, it is a clear break of all 3 MA´s and closes opposite direction (a short in a long or vice versa) "it means that the clear break down would be considered another extra confirmation for a possible short taken in 1, right?" - No, it just shows the indicated direction (a long trade) isn t valid anymore, the price didn t respect the MA´s. This happens often as 2rd, 3rd 4th 5th touch trades -- first are safest.. 2. " when the other variables are "nice" for the touch" - I can t say violate the 2 bar rule .. BUT -- Dancing is totally discretionary, nothing is 100%, if other conditions met and the price doesn t count bars .. Up to you-- as long as you produce more profits than losses= keep it -- that simple. 3.Sry, no idea if a "one bar" retrace to 10 ema is better or not-- I pull the trigger when I see something happens and Choros is excellent to see what the market does right now or the next couple of minutes.. "I also noticed the suggested TP level by the way, wish I used it!" I can strongly recomment to have a plan before entering.. where is the tp?-- half position out after xxx pips-?- or a when to set to BE ?-- or no BE-- ? SL? -whatever-- have a plan and you get rewarded. Stay tuned Guido

I got +12p with this one, but as you can see these H4 AAA Setups can give a lot more. Is giving more that 70 pips already. Nevertheless, I've seen these H4 AAA Setups working so well so many times, that I'm considering let these trades run longer. For example if I would have let this trade run for 3 hours, I could have gotten 70 pips. The thing is not to freak out when price is returning to your entry point, as you can see in the H1 chart, that happened on the next H1 bar after my entry. Attached Image (click to enlarge)

--- 帖子 #13536 ---
Yes, no splitting. It may be just me, but splitting plays games with my mind. Whenever I tried it, I found that I would have made more money by using one order. Just a piece of advice: in the beginning to build your confidence (and your account!) it may make sense to take quick profits. I still do it sometimes when the market is erratic, I grab quick 10-15 pips and close the trade. By experience, you will start feeling when a trade is worth giving time to develop to 30-40 pips. Usually, around 18-25 pips I close it.

--- 帖子 #13576 ---
Note that the immediate Higher Time-frame of your trade (H1 in this case) is in a Downtrend. That will not help the setup. We use the direction of the 35/50 to have a feel of the trend. Nevertheless, as you already noticed, one reason to avoid this one is the H1 pin bar. Just before pulling the trigger I take a last look at Higher Time-frames, if I see a pin bar that is about to close in any of the Higher Time-frames, I usually avoid the trade. An exception would be if the pin bar is forming but that Higher Time-frame has a strong trend in the direction of the trade. Like the one that Kostas did some days ago.

--- 帖子 #13577 ---
