--- 帖子 #13578 ---
This was a M15 10EMA trade. Until recently, I was taking these kind of setups exactly a the touch of the projection of the 10EMA, most of the trades were profitable but most of the times, as in this case, price retraced 10 to 15 pips before going my way. Getting use to those 10 to 15 pips retrace is dangerous because sometimes price never comes back and I had to accept big loses of 20 to 30 pips. So, as mentioned many times in this thread now I’m waiting for confirmation bars before pulling the trigger. In this example I could have entered at the close of the first M15 pin bar, nevertheless, the M5 bars were closing above de M5 12EMA and 23EMA, so I waited a bit more. The next M15 pin bar closed a bit lower, that particular M5 bar closed below the M5 12EMA and 23EMA, so I waited a bit more for price to retrace a little (as it usually do after a pin bar) and pulled the trigger. After entering the trade price retraced only less than 3 pips and not the 10 to 15 pips that I was getting use to. Something important is that the trend for M15, H1 and H4 is pointing down, the same direction of my trade. I set my TP for 20 pips, but I chickened out when price was hesitating and manually closed the trade at +15p. Attached Image (click to enlarge)

--- 帖子 #14083 ---
My friend...it is not constrainment. Constrainment normaly requires 3 or more SMALL bars respecting an MA or S/R line. In addition, the price action in H1 shows you that it is going to test H1 10EMA so in my opinion you should wait for price to hit H1 10EMA. One more thing is that price tested so many times the round number + Monthly pivot and rejected. Monthly pivot is very strong S/R level in my opinion because many long term traders use it. I decided not to use Pivot Points because I want my charts as clear and simple as possible but they are very powerfull espeacially Daily PP, Weekly PP and Monthly PP. I hope I helped you a bit...

--- 帖子 #14211 ---
For the entry of a touch trade, it has no problem, just a little bit lower (you could have better price). Several things against your trade: 1. it was a double bottom reversal 2. the entry bar was a big/strong bar, better waiting market to show her hand 3. after your entry, price staying between your open price and SL and above all MAs for 6-7 bars , it told you your entry is not good, it is time to exit with minimum loss, normally touch trades will rebound from MA within 1-2 bars. Suppose you entered a better price, it would be a even trade.

Hey everyone! One of the things I started thinking about is how great it would have been to have a place for all of us to chat in real time. I have seen that there has been multiple attempts earlier to create a similar site, yet none of these seems to be in use. That is why I thought it would be nice to start up a chat again. First of all, a chat like this would not be an attempt to replace this thread or Clay’s. It would merely serve as an additional tool to help improve our trading performances. As valuable as these two threads are, the one thing they do not provide is a real time opportunity for us to analyze the markets together. What I envision a chat like this to become is a place for all of us to: Share our thoughts about potential setups Casually chat about other aspects of the strategy This will be beneficial for multiple reasons. First, we will be able to watch real time potential setups. We can see each others thought process and hopefully make more informed decisions on whether to enter a trade or not. It will also serve as an alert mechanism, allowing us to trade setups we otherwise would not have spotted. Second, as the chat would be casual (yet still on topic), there will be room for all sorts of questions and comments that are related to the strategy. This way, we will not pollute this thread with comments that for some reason are less relevant here. As I wrote, this is not an attempt to replace this thread. If you truly want to learn this strategy this is the place to be. My hope however, is that a chat could become an additional tool for everyone trading the Dance.

Dear Kostas, The EA I was developing has turned into an Indicator that I use in my trading. The indicator shows Key levels I usually use, Round Numbers, all Daily Pivots, Weekly and Monthly central Pivots and Key levels I base on Strong Daily Swing Higher Highs or Lower Lows, all things I learned in your thread. The highlight of this indicator is that it shows some possible Choros Setups. The thing is, as with all indicators and EAs, you can't trust in it's signals blindly. We have to use our brain. If I would trade blindly all signals this Indicator gives me, I would be loosing all my money. I don't trade with Choros setups only. I consider Support/Resistance levels that I draw manually on my charts (like horizontal lines and trend lines), I watch Supply and Demand Areas in several time frames. I watch Price Action (Not only the last bar but shapes formed by dozens of bars, like triangles, channels, etc.). When many of those things tell me to trade, I usually use Choros Setups to fine-tune my entry and that Is what I post here. As an example of the indicator, take a look at the attached image form today with a couple of profitable trades. Happy trading.

Thanks Guido, this is exactly what I meant by knowing when not to take the trades. Could you (and of course others!) sum up when do you avoid trading although at first it may seem the basic setup of the strategy is in place? Example based upon previous post: - relevant session for a pair coming to an end - long wicks on both sides (with an extreme form known as the porcupine) Other known: - MA Soup / chaotic / ranging - any of the main pivots / big round numbers just above/below the direction of potential trade - hyper volatility - because of big news day or for any other reason making the market unpredictable - hitting daily loss limit / profit target What about : - HTF MAs just above/below the direction of potential trade, especially 35/50? Probably depending if flat or angled? - nice looking setup forming on M15 but the price got stuck between 1hr or 4hr 35/50? - price failed to make a Lower Low or Higher High just prior to a touch trade setup? - double/tripple top/bottom against the direction of formed setup? - S/R level that held up previously should be seen as an obstacle? - any other? I'm not sure if you agree but basic Dance/Choros setups are not quantum physics, after some reading and practice they are quite straight forward. But it's the experience and knowledge when NOT to trade although it seems like a setup is forming could be something that will separate profitable from not. This is something that is not in the manuals. If more experienced traders could sum up their observations in one post, then I think it could be a great booster for others' learning curve. Best, J.

--- 帖子 #14722 ---
This is to share the work that I have put into this setup incl. the collection of very useful tools (both scripts and indicators) to comfortably trade the Choros strategy. None of those tools were created by me, so the credit goes where it is due. The scripts are mostly (all?) the original Dance trade management scripts and the indicators were collected mostly on Forex Factory but also from various web sites and forums. Most of them are editable .mq4 format so you can adjust the code to your needs if necessary. The core idea behind this setup was to comfortably follow and trade multiple currencies on multiple timeframes on one screen, have all the necessary tools while maintaining a minimalistic feeling and not to overload charts with stuff that is not needed. The setup follows M15 as the main chart and supportive M5, H1, H4 and Daily. I am often hiding M5 and Daily underneath by resizing the M15 a bit to the right to make this main timeframe larger. F11 full screen is highly recommended. You only need to have the navigator open but resized as small as possible to just show those few scripts (using favourites allows to keep it even narrower). Alternatively they can be defined into hotkey shortcuts but I'd rather see them not to screw something up by mistake. Have a look at the picture to see how it looks on my screen. Brief description of most elements, some are obvious: INDICATORS 1) MAs: Each chart has Choros typical 10/35/50 MAs + grayed out higher timeframes' 35/50 MAs. The general rule is that the given timeframe except of 10, has 35/50 of its own and of two subsequent higher TFs. For example: M15 will have 10/35/50 and also 35/50 from H1 and H4 (represented as x4 and x16 multiplication of 35/50 in this case). The exception is M5 where 35/50 is shown for M5, H1 and H4, M15 is skipped). 2) Charts symbol changer and synchronizer (non editable .ex4 but highly customizable) This is such a smart little thing. Instead of having X charts on Y timeframes which makes it difficult to handle and switch between, it allows to open one currency on the required amount of timeframes and then, after customizing, freely switch between currencies on all those timeframes. It doesn't ever hide the bars which are always on top without disrupting the function. 3) Daily Range &amp; 4) mm Spread You are on your own here 5) JTrades Nice little tool to clearly visualize taken trades. The standard MT4 feature isn't so clear and is not customizable. 6) Market Hours Allow to define and visualize the market opening hours like London, NY, etc. Shows as a mini indicator subwindow on M15 chart in my setup that displays horizontal lines showing which markets are open. Opening times to be adjusted according to different time zones. 7) P4L CandleTime Shows the time remaining to current bar closing 8) Pivots Day What I instantly liked about this particular pivots is that it doesn't have those nearly vertical, angular lines that connect the periods and clutter the charts. Simultaneously it shows the previous periods correctly, which apparently is not so obvious in some other cases. It was also easy to modify the source code NOT to show the resistance and support levels but rather only Daily, Weekly and Monthly pivots which is recommended way to go. It also works well with the simulator (again, not obvious) yet as with all pivot indicators it slows the simulator down a bit too. 9) Plot 00 and 50 levels.ex4 Simple 00 and 50 round number indicator. 10) SweetSpots GOLD Same as above yet you can customize it for example for DAX and other non-FX price type instruments which will not work correctly with the one above 11) zScaleXX This is so great. No more manual adjustment of charts scale which is so annoying. (Both from the perspective of initially changing the type of scale and then scaling). Simply edit the number of pips you want to have in your particular timeframe (divided by two as it centers the current price line and it is the amount to bottom/top) and apply it just like an indicator. Therefore, it is also possible to save as a part of the template (which God knows why is unable to save this parameter as a standard functionality of MT4). This is even more useful as you realize you should always have the same height of your chart for any given timeframe not to skew the feeling of the market. Edit each of those .mq4 to adjust to your own taste. SCRIPTS (recommended already by the original Dance manual) 12) Kill All Closes all trades on all currencies 13) Kill Currency Closes only on the currency of the chart that is being dropped on. 14) Buy &amp; Sell Edit the file to adjust your position size, SL and TP. 15) SL &amp; TP Moves your SL and TP exactly where you drop it on chart of currently traded currency. Watch out - for multiple trades it will move (or create) an SL and TP in the selected spot for all of them. 16) Set BE+1 Drop it anywhere in the chart with an open trade and it will move your SL to Break Even + 1 pip Best, J.

From M15 window point of view, your entry has no problem, 1st 2-bars retrace after PA crossed EMA10, except: 1. there is a support (last day low) 10 pips below your entry, trend may reverse before that. 2. your entry was a bit late. 1st possible entry is EMA10 touch (COB last green bar); 2nd possible entry is EMA10 bounce (COB 2 bars before your entry bar) if you need more confirmation; 3rd possible entry is broke of last swing low which is one bar before your entry. After your entry, two facts spotted: 1. three red bars and one cross bar after the retrace, both body and height were becoming smaller and smaller, indicating a dry out of selling. 2. the strong green bar (13 pips) made PA above all MAs(10/35/50) which is also the biggest bar of the day, indicating a trend reversal, no reason to hold any longer. About your exit: 1. AU is a low volatile pair, definitely no need 20 pips SL. 2. 1st possible SL is last swing high which is 6 pips above your entry; 2nd possible SL is EMA10 plus 5 to 10 pips based on pair volatility; 3rd SL is after the COB strong reversal bar. You held losing position way too long! This is my after-facts analysis, I cannot do better than you in my live trading. Hope this help! Sorry for the long post.

Dear Eagle 1) Always look for confluence! This means that if you have a nice M15 2-3 bar 10 ema touch coming soon (I would like it to be the 1st touch), look at M5 chart if it confluences with M5 35/50 touch or maybe with a higher TF touch and/or any doji candle and/or any SR level like RN, Pivots etc. This is the perfect signal for me...If you see a nice and steep 10 ema touch coming in M15 but H1 35/50 are flat, stay out...M15 and H1 should follow the trend which means they should both heading either south or north (depending the trend). 2) I personally stuck in one pair when I was at the beggining. --- 帖子 #14817 ---
Adding to positions: I was thinking about this today and the idea is to get a good position from which the price will not go against you. In other words, rule #1 - don't lose money and rule #2 - don't forget rule #1. If you have a break in an 'area of interest' such as a round number and the price goes against you but stops on, say the 10 ema and then starts to reverse....in such a scenario, it might be good to add to that position - thus giving you an average of the two entry points. You would have to trade initially for less than you normally trade, i.e. a mini lot or whatever you are comfortable with. Then your overall average position would be better. For example, if you see the price going against you to the 35-sma and you know the trend and you've looked at your other time frames, you could theoretically improve your position by adding to the position. Now this has its limitations and I don't want to get into martingales and b.s. like that but it seems at first blush, a legit technique here mainly because we know or we have some idea of what a good position looks like....say a first touch of the 35 sma and a cross by the 10 ema while crossing a round number level. The support/resistance is very good (depending on where the trend is heading). Comments welcome.

--- 帖子 #14820 ---
Keep it simple. Unless you went long on a commodity being priced as close to 0 as possible or you want to average down your purchase price on an uptrending blue chip during correction phase - do not add to a losing position, especially while levereged on FX... You will blow your account this way. Try to keep minimum SLs and just take a loss when it happens. I work with corporate finance and have never seen a market company with an income but without a cost. Have you? Nope. Not possible in regular circumstances. FX is like business, you have customers, suppliers, financing (leverage), market analysis, incomes (winning trades) and... costs... Try to keep them down but accept them. No costs, no profits. If you want to add to a position (winning) have a read on Turtle Trading by Richard Dennis. Interesting concept of following long term trends and adding to the positions while they develop.

--- 帖子 #14852 ---
This system might work better for trading stock options, particularly SPY options which have a good liquidity. The problem I have found with Forex is that it is highly leveraged and stop loss hunting is a big factor. So we see titanic swings and then periods where nothing is happening. Its kinda schizophrenic, to be honest. I'm not dogging forex, its just the nature of these markets. I'm sure you've seen this. For example, right before the London Open or sometimes at the open, you get these huge spikes in either direction and sometimes fakeouts. To me, these represent opportunity to trade them but...they are not really consistent. Applying a 35-sma pullback may not work.They may run up so fast that the 5/10 ema's will lag and then pull back until its well beyond your stop loss. With the stock market, especially with SPY, I think you get a more consistent market which can also be volatile but can also trend much easier. And since this is a 'trend following system', it will probably work better. These are just my observations. I am not saying that you can't make money in forex. I'm just giving my opinion. I've been trying out the Dance/Choros system for the last month and it has not provided me with consistency. There are alot of false breaks. And so there are small losses. I'm sure that you have seen these too. Its not the price action signals. Its more likely that the markets are being manipulated and stop hunting is in. Once again, just my opinion. Please don't flame me if you disagree.

[quote=NameIsMethos;12730824]H1. Clay says the "Touch Trade" is valid for the 35 SMA and 50 EMA. How do I know whether to enter on the 35 SMA or the 50 EMA? In this case for example if we would have entered at the 50 EMA, the trade probably would have been taken out for a SL. Only the Entry at First Touch of the 35 SMA would have yielded the results Clay wrote about. Do we enter both Setups and if the first one (in this case 50EMA) fails just enter the second First Touch setup (in this case 35 SMA)? 2. I am a little confused because in the rules Clay specifies that the Touch Trade only applies if the "Touch" happens at the second bar latest. However in the image shown, the Touch of the 35 SMA is the fourth Candle, therefore nor really comply with the rules of the Touch Trade. Am I missing something? Hi Methos, I will try to explain the thinking that you should have for these kind of trades. You see the prie approaching the 35/50 like the example you posted. You think that the price will either bounce from 50 ema nor from 35. If you see that it takes only 1 or 2 bars with high momentum to touch the ema, then you expect quick reversal so I would take the 50ema touch. If you see that it takes more candles for the price to go there, you expect that price will maybe test both emas as well as the RN and then will reverse. So you wait for confirmation from lower TFs and this is what happened. Look at the M5...you see a nice doji-like bar and you have also double bottom in M15 so this is a nice signal that price will reverse. I hope I helped a bit...

--- 帖子 #15047 ---
Hi Methos. Basicly I m not sure if you understand the constrainments at the moment, what is absolutely okay. It is an advanced technique and I ll explain it a bit more simple, because you posted a pic with a chart and wrote constrainment where is none. A constrainment is mostly a when the wicks break the MA, but the body stays below or above the MA. Often you can follow a curve for that case. They can be really harsh and move quick up-or downwards. Often they try to catch stops before the play out. So. What Clay meant is IMO Not the doji in a constrainment is the entry bar, wait for confirmation. Hope that helped Guido

Hey everyone, since this thread is also about giving, I want to share something I noticed while trading in the simulator. I am now taking advantage of this pretty often and it's good for quit some pips. I noticed that the H1 MA's are pretty strong especially in 2 situations: When P/A is moving through MA's often and it seems hard to find Dance trades. If the H1 MA's show a trend in these situations, they often seem to be the "go To" since price can't really decide which way to go on M15. However the H1 MA's are reliable to act as kind of a bottom for P/A. (left circle) When a bigger revearsel is about to appear (right circle on the chart). In this case P/A wasn't able to get near the top a little bit to the left. Then there was a big move down intraday (with nice EMA10 constrainment). However it wasn't able to break the last low marked to the left with the 3 arrows. In a situation like this, I noticed that P/A often retests the H1 MA's. In this specific case there was also confluence with M15 MA's which made the trade especially powerful. I also marked some other areas, where the H1 MA's act as good Entry points for trades in the direction of the H1 trend. Now that said, you also have to be careful some times because sometimes entering a trade like this is counter trend against the M15 trend. This is especially true in the middle of the chart with the 3 arrows. However as noted in the box in the chart, the higher highs of the second and third touch signal a continuation of the upwards trend and therefore could have been used as an entry although strongly counter trend. Maybe this is no news to you. At least for me it elevated my trading with the Dance to a new level because it enables me to catch some bigger moves :-)

Hello Dancers, since 2012 I am amazed by this visual opportunity recognition tool, called the Dance. Whatever else I may try, something always gets me back to this thread. I want to thank the current active contributors Kostas, Guido, Haydel, iero4 and birdland and the rest - I am learning a lot from you guys. I find the dance a relativly simple, concise and xtremely reliable, if taken seriously, method. Currently I am focusing on the M15 35/50 Cross &amp; Retest Setup, aiming at 21 consecutive live trades by this setup, before moving to some more exotic ones. I've devised a simple check-box list to qualify and measure the reliability of this setup and since it is helping me a lot, here it is: Attached Image How I use it: if all 6 boxes are checked, it is an AAA setup; any 5 boxes checked gives an AA; 4 boxes - A; any 3 boxes - B; any 2 boxes - BB; 1 box only is a C setup. The order is not important, just the number. So far AAA &amp; AA behave extremely well, and anything below A is a waste of effort to me.

[quote=vinicio;12828452] Sure, Attached Image This was Friday on GU M15 that I actually traded: First Touch - checked . It was the first come back to the 35/50 after the morning thrust up crossing the 35/50 from below. 35/50 slope - steep angle - checked. At the moment of the First Touch, 35/50 are clearly sloped up and steepness seems good enough. Strong Thrust crossing the 35/50 - checked. 35/50 closely together - UNCHEKED. At the moment of the First Touch, 35/50 are apart. HTF in agreement - checked. The dotted lines are 10/35/50 on H1 and they are supportive to the upward direction Market/Session opened - checked . The setup was during the London session. One opened market is enough. With 5 boxes checked, you can qualify this setup as AA. If you decide to trade the Second Touch in this example, uncheck the First Touch box and you get an A setup. If you are not an experienced trader, keep in mind the following: this is not a sure thing tool. In your practice you WILL see A-AAA setups failing miserably and B-C setups work out nicely, but I believe the odds for a good potential profit (depending on your execution skills) will always be better with the higher ranking setups.

NameisMethos. I am relatively new compared to the other traders. I trade for about four hours daily, not continuously though. When I trade I watch the screen without interruption. Everyday provides various set ups across all currency pairs. With practice one becomes better, at first try not to loose too much money and then try to get to a point of ending the trading day breaking even. If you get to this point then you have reached a point of self reflection and you are on the path of becoming a successful and consistent trader. Eventually you look at the chart and the set ups stare you in the face.

Hi everyone, I keep working in the sim as well as with very little live money to learn the dance. I'm good at making pips in very trending markets. However I tend to give it back during more consolidation markets. I have attached an example of a market where I tend to loose my pips with the dance. Now my problem is not necessarily that I can't find entrys. My problem most of the times in these markets are the following: 1. Not finding a good Take Profit, hence either exiting BE or with a small loss 2. Taking entries which are fakeouts and in consequenze SL is hit very often. I think this happens to me because I can't identify which of the MA's are relevant in these markets. If if take a trade of the M15 35/50 MA because there is a valid setup, often price tests the H1 MA's and stops me out in the process. 3. I'm not able to see breakouts happening like on april 9th. --- 帖子 #15283 ---
you won't get rid of the series of losses, that's part of trading. again and again there are series of sideways markets. these lead to drawdons. the trading systems here at ff have all these "weaknesses". during this time most traders give up and switch to new systems or stop completely. in the end it's a psychological game like poker and only very, very few manage to survive these setbacks. this is only possible if you are a balanced personality. that's the key to success. you have to learn to think like an entrepreneur and not like an employee who gets a fixed income every day, week or month. in the shortterm, for every single trade, you need luck. in the long term, you need consistence. nothing new.

--- 帖子 #15284 ---
another very important thing i forgot is to reduce the position size when you are in a drawdown period. the main thing in this period is to survive and to stay psychological healthy. when things are running better then you can slowly increase the position size.

Hey guys, I've another question. I've attached an example to illustrate my point, it's EUR/JPY from today. At the indicated arrow I saw price hitting the SMA35 in confluence with a RN. I considered going short but since SMA35 and EMA50 started to separate and it's more than a 2 bar retrace I waited for additional confirmation. That confirmation was given at COB of the next bar (outsidebar). I don't know about you, but I feel uncomfortable entering at COB of an outside bar, because price already moved away a good portion from the S/R and therefore make Stoploss placement difficult. In this scenario a SL of about 15 pips would have been required, if the SL should be above the original SMA35 Touch. This is okayish in this case (I personally prefer a little smaller SL / better Entrys) but many times with an outside bar price already moved further away and even bigger SL would be necessary. I saw all of this happening and decided against entry at COB of the confirmation candle and instead waited for a little retrace upwards to give me a little better entry with a 10 Pip SL. Seeing how price progressed afterwards now leaves me frustrated, because my analysis was correct just the pullback for a better entry didn't happen. Did you find that in a scenario like this, the higher MA Bounce scenario is so strong, that you would have taken the trade even if the confirmation is an Outside bar with a COB further away from the initial Touch and maybe even set the stoploss closer and not above the high of the Touch Candle? --- 帖子 #15407 ---
I risk 1.5% of my account in 30 pips. When I do not use limit orders, I send market orders using a script that sets the SL to 30 pips risking 1.5% of the account. After the orders are open I usually finetune the position of the SL, sometimes I move it further, sometimes I move it closer. So, my risk it is usually around 1.5% in every trade. When I do not set a SL Order, I usually manually close the trade when the trade is around 30pips against me, that usually means that it is a bad trade. When I really like the Setup and I am sure it is an AAA setup, I use the script to open two trades at the same place, each trade risking 1.5% in 30 pips, so the real risk is 3% in 30 pips. Since it is a AAA Setup, I get the first 10 to 15 pips almost always, move the second trade to BE+1 and leave it running to a obvious target.

--- 帖子 #15410 ---
As mentioned in your PM, these are the scripts iero, similar concepts of Clay scripts but with updated code. These don't work with the simulator as I think Clay's did. Copy them to your [MetaTrader Path]\MQL4\Scripts folder. For them to work, you have to do two things. First, check the checkbox found in: Main Menu --&gt; Tools --&gt; Options --&gt; Expert Advisors --&gt; Allow automated trading Second, press the Auto Trading button in the toolbar. Then drag the SetLotSize script to your chart to set your risk. You can use this script again when you want to update the Lot Size for the scripts after your Account Size changed. After that you just drag one of the other scripts to your chart and it will do what the name of the script says. Try them on Demo first. Happy trading

--- 帖子 #15501 ---
I agree with your friend to some degree. We cannot beat institutional money and algos ( not on a large platform anyways ) - however we have an edge they do not have. that is that we can enter the market or choose to sit on the bench. They cannot sit on the bench and wait for perfect entries they have to get to work always. We can get into a trade once the direction is confirmed ride their push and out quickly and before its finished. I would hazard a guess as to why Kostas1 makes his daily target in 3-4 trades then leaves it alone.. he knows that institutions move price to suit their requirements and provide liquidity. 10-15 pips is better than none and Break even is better than minus 20... these small wins add up over 200 trading days to massive wins when compounded. If we get in and out cleanly then we can win in the long term by taking short term targets and staying in control psychologically and following a plan/strategy with iron discipline. Every time i have lost a trade that hurt, i have moved a stop or entered or exited on a hunch outwith my plan... if i lose and i executed the plan then it doesn't hold any emotional pain for me. I just move on to the next. We have to hold to a plan that suits us individually. Its been proven time and again that people with exactly the same plans do not make the same outcomes. --- 帖子 #15711 ---
I use price action a lot. If price action tells me to take the trade...I take it. I don't take 10EMA touch only because it is just a 10 EMA 1st touch. I prefer for example to see a doji bar in M5 35/50 to take the M15 10 touch. The same for the 35/50. If I see a 2 bar retracememt to the 35/50 with steep and parallel MAs I take the trade exactly at the touch. If it takes more candles for the touch, I am waiting for a nice price action confirmation like hammer, double top/bottom, pin bar etc and then I take the trade. Same with constrainment... So it has not to do with putting more weight to any kind of trade...this is not an automated trading system. It is a strategy that learns you to read the market and have the most odds by your side .

--- 帖子 #15846 ---
Our target on this strategy is to grab 30 pips a day using proper money management. Suppose your initial risk is 20-30 pips, but you see PA start to stop/against your trade, you can exit with 5-10 pips. Pips is pips, no one will broke taking plus pips. Forget about risk reward ratio, since we don't use fix SL/TP. You can also take partial profit or use trailing stop if you are not sure where the market going, actually no one knows.

--- 帖子 #16252 ---
Hi voynich, many of your questions come down to personal trading style. The following comments are just my opinion, others trade differently: In you original post you wrote about confluence of H1 10 and 35/50. This is not a real confluence in my book because only in extreme cases there will be no such confluence (H1 10 EMA is very similar to a H15 40 EMA). A better confluece would be other, higher TF MAs and round numbers, pivots etc. like in your second trade - that one had a lot of confluence going on. The first trade is what I call a "hero trade". You are trading a breakout of a range / resistance. If it works, there will be a strong move and you'll be the hero of the day. In this case, your take profit could have been way higher. Note however how many times H1 35/50 has failed before (that's why price is in a range). One famous quote from another trader (Tom Dante) applies here: "Successful trading is like getting pregnant. Everybody congratulates you when you manage it but nobody asks how many time you got f***** first" (and people in forums only show the successful trades). My personal rules for such a trade include: Well-defined support / resistance (not an area, but a line) and at least three previous touches. Sometimes I take the third touch for a breakout, but only if there is a nice setup on the lower times frames that allows my to define a good stop for protection. You can look at higher TFs like D1 and round numbers for clues (I suggest adding at least the 100 pip lines to your chart). Always ask yourself what you are trading. Usually, Choros trades pullbacks in a trend for continuation. If there is no trend you can also try to use it to trade breakouts, but personally I would add some additional criteria for this as outlined above. Going with the trend is always easier. As others have noted, you were a bit unlucky with this particular trade. There was some rejection going on from the MAs, and expecting 10-15 pips was not unreasonable. Edit: If you were not trying to trade a breakout, you were trading a move into the upper end of a range, and your entry was not far below it. This is not really a high probability trade since you are trying to squeeze out the last few pips of a move. Can this work? Yes. Are there other setups with a higher probabilty of working out? Definitely.

--- 帖子 #16280 ---
"When it doesn't meet your requirements STAY OUT." Wise words i will print them out and paste them on my wall and hopefully be disciplined enough to follow them. My basic questions are as follows: For MA10 touch - is price in a solid or forming a solid trend - Is the pull back 1 or 2 bars and has is touched or is close to the MA10 - Is the MA10 at a steep angle - Are the 35/50 tilting in the direction of my entry - Are the 35/50 flat or to wide apart or spreading - Has price recently come from a Higher Time Frame MA or a RN or a SnR - Is price to close too a Higher Time Frame MA or a Rn or a SnR For MA35/50 bounce - is price in a solid or forming a solid trend - if pullback is not 1 or 2 candles wait for price action signal - Is the pullback fast and almost vertical - Are 35/50 at a steep angle - Are the 35/50 flat or wide apart or spreading - Has price recently come from a Higher Time Frame MA or a RN or a SnR - Is price to close too a Higher Time Frame MA or a Rn or a SnR These are the questions i ask myself. Exactly as wrote them down

Again, no hard evidence, just a personal thought to potentially test further and of course strong setups very often return way more than 10 pips.

Hi, there are two issues with your analysis from my POV. Firstly, 1 &amp; 2 you have marked, if you look closely, they did not touch. Sure, depends how you count them and whether "nearly touches" matter. For me they don't. Either it touched or it didn't. I could look at it differently after a sharp retrace - if it missed a pip or two then conditionally I could count it. But not while the price had those little moves next to 10MA just before and then simply was sharply falling next to it. Also, the price is not created by the corner, which is just a result of individual, graphic interpretation of a candle. It is created in the vertical axis and it's the verticle distance that counts, not horizontal. See attached pictures. But secondly, most importantly, I did not trade the touch. That was a bounce from 10MA confirmed by that long wicked rejection bar that I have entered seconds before it closed. Markets don't move straight and clean so to me it doesn't matter that it made that 8 pips move just before, it happens. 35/50 steep and on top, no S/R below, rookie mistake you didn't take it. It wasn't far away from making this right, the price went through SL just a few pips only to hit the target later on. I highly value your experience and the fact that you are willing to share your knowledge, but it's not the first time your iritated tone while doing it is difficult to accept. Best, J.

Hi, one remark regarding the scale of the charts. It should be set in a way that reflects true angles. Drag the angle measurement tool so the line shows 45 degrees. Then draw a rectangle so that it has the previously drawn line of the angle tool as a diagonal. Obviously, the recangle should be effectively a square. If you want to be very precise you can take a screenshot, open it in Photoshop and measure whether its a true square. I don't think its neccessary though. If it looks like a square its good enough. If its clearly not a square and looks rather like a narrow rectangle, the evaluation of the MA steepness might be completely wrong, you will take trades in flat areas thinking its steep or miss some of the proper steepness thinking its flat, depending whether your scale it too large or too small. I have also checked this with the orignal Dance setup Eclayf was using and it is a very close match (if not perfect). In my case the workspace is 100 pips tall (with one chart top to bottom, or 50 with the two of them) with zoom set to the second closest one (zoom affects angles big time as it only zooms horizontally, not at all vertically). Yet of course this depends on your screen resolution and toolbars/tools you have open above and below the charts. I'm not sure whether this has been already addressed here, seems like a small detail but if you think about it, the scale might affect your trading decisions big time with this method. I also highly recommend using a scaling script - you define the pip numbers, drop it on a chart and it will always revert back to it so you don't need to readjust manually. BR, J.

--- 帖子 #16384 ---
Interesting trick ! The issue has been discussed here a few times. My solution is to keep "Scale fix" checked and always the same range in pips (50 for M1, 100 for M5, 150 for M15). I use the default scaling for H4, and Daily. Keeping the same scale, allows to judge the angle the same way each time.

--- 帖子 #16390 ---
If anyone is using MT5 and would like to be able to determine whether the MAs are at the correct min. angle before entry, here is a bunch of color changing MAs that will do the trick. One set of 35/50 is for 25 degree slope (changing colors from aqua and orange for 35 and 50 if the slope is right, if it isn't they are both white, easy to customize though). Third file is for 45 degrees 10MA and second set is optional - I guess it's nothing the original rules mentioned, yet I like to limit my 10MA trades only to the situations where 35/50 are also at least 45 degrees steep. This second set simply overlays the first one with darker blue for 35 and red for 50 once at least 45 deg. is reached. I have precisely aligned it with true angles (3.5 points for 25 deg. 1st set and 8.5 points for 45 deg. in the 2nd one) and now they will indicate the correct angles regardless of your scale setup. I think Kostas and few others were using this back in the day but I don't think it was for MT5 though. BR, J.

--- 帖子 #16391 ---
I was recently wondering about testing in practice some other pairs. GU and EJ work just fine, classics. But EU and AU are sometimes too slow and this means often crappy, ranging market. I thought about 2 initial criteria (before even eyeballing the chart for known patterns), the trick is that they are in a way mutually contradictive. A good pair should have fairly high volatility (represented here by ADR) but it is sometimes a result of low liquidity which in turn transaltes into higher spread (and jitter) - whereas my second criteria is obviously a low spread. So I was filtering out both of them and then tested through a ratio of ADR/spread (which came out as not such a great indicator after all - favouring AU as second best when in fact I want to possibly get rid of it ). Green are the ones I have been always looking at. Blue ones are worth further testing with EURAUD being clearly the leader. Red ones seemed interesting at first but the spread of 3 and above is too much for my taste and USDSEK is simply too crazy, jittery, clearly lacking liquidity. The 3 last ones despite their crazyness, in the very steep areas of 35/50 of at least 45 degrees, seem to react extremely well to the Dance at first sight, many times literally exploding in the right direction upon first touches while still enabling regular SL. I don't think I will be trading them coz of the spread but who knows, I will keep an eye. Yellow ones seem ok but they do not bring anything extra to the table except for slightly higher spread than pairs with similar ADR. With one exception - if someone was looking for more than 2 pairs to follow, then EURAUD, GBPUSD &amp; CDYJPY would be a top selection trio with 0 correlation, being beneficial in some cases. Of course, the results are not static, ADR changes daily, spread even faster and is also broker specific, obviously. Any other thoughts on pair selection are highly welcome. BR, J.

I simply used Swingman's three line indicator. I colored the H1 10 EMA the same as the chart background because have a 40 EMA (M15 10 EMA equivalent for H1) and a 50 EMA on the charts is redundant." That's also why 35/50 is stronger than 10 on any timeframe as it is effectively ~10MA on higher time frame BR, J.

Hi Dancers, this one was pure, pure beautie. They really don't come that great all too often. First picture is with scale changed by 50% to show the ovarall situation and the second one is the scale with true angles I trade with. 1) Start of a new trend 2) Rapid drop 3) Equally rapid retrace 4) Not following 2 bar rule which is still ok by the rules as long as the move is rapid (it's best to have progressively longer bars though which didn't happen here) 5) First 35/50 touch and confluence with a strong S/R level created by the day before yesterday's low. That support was holding up quite well even earlier today but then was broken and therefore became resistance. It was a second test from the bottom if you look closely which was a bit weaker though. 6) Entered exactly at the touch with SL16 and although the price hesitated a bit, it created two nice confirmation bars before it literally run down my way for a swift manual close at 26 pips. The more I trade the more belief I have in any type of 35/50 trades. This includes 35/50 bounces - just forget about all the rules for a moment and just look how often a pin bar that spikes through both 35 &amp; 50 that are close together will bring at least 10-15 pips, SL just below that pin bar. 35/50 don't even need to have an angle, it's sufficient if the price has at least slightly been already heading in the direction of the trade about to open (sometimes even simply creating some HLs or LHs just before). 10MA on the other hand lies to me too often, it's best to stick only to trades with very steep 35/50 and parallel when trading 10MA and trade only first touches or P/A at first retracements. MA10 is a deceitful little thing At least on M15. Have a nice weekend. J.

--- 帖子 #16417 ---
Hi Maxwell, Yes - take only signals in line with the rules (read them carefuly, multiple times) when there is a new trend forming and the 35/50 become very steep and close to or on top of each other and do not trade into 1 or 2 previous days/weeks/months low or high, i.e. make sure your opening price is a fair distance away from them. You will not trade too often that way (good! no overtrading) as such cases are not all that common but they are characterized by an increased success ratio. They also constitute an excellent starting point before it becomes easier to spot some of the other stuff. Trades from 35/50 seem to be stronger, as I have mentioned in my previous post, from my POV 10MA tends to be more tricky. Best, J.

At some point later in the thread, I have the MAs that I usually follow. Here they are again: H4: EMA 10, SMA 35, EMA 50, SMA 200 H1: EMA 10, SMA 35, EMA 50, EMA 40 (=H4 EMA10) M15: EMA 10, SMA 35, EMA 50, EMA 40 (=H1 EMA10), EMA 160 (=H4 EMA10) M5: EMA 5, EMA12, EMA 23, SMA 50, EMA 120 (=H1 EMA10) Just focus on the 35/50 first (preferably M15), just keep the H1 10 and H4 10 equivalents as a reference.

--- 帖子 #16481 ---
In the case of MAs 35/50, there is the following consideration as to whether it does not make sense to add the 40EMA . Why: H4 divided by 4 is H1, H1 divided by 4 gives M15. the 10EMA on H4 and H1 results in the 40EMA at the next smaller time frame. so the H4 10 is on H1 40 and H1 10 is on M15 40. so i would display 35/40/50 on the chart because its logical.
